news.Title: A SpaceX-Tesla Deal Could Come in December. Here's Why 1 Group of Investors Should Be Worried.
news.Content:
A merger between Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX) and Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) would have far-reaching consequences, not least by combining a leader in physical artificial intelligence (AI) -- Tesla's electric vehicles, robotaxi, and Optimus robots -- with a company that has a rapidly growing AI infrastructure services business (SpaceX).

That combination could have profound consequences for the major near-term catalyst for both companies, namely robotaxi, and that should be considered a threat to Uber Technologies (NYSE:UBER). Here's why.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

SpaceX and Tesla could merge

To be clear and consistent, I don't think aggressively pursuing a merger is in the best interest of Tesla shareholders right now. In truth, we don't know if a bid will occur and what the terms will be. However, it strikes me that Tesla shareholders have waited for years and endured plenty of missed robotaxi timelines, the disappointments of Cybertruck, and industrywide downward revisions to electric vehicle sales, only to sell out just as Tesla is set to scale up its robotaxi rollout.

That's an issue for Tesla shareholders, as they could end up with a larger share of the new company than the 47% ownership stake Bank of America analysts estimated in an all-stock deal. Still, I think there's another group of shareholders who should be more worried: Uber shareholders .

A merger would accelerate robotaxi development

A merger would create even better conditions for Tesla to realize its ambition to become a transportation-as-a-service (TaaS) company running a fleet of low-cost-per-mile Cybercabs. That's a direct threat to Uber's marketplace, at least in the areas where Cybercab has regulatory clearance. The threat has not gone unnoticed, and there's a reason Uber already has multi-partner autonomous robotaxi arrangements with companies like Waymo, Zoox, and Wayve.

When Tesla CEO Elon Musk says the "vast majority" of Cybercab will be "Tesla-owned and Transport-as-a-Service," this is highly unlikely to encompass a partnership with Uber.

Five reasons why a merger would enhance Tesla's robotaxi rollout

In addition, merging with SpaceX would bring many benefits for Tesla's robotaxi.

First, as part of a combined company, Tesla could implement SpaceX's Starlink connectivity to improve navigation and the functioning of the robotaxi fleet . This would help accelerate Tesla's journey toward lowering its cost per mile to near the $0.30-per-mile target.

Second, a merger would create AI and software synergies and provide access to SpaceX's compute. Tesla generates vast amounts of data from its autonomous driving software and robotaxi fleets, which could be analyzed more effectively using SpaceX's compute power. This would help accelerate learning and enable training and simulation of models on Tesla's Full Self-Driving (FSD) software. Again, this would help progress toward a lower cost per mile for Cybercab.

Story Continues

Image source: Getty Images.

Third, Tesla famously does not indulge in significant direct marketing, and the addition of the Starlink and xAI customer bases would immediately give Tesla a core subscriber base on which to promote its robotaxi service as it builds out its TaaS model.

Fourth, while there's a healthy debate around whether it's more a case of Tesla's cash flow bankrolling SpaceX's capital spending or the other way around, the reality is that robotaxi/Cybercab would be the key near-term catalyst for a combined company. Given the combined balance sheet, there's no doubt it could easily finance a massive rollout and a ramp-up in Cybercab production.

Fifth, there's already substantial talent sharing between Tesla and SpaceX, and a merger would only create a more conducive environment for it.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Where next for SpaceX, Tesla, and Uber?

All told, everything points to a merger making it easier for Tesla to ramp robotaxi and drive Cybercab's total cost of ownership (TCO) per mile lower. The latter is the key metric to follow, as it would facilitate a virtuous cycle in which low ride fares encourage further Cybercab fleet expansion. That's a real risk for Uber, because if its robotaxi partners can't achieve a comparable TCO, then Tesla's robotaxi could make significant inroads into some of its most profitable geographies.

news.Title: 5 High-Conviction Stocks Billionaire Philippe Laffont Is Betting On for 2027
news.Content:
Coatue Management's November 16 regulatory filing puts billionaire Philippe Laffont's positioning back in focus as investors look toward 2027. Its ten largest disclosed stock holdings represented 55.9% of a $54.5 billion reported portfolio at September 30, with chipmakers and equipment suppliers carrying much of the exposure.

In its May 6 public-markets update, Coatue highlighted the expanding token economy and identified AI agents as the industry's next major opportunity. That theme reaches beyond chip designers. Our look at AI holdings shared by two billionaire investors follows the spending into manufacturing equipment and electricity.

Those connections carry different risks. Infrastructure orders can support suppliers while construction bills pressure their customers' cash flow. A larger holding can also reflect price gains rather than fresh purchases. As with other high-conviction technology portfolios , the question for 2027 is whether growing demand will produce the earnings investors already expect.

Recently, we created a video looking at the 10 stocks billionaires Dalio and Laffont love. You can click below to see these stocks in our video on YouTube:

For our broader look at Coatue's largest positions, see our article 10 High-Conviction Stocks Billionaire Philippe Laffont Is Betting On for 2027 . Below, we present the five highest-ranked stocks from that list.

Our Methodology

To compile our list, we reviewed Coatue Management's Q3 2026 13F filing and identified its ten largest stock holdings as of September 30, 2026, excluding ETFs and options. We used each holding's weight in the reported portfolio as a proxy for investment conviction and ranked the stocks from lowest to highest based on the value of Coatue's stake. We also included portfolio weights, changes in shares held from the previous quarter, and Q2 2026 hedge fund holder counts from Insider Monkey's database.

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points ( see more details here ).

5. Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ: LRCX )

Coatue Management's Stake: $3.26 billion

Portfolio Weight: 5.98%

Market Capitalization: $263.36 billion

Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ:LRCX) sells the equipment that deposits and removes materials as chipmakers build increasingly complicated devices. More layers and more demanding production steps can mean additional work for its tools, making the company a way to follow the manufacturing investment behind AI.

Story Continues

The fund's Lam position illustrates why share counts deserve attention alongside market values. Coatue disclosed 9.93 million shares at September 30, an increase of 5.13%, even as the stake's value declined from $4.09 billion to $3.26 billion over the quarter.

On October 21, Lam reported September-quarter revenue of $8.22 billion, up 22% from the preceding quarter. Its GAAP operating margin reached 40.0%, compared with 37.4% in June. Management's December-quarter revenue forecast of $8.6 billion, plus or minus $400 million, pointed to another sequential increase.

Market confidence has been less steady than those operating results. Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon maintained a Buy rating and a $350 target on November 2, even as the chip-equipment group faced concern about the durability of AI spending. China supplied 35% of Lam's September-quarter revenue, leaving export restrictions and shifts in regional investment important risks.

Lam also earns money after its machines are installed. Customer support-related and other revenue reached $2.49 billion in the latest quarter. That business gives investors another source of sales to watch in 2027, alongside new equipment shipments. Our analysis of how much protection Lam's support revenue offers explains the limits: the category includes upgrades and equipment as well as service. Customers can defer some of that spending when their own growth slows.

4. Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ: META )

Coatue Management's Stake: $3.27 billion

Portfolio Weight: 6.01%

Market Capitalization: $1.58 trillion

Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) offers a clear example of the tension between AI-driven growth and the spending required to sustain it. On October 21, the company reported third-quarter revenue of $64.6 billion, up 26%. Ad impressions increased 10%, while the average price per ad rose 14%, showing that the advertising business was growing through both volume and pricing.

Coatue raised its disclosed share count by 78.72% during the third quarter, taking the position to 4.51 million shares. Meta's portfolio weight rose from 2.93% to 6.01%, making it one of the clearest increases in exposure among the fund's largest holdings.

Management attributed incremental advertising revenue to stronger engagement, better recommendations, and more efficient monetization from its AI investments. That gives shareholders an existing business against which to assess the spending. The prospect is that better results for advertisers support demand even before newer AI products make a substantial contribution.

For 2027, management expects to keep investing aggressively in both the core business and emerging AI initiatives. It anticipates strong overall revenue growth but has not provided a full-year revenue forecast. Other investors are considering additional ways to monetize the infrastructure, including Dan Niles' proposal for a public-cloud business . That remains an investor's idea rather than an established earnings stream.

Cash generation is the immediate constraint. Third-quarter capital expenditures, including finance-lease principal payments, reached $34.91 billion, exceeding operating cash flow and leaving negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion. Sustaining advertising momentum would strengthen the case for continued investment, but the timing of returns from the newer AI initiatives remains uncertain.

3. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT )

Coatue Management's Stake: $3.31 billion

Portfolio Weight: 6.08%

Market Capitalization: $3.85 trillion

Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) enters 2027 with a cloud business that is accelerating even as investors scrutinize the cost of expanding it. In results released on October 28, Azure revenue rose 48% to $33.2 billion for the quarter ended September 30. Total revenue increased 19% to $92.3 billion, giving the company a strong start to fiscal 2027.

Coatue more than doubled its disclosed share count during the third quarter, increasing it 119.93% to 6.46 million. Microsoft's weight rose from 2.25% to 6.08% of the reported portfolio. The change places greater emphasis on the company's ability to turn its cloud expansion into sustained earnings.

Microsoft sells cloud computing alongside the workplace software customers already use. That combination gives it several ways to benefit as businesses adopt AI: more computing consumption, additional software subscriptions, and tools that help customers build their own applications. The opportunity extends beyond selling access to any one AI model.

Commercial remaining performance obligations reached $677 billion, up 73% from a year earlier. Those commitments provide evidence of demand, although their value depends on when services are delivered and revenue is recognized. Our discussion of the revenue visibility behind Microsoft's backlog examines that distinction.

The margin trend deserves attention alongside the growth figures. Microsoft's cloud gross margin was 66%, compared with 68% a year earlier. For 2027, investors will watch whether additional capacity supports enough profitable usage to offset the infrastructure bill. A large backlog helps explain the appeal, but it cannot by itself establish how much cash the expansion will ultimately generate.

2. Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MU )

Coatue Management's Stake: $3.49 billion

Portfolio Weight: 6.40%

Market Capitalization: $813.52 billion

Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) offers a direct test of whether the AI investment cycle has changed the economics of memory. It supplies the DRAM and storage used in servers and devices, including high-bandwidth memory for AI systems. Customers need more of these products, but investors still remember how quickly shortages can become excess supply.

Coatue increased its disclosed Micron share count by 4.22% to 3.27 million during the third quarter. The stake's reported value declined despite that increase, yet Micron was the portfolio's second-largest stock holding at $3.49 billion.

The company's September 30 results showed fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $54.23 billion, compared with $11.32 billion a year earlier. Adjusted free cash flow reached $33.20 billion. Management forecast first-quarter fiscal 2027 sales of $61.5 billion, plus or minus $1.5 billion, and said strategic customer agreements increased its confidence in the durability of performance.

That visibility has helped keep analysts constructive through the selloff. Bernstein's Mark Li reiterated a Buy rating and a $1,300 target in early November, arguing that tight DRAM supply and contract pricing support earnings beyond the current quarter. Our coverage of Bernstein's view after the memory selloff explores the debate.

For 2027, the issue is whether customer commitments and pricing stay strong as investment expands. Micron's fiscal 2026 net capital spending reached $27.37 billion. More capacity can support growth, but it also raises the cost of being wrong about demand. The unusually strong cash generation provides room to invest while leaving the memory cycle as an important constraint on sentiment.

1. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited (NYSE: TSM )

Coatue Management's Stake: $4.31 billion

Portfolio Weight: 7.90%

Market Capitalization: $1.75 trillion

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited (NYSE:TSM) sits where competing chip designers converge: the factories that turn their designs into working silicon. That gives the company exposure to demand across AI processors and custom chips, although it also leaves shareholders funding an increasingly expensive manufacturing network.

Coatue's largest disclosed stock position was worth $4.31 billion at September 30, representing 7.90% of its reported portfolio. The fund held 9.44 million depositary shares, up 5.86% from June. Its commitment spans both the scale of the existing holding and an increase in the number of shares reported.

Results released on October 15 showed third-quarter dollar revenue of $46.72 billion, up 41.2% from a year earlier. The company expected fourth-quarter revenue of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion. Its newer 2-nanometer technology already supplied 8% of quarterly wafer revenue, offering an early indication of the production ramp that investors will be following into 2027.

Demand remained strong after the quarter closed. October revenue rose 59.7% year over year in local-currency terms. Bernstein analyst Mark Li raised his target to $600 on November 4 and retained an Outperform rating, pointing to custom-chip demand and growth at the most advanced factories.

The harder question is what those sales cost to deliver. Gross margin fell to 66.4% from 67.7% in the preceding quarter as the new process ramped. Our discussion of TSMC's record AI demand and growing costs examines that tension. Strong demand entering 2027 supports the expansion, but weaker factory utilization would leave the company carrying more capacity before it earns the expected returns.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of TSM as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: Dell Technologies (DELL) Q3 Earnings and Revenues Surpass Estimates
news.Content:
Dell Technologies (DELL) came out with quarterly earnings of $9.45 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $6.76 per share. This compares to earnings of $2.59 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +39.79%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this computer and technology services provider would post earnings of $4.97 per share when it actually produced earnings of $7.04, delivering a surprise of +41.65%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

Dell Technologies, which belongs to the Zacks Computer - Micro Computers industry, posted revenues of $54.94 billion for the quarter ended October 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 8.98%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $27.01 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

Dell Technologies shares have added about 166.1% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 5.7%.

What's Next for Dell Technologies?

While Dell Technologies has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for Dell Technologies was favorable. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to outperform the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Story Continues

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $7.64 on $54.72 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $26.25 on $194.94 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. In terms of the Zacks Industry Rank, Computer - Micro Computers is currently in the top 40% of the 250 plus Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

Another stock from the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector, Marvell Technology (MRVL), has yet to report results for the quarter ended October 2026. The results are expected to be released on December 1.

This chipmaker is expected to post quarterly earnings of $1.10 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +44.7%. The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.2% lower over the last 30 days to the current level.

Marvell Technology's revenues are expected to be $3.16 billion, up 52.2% from the year-ago quarter.

news.Title: Billionaire Philippe Laffont’s 10 High-Conviction Stock Bets for 2027
news.Content:
Coatue Management's November 16 regulatory filing puts billionaire Philippe Laffont's positioning back in focus as investors look toward 2027. Its ten largest disclosed stock holdings represented 55.9% of a $54.5 billion reported portfolio at September 30, with chipmakers and equipment suppliers carrying much of the exposure.

In its May 6 public-markets update, Coatue highlighted the expanding token economy and identified AI agents as the industry's next major opportunity. That theme reaches beyond chip designers. Our look at AI holdings shared by two billionaire investors follows the spending into manufacturing equipment and electricity.

Those connections carry different risks. Infrastructure orders can support suppliers while construction bills pressure their customers' cash flow. A larger holding can also reflect price gains rather than fresh purchases. As with other high-conviction technology portfolios , the question for 2027 is whether growing demand will produce the earnings investors already expect.

Recently, we created a video looking at the 10 stocks billionaires Dalio and Laffont love. You can click below to see these stocks in our video on YouTube:

We covered the full selection in 10 High-Conviction Stocks Billionaire Philippe Laffont Is Betting On for 2027 . Below, we look at the stocks ranked 10th through 6th.

Our Methodology

To compile our list, we reviewed Coatue Management's Q3 2026 13F filing and identified its ten largest stock holdings as of September 30, 2026, excluding ETFs and options. We used each holding's weight in the reported portfolio as a proxy for investment conviction and ranked the stocks from lowest to highest based on the value of Coatue's stake. We also included portfolio weights and changes in shares held from the previous quarter.

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points ( see more details here ).

10. Applied Materials, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMAT )

Coatue Management's Stake: $2.31 billion

Portfolio Weight: 4.24%

Market Capitalization: $277.96 billion

Applied Materials, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMAT) entered its new fiscal year with record results and a fresh analyst downgrade. That combination captures the argument around chip-equipment stocks: demand can remain strong while investors disagree about how much growth the shares already reflect.

Story Continues

Coatue increased its disclosed share count by 7.18% during the third quarter to 4.52 million. Applied Materials was the fund's tenth-largest stock position, even though its reported market value fell from the preceding quarter.

The company, which supplies materials-engineering equipment and services to chipmakers, reported fourth-quarter revenue of $10.41 billion on November 12, up 53% year over year. Non-GAAP earnings reached $4.16 a share, and quarterly free cash flow totaled $2.62 billion. Its first-quarter fiscal 2027 outlook called for revenue of $11.1 billion, plus or minus $500 million.

AI-related investment is broadening the opportunity. Applied expects calendar 2026 advanced-packaging revenue to grow approximately 90% and inspection and metrology revenue to rise more than 50%. These are tools customers need as they connect more chips and manufacture structures that are increasingly difficult to build accurately.

The following day, Summit Insights cut the stock to Hold from Buy. Analyst Kinngai Chan cited cleanroom constraints and expected 2027 equipment spending to favor lithography over etch and deposition. That makes the mix of spending as relevant as the overall budget. Our discussion of whether Applied Materials' AI growth is already priced in examines the expectations surrounding the business. Into 2027, investors will be looking for orders and cash generation to keep supporting the expansion.

9. GE Vernova Inc. (NYSE: GEV )

Coatue Management's Stake: $2.34 billion

Portfolio Weight: 4.29%

Market Capitalization: $206.42 billion

GE Vernova Inc. (NYSE:GEV) brings the electricity side of the AI expansion into this portfolio. The company supplies power-generation equipment and the grid hardware needed to deliver that electricity. Its opportunity extends well beyond data centers, although its growing power requirements have sharpened investor interest in turbine and transformer suppliers.

Coatue reduced its share count by 3.77% to 2.46 million during the third quarter. The remaining position still represented 4.29% of the reported portfolio, showing that a modest trim can coexist with substantial exposure to the power-equipment cycle.

On October 28, GE Vernova reported third-quarter revenue of $12.6 billion, up 27% from a year earlier. Backlog reached $197 billion, rising $20 billion sequentially, and management expected it to exceed $200 billion in the fourth quarter. For 2027, that order book provides visibility, but the important question is how efficiently factories can turn commitments into deliveries.

The company is also expanding through acquisitions. Its proposed $9 billion purchase of Trench Group would add high-voltage grid equipment and strengthen a supplier relationship. Closing is expected in late 2027, subject to regulatory approvals, so investors should distinguish the eventual contribution from the business already operating today.

Our coverage of GE Vernova's challenge of turning demand into durable growth examines the manufacturing demands behind that expansion. A larger installed equipment base can support future service revenue. Supply constraints, delivery delays, and continuing problems in the wind business could still interrupt the conversion of a growing backlog into stronger earnings.

8. Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ: AVGO )

Portfolio Weight: 4.30%

Market Capitalization: $1.63 trillion

Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO) has become a useful test of whether extraordinary AI sales can translate into durable shareholder returns. It designs custom accelerators and networking chips for large customers, alongside an infrastructure-software business that includes VMware. That combination links the stock to both expanding computing capacity and established enterprise spending.

Coatue's disclosed position grew 14.02% to 6.67 million shares during the third quarter. The increase made Broadcom one of the more actively expanded holdings within this group, although the filing does not explain the fund's reasons for adding shares.

Results released on September 2 showed fiscal third-quarter revenue rising 86% to $29.6 billion. AI semiconductor revenue reached $16.7 billion, up 221%, while free cash flow totaled $13.7 billion. Management also raised its fiscal 2027 AI chip revenue outlook to about $115 billion, Reuters reported. That forecast gives investors a concrete measure against which to judge the next stage of the buildout.

Analysts remain divided about the quality of that growth. On November 13, Rothschild & Co Redburn downgraded Broadcom to Neutral from Buy and cut its target to $398 from $595. The firm highlighted financing hurdles facing frontier AI customers and questioned how quickly the shares could earn a higher valuation.

Our examination of Broadcom's reliance on a few major customers explains why revenue growth alone does not settle the debate. Large custom-chip programs can produce substantial sales, but delayed customer funding or deployment schedules would matter. Progress toward the 2027 outlook will depend on those commitments becoming sustained deliveries.

7. Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN )

Coatue Management's Stake: $2.89 billion

Portfolio Weight: 5.31%

Market Capitalization: $2.79 trillion

Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) has given investors a specific growth expectation to test in 2027. In its October 29 earnings release, Chief Executive Officer Andy Jassy projected that Amazon Web Services revenue would grow more than 40% in both 2027 and 2028. The cloud business had just reported third-quarter sales of $46.0 billion, up 39% from a year earlier.

Coatue held 11.62 million shares at September 30, down 1.83% from June. The position's reported value nevertheless increased to $2.89 billion. That distinction matters: Amazon remained a major commitment, but the higher dollar value did not come from a larger share count.

AWS rents computing power, storage, and related services to customers, while Amazon's retail operations and advertising business provide other sources of revenue. The latest quarter showed improving profitability across the group: operating income reached $28.1 billion, including $17.8 billion from AWS. That mix gives the company substantial earnings with which to pursue its expansion.

Its own AI chips add another dimension. They could help Amazon offer customers more attractive computing economics and deepen demand for its cloud services. Our coverage of Amazon's custom chips and capital commitments explores how that opportunity connects to the spending bill.

The cash-flow figures show why investors still debate the pace of investment. Operating cash flow reached $168.3 billion over the preceding twelve months, but free cash flow was negative $42.4 billion as infrastructure purchases increased. Jassy's cloud forecast raises expectations for 2027; delivering it while containing the cash demands of construction will matter more than the growth rate alone.

6. Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ: SPCX )

Coatue Management's Stake: $2.94 billion

Portfolio Weight: 5.39%

Market Capitalization: $1.92 trillion

Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) gives investors exposure to satellite connectivity, launch services, and an expanding AI business under one roof. The appeal for 2027 rests on whether these operations can support one another as spending rises across the group.

Coatue increased its reported share count 4.82% to 19.46 million during the third quarter. SpaceX accounted for 5.39% of the disclosed portfolio at September 30, placing it between Lam Research and Amazon by stake value.

SpaceX reported third-quarter results on October 20, with revenue reaching $14.6 billion, up 161% year over year. Its Super Intelligence segment contributed $7.6 billion, while the connectivity business grew revenue 69%. Starlink ended September with 13.6 million consumer subscribers, up from 12 million at the end of June. Those recurring subscriptions provide a different source of demand from individual launch contracts.

Another development could reshape the connectivity business next year. SpaceX agreed on October 8 to acquire licenses in the 800 MHz band to advance Starlink Mobile, with closing expected in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory and other conditions. The deal would extend its efforts to connect satellite and terrestrial mobile services.

The scale of the ambitions also makes funding important. Our discussion of SpaceX's financing plans for its AI expansion explores that tension. Investors still need to see computing capacity generate returns while the company expands its satellite network. Regulatory approvals, infrastructure costs, and the pace of commercial adoption could all affect how much of the growth reaches shareholders.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of SPCX as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: Microsoft (MSFT) Is One of the Safest Ways to Own AI
news.Content:
Microsoft (MSFT) seems to be one of the safest ways to invest in artificial intelligence (AI). The cloud and software giant posted $45.9 billion in operating income in Q1 2027. I believe that gives it considerable room to fund its next stage of growth. CEO Satya Nadella recently remarked, "We think of Copilot as the new OS for work."

I like that ambition, but I also like the existing business behind it. Following the recent tech sell-off we've seen in the past few weeks, Microsoft's valuation makes that combination especially appealing. Thus, I rate MSFT stock a Buy .

Microsoft Has Several Ways to Win

While "safer" is relative in tech and MSFT stock is certainly not immune to sharp pullbacks, Microsoft has built multiple ways to win as enterprises adopt AI. Rather than betting the company on a single breakthrough, it relies on cash-flowing legacy subscriptions to fund a full-stack AI ecosystem. At the infrastructure layer, Azure sells the raw computing capacity needed to train and run AI, while custom in-house silicon alongside third-party processors from Nvidia (NVDA) and AMD (AMD) reduces its reliance on any single chipmaker.

Promotion

BLACK FRIDAY SALE

Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter , and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

Learn more about TipRanks Premium

Microsoft 365 Copilot embeds AI into daily office workflows, GitHub Copilot monetizes software developers, and its cybersecurity suite protects the resulting data. If rollout in one area slows, it still has several other growth engines that can pick up the slack.

In addition, I view its approach to models as quite appealing. Copilot's Auto mode automatically routes user prompts to whichever model offers the best balance of speed, capability, and cost for a given task. Similarly, Microsoft Foundry acts as an enterprise storefront offering Microsoft's proprietary models alongside rivals like OpenAI, Anthropic, and competing providers. This also includes open models. Microsoft can therefore earn from usage even when customers switch model suppliers.

At its Ignite conference in November , Microsoft pushed Copilot further into practical work. The company rolled out a unified starting hub in Copilot that merges Chat for quick queries with Cowork for longer, multi-step projects, while preparing a broad rollout of Copilot Code in the coming weeks so everyday employees can build custom apps without writing code.

Story Continues

At the same time, Microsoft rolled out governance and data tools designed to monetize the infrastructure around AI agents. Updates to Agent 365 help IT teams manage permissions and track return on investment across both Microsoft and third-party agents, while Microsoft IQ links those agents to a company's internal knowledge and workflows. As corporate AI usage scales, these supporting layers become increasingly sticky. So I think Microsoft can earn from the work happening around a model, even if it doesn't produce every winning model itself.

The Latest Quarter Shows It Working

The latest quarter shows it working already for Microsoft. In its Fiscal Q1 2027 results , Microsoft's revenue grew 19% year-over-year to $92.3 billion. Operating income increased 21% to $45.9 billion, while adjusted earnings per share (EPS) rose 18% to $4.89. Microsoft Cloud revenue climbed 30% to $63.9 billion.

Azure accelerated to 48% growth, with guidance for 49%–50% constant-currency growth this quarter. That suggests customers are already using the capacity Microsoft is building.

Moreover, adoption figures are encouraging. Daily Copilot users increased nearly 50% sequentially and more than fivefold year-over-year. Customers with over 50,000 Copilot seats increased more than eightfold year-over-year. Copilot revenue growth also accelerated sequentially. Foundry passed 120,000 customers, with revenue more than tripling year-over-year.

Customers building agentic applications with multiple models increased fivefold year-over-year. I believe these figures suggest broader deployment, with large organizations committing to substantial usage. Volkswagen's (VWAGY) planned rollout to over 330,000 employees is one example .

Microsoft also has $677 billion in remaining commercial performance obligations. This provides excellent visibility into future revenue. Operating cash flow reached $58 billion, leaving $18.6 billion of free cash flow after cash investment. So that gives it considerable internal funding for expansion.

Note that enterprises are still early in putting agents into production. Yet Microsoft already supplies much of their software and identity infrastructure. Selling additional capabilities to those customers should be easier than building those relationships from scratch.

The Sell-Off Has Improved the Valuation

Now, the recent sell-off has pushed MSFT's valuation to rather attractive levels, in my view. Today, MSFT trades at 24.59x Fiscal 2027 consensus EPS of $20.03. That falls to 20.33x Fiscal 2028 EPS of $24.23 and 16.31x Fiscal 2029 EPS of $30.20. Consensus expects roughly 16% EPS growth this year, followed by nearly 21% and 25%. I find those multiples exceptional for a business with Microsoft's recurring revenue and profitability.

The estimates may also leave room for further upside. Adjusted EPS of $4.89 beat the latest $4.72 forecast. The preceding quarter delivered $4.74 against $4.24 expected. Repeated beats don't promise more, but they make me reluctant to assume consensus captures the full earnings opportunity.

Azure's acceleration and wider Copilot adoption could keep driving upgrades. Delivering today's estimates alone would bring the multiple toward 16.31x by Fiscal 2029. So I don't think strong returns would rely on an aggressive rerating.

Lastly, I should mention that investors are right to question returns on enormous AI spending. Microsoft's quarterly capex reached $45.2 billion, including finance leases. Competition from Amazon (AMZN) and Google (GOOGL) remains intense, and other enterprise AI platforms are also competing for customers.

Infrastructure costs could pressure cloud margins, and Copilot adoption might slow. Sustaining 20%-plus earnings growth also becomes harder at Microsoft's size. However, today's cloud growth and cash generation give me more confidence in the spending. Its AI business is already producing revenue across several products.

Is MSFT Stock a Buy?

Wall Street rates MSFT a Strong Buy, based on 35 Buys and four Holds. The $632.48 average price target implies roughly 28% upside from today's price levels.

Conclusion

Microsoft offers AI exposure without requiring one model or application to dominate. Its existing businesses fund the expansion, while Azure and Copilot already show substantial demand. Ignite adds more ways to earn from enterprise agents. At roughly 20.33x Fiscal 2028 earnings, I think the sell-off has created an attractive entry point for what could be one of the safest companies to own AI. I remain Bullish .

news.Title: Tesla and SpaceX Just Assembled Deal Teams for a $3.2 Trillion Merger. Here's What Investors Need to Know.
news.Content:
Elon Musk has made no secret of the fact that he would like to have many (if not all) of the companies he runs under one roof. And the enigmatic CEO has already taken several steps to accomplish that goal. Artificial intelligence (AI) start-up xAI merged with Twitter (now called X) before the combined company was folded into Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX) aka SpaceX.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

However, Musk's biggest coup would be to bring together SpaceX and Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA). The long-rumored combination just took another step closer to reality. Reports emerged on Tuesday that the electric vehicle (EV) maker and rocket launch company had appointed a handful of directors to oversee the largest merger in corporate history.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

A marriage of titans

Bringing together two companies of this size will be a daunting task. SpaceX has a market cap of roughly $1.7 trillion, while Tesla's clocks in at $1.5 trillion, making the combined entity worth $3.2 trillion and placing it among the world's five most valuable companies (as of this writing).

SpaceX and Tesla have chosen five of the companies' directors to conduct merger negotiations, according to a report that first appeared in The Financial Times. The quintet of executives -- two from SpaceX and three from Tesla -- have been charged with hashing out the details for the all-stock merger, according to the report.

Roelof Botha of SpaceX: Former managing director of prominent venture capital firm Sequoia Capital. Botha spent more than two decades with Sequoia after serving as PayPal 's CFO under Musk and has served on numerous boards of directors, including Unity Software , Block , and MongoDB .

Randy Glein of SpaceX: Co-founder of venture capital firm DFJ Growth. Glein is an aerospace engineer, and his firm was an early investor in SpaceX, taking a $10 million stake when the company was worth roughly $550 million. He has been a board member or observer for dozens of companies.

Robyn Denholm of Tesla: Australian chartered accountant and has been the automaker's board chair since 2018. Former tech executive at Sun Microsystems, which was acquired by Oracle , and Juniper Networks, which is now part of Hewlett Packard Enterprise .

Kathleen Wilson-Thompson of Tesla: Former executive with Kellogg Company and Walgreens. Served on numerous boards of directors, including Vulcan Materials and Ashland , and has been with Tesla since 2018.

Jack Hartung of Tesla: Former President and CFO of Chipotle after more than two decades with the company. Previous executive with McDonald's . Served on the boards of directors of Portillo's and The Honest Company and joined Tesla's board in 2025.

Story Continues

The diversity and wealth of experience among this group should give it the tools needed to complete the job -- though it won't be an easy one.

A daunting task

The job at hand is extraordinarily complex and will face a number of challenges in combining two companies of this size. One such hurdle will be determining a fair "exchange ratio" between Tesla and SpaceX shares. If the exchange is seen as favoring one company over another, it might not get the shareholder votes needed to succeed. Even if it's ultimately approved, an appearance of inequity could lead to shareholder lawsuits that could drag on for years. Any deal must also pass regulatory muster, considering the potential antitrust and national security implications.

To get it right, the special committees from both companies have hired independent financial advisors to help develop and refine the financial models that will form the foundation for the merger discussions. The principals will also be charged with developing a governance framework and deciding who will lead the newly formed entity.

While Musk is barred from the proceedings -- due to his inherent conflict of interest -- the special committees are permitted to "consult" with senior executives during their negotiations -- and no one is more senior than Musk. He has described the process as an "odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking, and I can't be in the conversation."

What it means for shareholders

At this juncture, we simply don't have enough information to make informed decisions about the implications for shareholders of either company.

That said, there's a strong case to be made for the joining of SpaceX and Tesla. Both companies are investing heavily in AI, with Tesla's Full Self-Driving (FSD) and SpaceX's Grok at the heart of those efforts. The companies are already inextricably intertwined, with Tesla supplying Megapack battery systems, vehicles, engineering support, and various parts and accessories to SpaceX. The pair are also joined at the hip regarding Terafab, the joint semiconductor manufacturing project. If combined, SpaceX and Tesla could integrate their efforts in AI, robotics, and connectivity.

The success or failure of the deal will likely hinge on the valuations assigned to each company and any resulting shareholder dilution. It will then have to run the regulatory gauntlet.

Stay tuned.

news.Title: Morgan Stanley’s 4 Best Semiconductor and Server Stocks to Buy for 2027
news.Content:
The semiconductor industry's investment cycle has advanced: The Semiconductor Industry Association's November 3 release put global third-quarter sales at $517.7 billion, up 24.1% from the preceding quarter. September sales reached $172.6 billion, jumping 146.8% from a year earlier. World Semiconductor Trade Statistics compiles the monthly data as three-month moving averages; these totals cover the semiconductor industry. For another perspective on the sector, read our 10 Best Semiconductor Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires .

Manufacturers also plan to spend more on production. In its third-quarter World Fab Forecast update, SEMI projected $159 billion in global fab equipment spending for 2026, growing by 29%, followed by $180 billion in 2027. The association forecast installed capacity growth of 5% in 2026 and 6% in 2027. Its forecast puts logic and microprocessor equipment spending at $71 billion in 2026, the largest category, with memory following as AI demand supports investment.

Regionally, SEMI expects China to remain the largest equipment-spending market in 2026, while forecasting 98% growth in the Americas and 191% growth in Europe and the Middle East. Its database tracks 1,612 facilities and production lines, which includes 150 prospective facilities or lines that could begin volume production in 2026 or later. Therefore, project timing matters alongside the headline spending totals.

Power and permits are still the biggest hurdles close to the customer. In its November 11 assessment, Morgan Stanley shifted 20% of its projected 2028 U.S. data-center capacity into 2029 following the midterm elections. The bank expects potential delays in Texas and Ohio as incoming administrations establish new requirements. It is keeping its 2027 construction outlook unchanged for projects that have already started. Its revised global capacity forecast calls for 9% growth in 2028 and 20% in 2029.

Borrowing costs add another complication. Morgan Stanley asset-backed securities strategist Carolyn Campbell said in an AI Boom Faces a Higher-Yield Roadblock podcast that yields on the highest-rated data-center bonds had risen from below 5% at the start of 2026 to close to 7%. Operators often fix rental income through long-term leases before arranging that financing, leaving higher interest costs to squeeze returns. The bank's November assessment also points to greater scrutiny of tenant quality, access to electricity and contractual protections when lenders evaluate new construction.

Story Continues

Campbell's issuance figures noted the funding constraint and mentioned that through October 16, data center operators had issued approximately $15 billion in asset-backed securities and another $7 billion in commercial mortgage-backed securities during 2026. She described that pace as roughly in line with the previous year, even though demand for facilities was much stronger, and expected the financing slowdown to prove temporary.

We examined the companies financing the buildout in Morgan Stanley Says These 8 Companies Will Spend $1.6 Trillion on AI Infrastructure in 2027 . Here, we turn to the semiconductor, server, and chip-design suppliers in the bank's research. For related investment ideas across physical computing infrastructure, see our 7 Best Data Center Hardware Stocks to Invest in .

We provided the expanded list of Morgan Stanley's 8 Best Semiconductor and Server Stocks to Buy for 2027 . The top 4 stocks are provided below:

Our Methodology

We selected eight Best Semiconductor and Server Stocks to Buy for 2027 from US-listed companies appearing in Morgan Stanley's October 15, 2026 research, Following AI's $1.6 Trillion Money Trail: Mapping the Revenue Generated by the Capex Boom, using its exhibit. The bank's semiconductor-and-server grouping includes electronic design automation, so we identify Synopsys and Cadence as design-software and intellectual-property suppliers. We ranked the eight stocks by Morgan Stanley's estimated percentage of total 2027 revenue exposed to AI infrastructure demand given in the exhibit, from highest to lowest.

4. Dell Technologies Inc. (NYSE: DELL )

Morgan Stanley's Estimated 2027 Revenue Exposure to AI Infrastructure Demand: 42.0%

Dell Technologies Inc. (NYSE: DELL ) exited its fiscal second quarter with a $95 billion AI-server backlog after booking $60.9 billion in orders and recognizing $16.4 billion in AI-server revenue. Its September 1 earnings release puts AI servers at the center of its infrastructure growth. Delivering those orders, rather than booking them alone, drives the revenue opportunity. Our 10 Best AI Infrastructure Stocks to Buy According to Hedge Funds examines related infrastructure investments.

Dell reported $47.0 billion in total revenue, growing 58% year over year and posting $5.385 billion in GAAP operating income. Infrastructure Solutions Group revenue climbed 89% to $31.8 billion, with segment operating income reaching $4.8 billion. AI-optimized server revenue doubled, while traditional servers and networking grew 122%.

Management raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $192 billion from $167 billion and lifted its AI-server revenue target to $74 billion from $60 billion. Those targets describe Dell's fiscal year, not Morgan Stanley's calendar-2027 model.

Operating cash flow reached $2.225 billion, down from $2.543 billion a year earlier despite the revenue increase. Working-capital demands remain a risk as Dell finances a larger hardware pipeline, alongside the shipment schedules needed to meet its revenue targets.

3. Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL )

Morgan Stanley's Estimated 2027 Revenue Exposure to AI Infrastructure Demand: 64.8%

Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MRVL) supplies custom silicon and electrical interconnects for AI infrastructure. Its 2027 investment case rests on that existing business, even as a subsequent acquisition agreement points to a larger portfolio. On November 2, it signed a definitive agreement to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction carrying an implied enterprise value of $115 billion. The proposed combination would add optical technologies to Marvell's custom silicon and electrical interconnect portfolio.

Management expects closing in the first half of 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. It targets more than $1 billion in annual run-rate cost synergies. However, the pending acquisition adds approval and integration risks, while its projected closing date means standalone execution still drives the nearer-term financial case.

In its latest full quarterly report, Marvell reported that fiscal second-quarter revenue reached $2.739 billion, up 37%. Data-center revenue increased 46% to $2.172 billion, representing 79% of company revenue. It made $605.5 million in operating cash flow and posted $308.0 million in GAAP net income.

For additional chip-sector ideas, read 12 High Growth Semiconductor Stocks to Buy Now .

Alongside the November transaction announcement, Marvell maintained its preliminary third-quarter revenue midpoint of $3.150 billion and narrowed the range to plus or minus 2%.

2. Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ: AVGO )

Morgan Stanley's Estimated 2027 Revenue Exposure to AI Infrastructure Demand: 81.0%

Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO)'s AI chip growth already produces substantial cash. In its fiscal third-quarter report, the company reported $16.7 billion in AI semiconductor revenue, increasing 221% year over year. Custom accelerators and AI networking drove that growth. Total revenue rose 86% to $29.6 billion.

Broadcom generated $14.2 billion in operating cash flow and $13.7 billion in free cash flow after approximately $0.5 billion in capital expenditure. GAAP operating income reached $16.0 billion. Its separate infrastructure software business contributed $8.752 billion in revenue, up 29%. So Broadcom's consolidated results extend beyond semiconductors.

Management projected $34.8 billion in fiscal fourth-quarter revenue, including $21.7 billion in AI semiconductor sales. Investors considering another ownership-based selection can read our 8 Best AI Stocks to Buy According to Billionaire Ken Griffin .

The loans and leases funding AI rollouts create a new risk. news.Title: Even After Big Gains, Insiders Are Loading Up on These 5 Stocks
news.Content: Purchasing a stock following a sharp decline is easy to justify. However, buying it after a bullish run makes it harder. For that reason, insider purchases that occur after rallies deserve a closer inspection. It is also important to understand the underlying motivations behind insider buying and selling. Insiders can have several reasons for selling a stock, including compensation, taxation, or adjustments to their portfolios. Purchases, on the other hand, are very different since they are carried out through personal cash, and they reflect the insiders' conviction in the business. Insider Monkey recently published another list of 10 Buy the Dip Stocks Insiders Are Loading Up On , after the November 5 sell-off. When insiders continue purchasing a stock after the share price has already jumped, they are in effect signaling toward additional upside rather than a reversal. For market participants, this comes as a strong signal since these insiders have a more thorough understanding of their businesses compared to investors and analysts. Also check our list of 10 Best IT Services Stocks to Buy Now . 2026 has been a year of market swings between rallies and sell-offs. In such a landscape, executives and directors who are adding to their positions are essentially betting on the business fundamentals. We provided the expanded list of 10 Stocks Insiders Are Loading Up on, Even After Big Gains . The top 5 stocks are listed below. Methodology: To identify relevant stocks for this article, we carried out a sector-agnostic search across Insider Monkey's insider-purchase database for the U.S.-listed companies with market capitalization above $500 million. We narrowed down our search to stocks with a year-to-date share price increase of at least 17%, as of the November 19 closing. Finally, we shortlisted stocks with insider purchase values above $50,000 from October 19 to November 19, and ranked stocks in ascending order of their purchase values. Our selection excludes stock awards and option exercises from the qualifying purchases. 5. Stride Inc. (NYSE: LRN ) YTD Gain: 17.9% Insider Purchase Value: $8,102,077 Stride Inc. (NYSE:LRN) is an online educational platform that offers digital curriculum, career readiness programs, educational materials, and analytics. As an alternative to the traditional brick-and-mortar education system, its advanced and personalized interactive products enable users to track and monitor the progress of their learning outcomes. It ranked #8 in our recent list of Companies Opting for Activist Investor Settlements . Valuation multiples appear highly compelling, as the stock currently trades at a trailing earnings multiple of 10.7x. With a forward P/E ratio of 8.7x, earnings are expected to grow by almost 19% over the coming year. These metrics are highly discounted relative to peers, resulting in an upside potential for investors if execution stabilizes. Story Continues On November 5, board member Dylan Haggart bought 108,273 shares of common stock through his investment firm, Fivespan Partners. He spent a total of $8,102,077 at an average purchase price of $74.83, bringing his total position to 2,236,033 shares. See the history of insider purchases in LRN here . There is a notable pessimism regarding the potential margin strain stemming from a shift in underlying contract mix. The first quarter of fiscal 2027 saw gross margins go down to 37.7% compared to 39.0% during the same period last year. More importantly, management has shared a full-year FY2027 outlook for gross margins to drop by 100–200 bps relative to FY2026. Added pressure comes from operational costs associated with staffing and technology stabilization. 4. Intel Corp. (NASDAQ: INTC ) YTD Gain: 41.5% Insider Purchase Value: $9,709,680 Intel Corp. (NASDAQ:INTC) is a global provider of computing-related goods and services. The company manufactures edge connection solutions, discrete graphics units, and server CPUs. Along with enhanced driver assistance and autonomous car technologies, it also works on commercializing wafer fabrication services. It ranked #7 in Insider Monkey's list of Top 10 Stocks that Have Survived Major Founder Transitions . The operating story for Intel is showing signs of improvement. On a trailing basis, the company has delivered $19.14 billion EBITDA, along with an operating margin of 10.32%. Hence, its core business is exhibiting strength. However, below that operating line is where the picture darkens. The trailing net margin came in at -20.09%, and a -9.62% return on equity reflects ongoing net losses amid large non-operating accounting charges and heavy investment outlays for the foundry segment. Bears are also pointing to Intel Foundry's ongoing multi-billion-dollar operating losses. These include a $1.85 billion loss recorded during the third quarter of fiscal 2026 and around $2.1 billion during the previous quarter. On November 2, CEO Lip-Bu Tan bought 150,000 common shares at a price of $64.73, resulting in a total purchase value of $ 9,709,680. The purchase increased his reported position in Intel to 1,464,669 shares (see all insider purchases in INTC shares here ). 3. AnaptysBio Inc. (NASDAQ: ANAB ) YTD Gain: 58.2% Insider Purchase Value: $17,224,592 AnaptysBio Inc. (NASDAQ:ANAB) is involved in managing financial collaborations, royalty economics, and milestones for out-licensed therapeutic antibodies. The company now operates under a leaner structure following the spin-off of its biopharma segment into First Tracks Biotherapeutics, earlier in April this year. We recently explored the value of the company's royalty stream in detail, and also compared it with peers like PTC Therapeutics and Mirum Pharmaceuticals. From November 16 to 18, Oleg Nodelman bought 374,580 shares of common stock of the company through his biotechnology-focused investment firm, EcoR1 Capital. He spent a total of $17,224,592 in a series of insider purchases to bring his total holdings to 8,254,674 shares. Here is the history of insider purchases in ANAB . Highly streamlined operations have resulted in a low cost base for the company. Its virtual model now comprises very minimal R&D spending and few employees. However, it is still subject to some temporary transition and legal costs. Bears are also looking at the company's ongoing binary litigation against GSK and its subsidiary, Tesaro. It relates to a 2014 Collaboration Agreement around Jemperli, which is AnaptysBio's primary cancer immunotherapy asset. The final verdict is anticipated somewhere during the final quarter of 2026 or the start of 2027. 2. Kodiak Sciences Inc. (NASDAQ: KOD ) YTD Gain: 276.3% Insider Purchase Value: $24,340,835 Kodiak Sciences Inc. (NASDAQ:KOD) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company that develops eye treatments to ensure that patients require less frequent injections compared with standard therapies. The company leverages its Antibody Biopolymer Conjugate (ABC) platform to design therapies that also increase ocular durability. It also has a strong pipeline of late-stage therapies such as Zenkuda, KSI-501, and KSI-101. Back in April, Insider Monkey published a list of 10 Best 52-Week High US Stocks to Buy , and Kodiak ranked #7 on it. The bullish thesis for the stock also rests on the potential expansion across large retinal vascular segments such as diabetic retinopathy (DR), wet age-related macular degeneration (wet AMD), and retinal vein occlusion (RVO). Directors Julian Baker and Felix Baker carried out insider purchases during the first week of November through Baker Bros. Advisors. A total of 247,090 shares of common stock were bought at an average rate of $98.51, which equates to a total consideration of $24,340,835 (see the history of insider purchases in KOD ). With large outlays on R&D and clinical trials, there are growing concerns around the company's cash burn. The company is still operating at a pre-revenue stage with mounting net losses. Kodiak incurred a net loss of $66.2 million during Q3 2026, compared to $61.5 million during the same period last year. This brought its cumulative nine-month 2026 net loss to $190.0 million. 1. MSC Industrial Direct Co. (NYSE: MSM ) YTD Gain: 24.9% Insider Purchase Value: $28,984,169 MSC Industrial Direct Co. (NYSE:MSM) is a distributor of maintenance, repair, and operations (MRO) products, as well as metalworking and supply chain management solutions. It also delivers application & cost optimization, and procurement & inventory management services. It was added to our list of 10 Stocks You Are Selling and Insiders Are Buying , which we published in late October. The company enjoys stickiness across MSC Industrial Direct's managed inventory and technical programs. Its offerings are embedded deeply across the inventory management, supply chain, and cost-optimization functions, which allows for high switching costs. On October 23, director Mitchell Jacobson spent $28,984,169 to buy 250,000 shares of Class A Common Stock at an average price of $115.94. This brought his total holdings in the company to 4,286,124 shares (see the stock's history of insider purchases here ). The fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 resulted in growing bearish arguments. The discontinuation of its "Digital Core" modernization program resulted in an asset impairment charge of close to $42 million. This affected the quarterly bottom-line figure, as the GAAP diluted EPS dropped 15.8% compared to Q4 FY25. While we acknowledge the risk and potential of MSM as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: Micron vs. Sandisk: Which AI Memory Stock Is the Better Buy?
news.Content:
It has been a wild ride in 2026 for two leading memory chip stocks, Micron (NASDAQ:MU) and Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK).

Both are among Wall Street's best performers year to date, but their paths to those returns have been extremely volatile.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

At its 2026 closing high of $1,213 per share on June 25, Micron was up about 326% year to date. At its split-adjusted closing peak of $291 per share on June 22, Sandisk was up 870%.

Since then, Sandisk has lost 68% of its value, falling to $91 per share. But it's still up 209% from $30 per share at the start of the year. Micron had fallen 51% to $594 per share on Nov. 20, but bounced back on Nov. 23, climbing to $717 per share. It's still up 147% from $285 per share at the start of the year.

So, if you've owned shares since before this summer, you're still probably happy with the returns, despite the wild swings. But heading into 2027, which of the two is the better buy?

Image source: Getty Images.

Booming revenue

Both Sandisk and Micron have benefited from the current memory and storage supercycle , which was brought on by the fast advance of artificial intelligence computing. Demand for AI memory and storage has been magnified by the massive amount of AI infrastructure being built by hyperscalers, neoclouds, and others, and, in turn, chipmakers such as Nvidia , Intel , and Advanced Micro Devices .

The demand for chips that can provide quickly accessible memory and storage for the data AI requires and creates has boomed as a result. Because memory chips are essentially a commodity, the companies that manufacture them try to avoid overbuilding their production capacity. In the wake of the rapid surge in demand, they now can't keep up. This has given Micron, Sandisk, and their peers incredible pricing power and huge backlogs of orders.

While Micron and Sandisk have products that do directly compete with each other, their respective cash cow products are in separate areas. Micron's main product is high bandwidth memory (HBM) chips for AI data centers that can provide fast memory for AI processing. It is mostly sold out of HBM through 2027. Sandisk's main products are NAND and solid-state storage drives, which provide long-term data storage for AI computing.

Both memory giants also have long-term contracts with major hyperscalers and customers with commitments through at least 2030.

Story Continues

Which is the better buy?

Sandisk just underwent an 8-for-1 stock split on Nov. 20, which brought its previously lofty share price down to a more accessible $91 per share.

Though both of these stocks have dropped so sharply over the past few months, that was mostly due to factors beyond their business performance. Many investors took profits when the stocks were higher. They were also brought down by broader concerns about whether the enormous levels of spending on AI infrastructure will deliver the return on investment that the bulls promise. The downtrend was likely exacerbated by the U.S. midterm elections, in which voters in many locales made it clear that they want stricter regulatory and government controls around data center development. This has led to concerns that hyperscalers might negotiate down or out of their long-term chip deals.

The Jensen Huang Nvidia situation did not help AI stocks either, although he was just reinstated as CEO on Monday, so we'll see where that leads.

The fact remains that both Sandisk and Micron are vital suppliers in the AI boom, and even if there are more controls on where data centers can go and a greater level of concern for their environmental impact, that won't eliminate the need for AI processing and storage.

Also, both of these stocks are dirt cheap, made even cheaper by the recent sell-off. This is a testament to their massive earnings power. Micron is trading at just 3.4 times 1-year forward earnings. Sandisk is even cheaper with a 1-year forward P/E of 2.5. And both have minuscule 1-year forward price/earnings-to-growth ratios of about 0.05.

I own shares of Micron and will add more at this low valuation, but Sandisk is also a screaming buy.

news.Title: Applied Materials vs. Intel: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
As chip demand evolves, investors must decide between Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) and Intel (NASDAQ:INTC). Both play vital roles in the global tech ecosystem but currently travel very different financial paths.

Applied Materials provides the essential machinery used to fabricate advanced electronics, while Intel designs and manufactures the chips that power computers and data centers. Comparing them highlights the choice between a steady equipment leader and a legacy manufacturer in the midst of a massive structural turnaround.

The case for Applied Materials

Applied Materials provides specialized equipment and software for the fabrication of semiconductors and advanced displays. It serves a global customer base including logic, DRAM, and NAND memory manufacturers. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as two specific customers accounted for roughly 19% and 15% of net revenue in the latest annual report.

In the 12 months ended Oct. 25, 2026, revenue reached about $34.4 billion, representing growth of approximately 21.4% compared to the prior year. Net income for this period was about $10.1 billion, a significant increase from the roughly $7.0 billion reported in the previous year. This growth highlights the ongoing demand for sophisticated production tools among semiconductor stocks .

As of its October 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.3x. This ratio compares total debt to the value of shareholder equity, measuring how much a company relies on borrowed money. The current ratio, which measures a firm's ability to pay off its short-term obligations using assets it can convert to cash within a year, is roughly 2.3x. In the fiscal year ended Oct. 25, 2026, free cash flow was approximately $6.2 billion.

The case for Intel

Intel designs and manufactures processors and accelerators for cloud, enterprise, and PC markets. The company is currently pursuing an IDM 2.0 strategy, which involves expanding its own manufacturing capacity to serve external third-party customers through its foundry segment. Its three largest customers are highly concentrated, accounting for approximately 43% of net revenue in its latest annual report.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 26, 2026, revenue reached about $59.9 billion, a growth of roughly 12.1% over the prior twelve-month period. Despite the rise in sales, the company reported a net loss of around $12.0 billion. This loss reflects the immense costs associated with Intel's efforts to modernize its fabrication facilities and regain a competitive edge in processor architecture.

Story Continues

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.4x. The current ratio stands at roughly 2.0x, indicating a solid ability to cover near-term liabilities. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 27, 2025, free cash flow was a negative $4.9 billion. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented roughly 25.1% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Risk profile comparison

Applied Materials faces risks from the highly cyclical nature of the semiconductor industry and significant geographic concentration in markets like China and Taiwan. The company relies heavily on export licenses for sales to China and remains vulnerable to supply chain disruptions and trade restrictions. It also manages ongoing regulatory scrutiny, including a $252 million settlement with the U.S. Department of Commerce in 2026 regarding export compliance.

Intel faces intense competitive threats in its product and foundry segments from rivals such as Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) and other major fabricators. Financial pressures have led the company to cancel facility projects in several countries, including Germany and Israel. It also carries risks related to its reliance on third-party lithography tools and ongoing shareholder litigation concerning its financial disclosures and demand in the PC market.

Valuation comparison

Intel appears cheaper based on sales, but Applied Materials carries a significantly lower multiple relative to its future earnings estimates.
