Which stock would I buy for 2027?

Intel is pressing on with its plan to revive its business. In the spring it announced a partnership with Space Exploration Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ:SPCX) and Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA) to build Terafab, a massive AI chip-making plant aiming to produce as many as 200 billion AI chips a year. Intel is providing its foundry expertise and its 14A process, an effort to produce 1.4-nanometer chips it announced two years ago and is still developing.

Also this year, Intel signed a deal with Nvidia to help build a new AI GPU called Crescent Island that can work in tandem with Nvidia's Blackwell AI chips, and agreed to help develop an AI-centric chip for the Google division of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOG) , too. Last year, the company raised investments from the U.S. government and SoftBank to improve its capital position.

All that has generated some optimism on Wall Street. For fiscal 2026, sales are seen rising 17% to $61.7 billion, though a large $11 billion net loss is projected, reflecting the cost of expanding its U.S. foundries.

Applied Materials, meanwhile, is the largest supplier in the world of wafer fabrication equipment for semiconductors. Its wide slate of offerings in chip manufacturing gives it inroads with customers by selling integrated solutions across technologies, making it harder for competitors to dislodge it. The business posted a larger-than-expected rise in sales and income for full year 2026, reported earlier this month. The business posted a 22% increase in revenue to $34.5 billion with a 44% jump in net income to $10.1 billion. Wall Street expects full-year 2027 sales to hit $48 billion, with a very healthy 50%-plus gain in net income to $15.2 billion.

For the next few years, management sees AI demand as driving the business's sales and widening its margins.

So which stock is the better buy for 2027? Intel's shares are priced at a premium, given that much-ballyhooed projects like Terafab may not come to fruition. Applied Materials is growing fast, with quick profit growth, so its 15.7x forward P/E ratio seems like a bargain, especially considering the average S&P 500 stock trades at around 19x forward P/E.

news.Title: Is Microsoft the Best Big Tech Stock to Buy Now?
news.Content:
There has been a lot of talk surrounding Nvidia over the past few days, and rightfully so, amid serious allegations at the CEO level and potential company misconduct in the getting around U.S. export controls. Other companies have also been in the news such as Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) and its blockbuster initial public offering.

However, one that has flown under the radar is Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT). When the market has a bearish mindset, staying under the radar as a company is normally a good idea, but a company can only keep so much of a low profile when it's the second-largest in the world by market capitalization.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

But is Microsoft a good buy today? Or should the market be worried about it too? After all, it hit a fresh all-time high just days ago.

Image source: Getty Images.

Microsoft is being more conservative with its spending

The best companies to compare Microsoft to are Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) and Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN). These two may not seem like great comparisons on the surface, but they are all approaching AI in a similar manner: Investing in outside companies and building out computing power. All three of these companies have significant investments in AI labs to give them exposure to the companies pioneering AI technology.

While Alphabet and Amazon own a massive amount of Anthropic (about 30% combined), Microsoft owns nearly the same amount of OpenAI, its primary competitor . While OpenAI isn't public yet, it will likely become so in the near future, and is likely keeping an eye on how successful Anthropic is on the public markets. So, Microsoft's payday for its OpenAI investment will need to wait, which may not be a bad thing.

The other area these three compete heavily in is cloud computing . AI firms don't have the resources to build out an extensive data center network to power their workloads. So, they choose to rent it from providers like Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services (AWS), and Google Cloud. All three companies have seen their backlog explode from massive AI computing demand, and the backlog totals are in the hundreds of billions for each company. As a result, each company is spending heavily to build out its computing capacity.

However, Microsoft is being less aggressive, which the market respects. This year, both Amazon and Alphabet plan to spend at least $200 billion on data center capital expenditures. Microsoft only plans to spend $170 billion. While this may sound like it's falling behind, the reality is that Microsoft isn't stretching itself thin.

Story Continues

MSFT Free Cash Flow (Quarterly) data by YCharts

Microsoft has maintained strong free cash flow, meaning that it's still sending cash to the bottom line. Amazon and Alphabet have dipped into negative territory, meaning they are either burning through cash reserves to fund operations or taking out loans. Both of these two activities aren't favorable in the market's eyes. This could lead to Microsoft being viewed more favorably, but it could cost it some market share in the end if it isn't aggressive enough.

The market normally takes a short-term view for situations like this, which is why Microsoft's stock is viewed favorably. But does that make it a smart buy now?

Microsoft's stock isn't terribly pricey

Microsoft is already in its fiscal 2027, ending June 30. So comparing forward earnings price tags is a bit difficult to its peers. But at 25 times forward earnings, Microsoft is neither expensive nor cheap.

MSFT PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts

Amazon is nearly in line with Microsoft's valuation at 24.5 times fiscal 2027 earnings estimates, but Alphabet is far cheaper at 18 times next year's earnings.

GOOG PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts

That's a big mismatch, and could point to Alphabet being a smarter buy than Microsoft, especially if it can steal some of its cloud computing market share.

Microsoft is staying conservative in its spending. We'll see if it costs them, but as of right now, I'd say Microsoft is an OK stock to buy. It will likely beat the market, but won't do it by much due to its current price tag.

news.Title: 3 Unstoppable Stocks That Can Be Great Buys for Decades
news.Content:
Stocks that are great long-term investments have solid underlying financials, and there's a great deal of predictability around their futures. What the recent Nvidia scandal has brought to light is the importance of investing in a business that may not be highly dependent on just a single person or the outlook for artificial intelligence (AI).

Three companies that look like unstoppable investments for the long term, regardless of what happens with AI, are Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), and Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT). Here's why they can make for excellent buy-and-forget investments.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Amazon

Amazon's stock hasn't gotten much love over the past year. While it has generated decent 12% returns over the past 12 months, that pales in comparison to some of the gains tech stocks have accumulated over that stretch.

But for a company that's typically at the forefront of any tech innovation, its modest gains can actually be excellent news for investors who buy the stock today. While its financial results have been improving, its valuation hasn't taken off, and thus, it has become a much more attractive investment in the process.

The stock is currently trading at 23 times its expected future profits (based on analyst projections). That's a modest valuation for one of the leading tech companies in the world. It's developing robotaxis, its own AI chips, and deploying drones for delivery, among other opportunities it's pursuing. On top of all that is, of course, its massive e-commerce business.

To buy such a tremendous stock at a low valuation could prove to be a steal of a deal in the future.

Microsoft

Another tech giant that I like for the long haul is Microsoft. It's been a top name in tech for decades, and the reason I don't see that changing is because of how trusted and entrenched its software is within corporate environments. Businesses rely on Microsoft's Office software on a daily basis.

While there have been other options and there will continue to be more competition in the future, I think the reliability that its software offers and the trust it has built up over the years is what gives it a huge competitive advantage. And the company's investments in AI could also pay off significantly, with Microsoft's Office software now able to do much more, with its Copilot assistant helping create spreadsheets and documents in just minutes, potentially saving corporate clients hours each day.

Story Continues

Shares of Microsoft crashed earlier this year due to panic that AI would wreak havoc on software companies. I don't believe that will happen with Microsoft, and I am confident it'll be able to invest in AI effectively to add more value for its customers.

It's up less than 3% this year, and its forward earnings multiple of 24 is also not terribly high, especially for such a solid tech business.

Walmart

Another business that I'm confident isn't going anywhere decades from now is Walmart. The big-box retailer seems intent on going toe-to-toe with Amazon, as it has ramped up delivery options over the years to also provide customers with day-to-day goods and necessities quickly in order to be more competitive with the tech company.

Walmart continually generates solid, stable growth, as consumers flock to its stores for all types of goods, making it arguably the ultimate one-stop shopping location due to its diverse mix of products. And with a heavy grocery business, it makes it easy for consumers to come in to buy essentials and also purchase other items while they're inside its stores.

The stock has done well this year, rising by around 19%, as investors have loaded up on it for the long-term safety and stability it offers. The only thing I don't like about the stock is that it's trading at a high valuation -- close to 40 times projected future earnings. However, that just means that returns may be limited in the near term. But that becomes a relatively minor issue if investors are prepared to hang on for decades.

news.Title: Microsoft declares a code red in the middle of a 'Patchpocalypse'
news.Content: Companies are racing to patch a record number of software flaws this year. Microsoft just found out how long its own fixes take to reach the world. Microsoft ( MSFT ) has declared a code red, its top-priority alarm, after a 24-hour outage this month, according to internal memos reported by Reuters . The goal is to fix future problems worldwide within an hour. A recent urgent fix took five to six days to reach everyone. The Nov. 12-13 outage knocked out Outlook, Teams, and Copilot . The culprit was a flaw in Microsoft's own software , introduced in July, that went unnoticed for about four months. Microsoft ruled out hackers and AI agents . Microsoft promises business customers that Microsoft 365 will be up 99.9% of the time, which allows about 44 minutes of downtime a month. By Yahoo Finance calculations, one 24-hour outage used up nearly three years' worth, though not every customer was down that long. Responders traded more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats while the data they needed sat scattered across separate systems. The faulty component had "roughly ten years' worth of acceptable failures," Charles Lamanna, a Microsoft executive vice president, said in a code red review. The fix list includes dividing traffic by region, so trouble in one place doesn't spread everywhere, and also AI agents that comb through system data to find problems faster. It all comes in the middle of what Ben Emons of FedWatch Advisors calls a " Patchpocalypse ," a flood of newly discovered software flaws, many found by AI, that companies have to fix. Newly reported flaws hit a record of almost 17,500 in October. Emons warned that "every patch is a chance for something to break." Speed is now everyone's problem. Cisco ( CSCO ) President Jeetu Patel told Deirdre Bosa Live on Monday that the time between a flaw going public and an attack "is actually shrinking now, to minutes." The numbers back him up. In 2018-19, attackers took an average of 63 days to exploit a newly revealed flaw, according to Google's Mandiant. In 2024, attacks began on average a day before a fix was even available. Mandiant estimates that head start grew to about a week in 2025. "You can't just wait on these patches ... because patches are complicated. You have to bring down the system," Patel said. Cisco and OpenAI released a free tool Monday that puts temporary "shields" on systems while a fix is tested. OpenAI President Greg Brockman said on the same show that OpenAI once put a quarter of its production engineers on security alone, and every company should do the same. Story Continues "This needs to be a board-level priority, a CEO level priority." Internal AI tools helped analyze interview transcripts, research, and draft this post. Humans reviewed, edited, and fact-checked this post before publication. Jared Blikre is the global markets and data editor for Yahoo Finance. Follow him on X at @SPYJared or email him at jaredblikre@yahooinc.com . news.Title: Intuit vs. Palo Alto Networks: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
As digital transitions accelerate, investors must choose between established financial platforms and high-growth cybersecurity infrastructure. Deciding between Intuit (NASDAQ:INTU) and Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ:PANW) depends on your specific growth and valuation priorities.

Intuit provides essential tax and accounting tools for millions, while Palo Alto Networks secures the networks and cloud environments those same users rely upon. While both operate in the software space, they have different profiles in terms of profitability and market demand, making them frequent candidates for comparison in long-term portfolios.

The case for Intuit

Intuit serves approximately 93 million consumers, small and mid-market businesses, and accountants through its global financial technology platform. The company is a leading provider among tech stocks , offering critical tools like TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma, and Mailchimp. Distribution depends on third-party platforms such as those managed by Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) and Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL).

In the 12 months ended Oct. 31, 2026, revenue reached about $21.9 billion, representing growth of roughly 12.8% over the prior year. The company reported approximately $4.8 billion in net income during this period, resulting in a net margin of roughly 22%, measuring the percentage of revenue kept as profit. This performance demonstrates consistent expansion across its core tax and accounting segments compared to previous years.

As of its July 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.4x, measuring total debt against shareholder equity. The current ratio is nearly 1.5x, indicating current assets are sufficient to cover current liabilities. In the fiscal year ended July 31, 2026, free cash flow was approximately $8.7 billion. This metric represents the cash a company generates after accounting for spending on physical assets. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented roughly 23% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Palo Alto Networks

Palo Alto Networks focuses on a platformization strategy that integrates network, cloud, and security operations for a diverse range of customers. The company serves more than 70,000 organizations and utilizes cloud marketplaces provided by Amazon, Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT), Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOG), and Oracle Corp. (NYSE:ORCL). As of its latest annual report, two distributors accounted for 30% of total revenue, indicating that customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

Story Continues

In the 12 months ended Oct. 31, 2026, revenue reached about $12.5 billion, representing significant growth of roughly 30.3%. The company reported roughly $455 million in net income, representing a net margin of approximately 3.7%, measuring the percentage of revenue remaining after all expenses are paid. This growth rate highlights the rapid adoption of its security platforms, although net profitability is lower than that of its financial software counterpart.

As of its July 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.1x, calculated by dividing total debt by shareholder equity. The current ratio is nearly 0.9x, indicating current assets are slightly below current liabilities. In the fiscal year ended July 31, 2026, free cash flow was approximately $4.1 billion. This metric represents the cash remaining after the company pays for physical assets. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 39% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Risk profile comparison

Intuit faces significant competitive pressure from established entities, start-ups, and public sector tax service providers. The company also manages legal risks related to intellectual property and potential infringement claims, including those related to GenAI. Additionally, cybersecurity remains a critical risk as the company hosts sensitive financial data that attracts sophisticated, AI-driven attacks.

Palo Alto Networks faces intense competition from established companies like Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO), Fortinet (NASDAQ:FTNT), and Check Point Software Technologies (NASDAQ:CHKP). The company relies on channel partners to generate a substantial portion of revenue, creating exposure if these partners fail to perform. Managing rapid growth and integrating acquisitions such as CyberArk also present significant operational challenges and integration risks.

Valuation comparison

Intuit has a lower Forward P/E , comparing price to earnings estimates, and P/S ratio, using sales over the past twelve months, than Palo Alto Networks.

Metric

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

Agentic AI is reshaping enterprise risk and turning Palo Alto Networks' core cybersecurity offerings into a bigger priority for customers. Rather than relying solely on perimeter firewalls--which can fail from a single breach--Palo Alto Networks emphasizes widespread telemetry, deploying millions of sensors to spot malicious activity across systems.

Dealmaking and high-profile AI partnerships have reinforced that momentum. In February, the company completed its $25 billion purchase of CyberArk to expand its agentic AI security toolkit, gain a foothold in identity security, and bring in a large pool of engineers to support broader product development, alongside a push into data observability. Investor confidence has also been buoyed by Palo Alto Networks' selection, alongside one other cybersecurity firm, to test the Mythos AI from Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT).

That interest is already translating into commercial traction across large organizations, which already account for roughly two-thirds of the Global 2,000 in Palo Alto Networks' customer base. Following news of the Mythos testing role, the company reported holding 800 client meetings, fueling anticipation of future contract wins for fiscal 2027 and beyond. For fiscal 2027, look for 27% revenue growth to $14.6 billion and net income of $1.3 billion, more than quadruple 2026 levels.

Intuit, meanwhile, is under pressure from lower-cost competitors as pinched U.S. consumers seek out cheaper options to the company's popular TurboTax product. That has led management to sharply recalibrate its expectations for the product in fiscal 2027 and to aim to retool it. The upside is that its more premium products for businesses, like TurboTax Live, saw strong growth.

Wall Street analysts see Intuit posting a 9% revenue gain to about $23.4 billion, with a healthier 17% rise in net income to $5.4 billion. Longer-term, there is hope that partnerships with OpenAI and Anthropic to integrate Intuit's products and services through LLMs' interfaces will create a new revenue stream.

Intuit's bargain-based price, as seen in its valuation ratios, is tempting, but the forward P/E near 12x suggests investors see trouble ahead. Palo Alto Networks is pricey, but its top-line growth and the need for AI security products probably justify the premium. For long-term investors, PANW is probably the wiser choice.

news.Title: If SpaceX and Tesla Merge, History Says One Group of Shareholders Usually Wins. Here’s Which Side to Be On.
news.Content:
It looks like the two trillion-dollar companies led by Elon Musk are inching toward a marriage. Reports are out that Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX) and Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) are exploring the benefits of merging, with Musk claiming their ambitions are starting to overlap.

SpaceX launches rockets, but it's increasingly investing in AI infrastructure , while Tesla makes electric vehicles, but is increasingly working on battery storage, which is a useful technology for AI data centers. The companies have already formed a joint venture to produce computer chips.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

SpaceX's current market cap is $1.85 trillion, while Tesla is valued at about $1.53 trillion. Here's how a merger could shake out, and which stock you should buy for the better odds at superior returns from a potential tie-up, according to market history.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

The math behind a merger

As companies that are close to equal in market cap, SpaceX and Tesla would likely merge via an all-stock deal. However, since SpaceX is still the larger of the two, it would probably be the one acquiring Tesla. As such, a deal would require it to issue a massive number of new SpaceX shares and exchange them for the determined market value of Tesla. Cathie Wood of Ark Invest — who has followed Tesla for years — says SpaceX would need to offer a premium over Tesla's current share price for its shareholders to approve the deal.

This gets into the historical math of who profits from mergers. Typically, mergers and acquisitions are value-destructive. This does not mean all mergers fail, but on average, they do not work out as optimistically as investors hope.

With that being the case, the acquiring company (in this case, SpaceX) tends to perform worse than the target acquisition (in this case, Tesla) because the target receives an immediate premium over its current share price. Without knowing anything about the business plans for the combined entity, this is the statistic that investors need to understand.

Why SpaceX wants to acquire Tesla

SpaceX has grand plans to become the largest player in infrastructure investments for artificial intelligence (AI). This will require significant capital spending on data centers stuffed with Nvidia chips. Last quarter, SpaceX had $14.6 billion in total revenue but spent $19.6 billion on capital expenditures, primarily on data centers.

Story Continues

Tesla has multiple assets that SpaceX could use to accelerate its AI investments, and none of them have anything to do with electric vehicles. First, Tesla has plain old cash on its balance sheet — $45.5 billion as of the end of last quarter. SpaceX could use this excess cash to fund its capital spending in the race to build AI infrastructure. SpaceX believes it can quickly reach hundreds of billions of dollars in AI-related revenue annually, but it will need to spend a lot up front to make that happen.

Second, Tesla's battery storage and solar energy capabilities could help supply electricity to data centers, giving SpaceX an advantage over rivals that lack energy businesses. Third, the companies could consolidate their chipmaking plan under one corporate umbrella.

Fourth, Musk could consolidate his voting control over the businesses, since he has a much greater degree of voting control over SpaceX than he does over Tesla. That may not be in the interest of the other shareholders, but it sure is in Musk's interest.

Is Tesla stock a buy on the potential SpaceX merger?

Tesla stock might jump a little bit on an all-stock acquisition bid from SpaceX. Perhaps retail investors could even make a little return on a deal announcement. However, for long-term investors, the financials don't support what their combined market capitalization would be.

Together, these companies would have a market cap closing in on $3.5 trillion. On a trailing basis, the two businesses generate a total of less than $150 billion in revenue.

Even if one assumes that SpaceX can grow its AI business to $500 billion in revenue, it is difficult at this stage to calculate what sort of profit margins it will be able to generate by reselling computing power for AI workloads. Cloud infrastructure is also a highly competitive market, and many of the large customers in it — names such as Anthropic and OpenAI — are already building their own data centers. If a combined SpaceX and Tesla stock can generate $500 billion in revenue and has a profit margin of 20% (which may be optimistic for a capital-heavy business), that is $100 billion in earnings, or a price-to-earnings ratio (P/E) of 35.

Tesla shares will likely jump on a SpaceX merger announcement, but these are both risky stocks to buy right now.

news.Title: Solana Foundation DeFi head says utility is what makes tokenized stocks matter
news.Content:
Ramzy Ali, head of DeFi and trading at the Solana Foundation, told TheStreet Roundtable at Solana Breakpoint in London that tokenized stocks matter once holders can do more than buy them.

"We went from we can buy Apple, Tesla, you know, SpaceX, tokenized equities on Solana to we can borrow liquidity against them," he said.

Tokenized stocks now represent about $3.4 billion in distributed value worldwide , according to RWA.xyz data as of Nov. 23. That is down about 8% from 30 days earlier.

On Solana , circulating value reached $1.22 billion as of Nov. 19, nearly double the end-of-October level. The network posted a record $1.8 billion in weekly spot volume , 43% of the total across all chains.

Ali called utility the "word of the year" and said people can "construct a portfolio that not only allows them to express a spot opinion around the spot market, but they can do so while also creating a yield overlay, which is very rare."

A wider set of tokenized names

He pointed to xStocks, which went live on Solana on June 30, 2025 , in what he called "the first really big push into permissionless tokenized equities."

SpaceX listed on Nasdaq on June 12 after 24 years as a private company. Tokenized versions of the shares now trade on Solana, alongside Apple and Tesla tokens that were in the first xStocks set.

Ali said Sunrise, a gateway for new assets on Solana, offers "ninety plus names" and said xStocks has over 100 different assets today. Sunrise, which was built by Wormhole Labs, has listed 90 tokenized US stocks and ETFs . xStocks reached 100 assets on March 18 .

Ondo brought more than 200 tokenized US stocks and ETFs to the Solana network in January.

More news:

Grayscale picks 11 winners of AI's power crunch

These BTC miner stocks explode on shocking Nvidia news

CFTC chief gives major trading platform two ways into America

Lending against those assets

Ali said "something like a hundred million dollars of actively utilized liquidity in and against tokenized equities on Solana."

He also cited OnRe, a real-world asset (RWA) reinsurance firm whose ONyc token is a yield-bearing token tied to reinsurance, used in DeFi on Kamino. OnRe said its Kamino market passed $300 million in total size in September. DefiLlama showed OnRe's total value locked (TVL) at about $288 million on Nov. 23, after a peak near $310 million in September.

Ali said "we saw Figure really explode on the scenes with Prime and then with Auto."

Prime and Auto are yield tokens on Kamino, issued by Hastra and tied to home-equity loans and to US consumer auto loans structured through Figure.

Story Continues

"It's not just holding the assets on chain," Ali said. "That's absolutely not the case. It's people lending against it, people holding it as collateral, people borrowing these assets."

news.Title: Why Dividend Growth ETFs Deserve a Place in Tech-Heavy Portfolios
news.Content:
Stocks, particularly AI beneficiaries, surged yesterday on the news of Jensen Huang's return as NVIDIA (NVDA) CEO. However, they are giving back some of those gains today.

Last week's brutal sell-off was a stark reminder of why investors' portfolios should be diversified. I believe adding high-quality dividend growth ETFs can improve diversification, reduce risk, and enhance the long-term performance of tech-heavy portfolios.

Why Dividend Growth ETFs Deserve a Place in Tech-Heavy Portfolios

Mega-cap tech giants have driven most of the market's gains over the past few years, thanks to the AI boom. As a result, they now account for an outsized share of most investors' portfolios, leaving them heavily dependent on the AI trade.

The information technology and communication services sectors together account for about 45% of the S&P 500 and are dominated by AI-related names. This concentration increases portfolio volatility and the risk of a major drawdown when the AI trade comes under pressure, as we have seen over the past few weeks.

Over the long term, dividends have accounted for a significant share of the stock market's total return. Moreover, dividend growth ETFs invest in high-quality companies with strong balance sheets and stable cash flows, enabling them to increase their dividends consistently.

These ETFs also tend to provide meaningful exposure to other sectors, as technology companies have historically not been major dividend payers. While established tech names like Microsoft (MSFT) and Apple (AAPL) have paid dividends for more than a decade, Meta (META) and Alphabet (GOOG) joined the dividend club only in 2024.

Combining Dividend Growth and Momentum for Better Returns

According to S&P Dow Jones Indices, an equal-weighted blend of the Dividend Aristocrats and Momentum indexes outperformed the S&P 500 over periods ranging from one to 10 years through October.

I calculated the performance of three portfolios, each combining a 50% allocation to a dividend growth ETF with a 50% allocation to a momentum ETF, the Invesco S&P 500 Momentum ETF (SPMO). The three dividend growth funds tested were the Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD), the SPDR S&P Dividend ETF (SDY), and the ProShares S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats ETF (NOBL).

All three combinations outperformed the S&P 500 over the past 1, 5, and 10 year periods. The SCHD pairing delivered the strongest results, driven largely by its ultra-low expense ratio and profitability screen.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Story Continues

These results make sense because dividend growth and momentum have relatively low correlations and tend to take turns leading across market cycles. While momentum captures bull-market trends, dividend growers can help cushion drawdowns during rate shocks or value rotations.

SCHD holds 100 stocks that have paid dividends for at least 10 consecutive years. It also emphasizes dividend quality and sustainability while charging just 0.06% in annual fees. With a gain of about 32%, SCHD has also significantly outperformed the S&P 500 over the past year.

SDY invests in companies that have increased their dividends for at least 20 consecutive years. The highest-yielding companies within that universe receive the largest weightings in the portfolio.

NOBL holds S&P 500 companies that have increased their dividends for more than 25 consecutive years.

news.Title: 美股還能再漲近25%？德銀喊標普2027年底衝9000點
news.Content:
據《巴隆周刊》周二(24日)報導，德意志銀行(DB-US)看好企業獲利持續成長、人工智慧(AI)投資題材重拾動能，預估標普500指數2027年底可升至9000點，相較報導時水準有近25%上漲空間，位居華爾街最樂觀預測之列。德銀認為，輝達(NVDA-US)執行長黃仁勳離職又復職引發的市場震盪，並未改變其看多美股的判斷。

獲利估增19% 本益比降至近三年低點

由Binky Chadha領軍的德銀股票策略團隊預估，標普500企業2027年獲利將成長19%，指數整體每股盈餘(EPS)達430美元，較倫敦證交所集團彙整的市場共識高約3美元。

相較之下，LSEG資料顯示，市場預估標普500企業明年獲利成長16.4%，低於今年37.1%的估計增幅。報導指出，指數目前整體本益比約17.1倍，處於約三年來最低水準。

德銀全球總體經濟與主題研究主管Jim Reid表示，依年底獲利推估，目前股價仍較相應水準低約20%，估值、尤其預估本益比，也位於近幾年的區間低檔。

他將當前市場比作1960年代初期：即使國內政治與地緣事件不斷引發回檔，股價走勢最終仍受到企業獲利成長牽引。

AI投資轉向應用與獲利 回購規模仍創新高

德銀預期，獲利成長將進一步擴及科技業以外的領域，看好超大型成長股、科技股，以及金融與工業類股。能源股則可能因原油價格下跌，面臨獲利下修風險。

Chadha指出，超大型雲端業者的資本支出成長率可能見頂放緩，但隨著AI應用普及、商業化收益增加，這些公司的獲利成長反而有望加速。

大型雲端業者雖然減少股票回購，將資金投入資本支出，但受惠於這些投資的企業，以及標普500其他成分股，已提高回購規模。因此，整體股票回購的成長速度雖放緩，規模仍達新高。

看多股市仍估Fed升息 AI與政治風險未解

德銀的樂觀預測，也伴隨明確風險，包括AI基礎建設投資的不確定性、地緣政治、利率持續上升，以及民主黨掌控的美國國會將於2027年1月上任所帶來的政策變數。

利率方面，德銀認為，強勁的資本支出循環，加上實質可支配所得成長，將支撐就業市場，並使通膨維持在目標之上，促使聯準會(Fed)的溫和升息循環延續至明年。

不過，這項利率預測存在雙向風險。若市場對AI的信心轉弱，導致金融情勢急遽緊縮，政策利率可能低於德銀預期；反之，若勞動市場更加吃緊、薪資成長加速，或租金通膨回升，Fed就可能需要採取更多緊縮措施。

news.Title: Here's Why SpaceX Stock Slumped Today, And Why it Could Come Under More Pressure as Tesla Merger Talks Continue
news.Content: Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX) stock declined by 5.8% as of midday today. The fall came on the day the Financial Times reported that five directors, two from SpaceX and three from Tesla, have been appointed to handle committees discussing a potential merger between the two. How a SpaceX and Tesla merger might work The decline in the stock is yet more evidence of classic pre-deal positioning behavior when two companies are deemed to be in takeover talks. This is a particular consideration when the merger is believed to be an all-stock transaction; in other words, Tesla shareholders would see their shares converted into new SpaceX shares at a fixed exchange ratio. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » Image source: The Motley Fool. The key question in an all-stock transaction is: what will the fixed exchange ratio be? The answer is that the committees would be charged with negotiating the rate and then putting the agreement to both sets of shareholders. Buy the acquiree, sell the acquirer It's here that an opportunity arises for a certain type of investor: investors buy the acquiree (Tesla) and sell the acquiring company (SpaceX) because they believe SpaceX wants to do the deal, and figure that it will be willing to pay a hefty premium, or in this case a good ratio for Tesla shareholders, to do so. Forget about the fact that Tesla stock hasn't performed particularly well, and focus on the relative performance between the two because that's what many investors will be doing. TSLA data by YCharts The more speculation mounts, the more likely Tesla is to outperform SpaceX. However, this isn't a "game" that lasts indefinitely because such investors are, in effect, betting on SpaceX's willingness to pay a premium. That's a position that could unwind negatively if talks collapse, or the committee agrees to a meager premium for a deal. Even so, despite the potential for a near-term decline, collapsing talks might prove beneficial for Tesla investors in the long run, as the company's value could be significantly enhanced by successful robotaxi scaling next year, allowing them to capture the full upside potential of it. If you'd invested $5,000 then, you'd be sitting on $2,145,480 today.* Story Continues Now, for the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. It's a key player in the $1.8 trillion space race, and with the stock recently sitting 20% off its highs, the window to get in early is closing fast. news.Title: Why Sandisk Stock Plunged Today
news.Content:
Shares of Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) were trading sharply lower on Tuesday, tumbling as much as 14.6%. As of 12:27 p.m. ET, the stock was still down 12%.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The catalyst that sent the semiconductor specialist lower was bearish commentary by a Wall Street analyst.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Chips and dip

Investors are becoming increasingly concerned about the durability of demand for artificial intelligence (AI) chips -- with memory chips being particularly vulnerable. One Wall Street analyst seems to agree.

Evercore ISI analyst Amit Daryanani maintained his outperform (buy) rating on Sandisk, but lowered his price target to $175 from $200, in the wake of the company's 8-for-1 stock split , which was completed on Thursday, Nov. 19. To be clear, that new price target suggests the stock has room to roughly double compared to Monday's closing price of about $88.

In a note to clients, the analyst acknowledged the stock's recent decline, suggesting that the sharp correction in artificial intelligence (AI)-related infrastructure stocks has investors focusing on "pricing dynamics and potential downside risks."

There has been a broad-based sell-off in memory stocks in recent months, and Sandisk hasn't been spared. Producers are ramping up supply to meet the unprecedented demand fueled by AI adoption. Investors are concerned that this will ultimately lead to more supply than demand, ushering in a return to historical cyclicality.

These concerns have driven Sandisk down roughly 74% from its June peak (as of this writing), and the stock now sells for less than 5 times earnings. If you believe AI adoption will take years -- or even decades -- to play out, Sandisk stock is worth a look.

news.Title: SK hynix vs. TSMC: One Chipmaker's Revenue Is Exploding, but Is It the Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure has fueled substantial demand for advanced semiconductors, benefiting companies across the industry. SK hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM) are two major beneficiaries, supplying critical components for AI data centers. But while both companies are capitalizing on the same trend, their quarterly revenue performance reveals important differences in their growth trajectories.

SK hynix: Revenue Growth Accelerates in 2026

SK hynix manufactures advanced memory chips used in smartphones, computers, and AI data centers. The company has become a major supplier of high-bandwidth memory, an essential component of the processors powering AI infrastructure.

SK hynix experienced extraordinary revenue growth throughout 2026, accelerating from approximately $22 billion in the fourth quarter of 2025 to more than $72 billion in the third quarter of 2026. Quarterly revenue has more than tripled over that period, with particularly strong growth in the second and third quarters. The acceleration reflects surging demand for advanced memory products as technology companies expand their AI infrastructure investments.

TSMC Revenue Reaches New Highs

Unlike SK hynix, TSMC manufactures advanced processors for other semiconductor companies, including Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Advance Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD). Its position as a leading contract chipmaker provides broad exposure to growing demand for AI infrastructure.

TSMC has demonstrated a steadier revenue growth trajectory, with quarterly sales rising from approximately $26 billion in the fourth quarter of 2024 to nearly $46 billion in the third quarter of 2026. Although revenue growth has been less dramatic than SK hynix's recent acceleration, TSMC maintained its upward trajectory throughout most of the period.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Foolish Take

The most striking takeaway from this comparison is the dramatic acceleration in SK hynix's revenue growth. After trailing TSMC throughout 2025, SK hynix overtook its rival in the second quarter of 2026 and widened the gap substantially in the third quarter. This reflects the growing importance of advanced memory as technology companies invest heavily in AI infrastructure.

However, faster revenue growth does not necessarily make SK hynix the better investment. Memory chips are highly cyclical, and the recent surge in demand could eventually encourage excess production capacity, putting pressure on prices and profitability. TSMC, meanwhile, benefits from a broader customer base and demand for advanced manufacturing across multiple semiconductor markets.

Heading into 2027, I favor TSMC's more diversified business model and relatively consistent revenue growth. Although SK hynix offers greater exposure to the AI memory boom, TSMC provides a more balanced opportunity for investors seeking to benefit from long-term semiconductor demand without relying as heavily on a single industry cycle.

news.Title: Arm Holdings Stocks Fall 4.89% as Chip Rally Cools After Haas Commits Through 2033
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Arm Holdings ( NASDAQ:ARM ) shares slipped 4.89% to $168.03 in premarket trading at 8:48 a.m. ET on November 24, as semiconductor ETFs fell about 4% and Nvidia gave back part of its rebound. Arm had surged 16.08% to $176.67 on Monday. That move combined Nvidia's leadership reset with Arm's own news that Rene Haas will stay as CEO.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Sign with ARM.

Is ARM fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Arm disclosed on November 23 that Haas signed a new agreement to lead the company through 2033 and will become vice chairman of parent SoftBank Group on December 1. Parts of the retention package go to a shareholder vote at a general meeting, with notice to follow. The extension came after reports that Nvidia's board had sounded out Haas as a possible successor to Jensen Huang, according to a Stocktwits report citing the Financial Times.

With Haas tied in and SoftBank owning more than 86% of the shares, governance risk looks low, so valuation carries the debate. The premarket price sits about 19% below the GF Value of $208.07, which GuruFocus calls modestly undervalued, yet that discount relies on royalty growth staying steep. The next checkpoints are the shareholder vote on Haas's package and fiscal third-quarter results.

news.Title: Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom lead chip stocks lower as AI trade comes under pressure
news.Content:
Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock retreated 8% on Tuesday, giving back some of its 31% surge from the prior session after the board of the AI chip giant reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Peers AMD ( AMD ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) also declined from Monday's rebound as the overall AI trade came under renewed pressure.

Follow live updates and reactions to Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO

Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company ( TSM ), which manufactures Nvidia chips, and equipment maker ASML ( ASML ) fell roughly 2% each while chip designer Arm Holdings ( ARM ) was down 8%.

Shares of memory chipmaker Micron Technology ( MU ) and peer SK Hynix ( SKHY ) also dropped roughly 10%, giving back some of Monday's double-digit percentage gains. Storage and memory players SanDisk ( SNDK ), Seagate (STX ), and Western Digital ( WDC ) all fell at least 5%.

Other areas of the AI trade retreated, including the stocks of neocloud providers CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius.

news.Title: 《強勢美股特報》MRNA,TTWO,HUM,ACN等7檔
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-25 01:10:24 數位內容中心 發佈

Moderna（MRNA.US）： 成交價226.95美元，上漲7.01%，開盤212.68美元，盤中高點227.84美元，盤中低點212.58美元，均價222.68美元，成交量63.3萬股。

Moderna正把mRNA平台由新冠產品延伸到腫瘤治療與季節性疫苗。與默沙東合作的個人化mRNA癌症療法intismeran autogene，在高風險黑色素瘤第三期試驗中，讓復發或死亡風險較單用Keytruda降低42%，試驗納入1137名已完全切除腫瘤的患者，兩年無復發率為82.2%，高於對照組的70.0%，且未見新的安全訊號，兩家公司已就數據與監管機關接觸。另一項已落地的進展是mRNA流感疫苗mFlusiva已於8月5日獲FDA核准，其中50至64歲族群為完整核准，65歲以上則為加速核准並需補做確認性試驗。

Take-Two（TTWO.US）： 成交價221.95美元，上漲6.02%，開盤209.35美元，盤中高點222.8美元，盤中低點207.04美元，均價219.12美元，成交量26.59萬股。

Take-Two近來的營運主線仍圍繞《俠盜獵車手VI》預購熱度升高，且已成為未來一年最重要的收入槓桿。管理層表示，GTA6預購量遠高於初期預期，市場資料並顯示截至8月底已產生約490萬份預購。即使公司第二季營收15億美元略低於市場預期、單季淨預訂額下降18%，仍將全年營收展望上調至79.8億至81.8億美元，並重申2027財年淨預訂額80億至82億美元目標。相較之下，《NBA2K27》自9月上市以來銷量超過400萬套但表現低於市場預期，凸顯Take-Two目前的營運重心正更集中在GTA新作能否順利於11月19日推出並延續預購動能。

Humana（HUM.US）： 成交價404.74美元，上漲5.49%，開盤384.68美元，盤中高點404.92美元，盤中低點381.55美元，均價400.22美元，成交量7.08萬股。

Humana近期最明確的變化，是醫療成本控制優於預期，帶動全年獲利預估上修。公司先前將全年調整後每股盈餘預期由至少9美元調高至至少9.50美元，高於市場預期的9.15美元，核心證據來自保險部門醫療成本率降至93.7%，低於分析師預估的94.39%。會員規模也持續擴張，個人Medicare Advantage會員數較去年同期成長23%，與公司預計到2026年實現約25%會員成長的方向一致。最新第三季營收為411.6億美元，高於市場預估的404.6億美元。不過外部變數仍在，美國政府擬擴大Medicare Advantage稽核並追討不當給付，後續如何把監管風險反映到報價與獲利規劃，將成為下一步觀察重點。

Accenture（ACN.US）： 成交價233.46美元，上漲5.03%，開盤223.44美元，盤中高點234.24美元，盤中低點223.44美元，均價232.6美元，成交量22.65萬股。

Accenture最新變化是企業導入AI並未壓縮顧問與技術服務需求，反而把接單推上新高。公司2026會計年度全年新接訂單達845億美元創紀錄，第四季新接訂單221.7億美元，訂單營收比為1.2倍，其中顧問業務94億美元、託管服務127.7億美元，顯示企業仍持續把資料基礎設施與AI建設外包給大型服務商執行。當季營收186.8億美元，年增6%，高於公司原先展望上限，調整後每股獲利3.29美元。對2027會計年度，公司預估按當地貨幣計算營收成長3%至6%，並看好營業利益率擴大10至30個基點，反映其角色正由傳統顧問延伸為企業AI導入的核心執行方。

Ross Stores, Inc.（ROST.US）： 成交價226.39美元，上漲4.31%，開盤217.25美元，盤中高點226.61美元，盤中低點216.2美元，均價221.58美元，成交量17.37萬股。

Ross Stores近期交出的不是單純財報優於預期，而是折扣零售模式仍在擴大客流與市占。公司第三季總營收達63億美元，同店銷售成長8%，管理層指出成長主因是來店人次增加，其中化妝品與家居用品表現最突出。獲利面同樣改善，第三季每股盈餘1.91美元，營業利益率由去年的11.6%升至12.3%。公司並預估第四季同店銷售成長4%至5%，將2026全年每股盈餘目標上修至8.75至8.84美元。擴張策略也提前達標，全年新開115家門市，高於原定計畫。不過管理層也提到燃油價格上漲推升運費成本，且10月下旬異常溫暖天氣曾拖累秋季服飾銷售。

Intuitive Surgical（ISRG.US）： 成交價434.36美元，上漲4.35%，開盤412.1美元，盤中高點435.69美元，盤中低點411.24美元，均價429.75美元，成交量12.14萬股。

Intuitive Surgical持續把手術機器人優勢擴大到更高複雜度術式，同時維持以高頻耗材收入為主的結構。最新一代da Vinci系統近日在歐洲取得成人心臟手術適應症許可，涵蓋冠狀動脈繞道手術，代表其應用由既有成熟科別再延伸至心臟外科。商業化進展則由使用量驗證，截至9月30日，da Vinci全球裝機為12,094台，第三季再新增546台，第三季手術量年增14%，instruments and accessories revenue達18億美元，帶動營收年增22%至30.5億美元。另一份資料則指出，2026年第三季da Vinci與Ion合計手術量年增15%，並維持全年da Vinci手術量成長14%至15%的展望。

Adobe（ADBE.US）： 成交價232.85美元，上漲3.96%，開盤222.54美元，盤中高點233.64美元，盤中低點222.44美元，均價231.45美元，成交量14.79萬股。

Adobe最近最具公司特定性的變化，是管理層交棒正式明朗化。公司宣布由Anil Chakravarthy接任新任執行長，12月1日生效，屆時也將同時接下總裁職務並進入董事會；執掌公司18年的Shantanu Narayen則轉任執行主席。這次接班並非單純人事異動，因Anil Chakravarthy目前負責數位體驗及全球現場營運，且曾帶領團隊開發GenStudio等產品，意味Adobe下一階段仍將延續企業數位體驗與AI整合方向。財務面上，公司2026財年第三季營收67.6億美元、年增13%，淨利18.3億美元，AI-first終端年經常性收入增長超過150%，活躍用戶數則突破10億，顯示交接發生時，公司仍處在既有產品與AI商業化同步推進的階段。

news.Title: 台股暴力反彈678檔漲停！專家一看是「耐摔數字」點背後隱憂
news.Content:
台股24日上演驚天大逆轉，加權指數狂飆3310點、漲幅高達8.99%，一舉改寫台股史上最大單日漲點紀錄，全市場更有高達678檔個股強勢亮燈漲停。面對這波報復性反彈，財經專家葉育碩在臉書發文幽默點出，暴漲的「3310點」恰巧與當年號稱摔不壞的經典手機「Nokia 3310」數字相同，彷彿也在暗示台股極具「耐摔」韌性。不過，在市場一片歡騰之際，葉育碩也從籌碼面與成交量揭露了背後隱藏的警訊。

葉育碩分析，儘管今日大盤氣勢如虹，但觀察三大法人動向卻是站在賣方，合計賣超金額高達1230.11億元，其中外資賣超503.9億元、自營商大砍810.25億元，僅投信逆勢買超84.04億元；此外，外資台指期空單僅微幅回補250口，手中仍握有高達103,182口的龐大空單。更值得留意的是，在多達678檔股票漲停的盛況下，大盤成交量卻萎縮至僅有4203億元，顯示市場依然存在「流動性不足」的現象。

針對前幾天市場頻頻擔憂流動性枯竭，今日卻似乎無人問津的反差，葉育碩一針見血指出，其實「想賣的人賣不掉」與「想買的人買不到」，本質上都是流動性問題，只是發生在不同的市場方向。前幾日行情恐慌下殺，跌停板排滿逃命賣單卻無人承接；今日則是暴力反彈，數百檔個股一開盤或盤中即鎖死漲停，想進場的買盤根本買不到，持有者也惜售不願賣出，成交量自然大幅萎縮。他提醒，在指數暴漲與漲停家數創高之際，法人卻仍大幅調節，加上美國政壇動態變數仍在，後續盤面變化相當值得投資人謹慎觀察。

葉育碩直言，若市場普遍認為現行制度存在缺失，就應該持續推動改革並提出具體改善方向，而不是每逢股市重挫才出來高喊檢討，一旦行情反彈便船過水無痕、無人聞問，如此一來制度永遠不會真正進步。他也點名現行「漲跌幅10%限制」值得趁機深入討論，究竟這項機制是在保護投資人，還是在極端行情下反而阻礙了價格充分反映供需，進而造成流動性卡死的困境。葉育碩呼籲，市場應藉此思考如何建立更完善的防護機制，才能在下一場極端風暴來臨時真正守住投資人權益。

news.Title: AMD Stocks Fall 9.08% After Filing Registers 337 Million Shares for Resale
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Advanced Micro Devices ( NASDAQ:AMD ) shares sank 9.08% to $412.29 in regular trading at 10:15 a.m. ET on November 24, wiping out Monday's 6.85% gain to $453.46. A Monday filing put a number on the cost of AMD's biggest AI deals. Chip shares were also giving back Monday's rally as Nvidia's leadership questions lingered.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with AMD.

Is AMD fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

AMD filed an automatic shelf on November 23 registering 336.9 million shares for resale by existing holders, including 160 million shares under an OpenAI warrant and 160 million under a Meta warrant, each with a one-cent exercise price. The warrants vest as the buyers deploy AMD Instinct GPUs from 1 gigawatt up to 6 gigawatts, and the final tranche needs a $600 share price. AMD receives no proceeds and sells nothing, but it already booked a $1.097 billion non-cash warrant charge in the third quarter, when data center sales jumped 97% to $8.5 billion.

The math is simple: 320 million warrant shares equal about 19% of the 1.656 billion shares outstanding, worth roughly $132 billion at today's price. The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 88/100, a strong grade backed by a solid balance sheet and powerful momentum, with profitability good but not elite. The price sits about 28% above the GF Value of $322.22, and GuruFocus calls the shares modestly overvalued, so the dilution has to buy real GPU volume. The next test is fourth-quarter revenue against AMD's roughly $17 billion outlook and the first MI450 gigawatt shipments.

news.Content:

news.Title: Mark Zuckerberg's Meta Faces New Battle Over Control
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) has agreed to delay issuing a new class of shares amid a shareholder lawsuit, putting a planned $60 billion stock sale program on hold as Mark Zuckerberg ramps up spending on artificial intelligence.

In a November 23 regulatory filing, Meta said it would not issue Class C common stock during pretrial and trial proceedings in Delaware's Court of Chancery.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Sign with META.

Is META fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The lawsuit challenges a recapitalization plan announced in October that would create nonvoting Class C shares beginning in January 2027.

Under the proposal, existing shareholders would receive one Class C share for every Class A or Class B share they own, effectively creating a two-for-one stock split.

The structure would also allow Meta to raise capital, fund acquisitions and compensate employees without reducing Zuckerberg's voting control.

However, shareholders argue that the arrangement unfairly strengthens the founder's influence over the company.

The legal challenge has now delayed Meta's planned $60 billion at-the-market stock offering, which cannot begin until Class C shares start trading.

Zuckerberg has also waived an earlier deadline requiring the company to distribute the shares shortly after the recapitalization takes effect.

Investors Takeaway

The trial is scheduled to begin April 19, 2027.

For Meta investors, the dispute raises questions about corporate governance and the company's financial flexibility as AI infrastructure spending accelerates.

The immediate concern is not that Meta has run out of funding, but that one proposed financing option remains unavailable.

The next test is whether Meta can resolve the litigation without compromising its capital-raising plans or Zuckerberg's control.

news.Title: AAOI vs. Lumentum: Which Optical Networking Stock Has an Edge Now?
news.Content:
Applied Optoelectronics AAOI and Lumentum LITE are key suppliers in the optical networking market. While Applied Optoelectronics specializes in high-speed optical transceivers, laser components, and other fiber-optic networking products that enable AI data center connectivity, LITE offers optical and photonic components that support similar high-speed data-center and telecommunications applications.

Applied Optoelectronics or Lumentum — Which of these Optical Networking stocks has the greater upside potential? Let's find out.

The Case for AAOI Stock

Applied Optoelectronics is benefiting from accelerating optical networking demand, driven by artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure investments and hyperscale data center upgrades. The growing adoption of 400G, 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers is strengthening Applied Optoelectronics' position in the data center market and supporting robust revenue growth.

In the third quarter of 2026, data center revenues increased 254% year over year and 45% sequentially to $155.6 million. Revenues from 800G products nearly quadrupled sequentially to $47.5 million, while 400G revenues nearly doubled to $93.4 million. This momentum highlights strong demand for advanced optical connectivity solutions supporting AI workloads.

The company's growth prospects improved with a multi-year agreement with a Tier 1 hyperscale customer for 1.6T transceivers. AAOI expects this agreement to generate $1 billion to $1.5 billion in revenues through May 2029, subject to customer demand and supply conditions. The transition toward 1.6T products should support higher average selling prices and improved margins.

AAOI is aggressively expanding manufacturing capacity to capitalize on these opportunities. It expects monthly production capacity for 800G and 1.6T products to exceed one million units by the end of 2027. Growing opportunities in co-packaged optics and high-power lasers provide additional long-term growth avenues.

Despite its expanding portfolio, Applied Optoelectronics faced margin pressure in the third quarter of 2026 due to an unfavorable product mix. Non-GAAP gross margin declined to 28.7% from 31% a year ago, falling below management's guidance of 29-30.5%. A faster-than-expected customer transition from 800G to 1.6T transceivers resulted in lower-than-anticipated 800G sales and a higher proportion of 400G products. 100G transceiver revenues also declined as a customer faced switch shortages linked to industry-wide memory supply constraints. Manufacturing capacity limitations and supply-chain bottlenecks also restricted the company's ability to fully capitalize on strong demand.

Story Continues

The Case for LITE Stock

Lumentum is benefiting from strong demand for optical networking solutions, driven by accelerating investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, cloud computing and high-speed data center connectivity.

In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Lumentum's revenues surged 136.5% year over year to $1.26 billion, with pump lasers and OCS driving most of the growth. Components revenues increased 98.9% year over year to $754.2 million, while Systems revenues jumped 228.8% to $508.4 million. Strong demand for cloud optical modules and improving profitability further supported the company's performance.

Lumentum's expanding presence in near-packaged optics (NPO) and co-packaged optics (CPO) presents significant growth opportunities. The company secured its second major NPO/CPO design win, backed by purchase commitments exceeding $5 billion. Moreover, strengthening demand visibility for OCS positions optical switching to become a multibillion-dollar annual revenue opportunity.

Lumentum's expanding portfolio has been noteworthy. In October 2026, Lumentum announced a collaboration with Astera Labs and Corning to demonstrate 1060 nm VCSEL-based PCIe-over-optics connectivity at the 2026 OCP Global Summit. The technology aims to improve bandwidth density, power efficiency, and signal quality while addressing connectivity challenges in large-scale AI infrastructure.

For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, Lumentum expects revenues between $1.575 billion and $1.625 billion, with a non-GAAP operating margin of 45-46%. Robust AI-driven networking demand, expanding customer commitments, next-generation optical technologies and improving profitability bode well for LITE's long-term growth prospects.

Price Performance and Valuation of AAOI and LITE

In the year-to-date period, AAOI shares have gained 11%, underperforming LITE shares, which have risen 47.7%. Lumentum is benefiting from the rapid expansion of AI and cloud infrastructure, which is increasing bandwidth requirements within data centers and accelerating the adoption of high-speed, energy-efficient optical connectivity solutions.

Despite Applied Optoelectronics' strong AI-driven optical networking demand, growing hyperscaler relationships and expanding manufacturing capacity, margin pressure, supply-chain constraints and intense competition remain headwinds.

While both AAOI and LITE stand to benefit from robust AI-driven optical networking demand, Lumentum appears better positioned, backed by stronger earnings growth, rising estimates and accelerating demand for next-generation optical solutions.

Despite AAOI's expanding portfolio, intensifying competition from larger rivals, and supply chain challenges, these remain headwinds that could hurt the company's financial performance.

news.Title: KLA: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
news.Content:
On its first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, KLA (NASDAQ:KLAC) reported quarterly revenue of $4.14 billion and operating margins above 46%. This growth matters to long-term investors because expanding artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure requires process control--the specialized inspection equipment used to detect microchip manufacturing defects.

Three key takeaways from management stand out.

1. Advanced Packaging Revenue Is Surging Faster Than the Market

Advanced packaging combines multiple chiplets into single systems, making inspection far more vital during manufacturing. KLA continues capturing share as customers migrate to complex chip architectures to handle AI workloads.

For calendar 2026, Advanced Packaging Process Control Systems revenue remains on track to hit $1.1 billion or more than 70% year over year growth. Nearly twice the growth rate of the advanced packaging market.

-- Rick Wallace, Chief Executive Officer

2. Memory Manufacturing Intensity Is Shifting Toward Logic Levels

Production requirements for dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) are becoming as complex as advanced logic chips. Rising yield demands for high bandwidth memory (HBM) force chipmakers to add more inspection steps throughout production.

In some products we see intensity levels in DRAM that are similar to leading edge logic. So the market is definitely shifting there.

-- Bren D. Higgins, Chief Financial Officer

3. Unprecedented Funnel Visibility Signals Multiyear Market Expansion

Tool lead times of 12 months give KLA clear forward visibility into customer construction plans. Expanding backlog and new greenfield fabrication projects point toward accelerated capital investment through 2027.

We currently expect the wafer equipment market to exceed $200 billion in calendar 2027. Customer engagement remains robust with numerous new fab projects and greenfield facilities.

Looking Ahead

Supply chain bottlenecks are easing as long lead time optical components come online, allowing tool deliveries to accelerate across manufacturing sites. KLA relies on its high customer switching costs, technological moat, and expanding service contract base while managing memory component cost headwinds.

Our expectations of revenue growth acceleration in the second half of 26 are playing out as more capacity comes online in our long lead time supply chain areas.

With customer investment cycles extending across multiple years, KLA is positioning its production capacity and research and development roadmap to support long-term semiconductor industry expansion.

Story Continues

As we progress toward our 2030 target model, we remain committed to disciplined execution, technology leadership, and our proven capital allocation strategy, which will allow us to create durable shareholder value.

news.Title: Airbnb vs. Uber Technologies: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
The rise of the gig economy has produced two dominant platforms that changed how people travel and commute. Deciding between Airbnb (NASDAQ:ABNB) and Uber Technologies (NYSE:UBER) requires looking at their different paths to growth.

Airbnb operates a high-margin marketplace for lodging and experiences, while Uber Technologies focuses on high-frequency mobility and delivery services. Both companies have moved past their early loss-making stages to become profitable enterprises. This comparison examines their business models, financial health, and current valuations to determine which stock is better positioned for investors through 2027.

The case for Airbnb

Airbnb operates a massive global marketplace for stays and unique experiences, supporting more than 9 million active listings across 220 countries and regions. The company maintains a specialized Co-Host Network that pairs property owners with support personnel and utilizes Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) for its critical cloud infrastructure. This strategy contributes to the growth of consumer discretionary stocks within the global travel market.

During the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, the company reported that revenue reached about $13.9 billion, representing a growth rate of roughly 16.7% compared to the previous year. Net income for this period was around $3.2 billion, reflecting a consistent demand for travel across major markets like the United States and the United Kingdom. This financial performance shows the ability of the platform to generate significant profits while expanding into newer geographic territories.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.3x, which measures total debt relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio is roughly 1.4x, which compares current assets to current liabilities to show how easily the company can cover short-term financial obligations. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was about $4.6 billion, though note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented roughly 34% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Uber Technologies

Uber Technologies connects riders, drivers, and merchants through a platform that spans mobility, delivery, and freight across more than 15,000 cities. The company has established major partnerships with retailers like Best Buy (NYSE:BBY) and Tractor Supply Company (NASDAQ:TSCO) to provide on-demand delivery services to their customers. It also maintains a strategic relationship with Amazon, allowing Prime members to access fee-free orders through its delivery app.

Story Continues

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $56.5 billion, which represents a growth rate of approximately 13.9% over the previous period. The company generated net income of about $3.5 billion during this period, supported by its presence in more than 75 global markets. This growth reflects the continued adoption of its mobility and delivery services by more than 215 million monthly active platform consumers.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.4x, measuring the total debt of the company against its shareholder equity. The current ratio is approximately 1.1x, which shows that current assets are sufficient to cover current liabilities as they come due. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow reached nearly $9.8 billion, providing the company with significant liquidity to fund its operations and expansion plans.

Risk profile comparison

Airbnb faces significant risks from evolving regulatory environments, such as the European Union short-term rentals regulation and local bans in major cities like New York. The company also manages ongoing tax audits and disputes in several jurisdictions, including Italy and the United States, which could impact financial results. Additionally, competition from traditional hotel chains and search engines like Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOG) remains a constant pressure on its marketplace dominance.

Uber Technologies faces ongoing legal challenges over the classification of its drivers as independent contractors, a situation that could fundamentally alter its business model. The company competes in a crowded market against well capitalized rivals like DoorDash (NASDAQ:DASH) and Lyft (NASDAQ:LYFT) for both drivers and consumers. It also faces operational risks related to safety incidents and the complex technical hurdles of scaling autonomous vehicle technology across its global network.

Valuation comparison

Based on their current Forward P/E and P/S ratio, Uber Technologies carries a lower valuation relative to its future earnings estimates and sales than Airbnb.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

Airbnb reported an excellent third quarter of fiscal 2026, typically its strongest period of the year, beating consensus revenue estimates by some $120 million, reporting $4.87 billion in sales, up 19% from the same period in 2025, driven by a strong increase in booked nights. North America bookings grew at their fastest rate in four years, while growth accelerated in its other major markets, the U.K., France, and Australia.

The business is finding ways to expand its popular travel business, embracing features like buy now, pay later (BNPL) on reservations, a form of short-term lending. Management has also seen great success getting hotels onto its platform, and says 35% of new Airbnb customers are booking hotels through it. The network advantage of Airbnb's history, over 2 billion guest arrivals since 2008, and the lack of host presence on AI (meaning a competitor using AI has little data to scrape to form a competing product) give it a competitive moat.

For the full year, Wall Street expects sales of $14.4 billion with net income of $3.3 billion.

Uber revolutionized the taxi industry when it rolled out its ride-sharing network, allowing anyone with a car to earn a side gig. Both the industry and the company have come a long way.

Uber Technologies is by far the largest player in the developing ride-share market by revenue. Wall Street expects Uber's sales to increase by $6 billion from last year to $58 billion this year, accompanied by net income of $6.4 billion. But as a sign of the expenses Uber faces in expanding its business model, that would be roughly $3.6 billion less income than in 2025. In the long run, its global ride-sharing, delivery, and autonomous solutions business will be strong, according to analysts.

So which is the better buy for 2027? Uber trades at just about the average S&P 500 stock in terms of forward P/E, and its P/S ratio is also quite reasonable. That doesn't mean Airbnb is bad, although its premium valuation to its main competitor, Booking Holdings (NASDAQ:BKNG), causes concern over how Airbnb holds onto its valuation in the long term. That gives the nod to Uber.

news.Title: META Rides on Strong Demand in Ad Business: Can It Beat RDDT and SNAP?
news.Content:
Meta Platforms META is benefiting from strong demand in its advertising business, driven by increasing user engagement, AI-powered advertising tools and improving monetization across Facebook, Instagram and Threads. The company's extensive user base and advanced advertising capabilities strengthen its competitive position against Reddit RDDT and Snap SNAP in the digital advertising space.

In the third quarter of 2026, Meta Platforms reported advertising revenues of $63.1 billion, up 26% year over year. Total ad impressions increased 10%, while the average price per ad rose 14%, reflecting improving advertising performance and engagement. META's Family of Apps reached 3.64 billion daily active people, highlighting its extensive advertising reach.

Meta Platforms' growing investments in artificial intelligence (AI) are improving advertising targeting, recommendations, and conversions. In the third quarter of 2026, enhancements to its GEM advertising model increased app ad conversions by 9.6%, while improvements to Andromeda boosted Facebook conversions by 1.4%. Advertisers adopting Meta AI business assistant recommendations achieved nearly 5% more conversions at the same cost per conversion.

The growing adoption of generative AI advertising tools remains another key catalyst. Nearly 10 million advertisers used at least one such tool in the third quarter of 2026. Meanwhile, Meta Platforms' partnership ads business grew more than 97% year over year, surpassing a $15 billion annual revenue run rate.

Meta Platforms expects continued gains from AI-powered recommendations and advertising optimization. With strong user engagement, expanding AI capabilities, and a massive advertiser base, META appears well-positioned to maintain its advertising momentum and stay ahead of Reddit and Snap. For the fourth quarter of 2026, META expects revenues between $73 billion and $76 billion.

How Competitors Fare Against META

Despite Meta Platforms' expanding portfolio, the company faces stiff competition from Reddit and Snap. Both companies are expanding their footprint in the rapidly growing digital ad market.

Reddit is benefiting from robust advertising demand, improving monetization, AI-driven ad enhancements and growing adoption of its performance advertising solutions. The company's investments in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning and advertising automation are strengthening its competitive position. In the third quarter of 2026, Advertising revenues surged 54% year over year to $847 million, supported by higher pricing and impressions. Total revenues increased 53% to $895 million. Click volumes grew more than 50%, while conversion volumes more than tripled, highlighting improvements in advertising effectiveness.

SNAP is benefiting from strong direct-response advertising demand, improved AI-powered ad targeting and expanding monetization opportunities across Snapchat. In the third quarter of 2026, Snap's advertising revenues grew 4% year over year, supported by robust performance in app and web purchase campaigns. App purchase revenues surged more than 54%, while web purchase revenues increased 11%. Sponsored Snaps revenues jumped 56% sequentially, reflecting growing advertiser adoption.

news.Title: BTQ Technologies Corp (BTQ) (Q3 2026) Earnings Call Highlights: Quantum-Secure Deals, QSIM Chip ...
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Release Date: November 17, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript .

Positive Points

BTQ Technologies Corp ( NASDAQ:BTQ ) signed a three-year commercial agreement with Kaya DLT Foundation and has executed about 100,000 QSN transactions on the mainnet.

BTQ Technologies Corp ( NASDAQ:BTQ ) partnered with MoonPay Korea as their security partner for quantum blockchain networks, covering Korea's full stablecoin stack.

BTQ Technologies Corp ( NASDAQ:BTQ ) completed its acquisition of QPerfect and launched Mimic on Kubrate, making it available to over 35,000 quantum developers.

BTQ Technologies Corp ( NASDAQ:BTQ ) validated its core QSIM chip in TSMC 28-nanometer semiconductors with ITRI and welcomed Dr. Michael Grace, former head of security at Samsung, to lead product security.

BTQ Technologies Corp ( NASDAQ:BTQ ) has a strong cash position of $21.5 million and has raised just under $30 million from its ATM to fund operations.

Negative Points

BTQ Technologies Corp ( NASDAQ:BTQ ) has not yet generated significant revenue, with commercial agreements still in early stages and revenue expected to scale gradually.

BTQ Technologies Corp ( NASDAQ:BTQ ) faces potential dilution from its ATM facility, which it continues to use to fund operations, and the stock price has been under pressure.

BTQ Technologies Corp ( NASDAQ:BTQ ) delayed the mainnet launch of Bitcoin Quantum, revising expectations, although the delay is not due to technological barriers.

BTQ Technologies Corp ( NASDAQ:BTQ ) is still working on security certifications (FIPS 140-3, Common Criteria) for its QSIM product, which are necessary for commercialization and could take time.

BTQ Technologies Corp ( NASDAQ:BTQ ) operates in a highly uncertain regulatory and standards environment, with fragmented post-quantum cryptography standards globally, which may impact adoption.

Q & A Highlights

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 1 Warning Sign with BTQ.

Q : On Kaya, now the three-year agreement is signed and LINE's unified wallet is expected to be the first consumer use case. What specifically must occur before BTQ recognizes first revenue, and does the agreement include any minimum payment, implementation fee, or committed transaction volume, or is revenue entirely dependent on usage? A : Chris Tam, President and Head of Innovation, explained that the first consumer use cases primarily address stablecoin usage, with the largest revenue opportunity tied to the portion of stablecoin transactions going toward tokenized equities and tokenized securities. He confirmed the agreement includes service integration fees for every cryptographic module provided, which serve as a base minimum payment, with any subsequent transaction volume revenue in addition to that.

Story Continues

Q : You mentioned 100,000 secured transactions on Kaya. Can you help us understand the economics of the license fee and, based on recent Kaya transaction volume trends, what types of revenue and fee-sharing transactions you expect to generate in 2027? A : Chris Tam, President and Head of Innovation, said the license fee is structured as an integration fee for each cryptographic algorithm supplied in a module, with opportunities to integrate more modules over time and upgrade existing ones. He noted the agreement is also structured to capitalize on capital moved on-chain into quantum-secure custody, so BTQ would receive a share of deposits into quantum-secure savings or yield-generating accounts, not solely transaction volumes.

Q : How should investors think about the FPGA IP release in terms of sales cycles and revenue contribution? Will 2027 revenue be modest given validation is expected at the end of next year? A : Sean Hackett, who leads the QSIM team, said the commercialization strategy targets distributors who can integrate the product into many systems at once, describing it as a high-assurance security component rather than standard semiconductor IP. He emphasized that all focus is currently on achieving a secure, certified component, and that BTQ plans to add software offerings on top of the FPGA IP to create a more compelling full-stack offering, with announcements expected in the coming months.

Q : Are you able to answer whether the current quantum [Bitcoin Quantum] will have a company treasury, and if we will get an MNAV for the share? Can you explain that process? A : Chris Tam, President and Head of Innovation, said a company treasury is absolutely something being considered and would make a lot of sense given the market structure problem Bitcoin Quantum solves. He said details on how it is structured will be revealed over time through due process, and that since the technology was incubated within BTQ, there will be a trickle back up to shareholders for the value at risk that Bitcoin Quantum secures.

Q : Given the changing landscape of encryption, would you see the MLDSA encryption on Bitcoin Quantum need to be changed in the future? A : Chris Tam, President and Head of Innovation, said BTQ hopes MLDSA remains secure for a very long time but is preparing for the worst. He noted that at the heart of Bitcoin Quantum's design is rigorous thinking about how to enable signature schemes to be swapped out on the fly, which he sees as one of the primary value drivers for the network and the asset.

Q : When do you expect a binding commercial manufacturing agreement, and can the computer memory IP be licensed independently via third-party hardware? A : Management said the agreement is hoped to be finalized before the end of the year, and that the IP can be licensed independently. Olivier Roussy Newton, CEO, added that the question pertains to the ICTK development agreement, BTQ's South Korean manufacturing partner for QSIM, and that as IP results come in, BTQ is defining how sales agreements work, noting it is BTQ's IP and BTQ governs where it goes, while ICTK has distribution networks in Asia and BTQ plans different distribution networks worldwide.

Q : On error correction, can you speak to progress milestones and which quantum modalities BTQ is positioned to support? A : Guido, of QPerfect, said the team is targeting neutral atom systems, especially on the compilation side, because neutral atoms are highly scalable and have demonstrated the highest number of qubits trapped and used in computation. He noted neutral atoms pose difficult compilation challenges because atoms must be moved around, and that QPerfect is focusing on QLDPC codes for quantum error correction, with long-range interactions on the platform enabling efficient implementation of these codes.

Q : Can you provide an update on the cash position and the ATM program, and whether BTQ will keep using the ATM? A : Management reported a cash position of CAD 21.5 million at quarter end and net proceeds from the ATM to date of just under CAD 30 million. They said BTQ is being cautious about not selling too much when the stock is under pressure and volume is low, that the ATM is the least dilutive instrument to fund operations into commercialization, and that there is still shelf capacity for a raise if the stock improves, potentially for a transformational acquisition.

Q : What is the status of the QSIM chip and the broader silicon roadmap? A : Olivier Roussy Newton, CEO, said the core QSIM chip was validated in TSMC 28-nanometer semiconductors with ITRI, the Taiwanese research institute that founded TSMC and UMC, and that work continues with ICTK on the QSIM chip design. Sean Hackett added that the ASIC beta is targeted for finalization in Q1, with first samples from the ICTK partnership expected early in the new year and a tape-out date aimed at a commercializable product later in 2027.

Q : What is the status of Bitcoin Quantum's path to mainnet, and why have expectations been revised? A : Chris Tam, President and Head of Innovation, said BTQ is deep in the process of getting Bitcoin Quantum to mainnet and that the delay is not a technological barrier, with external audit results from several audit parties close to being finalized and published.
