Terex眼前最重要的變化，不是新接單或併購消息，而是公司轉型能否把原本偏週期性的設備製造商，推向獲利品質更穩的結構。現有資料顯示，外界主要檢視三件事，包括既有訂單能否持續轉成營收、併購後成本協同是否如期發揮，以及高毛利、低波動業務占比能否提高。管理層先前提出2026年調整後EBITDA9.65億美元目標，因此近期判讀重點也圍繞這項指標能否逐步兌現。換言之，Terex當前的營運故事在於結構調整，而非單一季度數字是否短暫改善。

Booz Allen（BAH.US）： 成交價86.4美元，上漲4.92%，開盤82.21美元，盤中高點87.4美元，盤中低點82.21美元，均價86.53美元，成交量5.84萬股。

Booz Allen近14日內未見可明確辨識的公司特定新事件，現有資料沒有提供新的財報、重大合約、併購、財測修正或產品更新，因此暫時看不到足以重估營運方向的新增催化。對這類政府與企業顧問服務公司而言，更具解釋力的通常會是大型標案得失、國防與數位轉型相關專案進展，或管理層對成長與獲利路徑的更新，但本次公開資訊並未出現相關新事實。這代表外界目前仍較難僅憑近期消息，重新校準Booz Allen的接案節奏或後續獲利輪廓。

Ollie's Bargain Outlet（OLLI.US）： 成交價93.4美元，上漲5.36%，開盤89美元，盤中高點93.78美元，盤中低點88.95美元，均價92.17美元，成交量4.04萬股。

Ollie's Bargain Outlet近14日內未見新的財報、財測修正、重大展店、併購或關鍵供應合作更新，公開資料不足以辨識足夠重新定義營運方向的新增事件。對折扣零售商而言，更能改變後續判讀的通常是清倉貨源取得能力、同店銷售、展店節奏，以及能否以低成本持續取得具吸引力的品牌商品，但目前資料沒有新增這些關鍵事實。也就是說，Ollie's Bargain Outlet現階段缺乏新的公司事件可供驗證成長是否延續，後續觀察焦點仍會回到門市擴張與採購條件是否出現更明確更新。

Guidewire Software（GWRE.US）： 成交價147.25美元，上漲3.73%，開盤140.52美元，盤中高點148.71美元，盤中低點140.45美元，均價146.42美元，成交量2.87萬股。

Guidewire Software近期最核心的變化，是市場重新下修對其雲端成長速度的期待，而非單季財報失色。公司2026財年第四季非GAAP每股盈餘0.99美元、營收4.11億美元都高於預期，ARR年增19%，訂閱與支援收入成長33%，顯示保險核心系統雲端化仍在推進。不過2027財年的ARR指引雖大致貼近共識，卻低於部分原先更樂觀的成長假設。資料也顯示，雲端ARR已占ARR的84%，年增35%，與Nationwide等大型客戶的長期遷移案仍提供支撐，AI產品ProNavigator與PricingCenter銷售也超出公司原規劃。

Roivant Sciences（ROIV.US）： 成交價41.38美元，上漲4.42%，開盤40.36美元，盤中高點42.38美元，盤中低點40.36美元，均價41.47美元，成交量25.75萬股。

Roivant Sciences已把Lisraya推進到商業化階段，這是近期最具公司特定性的進展。公司表示，該皮肌炎新藥在8月獲准後已開始貢獻銷售，單季營收為3,100萬美元，主要反映約5週上市表現，截至9月底已有數百名患者完成付費用藥，到了11月初付費病患數進一步增加。管理層同時提到，初期開方醫師基礎廣泛，與付款方互動大致順暢。不過專業藥局在9月30日時持有大量尚未出貨庫存，隨庫存逐步回歸正常，公司預期第四季可能因此面臨小幅逆風。另一項研發進展是IMV-G-1402-RA第二期退盲試驗結果正面，讓商業化與臨床管線同步推進。

V.F.（VFC.US）： 成交價20.81美元，上漲3.89%，開盤20.04美元，盤中高點20.86美元，盤中低點20.04美元，均價20.63美元，成交量41.05萬股。

V.F.近14日內未見可辨識的公司特定新消息，現有資料沒有提供新的財報、品牌策略更新、資產交易、財測修正或重大通路合作，因此暫時缺乏足以重新界定營運方向的新增事件。對服飾與戶外品牌集團而言，真正更具解釋力的訊號通常會來自核心品牌需求變化、庫存去化進度、批發與直營通路表現，或管理層對獲利修復路徑的更新，但本次公開資訊並未出現相關新事實。換言之，外界目前仍難僅憑近期消息判斷V.F.是否已出現新的營運轉折。

Molina Healthcare（MOH.US）： 成交價204.77美元，上漲3.82%，開盤196.19美元，盤中高點205.01美元，盤中低點195.95美元，均價203.1美元，成交量2.45萬股。

Molina Healthcare目前最受檢視的變化，是醫療成本壓力雖仍偏高，但管理層已指出成本走勢開始趨於平緩。這對公司特別重要，因為獲利彈性更依賴醫療給付成本能否穩住，而不只是保費收入規模。公司最新一季財報優於預期後，全年保費營收預估仍維持約420億美元不變，顯示管理層沒有因單季表現就轉向更激進的成長假設，整體經營基調仍偏審慎。另一個需要一起看的變數是政策面，近期ACA補貼與Medicaid相關討論再度升溫，使後續投保人數、給付環境與保險利潤結構都更容易受政策牽動。

news.Title: Follow the Smart Money: This Billionaire Tech Investor Has Been Loading Up On Shares of These 3 AI Chip Stocks
news.Content:
Chase Coleman's Tiger Global is one of the preeminent technology-focused hedge funds in the world, with many investors who have worked under him eventually starting their own successful funds. In the third quarter, the billionaire tech investor was busy trimming many of his larger stakes. However, one area he was buying was artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductor stocks , increasing his positions in Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), Cerebras (NASDAQ:CBRS), and Intel (NASDAQ:INTC).

Let's look at what Coleman may find attractive in these AI stocks .

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

1. Nvidia

At the end of Q2, Nvidia was only Tiger Global's third-largest holding, but three months later, after Coleman bought more shares, Nvidia was its largest holding, representing over 13.5% of its portfolio. While the stock has been on a roller-coaster ride in the past two months, there is still a lot to like about it.

Nvidia continues to see incredible growth despite its size, with its revenue more than doubling last quarter and the company forecasting 75% revenue growth next fiscal year. Despite that, the stock trades at a forward P/E of just 10 times fiscal 2028 (ending January 2028) analyst estimates.

While Nvidia is facing intensifying competition in the data center segment, it still holds distinct advantages. The company has transformed itself into a complete AI infrastructure player and, as such, is starting to capture a larger share of the revenue pie. With its Grace Hopper architecture, it was getting about $18 billion per gigawatt of capacity, while with Grace Blackwell, it captured around $25 billion per gigawatt. With the addition of more chips to its platforms, such as language processing units (LPUs) for inference, and an expanded software stack, it is now getting $40 billion per gigawatt with Vera Rubin. Meanwhile, Nvidia has locked up important fab capacity and access to scarce high bandwidth memory (HBM) that will help it maintain its leadership in the data center segment.

2. Cerebras

Cerebras is one of the most interesting AI chip stocks, in my view, and may have the most upside potential of any. The company's chips are the fastest for inference, but due to their unusually large size and their unique power management and cooling requirements, they are also expensive. This has made its systems more of a niche solution, and the company often rents out capacity on them to clients.

Story Continues

However, Cerebras has a major commitment from OpenAI and has secured deals with Amazon , Oracle , and Microsoft . The company has also teamed up with Advanced Micro Devices for a cheaper disaggregated solution that uses Cerebras systems for the ultra-fast decode phase of inference and AMD's GPUs for the pre-fill phase. Analysts at Morgan Stanley have projected that the total addressable market for fast inference will surge from around $4 billion this year to $550 billion by 2030. That's a huge opportunity. Tiger Management added about 1.45 million shares to its position in Q3, increasing its share count by about 48%.

3. Intel

Intel is the third chip stock that Coleman bought in Q3. His timing wasn't the best, and investors can now grab the stock at a much lower price than Tiger Global was paying, as the company issued weak guidance in late October amid a weakening PC market. High memory prices have pushed up computer costs, decreasing demand, and Intel still has considerable ties to the PC market.

Intel's central processing unit (CPU) server opportunity and the potential to turn around its money-losing foundry business are what likely attracted Coleman to the stock. Data center CPU demand is currently through the roof, given the emergence of AI agents, which require far more of them than prior iterations of AI. In servers built for AI model training, the ratio of GPUs to CPUs is 8 to 1, but for those being used to handle inference workloads — the actual use of the models — the ratio dropped to 4 to 1. For agentic AI, which involves less of the heavy parallel processing that GPUs provide, and more computing tasks that must be handled sequentially (which CPUs are built for), the ratio is heading toward 1 to 1.

Meanwhile, Intel has spent a boatload of money over the last several years building new fabs in the hopes of competing more effectively with the world's leading foundry, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing . Intel hit a major milestone earlier this month, announcing that it had signed its first external customer deal for its 18A chip fabrication technology. If Intel's foundry operation can become a viable alternative to TSMC for high-end chipmakers, that would be a huge boost to the company.

news.Title: Lam Research Stock Outlook: Is Wall Street Bullish or Bearish?
news.Content:
Lam Research Corporation (LRCX), headquartered in Fremont, California, designs, manufactures, markets, refurbishes, and services semiconductor processing equipment used in the fabrication of integrated circuits. Valued at $228.9 billion by market cap, the company's products are used to deposit special films on a silicon wafer and etch away portions of various films to create a circuit design.

Shares of this semiconductor giant have outperformed the broader market over the past year. LRCX has gained 31.7% over this time frame, while the broader S&P 500 Index ($SPX) has rallied nearly 9.6%. In 2026, LRCX's stock rose 15.7%, surpassing the SPX's 5.7% rise on a YTD basis.

More News from Barchart

Dear Dollar Tree Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 24

Dear Dell Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 24

CoreWeave's Co-Founder Says He's 'Never Been More Confident' in the Company as He Buys $30 Million of Its Bonds. Why That Matters More Than a Stock Buy for CRWV.

Markets move fast. Keep up by reading our FREE midday Barchart Brief newsletter for exclusive charts, analysis, and headlines.

Narrowing the focus, LRCX has lagged behind the Invesco Semiconductors ETF (PSI). The exchange-traded fund has gained about 34.3% over the past year. Moreover, the ETF's 25.3% gains on a YTD basis outshine the stock's returns over the same time frame.

LRCX's mixed performance reflects strong AI-driven demand across memory and foundry, fueled by higher deposition and etch intensity, upgrades to higher-layer NAND and advanced DRAM (including low-latency SLC NAND architectures), panel-level packaging traction with the Kallisto platform, strong China spending, and double-digit CSBG growth in upgrades, spares, and service contracts, tempered by near-term clean room space and component supply constraints affecting shipment timing. CEO Tim Archer noted that while supply bottlenecks weigh on near-term shipments, management is working with suppliers to accelerate capacity and prioritizing R&D and manufacturing investments to capture multi-year AI and device-complexity growth.

For the current fiscal year, ending in June 2027, analysts expect LRCX's EPS to grow 65.2% to $9.60 on a diluted basis. The company's earnings surprise history is impressive. It beat the consensus estimate in each of the last four quarters.

Among the 33 analysts covering LRCX stock, the consensus is a "Strong Buy." That's based on 22 "Strong Buy" ratings, four "Moderate Buys," and seven "Holds."

This configuration is less bullish than a month ago, with 23 analysts suggesting a "Strong Buy."

Story Continues

On Nov. 17, Stacy Rasgon from Bernstein maintained a "Buy" rating on LRCX, with a price target of $350, implying a potential upside of 66.9% from current levels.

The mean price target of $360.03 represents a 71.6% premium to LRCX's current price levels. The Street-high price target of $500 suggests an ambitious upside potential of 138.4%.

news.Title: 'Awaiting the king's return': Taiwan celebrates Huang's return to Nvidia
news.Content:
By Wen-Yee Lee and Yi-Chin Lee

TAIPEI, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Taiwan, the birthplace of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, celebrated on Tuesday with video tributes across its biggest cities the return of its homegrown hero as head of the company he co-founded less than two weeks ‌after his abrupt resignation.

Huang has a rock star status in Taiwan, home to the world's largest contract chipmaker, TSMC, and the island is ‌a critical link in the global AI supply chain.

His visits regularly draw crowds of fans and reporters, a phenomenon that local media have called "Jensanity."

On Tuesday, at Banqiao bus station in New Taipei, ​a screen showed Huang in his trademark black leather jacket beside a red heart and a line-drawn skyline. The messages read "Awaiting the king's return" and "Awaiting your comeback, Jensen."

A dozen outdoor screens at transport hubs and shopping districts in Taipei, New Taipei and Taoyuan played a 217-second tribute, the organisers said in a statement. The length refers to Huang's February 17 birthday.

Huang's resignation earlier this month, following revelations of his extramarital affairs including one with an alleged spy for Beijing, was met with shock in ‌Taiwan. Supporters have said they never ruled out a ⁠comeback.

"For Taiwan, I think this is very good news ... You only have to look at how sharply Taiwan's stock market fell in the days after he stepped down," said Venus Chang, 51, who works in finance in Taipei. "His contribution to Taiwan ⁠has been enormous. That's why I'm genuinely delighted to see him return."

Gary Wu, a 31-year-old engineer, said his first thought after seeing the news of Huang's return overnight was the likely boost to Taiwan's stock market.

"Sure enough, by this morning I could see it had hit the daily limit-up," he said.

Taiwan's benchmark index closed up 9% on Tuesday, ​rebounding ​from an eight-month low.

'TAIWAN LOVES JENSEN'

Last week, prominent figures from Taiwan's technology industry organised a ​two-night light display on the Taipei 101 skyscraper featuring messages ‌including "Taiwan Loves Jensen," "Family and Friendship" and "Thrive Together."

"I always felt he would come back," said Jane Kuo, 50, who runs Flower Restaurant, a Taipei eatery that Huang frequented during his Taiwan trips. "He pulled through. That's great."

Kuo said she was ready to welcome Huang back whenever he next visits Taiwan, saying he boosted business at her restaurant, bringing colleagues and family members and sometimes ordering takeaway to bring on his private jet.

Story Continues

His dramatic comeback after pressure from US President Donald Trump though has revived questions over the risks created by Nvidia's dependence on Huang and by the billions of dollars the company has poured into AI startups that ‌buy its chips.

The historic rally in Nvidia shares lost steam on Tuesday as investors refocused ​on the political and governance risks surrounding his reinstatement. The company and its boss also faces ​a host of state and federal probes and reviews.

DEEP INDUSTRY TIES

Beyond ​his celebrity status, Huang spent decades cultivating close personal relationships with Taiwan's tech leaders, helping build a supplier network that became ‌the backbone of Nvidia's dominance in AI computing.

During his frequent ​visits to the island, he hosted gatherings ​of executives from TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, Quanta Computer and other suppliers. Local media dubbed them "trillion-dollar dinners," a reference to the combined market value of the companies represented.

In May, Huang described Taiwan as the "epicentre" of the AI revolution and said Nvidia planned to invest about $150 billion a year in ​the island.

"Of course Taiwan really welcomes Jensen Huang's return," ‌said Lee Chang-ken, the president of Cathay Financial, Taiwan's largest financial holding company. "Naturally, we look forward to AI development continuing so that Taiwan's ​supply chain companies can keep making big profits."

(Reporting by Wen-Yee Lee and Yi-Chin Lee in Taipei; Additional reporting by Emily Chan and ​Ben Blanchard; Writing by Casey Hall; Editing by Thomas Derpinghaus and Tomasz Janowski)

news.Title: Have robotaxis hit a tipping point? Wall Street and experts are split.
news.Content: If you live in a major city, robotaxis are seemingly everywhere. You've probably seen one, know someone who's ridden in one, or even had a Waymo drive you somewhere. Most people are either enamored or terrified. But the robotaxi tipping point may be upon us, though there are still a number of hurdles for the industry's major players to surmount before hailing a robotaxi on any US road becomes a reality. "We're past the tipping point," Anthony Townsend, senior research associate at Cornell Tech and author of "Ghost Road: Beyond the Driverless Car," told Yahoo Finance. "Robotaxis are a technology that has become too big to fail." But not everyone agrees. Katie Driggs-Campbell, associate professor of electrical and computer engineering at the University of Illinois Grainger College of Engineering, said a true tipping point arrives when "these systems could really be deployed anywhere and everywhere and when it is safe to assume that most people have ridden in one." That may be close in the Bay Area, she said, but "certainly not in Central Illinois." But robotaxi operators like Waymo and Tesla ( TSLA ) would like to change that — and fast. Here's where the robotaxi space stands. Expansion everywhere Take Alphabet's ( GOOG , GOOGL ) Waymo. The service operates in 15 US cities , and last month Waymo added nearly 250 square miles of service across five cities, including Torrance in Los Angeles, La Jolla in San Diego, and a connection to BART's Berryessa Station in the Bay Area. It also opened rides to everyone in San Antonio, San Diego, and Tampa, and added pickups at the Harry Reid International Airport in Las Vegas for existing riders. But Waymo hit a major setback last week. California's DMV barred its robotaxis from the state's freeways , saying the driverless freeway operations pose an "imminent hazard to public safety" and citing "recurring incursions" by its vehicles into active construction zones. Waymo responded by pulling its robotaxis off freeways in every US market where it offers them, saying it had "temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance." The likely path back is a software update, proof to regulators that the problem is fixed, and a relaunch. Then there's Tesla ( TSLA ). Tesla started selling its driverless Cybercab to private buyers this month, but only to a hand-picked few, and only if they agree to a monthly fee on top of the sticker price. The two-seater, which has no steering wheel or pedals, costs $29,990 before taxes, with deliveries estimated for December. Buyers also put down a $1,000 nonrefundable deposit and sign up for a $299-per-month "Autonomy Subscription," with the first month free. Story Continues Musk revealed that Tesla plans to build a Model Y with no driver controls to enable robotaxi rides for larger groups of passengers. JPMorgan analyst Rajat Gupta sees this as an early sign the self-driving bet is working. Tesla's rapid robotaxi ramp, "including this weekend's launch of customer Cybercab sales, is starting to present early validation of the company's unique advantage in physical AI," Gupta wrote in a note to clients Sunday. Gupta expects customer-owned vehicles running unsupervised Full Self-Driving (FSD) to become "another, capital-light source of supply" for the network starting in the second quarter of 2027. Scale matters too, as JPMorgan ties 40% of its sum-of-the-parts Tesla valuation to robotaxis. Tesla now has 1,306 registered robotaxis in Texas, compared with 1,321 for Waymo. But registrations aren't rides. JPMorgan estimates 690 Teslas are operating nationally without a safety driver, vs. 4,000 driverless Waymos logging 4 million miles a week, more than six times Tesla's 635,000. Austin is where much of the robotaxi action is. Gupta estimates Tesla now accounts for half of all autonomous miles in the city, with a 440-square-mile service area versus Waymo's 150, despite launching unsupervised rides 10 months later. His model has Tesla matching Waymo's national weekly mileage in the second half of 2027 with a fleet of 18,000 robotaxis. Barclays analyst Dan Levy upgraded Tesla to Overweight last month, citing in part "signs of Robotaxi inflection." He wrote, "Tesla appears to be starting the rapid scaling that investors had long been waiting for, especially in Austin," though he doesn't "expect Robotaxi to be financially material in the near/mid-term." Tesla already operates its own robotaxi network of Cybercabs and Model Y SUVs in Austin, Dallas, Fort Worth, Houston, Miami, Orlando, San Antonio, and Tampa. And it is in those areas that personal Cybercabs will also operate. "We view personal ownership as a complementary opportunity alongside Tesla's company-operated robotaxi fleet," Morgan Stanley analyst Andrew Percoco said in a note published this week. "Selling the vehicle allows customers to fund the hardware while Tesla generates recurring subscription revenue." So who has the better technology? Experts lean Waymo, for now. "Everyone knows Waymo's technology is better. But Tesla is much better at rapid improvement and scaling. It's their race to lose," Townsend said. "Just based on the real-world experience and safety assessments, I think Waymo is likely safer and more reliable," Driggs-Campbell said. Columbia Business School professor Len Sherman said, "None of the current providers has an optimal solution and insurmountable competitive advantage yet." Waymo has "an admirable safety record, but their current technology is much too expensive," while Tesla's tech "has yet to be fully proven." "We're still in early innings of the robotaxi game," Sherman said. Regulatory hurdles "Local regulation is the biggest barrier right now, but that's a good thing," Townsend said. "This technology is far from perfect, and right now it's mostly a tool for perpetuating auto dependency. Big cities want to force taxibot companies to feed passengers to buses and train lines rather than compete with them, and to make roads safer for cyclists and pedestrians. I think they'll succeed." The state-by-state patchwork slows things down, Driggs-Campbell said. Illinois is still working through its regulatory process, so Waymo's vehicles are only collecting data in Chicago. Tesla has picked its battles accordingly. Per JPMorgan, Texas permits driverless operations through self-certification and vehicle registration, Florida requires no additional state-level authorization, and Nevada granted Tesla and others permission in August to operate up to 5,000 vehicles in Clark County (where Las Vegas is located). Together with Arizona, those states hold 20% of the US population. California is another story. Tesla still needs separate approvals from the DMV and the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) there , keeping its Bay Area rides supervised. Safety headlines are a separate problem. "Local media attention to robotaxi incidents is a very misleading gauge of actual AV safety performance," Sherman said. "Robotaxi vehicles are three to four times safer than human drivers on a per-mile basis, but are probably ten times more likely to receive media coverage for each safety incident." What needs to happen for robotaxis to be ubiquitous Rider demand isn't the main constraint. "Resistance to this technology fades quickly with exposure. But our expectations are also much higher than human drivers," Townsend said. Sherman pointed to survey data showing consumers "gain trust in AV technology shortly after their first ride." "Supply side constraints will be far more important than consumer acceptance in pacing the growth of robotaxi services," Sherman said. That means companies devoting substantial capital to fleets, plus the charging, cleaning, and maintenance facilities that support them. The tech isn't fully baked either. Driggs-Campbell said weather and mapping are still hurdles, and she's not sure the cost per ride has improved enough to make each trip profitable. "The opportunity is meaningful, but the pace of adoption will depend on how useful — and economical — the vehicle becomes for everyday ownership," Morgan Stanley's Percoco said. Tesla's first Cybercab owners will start testing that when deliveries begin next month. news.Title: Should You Buy Intel as Earnings Recover Despite a Premium Valuation?
news.Content:
Intel Corporation INTC is rebuilding earnings as server demand and manufacturing execution improve. The investment challenge is whether that recovery offers enough support for a valuation above both its industry benchmark and historical sales multiple.

The answer depends on how consistently operating gains reach shareholders. Better quarterly profitability strengthens the case for continued ownership, while capital demands, competition and weakness in PCs argue for discipline when considering a new position.

Intel Earnings Recovery Has Operating Support

Third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings reached 52 cents per share, increasing 126.1% year over year. Revenues rose 20.9% to $16.51 billion, while non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 19.6% from 11.2%. Growth was translating into operating leverage.

Manufacturing improvements helped. Higher yields and shorter production cycles reduced wafer costs, with Intel 18A costs down approximately 40% from first-quarter levels. These changes support product economics, although they do not eliminate the expense of developing future technologies.

INTC Valuation Requires Sustained Progress

Intel's Nov. 23 forward 12-month sales multiple stood at 4.7X, compared with 4.2X for its semiconductor sub-industry and a five-year median of 2.5X. Investors were already paying for progress beyond the latest quarterly improvement.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate stood at $1.49 per share for 2026 and $1.74 for 2027. Those forecasts indicate further earnings improvement, but expectations remain vulnerable to production setbacks and the pace of recovery in client demand.

Intel Cash Gains Face Heavy Capital Demands

Intel generated $5.08 billion of operating cash flow and $1.64 billion of adjusted free cash flow in the third quarter. Stronger cash generation gives the company more operating funds to contribute toward its manufacturing investment program.

Management nevertheless expected approximately $20 billion of gross capital expenditures in 2026 and a strong increase in 2027. August's $23 billion equity offering strengthened funding capacity but increased the share base. Operating improvement must therefore support both expanding capacity and per-share returns.

INTC Competition Tests Recovery Durability

Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. AMD launched sixth-generation EPYC server processors in November, keeping pressure on server execution. NVIDIA Corporation NVDA also began shipping Vera Rubin systems, broadening the platforms competing for AI infrastructure spending.

Intel's external foundry revenues reached $411 million in the third quarter, with the sequential increase primarily attributable to a non-recurring customer program. That result does not establish a scaled recurring business. Meanwhile, management's expectation of another PC unit market decline in 2027 limits recovery visibility.

Story Continues

Intel Growth Appeal Calls for Price Discipline

Intel offers measurable earnings improvement, but its premium valuation and substantial reinvestment needs leave limited room for execution setbacks. A measured holding stance remains easier to justify than an aggressive new purchase before earnings durability becomes clearer.

The stock carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). Its Growth Score of A and VGM Score of B support interest in its growth characteristics, while a Value Score of F reinforces valuation concerns. Style Scores refine the investment assessment alongside the Zacks Rank and do not override it.

news.Title: 〈美股早盤〉狂歡只一天？黃仁勳回歸行情降溫 輝達拖累主要指數開低
news.Content: 美股周二(24日)開低，道瓊下跌約101點，標普500跌0.90%，那斯達克跌1.43%。黃仁勳重返輝達(NVDA-US)帶動的AI反彈行情降溫，輝達與相關類股回落，美股回吐前一交易日的部分漲幅。投資人同時等待本周通膨數據，尋找聯準會(Fed)12月利率決策的最新線索，評估後續政策走向。 截稿前， 道瓊工業指數 漲近200點或0.4%， 那斯達克綜合指數 跌逾300點或近1.3%， 標普 500 指數 跌近0.5%， 費城半導體 指數跌逾6.0%，台積電ADR跌近4.0%。 黃仁勳重返輝達(NVDA-US)帶動的美股漲勢迅速降溫，投資人重新評估人工智慧(AI)行情能否持續反彈，加上美國擬提高對中國及其他數十國關稅的消息，壓抑市場風險胃納。標普500指數期貨下跌1.2%，那斯達克100指數期貨下挫2.1%。 輝達盤前下跌逾4%，回吐前一交易日的部分漲幅。該公司周一因黃仁勳回任執行長，市值大增近9,500億美元。AI模型開發商Anthropic(ANT-US)也一度跌破每股83美元的首次公開發行(IPO)價格，顯示市場對AI類股的追價熱情再度受到考驗。 慧與科技(HPE-US)盤前重挫12%，因營收展望未能滿足市場最樂觀的預期。一檔追蹤主要晶片股的指數股票型基金(ETF)也下跌逾4%，進一步凸顯AI反彈行情面臨的壓力。 《華爾街日報》報導美國正準備提高對中國及其他數十國的關稅後，市場跌勢擴大。資金轉向美債避險，推升各天期美債價格、美債殖利率走低。布蘭特原油在8月以來低點附近震盪，美元下跌0.2%，黃金、銅與比特幣則再度走低。 黃仁勳回歸雖減輕了股市面臨的一大不確定性，但輝達與客戶間的循環融資安排，以及公司治理問題，仍有待市場檢視。Axios另報導，Anthropic與OpenAI不少員工認為，部分尚未公開的模型正變得過於強大，讓AI安全疑慮再度浮上檯面。

news.Title: Can Intel Turn Its Microsoft Cloud Deal Into a Bigger Packaging Win?
news.Content:
Intel Corporation INTC gained a concrete advanced packaging opportunity through its November 2026 cloud agreement with Microsoft Corporation MSFT. Microsoft became the first company to announce use of Intel Foundry's Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge, or EMIB, for Azure first-party silicon.

The agreement expands Intel's potential role beyond supplying its own processors. Its investment significance rests on converting that customer engagement into a repeatable packaging business while meeting the production requirements of a demanding cloud customer.

Intel Gains an Azure Packaging Customer

Microsoft's Azure infrastructure plans connect Intel's packaging capabilities with customer-designed silicon. That creates another route for Intel to participate in cloud investment, including systems whose value extends beyond purchases of conventional server processors.

The distinction matters because external foundry revenues were $411 million in third-quarter 2026, and the sequential increase primarily reflected a non-recurring program. A named packaging customer strengthens commercial credibility, but sustained production programs remain necessary to establish recurring external demand.

INTC Xeon Agreement Extends the Cloud Opportunity

The Microsoft agreement also confirms multiyear Xeon supply capacity, including next-generation Diamond Rapids processors. Intel's October roadmap called for that product to ramp in 2027, linking a future processor generation with a major customer's infrastructure planning.

Oracle Corporation ORCL separately announced an intended multiyear collaboration in October covering current and future Xeon platforms, including planned X14 cloud offerings based on Diamond Rapids. These plans widen customer engagement, although future products and intended collaboration remain distinct from completed deployments.

Intel Manufacturing Progress Supports the Plan

Intel's factory performance offers support for its broader customer ambitions. Third-quarter foundry operating loss narrowed to $1.85 billion, while Intel 18A manufacturing costs declined approximately 40% from first-quarter levels as yields and production cycles improved.

These wafer improvements strengthen overall manufacturing economics without establishing EMIB profitability. More directly relevant to packaging delivery, Intel was adding capacity in New Mexico and Malaysia for customer ramps in 2027. That expansion provides a practical next step toward serving additional programs.

INTC Supply and Capital Needs Limit the Ramp

Story Continues

Advanced organic substrate shortages were already restricting the scaling of EMIB-packaged products. Management expected industry supply limitations throughout 2027 and into 2028, making component availability a constraint even when customer interest and packaging capacity improve.

Funding requirements are substantial. Intel expected roughly $20 billion of gross capital expenditures in 2026 and a strong increase in 2027. Two subsequently signed substrate agreements also entail approximately $3.3 billion of payments by the end of 2027, adding commitments before the full commercial payoff.

Intel Cloud Progress Still Requires Execution

The Microsoft relationship gives Intel an important packaging customer and a broader connection to cloud infrastructure plans. Progress should be judged by production execution, sustained external business and improving economics as the company builds capacity for future customer ramps.

Intel carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), alongside a Growth Score of A and VGM Score of B. These favorable style characteristics complement the neutral ranking signal, while a Value Score of F adds valuation caution. They do not establish the timing or profitability of the cloud agreement.

news.Title: 黃仁勳重返輝達點火台股！謝金河警告「未來兩大變數」
news.Content:
輝達（NVIDIA）執行長黃仁勳正式重返崗位並恢復所有職務，激勵全球科技股與台灣市場強勁反彈。財信傳媒董事長謝金河今（24）日在臉書發文分析，黃仁勳不僅是人工智慧（AI）領域無可替代的領路者，更是為台灣打造高毛利供應鏈的關鍵推手；雖然短線受惠於重返消息而大漲，但未來仍須密切關注美國對中晶片管制與國安調查這兩大變數。

謝金河指出，黃仁勳此次重返輝達的戲劇性發展，印證了「世界需要黃仁勳，股市更需要黃仁勳」的市場現實。在美國總統川普態度轉變並鋪平道路後，輝達股價單日飆漲31.48%，市值一舉暴增9530億美元。謝金河認為，黃仁勳同時身兼AI藍圖的擘畫者與技術開發者，一旦缺乏他的領導，整個AI產業便會頓失方向。

他進一步比喻，這波轉折與去年4月川普面對關稅引發股市崩盤後改口協商如出一轍，即便黃仁勳先前接連捲入緋聞、晶片違規銷中及國會調查等風暴，但在市場重挫的壓力下，川普仍選擇力挺，展現資本市場對黃仁勳的高度依賴。這股效應也直接反映在亞洲股市的表現上。台股24狂飆3310.46點、漲幅高達8.99%，表現遠優於日本股市的3.91%及南韓股市的6.22%。

謝金河強調，台股之所以能展現如此強勁的爆發力，最核心的原因在於黃仁勳為台灣搭建了堅實且高獲利的AI供應鏈。過去台灣高度仰賴蘋果（Apple）供應鏈，在執行長庫克（Tim Cook）精準壓縮代工成本的策略下，台廠多半陷入「毛三到四」的微利苦戰；然隨著輝達崛起，台灣供應鏈的獲利結構徹底翻轉，毛利率節節攀升，包括川湖毛利率高達82.56%，致茂達57.5%、鴻勁56.93%、穎崴40.55%，以及台光電37.7%與奇鋐33.86%，顯示黃仁勳打造的生態系為台廠帶來實質且豐厚的利潤。

儘管黃仁勳回歸對台灣產業是一大利多，但謝金河也提醒投資人，這場風暴讓全球重新檢視AI產業的潛在風險，輝達股價單日暴衝後，未來仍面臨兩大不確定性。首先是美國對輝達晶片銷往中國的管制勢必趨嚴，此舉已衝擊香港與深圳股市走跌，中國大型語言模型（LLM）相關企業如智譜、稀宇科技股價雙雙重挫並創下新低，而輝達若失去約占20%的中國市場，後續業績恐受波及。

其次謝金河指出，針對黃仁勳的國安調查尚未落幕，即便川普強勢主導局勢，華府內部的反黃仁勳勢力仍不容小覷。謝金河總結，台灣供應鏈短期內難免隨消息面出現震盪，但從長遠來看，隨著「非紅供應鏈」逐步落實，台灣依然會是這場全球科技變局中的最終贏家。

news.Title: 台股大跌後反彈！呂文婉曝「定存利率」直呼慶幸：寒冬送暖
news.Content:
資深媒體人呂文婉不時會透過社群平台分享生活點滴與理財觀念，台股日前重挫，投資人心情也跟著跌宕起伏，如今輝達（NVIDIA）創辦人黃仁勳回歸執行長職位、台股隨之反彈，呂文婉23日發文透露，接到銀行通知定存到期，讓她忍不住直呼：「真的好慶幸自己還有定存」。

呂文婉在臉書發文表示，「早上接到銀行的電話，通知我定存到期了，可以臨櫃辦理續約。沒想到還捎來一個好消息！因為我是長期優良客戶，銀行特別給予優惠，利率可以從原本的 1.725% 調升至2%。」

面對近期股市波動，呂文婉也坦言，「雖然定存賺不了大錢，不過至少穩穩當當的......或許有人覺得，2%實在太少了，然而在股市一片慘澹的這時候，倒也算得上是寒冬送暖......真的好慶幸自己還有定存」。

進一步分享個人看法，「投資理財本來就不該只有一種方式，有時候，能守住本金、每月固定收息，也是種平凡的幸福。」貼文中，呂文婉也提及黃仁勳回歸輝達執行長一事，文末還幽默附上「PS.可以不用睡車站了」。

不少網友也紛紛留言分享理財觀念，表示，「好羨慕您，會賺錢又會存錢」、「千萬存款2%就很厲害咯」、「保本是理財的先決條件」、「理財的前提不是賺多少，而是先求穩定收益，再依個人風險屬性去做另外的配置」、「分散風險、不貪便是」、「雞蛋要放幾個籃子」、「恭喜錢錢越來越多！」、「很棒的分擔風險管理，寧可備而不用，總是會有需要的時候」。

news.Title: 砸7450億在德州蓋2奈米廠？台積電回應：持續評估
news.Content:
外媒今（24）日報導，台積電旗下子公司於周一向德州政府提交申請，並告知當地官員，能否獲得房產稅減免，將是在當地興建晶圓廠的決定性因素。台積電目前計畫晶圓相關設施建造價值約為226億美元（約新台幣7450億），廠區占地將超過3200英畝。

根據《路透社》報導，台積電子公司TSMC Arizona Corporation此次規畫將在德州布拉索斯郡（Brazos County）投資，計畫興建的設施將包括一個或多個晶片製造廠以及配套基礎設施，佔地超過3200英畝，並將採用2奈米或更先進技術，製造用於人工智慧、高效能運算和行動裝置的晶片。且根據台積電的文件，該計畫預計將在未來四十年內創造至少2099個直接就業機會。

不過文件中提到，台積電自2024年一直在亞利桑那州運營半導體製造廠，在當地擴廠可以帶來「一定的營運和經濟優勢」。因此，德州在此次競爭當中，仍有對手存在。美國總統川普近期接受訪問時，也稱台積電董事長魏哲家當下將大量業務移到美國，且要在德州啟動一座大型工廠。

針對有意在德州布局的傳聞，台積電回應，提交申報的資訊，是為了確保持續評估該地區的潛在投資過程，維持與當地透明且良好的溝通，仍在持續評估。

news.Title: Tesla and SpaceX assemble deal teams for a merger that could give Musk majority control
news.Content:
Tesla ( TSLA ) and SpaceX ( SPCX ) have enlisted five directors and three investment banks to help move forward what could be the biggest merger in history — and one that could give Elon Musk greater voting power than he currently has at Tesla.

The companies have tapped two directors from SpaceX and three from Tesla — Roelof Botha and Randy Glein from SpaceX, and Robyn Denholm, Kathleen Wilson-Thompson, and Jack Hartung from Tesla — to serve on two special committees overseeing the potential $3.5 trillion merger, the Financial Times reported .

Although all five have longstanding ties to Elon Musk, the CEO of both companies, they were deemed financially "disinterested" parties.

The committees have enlisted Morgan Stanley ( MS ) and Goldman Sachs ( GS ) for SpaceX and Evercore ( EVR ) for Tesla to develop financial models for the proposed all-stock merger. The exchange ratio — which will determine how much of the combined company existing Tesla and SpaceX shareholders will own — has yet to be agreed upon.

The deal, which could be reached before year's end, could give Musk something he's long sought: greater voting power than he currently has at Tesla. That could give Musk more latitude to pursue his ambitions in AI and robotics while diminishing other shareholders' ability to challenge his decisions.

Musk controls about 20% of Tesla's voting power, compared with 84% at SpaceX, where he holds supervoting shares. Depending on the terms of the deal and the governance structure of the combined company, Musk could end up with majority voting control.

news.Title: 快訊》台指期夜盤下殺2024點 失守39K 費半早盤崩跌近8％
news.Content:
（23：30更新）台股今（24）日才上演史詩級反彈，狂飆3310.46點，以40122.35點作收，但台指期夜盤卻再度上演殺盤行情。儘管稍早一度上漲576點，報40900點，但隨後賣壓湧現，指數一路向下摜破4萬點大關，在美股早盤，最低更觸及38300點，暴跌2024點。

美股同樣面臨賣壓。周二（24日）美股一開盤，主要指數全面下殺。道瓊工業指數開盤走跌，但早盤翻紅，一度上漲逾300點，那斯達克指數早盤則一度大跌逾400點，與台股連動密切的費城半導體指數早盤跌幅一度近8%。前一個交易日狂飆31.48%的輝達回檔逾7%。台積電ADR走跌逾5%。與此同時，Anthropic大跌逾9%，跌破IPO發行價，進一步給大盤帶來下行壓力。

news.Title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq fall as chip stocks tumble, investors test Nvidia-fueled rally
news.Content:
US stocks fell on Tuesday after a blistering rally, as investors took stock of what's next for Nvidia ( NVDA ) and the AI trade now that Jensen Huang is back as CEO.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell 0.4%, while those on the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) declined 1.2%. The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) fell 1.8% after stocks logged their best day since the "Liberation Day" recovery of April 2025.

Tech stocks fell, led by declines in the chip sector. Nvidia shares declined 5% following a 31% surge. AMD ( AMD ), Micron ( MU ), and Broadcom ( AVGO ) shares also tumbled.

After paring back bets of a rate hike in December, traders shifted their odds again to forecast a 95% probability that the Federal Reserve will increase rates by 25 basis points and 5% odds of a jumbo 50 basis point hike. The AI rally stoked inflation concerns, while oil prices fell by about 1%.

Several companies are getting their earnings reports in before the Thanksgiving and Black Friday holidays, including Dell Technologies ( DELL ), Dollar Tree ( DLTR ), HP ( HP ), Best Buy ( BBY ), and Dick's Sporting Goods ( DKS ). Best Buy shares rose after the electronics retailer posted its best same-store sales growth in five years.

LIVE 8 updates

22 mins ago David Hollerith

Stocks fall as Nvidia shares drop and rate hike bets return

US stocks tumbled at Tuesday's open as investors pulled back after Monday's blistering rebound, with Nvidia giving back some of its gains and the return of rate-hike expectations weighing broadly on stocks.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell 0.6%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) declined 1.3%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) fell 1.8%.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares fell after surging 31% Monday following Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO. The pullback came as investors reassessed how much further the AI trade can run after stocks posted their strongest day since the April 2025 "Liberation Day" rebound.

41 mins ago Ines Ferré

HPE stock declines as disappointing margin forecast outweighs upbeat guidance

Hewlett Packard Enterprise ( HPE ) stock dropped 13% in premarket trading on Tuesday after the server and networking products maker reported fourth quarter results.

The company said it expects Cloud & AI operating margins to fall to about 14% in fiscal 2027, down from 18.4% in the latest quarter, raising concerns that pricing tailwinds are beginning to fade.

The outlook overshadowed better-than-expected 2027 revenue guidance and strong order growth. Quarterly cloud and AI revenue grew 68.6% from the same period a year earlier.

Shares of peer Dell ( DEL L) also fell 7% in premarket trading amid a broader retreat in the AI-related trade. Dell is scheduled to report earnings after Tuesday's market close.

Today at 1:22 PM UTC Jennifer Schonberger

AI market whipsaw puts Kevin Warsh's rate-hike strategy to the test

When stocks tanked last week, Wall Street briefly bet the Federal Reserve would ease up on interest rate hikes. Now Monday's massive rebound — sparked by Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia — has revived bets on at least two more interest rate hikes.

Yet with AI stocks still off their highs, the sector's volatility is emerging as a critical test for Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh and the central bank's path for rate hikes.

"AI stress is not mostly due to the Fed. But it is not a coincidence it is occurring when the Fed is hiking," said Krishna Guha, head of central banking and the economy for Evercore ISI. "Talk of 50-basis-point hikes or faster tightening adds to stress. Fed Chair Warsh not talking is a problem. It leaves the market guessing: Is he a hardcore hawk or a market-sensitive hawk? The gap is filled by others whose views can lag the leadership."

"This is a serious test for Warsh," Guha added.

Today at 12:35 PM UTC Brooke DiPalma

Best Buy posts best sales growth in 5 years, stock jumps on raised outlook

Best Buy ( BBY ) reported third quarter earnings results that blew past Wall Street's expectations in the midst of the most critical shopping season for retailers. The quarterly results marked Jason Bonfig's first as chief executive.

The electronics retailer posted same-store sales growth of 6.1%, its best quarter in five years. Sales growth also surpassed forecasts for a 2.3% gain and the 2.7% growth reported this time last year.

The results were driven by consumers replacing their tech or upgrading to new models. Revenue grew 5% to $10.2 billion, above expectations of $9.9 billion and up from the $9.7 billion posted in Q3 last year. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $1.62, above the expected $1.49 and well ahead of the $1.40 reported a year ago.

"Disciplined execution, a compelling product cycle and continued market share gains helped drive broad-based topline momentum across nearly all product categories," Bonfig said, which gave the retailer confidence to raise its guidance.

Best Buy stock rose by 5% before the bell on Tuesday.

Today at 11:52 AM UTC David Hollerith

Anthropic's stock slips below IPO price

Only three days after its blockbuster public listing, shares of AI lab Anthropic ( ANT ) briefly slipped in Tuesday's premarket below its IPO price of $83 per share.

The stock of the Claude model maker fell as much as 6% early Tuesday, trading at $82.30 as of 6:30 a.m. ET before recovering some of those losses. The move comes after the stock market's newest AI giant missed out on a Monday rally that came as chip giant Nvidia ( NVDA ) reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO .

Anticipation around Anthropic's enormous capital needs and its yet-to-be-shared credit rating, a potential stock supply overhang from insider selling, and ordinary post-IPO profit-taking are all reasons for the lackluster performance, according to Needham analysts.

Today at 11:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell

How fear of AI displacement is fueling a hiring recession

Yahoo Finance's Hamza Shaban writes in today's Morning Brief newsletter:

The US labor market has proved remarkably resilient in the post-pandemic era. But as anyone looking for a job can tell you, it's rough out there. Just getting your resume past AI screeners and in front of a real person is a small victory in itself.

What's been described as a hiring recession is a labor market that has low unemployment but also one that has settled into a low-hire, low-fire environment. One of the reasons workers are staying put and fewer people are being welcomed aboard is artificial intelligence.

After a surge in people quitting their jobs or switching careers during the pandemic, workers are settling back in. But the lower levels of churn, or workers moving between jobs, are especially evident in industries closer to AI, suggesting a connection between a lack of labor dynamism and concerns around the technology.

"Churn has fallen further below pre-pandemic levels in industries with greater AI adoption and automation potential, as workers increasingly stay put amid rising job insecurity," analysts at Goldman Sachs wrote in a research report published Monday.

news.Title: Nvidia's stunning comeback delivers new shock to Fed rate-hike bets
news.Content:
Leather Daddy lasted a full Scaramucci before going back to work as CEO of Nvidia, and the market rewarded his return after 11 scandal-ripe days with a great big rebound in the tech sector Nov. 23.

As a result, traders revived the nearly 100% probability of an interest-rate hike when the Federal Open Market Committee meets Dec. 8-9.

The CME Group FedWatch Tool rose to a 95.3% probability that the FOMC will raise rates by 25 basis points, but took a 50-basis-point hike off the table. Futures traders also penciled in at least two more 25-basis-point hikes into July 2027.

Why? Because Jensen Huang's victory tour at Nvidia's Silicon Valley headquarters fueled the pro-hike tailwinds trailing the streaming hot mess at the intersection of politics, corporate governance and national security.

"As I live and breathe, I've never seen anything like it,'' is how CNBC's resident stock guru Jim Cramer described the Nov. 23 rally's timeline after the market closed.

President Donald Trump, in a nearly hour-long phone call with the cable network earlier in the day, called Huang a "national treasure" and claimed his personal intervention with the Nvidia board paved the way for Huang's return.

It was a stunning, shocking revelation (frankly, I was gobsmacked while watching it), especially after the Nvidia board of directors said late last week that Huang would not be returning to the chipmaker leading AI computing, GPUs, data centers, graphics, and robotics.

By the end of the day on Nov. 20, Nvidia lost roughly $491 billion in market value, with shares plunging 14.01% to close at $125.53 and bringing its market cap down from ~$3.52 trillion to ~$3.03 trillion.

Nvidia stock rebounded to close at $165.05 Nov. 23, surging 31.48% or $39.52 per share from the Nov. 20 close but still roughly 31% below its record close of $239.24 on Oct. 6.

Hence the frothy market reaction to the unprecedented presidential move to influence a publicly traded company that shocked politicians, government officials, corporate accountability leaders, and even market experts.

But the volatility has a price to pay. And that's where higher interest rates come in because, as most American consumers and businesses will tell you, prices are just too damn high.

A tech-stock rally does not, by itself, cause the Fed to raise interest rates. Future traders are responding to broader inflation expectations, economic resilience, AI-related investment, and hawkish Fed commentary.

Nvidia rally triggers new Fed rate-hike bets

Story Continues

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has repeatedly said since taking over the role in May that the Fed is committed to its dual mandate: use interest rates and balance-sheet policy to keep prices stable and the labor market at full employment.

The labor market has been solid for months, but inflation has missed the Fed's 2% target for nearly six years.

The alleged "Fed put" — investor confidence that the U.S. central bank will be there to rescue if the S&P 500 sells off — was MIA.

A put option gives investors downside protection if a stock falls below a certain level.

While the Fed wouldn't sit by indefinitely, it may have waited until something closer to a 20% bear market decline as it did back during the 2018 rate-hiking cycle.

As the S&P 500 rocked after the Huang announcement, traders penciled in nearly a 100% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike in December, then walked those odds back on Nov. 20 after Nvidia.

Odds of a further quarter-point rate hike by the Jan. 27 Fed meeting climbed to 69% from 49% on Nov. 20. That would raise the target for the Fed's benchmark rate to a range of 4.25% to 4.5%.

But wait, there's more.  Odds of another 25-basis-point hike to a 4.5% to 4.75% range by the June 9 Fed meeting rose to 62.5% from 41% on Nov. 20.

FedWatch probabilities reflect futures market expectations and are neither an official Fed forecast nor a guarantee that the FOMC will raise rates.

December F OMC meeting to focus on sticky inflation

October PCE , the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, will be released Nov. 25 and the November jobs report will come Dec. 4, giving the 12-member FOMC the latest data to weigh how monetary policy can best meet its dual mandate: price stability and maximum employment.

As New York Fed President John Williams said Nov. 23: sticky inflation boosted by tariffs, the energy shock from the Iran War, and the artificial intelligence supply-demand dynamics mean the central bank has work to do to cool inflation by extending its tightening cycle.

"We must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2% goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis," Williams said in prepared remarks. "There is still work to do to ​get that done.''

Rate-hike impact on wallets and retirement portfolios

For consumers, businesses and investors, the message from Wall Street is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore: The era of waiting for lower interest rates may take longer than anyone wants.

This means consumers and businesses can expect interest rates on credit cards, private student loans, and home-equity loans to rise through early 2027, and, indirectly, mortgage rates and Treasury bond yields will also be influenced.

As for investors, higher interest rates ripple through the stock market and investor portfolios via several core channels ranging from discounted cash flows and corporate borrowing costs to shifts in asset allocation.

Fed rate-hike pause may be temporary as inflation flares

As I reported , minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee October meeting released Nov. 18, along with some very pointed public remarks from top Fed officials, show the U.S. central bank is becoming increasingly alarmed that price pressures are moving away from its 2% target, but there's a wide range of opinion within its ranks as to the best approach to lower price pressures.

In fact, when the FOMC held its benchmark short-term interest rate steady at 3.75% to 4% in October with a divisive 10-2 vote, the minutes show several participants described the pause as a "close call."

Fed Governor Lisa Cook, one of the two FOMC members who voted to raise rates by 25 basis points in October, said Nov. 20 that the October pause threatened to put the Fed behind the curve in its battle to tame persistent inflation.

Related: J.P. Morgan prices in stunning shift in Fed rate-hike call

"In a different environment, the (Federal Open Market) Committee could afford to be patient, but I continue to believe that in this economic climate we do not have that luxury," given how ​high inflation is and for how long it has been above the Fed's 2% target, Cook said.

Cook said the AI buildout is a global undertaking, and it is reshaping economies in ways that are only beginning to be understood.

"In the U.S., labor markets appear resilient to date, but AI adoption is still in its early stages, and I think it is too soon to feel comforted. We do see that some workers have already been affected by AI,'' she said.

Fed governors send definite hawkish signals

Cook was one of four Fed Governors — including Vice Chair Philip Jefferson, Michael Barr , and Christopher Waller — signaling decidedly hawkish tones last week.

Waller doubled down on his comments earlier this month, saying that rising price pressures call for a jumbo 50-basis-point rate hike in December.

"You might need to, like, shock people," he said .

The Nov. 23 market rally took a possible 50-basis-point hike off the table for many Fed watchers.

Related: Fed rate-cut hopes for 2027 take a stunning turn

news.Title: Nvidia live updates: Nvidia stock falls as exuberance fades after Jensen Huang's return as CEO
news.Content: Nvidia's ( NVDA ) stock fell 5% on Tuesday, reversing from a strong 31% rally on Monday, after the company's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. In a statement, the board said it had a series of discussions with Huang and was satisfied with his candor and ability to lead the company. "The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said. Jones will remain the chair of Nvidia's board. In an interview on Monday, President Trump said he had spoken "directly and indirectly" with the board and "convinced" them to make a deal. Top administration officials also reportedly assured the Nvidia board that Huang wasn't a national security risk and wasn't facing alleged chip-smuggling charges. "I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said in a statement. LIVE 50 updates 27 mins ago Brian Sozzi Jensen Huang is back at Nvidia. Should AMD be worried? When it comes to the AI trade, this has been the year of AMD ( AMD ). AMD's stock has sizzled, up 112% year to date compared to an 11.5% drop for its top rival Nvidia. As Nvidia's ( NVDA ) founder Jensen Huang has been embroiled in scandal and the tech trade has been pressured, AMD shares have hung tough. The stock is down 12.2% over the past month versus a 22% decline for Nvidia. The biggest question for AMD right now is this: Does Huang's stunning return as CEO of Nvidia mean bad news for AMD in 2027 and beyond? Pros think AMD will be just fine, for now. "I don't see how this changes it completely," Moor Insights & Strategy founder Patrick Moorhead said on Sozzi Unleashed . "I was saying early on when Jensen left that nothing changes for 18 months. And the reason is the supply chain is locked, the wafers are locked, data center configurations are locked around Nvidia design. So nothing would change, I think, if Jensen had been removed permanently." Today at 1:30 PM UTC Brian Sozzi Nvidia's longtime CFO and now former interim CEO Colette Kress was left in the dark about Jensen Huang's return: Report Colette Kress has been the CFO of Nvidia ( NVDA ) since 2013, helping to build the company at the center of the AI boom alongside founder and public face Jensen Huang. She stepped into the line of fire for 12 days as interim CEO while Huang worked behind the scenes to return. She withstood fresh reports of Huang berating her in meetings, and President Trump saying in an interview that she did a poor job in her post-earnings TV interview last week. In the end, Nvidia's longtime CFO Colette Kress — a widely respected figure on Wall Street — has been left holding the bag. And, apparently, left out of the loop on Huang's return. "The talks that culminated in an Nvidia board meeting late on Sunday were so secretive that even interim chief executive officer Colette Kress was kept out of the discussions," a new report on Tuesday from the Financial Times said, citing people familiar with the matter. Today at 1:23 PM UTC Jennifer Schonberger Nvidia rebound revives rate-hike bets, testing Fed Chairman Warsh When stocks tanked last week, Wall Street briefly bet the Federal Reserve would ease up on interest rate hikes. Now Monday's massive rebound — sparked by Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia — has revived bets on at least two more interest rate hikes. Yet with AI stocks still off their highs, the sector's volatility is emerging as a critical test for Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh and the central bank's path for rate hikes. "AI stress is not mostly due to the Fed. But it is not a coincidence it is occurring when the Fed is hiking," said Krishna Guha, head of central banking and the economy for Evercore ISI. "Talk of 50-basis-point hikes or faster tightening adds to stress. Fed Chair Warsh not talking is a problem. It leaves the market guessing: Is he a hardcore hawk or a market-sensitive hawk? The gap is filled by others whose views can lag the leadership." "This is a serious test for Warsh," Guha added. Today at 1:00 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Jensen Huang's return revives an old Wall Street trade: Bet on the comeback CEO Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi reports: Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia ( NVDA ) could be good for more than a one-day pop in its stock price. Just look at the evidence from the case studies on the returns of founders like Apple's ( AAPL ) Steve Jobs, Starbucks' ( SBUX ) founder Howard Schultz, and Charles Schwab's ( SCHW ) founder Charles Schwab. A new analysis of six high-profile CEO returns by Rand Group Research found that four of the six companies outperformed the S&P 500 over the three years after their leaders returned. The biggest winner was Apple, where Steve Jobs' return in September 1997 was followed by a staggering 414% stock gain, versus 59% for the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ). The stock price gain reflected Jobs' innovation streak, which led to world-changing products like the iPhone and iPod. There were exceptions, however. Disney ( DIS ) shares rose just 14% after Bob Iger returned in 2022, badly trailing the S&P 500's 67% gain, while Under Armour ( UA ) has fallen 40% since Kevin Plank returned in 2024. The takeaway for Nvidia investors? A founder's return can be a powerful catalyst, particularly when that founder has a deep understanding of the business and a track record of creating shareholder value. But it's no guarantee. Jensen Huang has the opportunity to join a pretty impressive comeback club — but he'll still have to deliver. Today at 12:22 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Nvidia shares slide 5% as premarket trading indicates 'turnaround Tuesday' Nvidia shares slid 5% on Tuesday, retreating from yesterday's monster 31% rally. As Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre points out, "turnaround Tuesday" is pretty par for the course. He writes: The old Wall Street saying that Tuesday undoes Monday has a point. In the 20 times since 1993 that the SPDR S&P 500 ETF ( SPY ) opened Monday 2% or more higher, it rose the next day only 9 times, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. By Friday, it was a coin flip. Patience usually paid. A year later, SPY was higher in 17 of the 20 cases, with a typical gain of about 26%. The bad cases were really bad, though. In a quarter of them, SPY fell 12% or more within three months. Five of the 20 came in the fall of 2008. Today at 1:30 AM UTC Ines Ferré Elon Musk on his support for Jensen Huang: 'Fair-weather friends are worthless' Tesla ( TSLA ) and SpaceX ( SPCX ) CEO Elon Musk once again came out in support of his friend Jensen Huang on Monday after Nvidia's board unanimously decided to reinstate Huang as CEO. Musk also took a swipe at those who may not have stood by Huang as publicly or forcefully as he did. "Everyone is your friend when the chips are up, but those who support you when the chips are down are your real friends," Musk wrote on X on Monday in response to a post about his support for Huang. "Fair-weather friends are worthless," Musk added. Earlier on Monday, Musk immediately responded to the news that Nvidia's board had reinstated the founder as CEO, writing, "It is done." Later, he added, "The mistake has been corrected." Musk was one of Huang's biggest supporters throughout the ordeal that led to Huang's resignation. He was also vocal about a campaign to bring back Huang, citing a circulating petition. news.Title: Dan Loeb’s Third Point Takes $475 Million Stake in Meta as Institutional Investors Concentrate Their Wealth in Tech Winners
news.Content:
Shifting hedge-fund allocations across mega-cap tech underscore how selective institutional managers have become toward artificial intelligence (AI) spending. Rather than chasing broad sector momentum, prominent activist investors are concentrating capital into scaled digital ad platforms where proprietary AI algorithms already deliver measurable user engagement and durable free cash flow.

Demonstrating this conviction, Dan Loeb's Third Point recently revealed a fresh third-quarter stake in Meta Platforms (META) of 655,000 shares. The stake is valued at roughly $475 million.

More News from Barchart

Dear Dell Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 24

CoreWeave's Co-Founder Says He's 'Never Been More Confident' in the Company as He Buys $30 Million of Its Bonds. Why That Matters More Than a Stock Buy for CRWV.

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

Meta Platforms is the global technology company behind platforms like Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger. Led by CEO Mark Zuckerberg, the company generates most of its revenue through digital advertising while expanding into AI, smart glasses, and virtual reality. Meta's growing AI infrastructure investments are central to its long-term growth strategy.

About Meta Platforms Stock

Shares of Meta Platforms have faced pressure in 2026 as investors have weighed rising AI infrastructure spending, legal expenses, and the potential returns from its expanding technology investments. META stock currently trades around $598 per share, down approximately 9% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis. Despite the pullback, the company's advertising business continues to benefit from AI-powered recommendations, improved ad targeting, and stronger monetization across its Family of Apps.

Meta Platforms Reports Q3 Results

On Oct. 21, Meta reported Q3 2026 revenue of $64.6 billion, up 26% year-over-year (YOY) and exceeding the analyst consensus estimate of approximately $63.3 billion. Adjusted EPS, excluding a substantial legal charge, came in at $7.40, beating the consensus estimate of $6.54. However, reported GAAP diluted EPS was $3.83, reflecting the impact of the legal expense. Net income reached $9.86 billion, compared with $2.71 billion in the year-ago quarter, while revenue growth was primarily driven by stronger advertising performance across its platforms.

Story Continues

Meta's financial metrics highlighted the growing contribution of AI to its advertising business. Ad impressions across its Family of Apps increased 10% YOY, while the average price per ad climbed 14%. Family daily active people reached 3.64 billion in September, up 3% YOY. However, total costs and expenses surged 68% to $51.61 billion, including a $9.89 billion legal charge. Operating income declined 37% to $12.99 billion, bringing Meta's operating margin down to 20% from 40%. Capital expenditures reached $34.91 billion during the period, while operating cash flow stood at $32.79 billion.

Looking ahead, management expects Q4 revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion, supported by continued ad momentum and AI-driven improvements in engagement and monetization. Meta raised its full-year total expense outlook to a range of $175 billion to $179 billion, incorporating the Q3 legal charge, and expects 2026 capital expenditures of $135 billion to $145 billion. Meta also anticipates Reality Labs operating losses of $18 billion to $19 billion for 2026. Beyond this year, management plans to continue investing aggressively in AI models, data centers, and infrastructure, while expecting AI-related improvements and emerging products to support strong revenue growth through 2027.

Third Point Takes a New Stake in Meta Platforms

Dan Loeb-founded Third Point established a new position in Meta Platforms during Q3, acquiring approximately 655,000 Class A shares valued at $475 million as of Sept. 30, according to its latest 13F filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The investment adds Meta to the hedge fund's portfolio as investors continue to assess the company's AI-driven advertising growth and expanding technology ambitions.

Third Point also initiated new positions in Nvidia (NVDA) and Unum (UNM) while completely exiting Amazon (AMZN). Additionally, the fund increased its SpaceX (SPCX) investment to 980,400 shares and significantly reduced its Alphabet (GOOGL) Class A position.

The filing offers a snapshot of Third Point's portfolio changes, although it did not disclose the specific reasons behind its Meta investment.

Should You Buy META Stock?

Third Point establishing a new $475 million position in Meta Platforms during Q3 adds to the institutional interest surrounding the social media giant. With its AI-powered ad business, expanding tech ecosystem, and growing investment in AI, Meta continues to offer compelling long-term growth opportunities, although execution and spending risks remain.

Wall Street sentiment is bullish, with META stock carrying a consensus "Strong Buy" rating overall. Of the 55 analysts with coverage, 46 have a "Strong Buy" rating, two have a "Moderate Buy," and seven analysts have a "Hold" rating. The mean price target of $855.96 implies potential upside of approximately 43% from current levels.

news.Title: Target vs. Walmart: Which Consumer Goods Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
As the retail landscape shifts toward automation and digital convenience, investors are weighing the value of brand loyalty against the benefit of massive global scale. Choosing between Target (NYSE:TGT) and Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) requires examining their unique paths.

Target attracts shoppers with its curated merchandise and exclusive shop-in-shop partnerships, while Walmart dominates through sheer volume and a rapidly expanding e-commerce network. These retail titans compete for the same household dollars but rely on different operational engines to drive shareholder value, making their comparison a study in efficiency versus brand loyalty.

The case for Target

Target relies on its store network and digital services, such as Shipt, to provide a differentiated guest experience. The company leverages high-profile partnerships with Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), Starbucks (NASDAQ:SBUX), and Ulta Beauty (NASDAQ:ULTA) to drive traffic to its physical locations and its Target Plus digital marketplace. While the shop-in-shop operating agreement with Ulta Beauty is scheduled to end in August 2026, these brand collaborations remain core to its merchandise strategy.

In the 12 months ended Oct. 31, 2026, revenue for this player in consumer staples stocks reached nearly $109.5 billion. This represented revenue growth of roughly 4% compared to the previous 12 months. Net income for the period was close to $4.9 billion, showcasing the company's ability to remain profitable while expanding its digital footprint.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 1.3x, meaning total debt was 1.3 times shareholder equity. The current ratio was nearly 0.9x, measuring the ability to pay short-term obligations with short-term assets. In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $2.8 billion, which is the cash remaining after subtracting capital expenditures from operating cash flow.

The case for Walmart

Walmart operates as a tech-powered retailer with over 10,750 locations worldwide. The company uses automation through partners like Symbotic (NASDAQ:SYM) to streamline its massive fulfillment network and improve distribution efficiency. This immense scale allows it to serve roughly 280 million customers every week through a combination of physical stores and a growing global omnichannel model.

In the 12 months ended Oct. 31, 2026, revenue reached nearly $745.2 billion. This figure reflects revenue growth of approximately 6% compared to the previous 12 months. Net income for the company reached nearly $20.9 billion, underscoring its status as the world's largest retailer by total sales volume.

Story Continues

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.7x, indicating that total debt was less than shareholder equity. Its current ratio was approximately 0.8x, calculated by dividing current assets by current liabilities. In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, free cash flow totaled nearly $14.9 billion, reflecting cash generated after accounting for necessary capital investments.

Risk profile comparison

Target faces significant operational pressure from inventory shrink, including theft and organized retail crime, which impacts asset impairment and store closures. The company relies heavily on imports from China, making it vulnerable to shifting trade policies and evolving tariffs. Additionally, it depends on third-party technology and fulfillment services to maintain its digital guest experience, adding a layer of logistical complexity.

Walmart must manage the high costs and uncertain returns of its heavy investments in artificial intelligence and automation tools. The retailer faces complex regulatory risks, including ongoing litigation over labor practices, product safety, and pharmacy dispensing. Macroeconomic factors such as currency fluctuations and geopolitical instability also affect its international operations across the 19 countries where it maintains a presence.

Valuation comparison

Target looks cheaper using its Forward P/E , based on future earnings estimates, and its P/S ratio measuring sales over the past twelve months.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

When comparing Target and Walmart, investors should consider a few key factors. Let's have a look at them and see what that tells us about each stock.

Firstly, we should consider revenue growth. Walmart has delivered higher average year-over-year revenue growth over the past three years at 5.3%, while Target's rate has been 1%. Yet in recent quarters, Target has not only closed the gap but also surpassed Walmart. In Target's most recent quarter, revenue growth surged to 7.1%, while Walmart's dipped slightly to 5.2%.

Another factor to consider is each company's profitability. Both companies have relatively thin margins given their enormous revenue bases. However, Target has a slightly higher operating margin of 6.3%, while Walmart's is 4.5%. That gives Target a small but durable edge in profitability.

Lastly, there's valuation. Both companies have been consistently profitable, so we'll examine their respective price-to-earnings (P/E) multiples. Walmart has a P/E ratio of 49.6x, while Target's is 15.6x, making it far more affordable than Walmart. That gives Target stock a key advantage in the overall matchup.

To sum up, both of these consumer stocks have their strengths. Both exhibit solid revenue growth and consistent profitability. However, valuation tips the scales in Target's favor, in my view.

news.Title: Is Intel a Buy After Its 14.1% Drop in 1 Week as Recovery Risks Mount?
news.Content:
Intel Corporation INTC shares fell 14.1% in the week through Nov. 23, 2026. The semiconductor industry declined 16.7%, while the S&P 500 lost 2.4%, putting Intel's weakness within a broader selloff.

The decline raises an investment question as server demand improves but near-term earnings face pressure. A lower share price alone does not establish a bargain when manufacturing constraints and a PC correction complicate the recovery.

Intel Faces a Sharp Near-Term Earnings Reset

Intel's October outlook called for fourth-quarter 2026 revenues of $15 billion to $16 billion and adjusted earnings of 25 cents per share. Non-GAAP gross margin was projected at 38%, underscoring the difficulty of sustaining recent profitability. Third-quarter adjusted earnings were 52 cents per share, making the outlook a reminder that the recovery remains uneven.

Management expected Client Computing and Physical AI Group revenues to decline more than 20% sequentially as customers reduced inventories. Memory shortages and higher component prices were constraining PC purchases, creating a tangible obstacle to an immediate earnings rebound.

INTC Server Growth Offers a Counterweight

Data Center and AI revenues reached $7.32 billion in the third quarter, rising 77.8% year over year. Its 41.5% operating margin demonstrates how additional server shipments can strengthen profitability as infrastructure customers expand capacity.

Competition remains active. Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. AMD announced sixth-generation EPYC server processor availability in November. NVIDIA Corporation NVDA began shipping Vera Rubin systems, extending customers' infrastructure choices as Intel works to rebuild its position.

Intel Must Convert Demand Into Deliveries

An October accident at Fab 28 in Israel complicated Intel's ability to serve demand. The initial fourth-quarter outlook incorporated roughly $300 million of lost revenues and a 200-basis-point gross margin impact, primarily involving 10nm server products.

The problem extends beyond one factory. Management expected industry supply constraints throughout 2027 and into 2028, while shortages of advanced organic substrates limited packaging output. Better demand therefore needs reliable production before it becomes additional sales.

INTC Still Lacks a Clear Valuation Cushion

As of Nov. 23, Intel traded at 4.7X forward 12-month sales, compared with 4.2X for its semiconductor sub-industry. The multiple also exceeded its five-year median of 2.5X, limiting valuation support if the recovery disappoints.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for current-year earnings had increased 1.1% in the past month. That improvement offers an offset to operating uncertainty, but the sales premium still requires sustained progress rather than a rebound in sentiment alone.

Story Continues

Intel Signals Favor Patience After the Decline

Intel's decline leaves investors weighing server growth against an uneven delivery and earnings outlook. Existing holders have operating improvements to monitor, while prospective buyers may prefer clearer evidence that supply and client demand are stabilizing.

Intel carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), with a Growth Score of A, Momentum Score of B and VGM Score of B. Its Value Score of F signals weaker valuation appeal. The favorable scores complement the neutral ranking signal without establishing that the selloff has created an attractive entry.
