news.Title: The S&P 500 Just Had Its Worst Week of 2026. Here's Why I'm Still Investing.
news.Content:
Last week was rough for pretty much anyone with a brokerage account. The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) dropped sharply, finishing the week down 8.57% from the previous Friday's close. That officially put the index into correction territory, down 11.5% from its record high in early October.

Although weeks like that are stomach-churning for investors, I'm definitely not pulling my money out of the market. Here's why I'm still investing, even after the S&P 500's worst week of 2026.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

It wasn't a normal week

Last week was an abnormal one, with several high-profile market shocks landing one after another.

Right before the market closed on Friday the 13th, the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop to all U.S. flights. The stop lasted four hours, but the repercussions echoed throughout the air travel system for days.

Other service outages to Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) Outlook and Teams, and to the Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) Store and Apple Music, led to fears that these incidents were connected and potentially related to faulty artificial intelligence (AI) or cybersecurity breaches.

Next, there was fallout from Nvidia 's (NASDAQ:NVDA) Q3 earnings report on Tuesday, which was delivered after CEO Jensen Huang's resignation (and before his Monday reinstatement). On Wednesday, Alaska's Senate race was called for Democrat Mary Peltola, reigniting concerns about how a Democratic-controlled legislature might regulate AI and data centers. That was followed by the largest IPO of all time, as major AI player Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT), the developer of the Claude AI model, began trading on the NASDAQ on Thursday.

That's a lot to digest all at once, especially given how much the S&P 500 has relied on AI spending for its recent gains.

10% drops are normal

Remember, a market correction isn't a bear market, and it isn't a recession forecast either.

Corrections -- in which an index drops more than 10% from its high -- are a normal (if uncomfortable) part of investing. Bear markets are relatively few and far between, but there have been plenty of market corrections that have reversed themselves before ushering in a prolonged downturn.

The other good news for investors is that a market correction -- in which quality stocks get punished alongside shaky ones -- can be an excellent buying opportunity.

Story Continues

Be on the lookout

After last week's market correction, it looks to me like more of the fear and risk around AI spending and deployment is baked into the market right now than before. That doesn't mean prices can't fall further, but it does mean there's more upside in some great companies now trading at more attractive prices.

It might be different if the concerning events of last week showed signs of persisting, but as I write this on Monday, Nov. 23, flights are taking off and landing as normal, Microsoft Outlook and Apple Music are both functioning, and Nvidia's stock is soaring.

So I'm checking my shopping list to see if there are any businesses that look too compelling to ignore, and you may want to do the same.

Last week was scary, but it may turn out to be a gift for patient, long-term investors.

news.Title: If I Had to Start Investing Again With $10,000, These 3 Dividend Stocks Would Come First
news.Content:
Picture a blank brokerage account and a fresh $10,000. The temptation might be to invest in whatever trend or industry is loudest this week, but tactics like those are how many beginners get burned. I'd do the opposite and look for investment themes that benefit from more basic ideas — what people spend money on when they're stressed, celebrating, or hungry.

I'd also lean on dividend payers in those areas. Checks that show up reliably whether a stock is up or down make it easier to sit still, and if you use a dividend reinvestment plan , you can use those payouts to boost the compound growth of your assets.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

1. Dollar General: The shop around the corner

Dollar General (NYSE:DG) is where cash-strapped families shop when budgets get tight, and CEO Todd Vasos is blunt about that.

"Our core customers continue to be financially constrained with a variety of factors impacting their budget," he said on the August earnings call. Yet traffic grew for a fifth straight quarter, and "we were especially pleased to see our share gains accelerate."

The company says about 75% of Americans live within five miles of one of its more than 21,000 stores. That's a footprint and level of accessibility that would be tough to replicate.

What I like most is that shoppers outside of its core demographics are broadening their horizons. Dollar General says more customers with household incomes above $100,000 are switching to the chain for value. It's also leaning on more than 2,000 items priced at or below $1, and it plans to restart share buybacks this quarter.

Here's the part to be honest about. Management has held the dividend steady at $0.59 per quarter for more than three years, and at the current share price, it yields about 1.8%, so this is a stability pick, not an income pick. High fuel prices are also squeezing its shoppers, and the tariff refunds the company got back after the Supreme Court struck down President Donald Trump's tariffs helped this quarter's profits. But those refunds will not buoy its numbers for long.

2. Ralph Lauren: Style that doesn't go out of style

I know, a polo shirt company on an income-stock list sounds odd. Ralph Lauren (NYSE:RL) has spent years making its brand harder to discount, and it's working.

Story Continues

On Nov. 5, it raised its full-year outlook again, with revenue in its fiscal 2027 Q2 up 10% in constant currency, sales in Asia up 28%, and 1.7 million new direct-to-consumer customers. "We delivered strong second-quarter performance, enabling us to raise our fiscal 2027 outlook once again," CEO Patrice Louvet said.

The edge is loyalty.

"We have, I believe we can say, the most loyal customer in the industry," Louvet told analysts. Shoppers are paying full price too, with average unit retail up 9%. That's a sign of a company with real economic moat power, not just one attracting customers with discounts.

The trade-off is that this is the least dividend-heavy name of the three, with a yield of about 1%. Sales in Europe are soft, with comparable store sales down 1%, and management is planning for U.S. tariff rates to climb back into the high teens in its fiscal fourth quarter.

3. Tyson Foods: Protein is the plan

Tyson Foods (NYSE:TSN) is the messy one, and that's why it's useful. Its beef business is losing money amid tight cattle supply, and Tyson expects fiscal 2027 beef operating income to be between a loss of $300 million and a profit of $100 million. Its chief operating officer called it plainly: "The challenges in our Beef segment are a cattle cycle issue, not a broad deterioration in the business."

Meanwhile, the rest of the company is carrying its weight. Chicken earned $1.9 billion in a year when prices fell, and the prepared foods segment, home of Jimmy Dean and Hillshire Farm, grew operating income by 5.5% to $1.3 billion. New CEO Jeff Schomburger has an easy pitch: "Selling more protein is fun." He also admits, "Our innovation success rate is not where it needs to be."

The board still raised the quarterly dividend to $0.52 per Class A share, the company's 15th straight annual increase. That works out to about a 3.1% dividend yield at the current share price, the highest of my three. Adjusted earnings per share fell 17% in fiscal 2026 to $3.44, and the CFO warned that chicken and pork headwinds "could outweigh the controllable improvements."

My investing strategy

If I were starting over, I wouldn't try to be clever. I'd begin building my portfolio around a store people need, a brand people love, and a food company people can't stop eating, and I'd let the dividends keep arriving while I learned. A good buy-and-hold strategy is mostly patience, and each of these investments gives you something to be patient about: a growing store base, a pricing-power brand, and a dividend streak that has survived a rough beef cycle.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

news.Title: 台股救市18套劇本再添一招？ 金管會：檢討處置股制度
news.Content:
台股救市還有新招？金管會指出，證交所27日將召開專家會議，檢討處置股方式、標準及時間三大面向，包括市場劇烈波動時，預收款券能否彈性放寬、暫時甚至全面取消，都可納入討論。

工商協進會理事長吳東亮23日在行政院召集的產金界座談中指出，現行處置股預收款項制度，在股市下跌時可能阻礙買盤，建議研議在市場波動度高時，暫時放寬相關規定。

證期局副局長黃仲豪說，公布注意或處置股票，主要是提醒投資人注意交易風險，但近期股市急跌，不少個股被列為注意或處置股票，預收款項可能影響投資人進場意願，因此業界提出調整建議。

處置股票主要有兩種手段，一是拉長撮合時間，二是預收款券。

黃仲豪指出，預收款券是為防止違約交割，若在特殊市場情況下放寬，適用條件如何訂定、是否彈性或暫時取消，都須徵詢各界意見。

事實上，處置股制度今年8月才進行一波改革。8月10日起，處置期間由10個營業日縮短至5日、當沖異常者為7日，撮合間隔也從5或20分鐘縮短至原則上2分鐘，並放寬高價股注意交易標準。

上次改革著重提升交易效率，這次業界則將焦點轉向預收款券，盼降低買盤進場的資金障礙。

黃仲豪說，先前推出處置股新制時，就規劃每半年檢討一次，證交所將於27日邀集專家，討論處置方式、標準與時間，吳東亮的建議也將一併納入。

至於新措施何時上路？黃仲豪表示，須視專家會議結論、相關配套及交易所規章修正而定，若涉及券商系統調整，也須考量所需時間，目前尚無時間表。

news.Title: Nvidia's Huang returns to cheers in China, but political hurdles mount
news.Content:
By Eduardo Baptista and Xiuyuan Ning

BEIJING, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO restores one of the most influential advocates for technology ties between the United States and China, but he returns to a more restrictive business ‌environment, with political pressure mounting on both sides.

Even as Chinese investors welcomed Huang's reinstatement on Monday following intervention by US President ‌Donald Trump, Washington tightened its grip on China's access to advanced American chips and Chinese state-backed media renewed calls for technological self-reliance.

Few American executives enjoy Huang's popularity in ​China. During a visit to Beijing in July last year, the Taiwan-born billionaire posed for selfies with fans and signed leather jackets. He wore traditional Chinese-style attire at a trade expo and praised Chinese technology companies, including Nvidia rival Huawei.

Huang's reinstatement and the reasons behind it were among the top trending topics on Chinese social media platform Weibo on Tuesday.

Chinese American billionaire investor Duan Yongping, founder of electronics conglomerate BBK and a long-time ‌Apple shareholder, also welcomed the news.

"I'm very happy ⁠that Jensen is coming back," Duan wrote on Chinese investment platform Xueqiu.

Lian Jye Su, chief analyst at Omdia, said Tuesday's rally in Asian technology shares demonstrated Huang's importance to the global AI industry and his ability ⁠to connect increasingly divided Chinese and Western economies.

But Chinese stocks lagged the global rally as investors bet the bridging role he played between China and the US had diminished.

China's state-backed Global Times newspaper cautioned in an editorial on Tuesday against interpreting Huang's return as a sign Washington would ease chip restrictions, ​stressing ​the need for China to strengthen semiconductor self-reliance.

NARROWING ROOM FOR MANOEUVRE

Huang was only ​gone for 11 days, after resigning on November 12 ‌following revelations of extramarital affairs including one with an alleged spy for Beijing, Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang.

But Huang returns to a far more restrictive business environment.

On Monday, Washington added Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed, which Alice Huang formerly led and controlled, and a Singapore subsidiary of Chinese technology group Alibaba to its trade blacklist.

The move followed a Commerce Department rule issued last week that requires US export licences for advanced chip shipments to Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil.

Story Continues

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer vowed on Monday to investigate Huang, other Nvidia executives and ‌the Trump administration when Democrats take control of Congress in January.

Huang faces an ​early test of his political influence on December 3, when he is due to ​testify before the Senate Banking Committee at a hearing on ​US export controls.

There have been changes at Nvidia too. The company said last week it had stopped shipping ‌previously licensed AI chips to China, after generating $2.4 billion ​in sales of such products in ​its latest quarter.

The company also established a committee of independent directors to oversee export-control compliance and national security risks.

Alfredo Montufar-Helu, Beijing-based managing director at Ankura Consulting, said Huang's popularity among ordinary Chinese people and access to both countries' leadership made his return ​positive for bilateral relations.

But an incoming Congress critical ‌of Trump's trade truce with Beijing was likely to push for tighter chip restrictions, he said.

"That heightened scrutiny will complicate ​business for US tech firms in China and ultimately constrain the bridging role Huang can play."

(Reporting by Eduardo Baptista ​and Xiuyuan Ning in Beijing; Editing by Josephine Mason and Emelia Sithole-Matarise)

news.Title: Jensen 2.0
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Jensen Huang is getting a second chance. And judging by his first day back at Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), he knows he has something to prove.

Our AI stock portfolio is beating the S&P 500 by 118%. Discover the stocks we're buying and the opportunities we're watching next. Exclusive for Yahoo! Finance readers: 55% off for Black Friday, plus an extra 15% at checkout. Subscribe today! »

On Monday, following his surprise reinstatement as CEO by the board, Huang returned to Nvidia's offices for the first time, greeted by hundreds of employees packed into the lobby.

"This is my first day of work. I don't have a computer, so the IT department is going to give me a new PC. I'm hoping it's an RTX Spark," he joked.

But the humor quickly gave way to something more personal.

"I want to thank all of you. I'm terribly sorry for putting all of you through all of this. I've made some very terrible mistakes, and I'm going to work on coming back."

An employee rushed forward to hug him as the crowd erupted into chants of "Jensen! Jensen! Jensen!"

"Thank you all for the second chance," Huang said. "I'm going to be a better CEO the second time around."

It was quite a moment. But the circumstances behind his return are anything but ordinary.

President Trump revealed yesterday that he had lobbied Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang, who had been under pressure to step down after multiple alleged affairs came to light, including one involving a possible Chinese spy and another with a direct report.

Trump's message was straightforward: We have to protect our geniuses.

Stop chasing stocks after they've already rallied. Find your next investment opportunity with AI stock picks, earnings insights, and market-moving news. Yahoo! Finance readers get an extra 15% off on top of the 55% off Black Friday price. Join today! »

That may explain why Huang is back, but it doesn't necessarily erase the concerns surrounding his leadership.

Beyond the personal scandals, reports from The New York Times and court records have painted a picture of an extraordinarily demanding, sometimes abusive boss. Huang was reportedly known to berate employees publicly, with witnesses describing deeply disturbing personal insults and threats. Among the alleged comments: telling an executive that his mother should have aborted him, threatening to rip a subordinate's arms off and beat them to death with them, and telling another he would remove the top of their head and "pee on your brain."

Not exactly the image of a modern, people-first CEO.

Story Continues

And perhaps that's precisely what Jensen 2.0 is meant to address.

Even his wardrobe offered a subtle clue. Huang, famous for his trademark black leather jacket, skipped it for his first public appearance back, opting instead for a more casual cotton-poly blend jacket.

A small detail? Perhaps. But image matters, particularly when you're trying to reset the narrative.

The message seems clear: a more approachable Jensen, a more relaxed leadership style, and perhaps a greater emphasis on family, relationships and the people who make Nvidia successful.

Wall Street certainly welcomed his return. Nvidia shares surged 31.5% on Monday following the news, reflecting investor enthusiasm and the importance of leadership stability at one of the world's most valuable technology companies. On Tuesday, however, the stock was taking a breather, falling 5.7% in premarket trading. Despite Monday's rally, shares remain down for the year and significantly below levels seen before the controversy erupted.

The real test for Jensen 2.0 won't be a new jacket, an emotional speech or a standing ovation from employees.

It will be whether he can change the way he leads, rebuild trust and prove that being a genius doesn't give you a free pass to treat people badly.

Nvidia may have given him a second chance. Now he has to earn it.

news.Title: MP vs. USAR: Which Rare-Earth Stock Has an Edge Right Now?
news.Content:
MP Materials MP and USA Rare Earth, Inc. USAR are U.S.-listed rare-earth companies seeking to strengthen domestic supply chains and reduce dependence on China. While MP Materials has established mining, processing and magnet manufacturing operations, USA Rare Earth is building an integrated mine-to-magnet business, with an emphasis on expanding heavy rare-earth production.

This presents an interesting comparison between an established producer scaling its downstream operations and an emerging player investing heavily to establish its presence across the supply chain.

The Case for MP Materials

MP Materials operates the Mountain Pass mine and processing facility, producing refined rare-earth products, concentrates and related materials. It also owns the Independence facility in Fort Worth, TX, where it manufactures magnetic precursor products and began producing permanent magnets in December 2025. Supported by government incentives, the company is constructing the second domestic magnet manufacturing facility (the 10X Facility) in Northlake, TX, which will lift its total U.S. magnet capacity to 10,000 metric tons.

MP has been making progress in expanding its rare earth production. Neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr) production increased 41% year over year to 1,018 metric tons in the third quarter of 2026. Sales volumes rose 94% to 1,020 metric tons.

The Materials segment revenues rose 322% year over year to $133.5 million. NdPr oxide and metal revenues increased 226.6% to $100.96 million. Other revenues included $31.6 million from the sale of SEG+, a mixed product containing samarium, europium, gadolinium and other heavy rare earths, to an aerospace and defense customer.

The Magnetics segment revenues decreased 15% year over year to $18.6 million. The allocation of manufacturing costs toward magnet production reduced precursor revenues under existing pricing arrangements.

MP's total revenues increased 175.7% year over year to $147.7 million. MP also recorded $8.11 million in income tied to a price protection agreement (PPA) with the Department of War (DoW).

For the fourth quarter of 2026, management expects approximately 1,000 metric tons of NdPr sales at realized oxide pricing near $100 per kilogram. Expected PPA income is about $8 per kilogram on sold NdPr, with none anticipated on NdPr contained in stockpiled concentrate.

The company remains on track to begin producing terbium (Tb) and dysprosium (Dy) in the fourth quarter of 2026, with initial samarium production targeted for 2028.

Story Continues

On the downstream front, MP is making progress in commercializing its magnet operations. During the third quarter, the company completed the magnet qualification process with General Motors Company GM, with saleable magnet deliveries and associated revenues expected to commence in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Magnet volumes are expected to increase more substantially in the second half of 2027, including deliveries to Apple Inc. AAPL. Management anticipates modest overall Magnetics adjusted EBITDA in 2027, followed by a fuller contribution in 2028.

Additionally, Project Swarm, an initiative developed with U.S. and allied drone manufacturers, aims to aggregate and standardize future magnet demand. MP has already secured subscription agreements with several participants.

However, rising costs remain a concern. Cost of sales increased 76.6% year over year in the third quarter, while selling, general and administrative expenses climbed 33.8%. Start-up costs also surged to $14.15 million from $1.41 million in the year-ago quarter. Further cost pressures are likely as MP scales its manufacturing operations.

Thus, while government support, higher production and downstream integration provide significant growth opportunities, MP still needs to demonstrate that its expanding operations can translate into sustainable profitability.

The Case for USA Rare Earth

USA Rare Earth is developing an integrated supply chain spanning mineral extraction, separation, metal and alloy production, and neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) permanent magnets. The company has accelerated this strategy through acquisitions and investments aimed at expanding its upstream and downstream capabilities.

In November 2025, USAR acquired Less Common Metals, a manufacturer of rare-earth metals and alloys. In August 2026, it completed the acquisition of Texas Mineral Resources, securing full economic ownership of the Round Top project in Texas. It also completed the acquisition of Serra Verde in September 2026, adding the Pela Ema operation in Brazil. Serra Verde is the only scaled producer outside Asia of all four key rare earths used in NdFeB magnets — neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium — along with yttrium and other critical heavy rare earth elements. USAR has also agreed to acquire a minority interest in French separation specialist Carester, although the transaction remains pending.

In September 2026, Serra Verde's mining and processing operation in Goiás, Brazil, successfully completed Stage 1 of its optimization and commissioning program. Commercial-scale shipments to its offtake customer began in October, with sales recorded in November.

The Stage 1 expansion is now ramping up toward 4,000 metric tons per annum (tpa) of total rare earth oxide (TREO) capacity. Stage 2 is expected to add another 2,400 tpa by the end of 2027, with construction completion and commissioning targeted for the third quarter of 2027. Serra Verde expects to sell at least 325 tons of total rare earth oxide content in the fourth quarter of 2026.

In October 2026, USAR achieved first production and delivered yttrium oxide samples to a major integrated defense, medical and specialty coatings company. This milestone strengthens USAR's position in the yttrium supply chain, an area where capabilities outside China remain limited.

USAR is also advancing its domestic magnet manufacturing operations. In September 2026, USAR sold the first NdFeB magnets produced at its 600-tpa facility in Stillwater, OK. The company has installed its first magnet finishing line at the facility, with a second line expected by the end of 2026 to broaden its product offering.

USAR broke ground in September 2026 on a new rare-earth metal and magnet manufacturing facility in Blacksburg, SC.

To finance its ambitious expansion plans, USAR has strengthened its balance sheet through equity financing, government support and acquisitions. A January 2026 private placement raised $1.5 billion in gross proceeds. As of September 2026, unrestricted cash and cash equivalents totaled $1.09 billion. Definitive agreements with the Commerce Department also provide for up to $277 million in direct awards and guarantees supporting up to $1.3 billion in borrowing, with disbursements linked to project milestones.

Despite these operational milestones, USAR's financial performance remains weak. Third-quarter 2026 revenues were $3 million compared with no revenues in the year-ago quarter. Less Common Metals contributed $2.8 million, while magnet operations generated $0.2 million.

However, cost of revenues reached $22.9 million, resulting in a gross loss of $19.9 million. The loss primarily reflected non-inventoriable labor and material costs associated with initial magnet production and mining activities, as well as an inventory adjustment at the metal-making facility. Gross margin was further affected by under-absorption of labor and overhead costs due to raw material supply constraints and higher input costs at Less Common Metals.

Operating expenses surged to $121.6 million from $15.9 million in the prior-year quarter. Higher headcount, acquisition-related activity and legal expenses contributed to the increase, while research and development costs rose with Round Top drilling and the addition of Serra Verde. Consulting and legal expenses also increased primarily due to acquisitions.

Consequently, USAR reported an adjusted third-quarter 2026 loss of 44 cents per share, wider than the loss of 25 cents in the year-ago quarter.

How Does the Zacks Consensus Estimate Compare for MP & USAR?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MP Material's 2026 revenues currently stands at $466.4 million, suggesting year-over-year growth of 108%. The consensus mark for 2027 suggests growth of 44.1%.

The estimate for USA Rare Earth's 2026 revenues is $51.57 million, indicating significant growth from $1.64 million in 2025. The estimate for 2027 revenues is $303.7 million, suggesting growth of 489%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MP's earnings for 2026 is currently at a loss of 4 cents per share, which is narrower than the loss of 24 cents in 2025. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings for 2027 is pegged at 59 cents per share.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for USAR's 2026 bottom line is pegged at a loss of $1.14 per share. The company's consensus estimate for earnings for 2027 is also pegged at a loss of $1.79 per share.

Earnings estimates for 2026 and 2027 for both MP and USAR have moved down, as shown in the chart below.

Price Performance and Valuation of MP & USAR

In the past six months, MP shares have fallen 44.8%, while USAR stock declined 72.2%.

MP Materials is trading at a forward price-to-sales multiple of 9.73X, while USA Rare Earth's forward sales multiple sits at 9.47X.

Final Take

MP Materials has a stronger operating foundation than USAR, supported by established mining and processing operations, rising NdPr production, government backing and growing magnet manufacturing capabilities. Its partnerships with GM and Apple also offer meaningful downstream growth opportunities. However, elevated costs, substantial expansion spending and the time required to scale magnet production continue to weigh on its near-term profitability. Moreover, downward earnings estimate revisions and a steep share-price decline temper the investment outlook. Thus, despite its long-term potential, a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) appears appropriate for MP.

USAR, meanwhile, has made considerable progress in building its mine-to-magnet platform through acquisitions, new facilities and government support. However, its commercial operations remain at an early stage, with minimal revenues, substantial gross and operating losses, and significant execution and commercialization risks. The sharp increase in expenses and downward earnings revisions further weaken its near-term outlook. With its growth ambitions yet to translate into meaningful financial results, a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) is justified for USAR.

news.Title: FORM Benefits From Rising Industry Usage of HBM: What's Ahead?
news.Content:
FormFactor Inc. FORM is benefiting from rising demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and advanced semiconductor testing as Artificial Intelligence (AI) infrastructure expands. Increasing test complexity across memory, data-center CPUs, GPUs and custom application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) is supporting growth in its Probe Cards business. Broader exposure to foundry and logic applications is also expanding the company's growth opportunities beyond memory.

Higher semiconductor test intensity across advanced packaging, high-performance compute and photonics is a major growth driver for FORM. Expanding GPU and custom ASIC programs broaden its opportunity beyond memory, while HBM testing remains a key driver. FormFactor differentiates itself in HBM final stack testing through its SmartMatrix DRAM architecture, delivering high-speed test performance, productivity and parallelism. Looking ahead, management sees strong momentum across HBM4, HBM4E and HBM5.

Supported by partnerships with Teradyne and Advantest, and upcoming capacity relief at Livermore as Foundry & Logic ramps in Farmers Branch, TX, FormFactor is well-positioned to scale alongside HBM demand. For FormFactor, advanced packaging continues to raise test complexity in DRAM, particularly as HBM evolves toward faster interfaces. FORM's third-quarter 2026 DRAM revenues held near the second-quarter record at $84.9 million despite a shift from HBM to DDR5. FormFactor's SmartMatrix technology supports testing of completed HBM4 stacks at speeds above 10 gigabits per second.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, FormFactor expects revenues of $285 million, plus or minus $10 million, reflecting continued broad-based demand. Non-GAAP earnings are expected to be 95 cents per share, plus or minus nine cents. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for FORM's fourth-quarter 2026 earnings shows year-over-year growth of 100%. news.Title: US stocks set to slide as Nvidia rally fizzles out
news.Content:
By Sruthi Shankar

Nov 24 (Reuters) - US stocks were set to tumble on Tuesday as the early euphoria after Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia faded, with investors cautious about further AI-driven gains and US inflation data.

Nvidia's shares dropped nearly 5% in US premarket trading, having ‌soared 31.5% on Monday after the AI chip giant reinstated Huang as CEO under pressure from US President Donald Trump.

Nasdaq futures fell 2.2% after ‌the tech-heavy index climbed by nearly 7% the previous day. Anthropic briefly fell below its IPO price of $83, a striking drop only days after the Claude developer's record-breaking market debut. [.N]

The pan-European STOXX 600 ​index dropped 0.6%, weighed down by a sharp slump in miners. [.EU]

AI WHIRLWIND

Huang's comeback capped a whirlwind week of events that whipped markets and tore through the AI ecosystem, which has relied on Nvidia for everything from supplying chips to bankrolling the industry's massive buildout. But it also left unanswered questions over Huang, who had resigned after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

"With Jensen's return, it assures people massively and gives hope that the data centre construction continues and ‌that boosts US GDP," said Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at ⁠IG Group in London.

"But it then opens up a whole list of questions that may not be answered very quickly. What did he know? What else did he do? How much went to China? And these questions will continue to chip ⁠away at market confidence."

Nvidia shares marked their biggest daily percentage gain in 23 years on Monday and restored nearly $1 trillion in value to the company, though the stock remains about 30% below its record highs in October.

Asian stocks rallied sharply, echoing a strong overnight session on Wall Street, on expectations that Huang's return as CEO would dispel uncertainty ​over ​product plans and the risk of scaling back investments in AI startups.

"By the end of ​the day, these businesses need to make enough money to ‌justify investors' expectations. My point is: Jensen's return does not solve this. So the sentiment is more emotional than sensible, in my opinion," Glenn Yin, director of research at online trading platform ACCM, told the Reuters Global Markets Forum.

Chinese shares were an exception to the relief rally, making only small gains owing to concerns that tighter curbs on exports of US chips are in the works.

DOLLAR AND BONDS AWAIT INFLATION DATA

Investors are set to focus on Wednesday's PCE Index data, the last key data set ahead of the Federal Reserve's final meeting of 2026 in December.

Story Continues

New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said late on Monday that persistently ‌high inflation continues to point the US central bank towards tighter monetary policy, while ​emphasising that the pace of future increases to interest rates will depend on incoming economic data.

Fed ​funds futures traders are now pricing in an increase at the ​US central bank's December meeting as a certainty, compared with 89% odds on Friday, when stocks tumbled, CME Group's FedWatch tool shows. ‌However, the market-implied chance of a supersized increase of 50 basis ​points was wiped out by Tuesday ​morning.

The dollar retreated by 0.4% against a basket of major currencies, easing from a 20-month high touched earlier in the session. The yield on the benchmark US 2-year Treasury note dipped and was last at 4.6415%, while the yield on the 10-year note edged down to 4.8919%. [US/]

Brent crude futures ​firmed to $89.61 a barrel but remained near a three-month low touched ‌earlier in the session on rising Middle East supplies. [O/R]

Spot gold lost 0.4% to $3,626.40 an ounce while copper, a key material in data-centre infrastructure, retreated ​3% after jumping 5% on Monday. [GOL/] [MET/L]

(Reporting by Jiaxing Li in Hong Kong and Sruthi Shankar in BengaluruAdditional reporting by Summer Zhen in ​Hong Kong and Ankika Biswas in BengaluruEditing by Susan Fenton and David Goodman)

news.Title: 黃仁勳回歸台股噴3310點！會漲到哪？杜金龍曝1操作關鍵：挑這類股
news.Content:
輝達（NVIDIA）執行長黃仁勳重返全球科技舞台，瞬間為市場注入強心針，激勵台股今（24）日上演戲劇性V轉行情，終場暴漲3,310.46點、漲幅高達8.99%，強勢收復四萬點大關，收在40,122.35點，成交金額4,194.05億元。面對大盤狂飆，有 「股市老先覺」之稱的資深分析師杜金龍 指出，日前大盤跌破年線僅短短三天便強勢收復，屬於 標準的「假跌破」 ， 本波短線反彈先看4萬4千點附近 ；他也大方公開1項關鍵操作策略，直言搶反彈要挑先前重挫的「跌深族群」，部分跌深個股的反彈幅度有機會挑戰5成。

【黃仁勳回歸引爆V轉 杜金龍揭「假跌破」看4萬4】

前陣子台股自高點一路修正逾1萬4千5百點、波段跌幅高達29%，無數投資人在年線失守的恐懼中徹夜難眠。然而隨著黃仁勳重掌兵符消息傳出，台股迅速展開強勁V轉。杜金龍剖析，本波大盤回測年線下方扣抵區間，但短短三天便強勢站回，技術面上已確立為「假跌破」。目前短線已彈升修正幅度的三分之一， 預計本波反彈將挑戰二分之一位置（約4萬4千點附近）並進行整理 ；放眼長線，多頭主升段目標仍維持上看5萬至5萬3千點，展現對台股基本面的深厚信心。

【搶反彈別追權值股？老手：跌深PCB、載板彈幅看5成】

針對搶反彈的選股關鍵，杜金龍點出，先前 因市場過度疑慮AI供應鏈而遭錯殺、股價重挫6至7成的族群，將是本波最具爆發力的殺手鐧。 包括PCB、CCL、ABF載板（如欣興）以及ASIC與DRAM等龍頭個股，先前遭受市場嚴重超跌，在黃仁勳效應重回正軌與投信年底作帳雙重加持下，短線強烈反彈幅度預計上看50%。反觀台積電（2330）、聯發科（2454）、鴻海（2317）等大型權值股，因先前有國安基金護盤、跌幅較小，在短線反彈1至3根漲停後空間相對有限，呈現「抗跌但也抗漲」的特性。

【曝99.9%滿倉心聲 杜金龍公開操盤密碼：逢高停利】

「上半年賺的錢，下半年差點白忙一場！」杜金龍感性坦言，面對大盤動輒數千點的劇烈洗盤，即便是市場老手也承受沉重壓力。他透露自己上週五持股一度高達99.9%，但隨著指數強勢反彈衝高，他選擇不盲目追高，而是採取 「逢高停利、分批打包減碼」 的彈性操盤法，逐步回收現金、降低持股水位以應對後續震盪。杜金龍提醒，積極型投資人可鎖定跌深龍頭股來回操作，但務必嚴守紀律、適時落袋為安，才能將帳面獲利轉化為口袋裡最真實的財富。

news.Title: SNDK's Data Center Revenues Gain Momentum on AI Demand: What's Ahead?
news.Content:
SanDisk 's SNDK Data Center revenues are surging as Artificial Intelligence reshapes memory economics and storage demand. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Data Center revenues reached $4.802 billion, rising 61% sequentially from $2.977 billion in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 and jumping 1,682% from $269 million in the first quarter of fiscal 2026.

The expansion of the data center business surged total company revenues to $11.031 billion, up 23% quarter over quarter and 378% year over year, alongside an 85.1% non-GAAP gross margin. A primary catalyst is AI inference. As models process longer prompts, multimodal inputs and persistent context, growing Key-Value (KV) caches require high-capacity storage that retains context without costly recomputation.

Management noted that SSD-equipped systems delivered roughly 3x token throughput and approximately 75% lower energy use than volatile-memory-only setups in AI lab comparisons, and projected KV cache could represent about one-third of the AI data center flash market by decade-end.

Product execution and supply allocation reinforce this momentum. SanDisk directed more supply toward data centers in the first quarter and paired its BiCS8 CMOS Directly Bonded to Array (CBA) technology, ramping across TLC and QLC, including its QLC product with future roadmap investments like BiCS9, BiCS10, and High Bandwidth Flash (HBF), which completed its first die tape-out in the first quarter.

Simultaneously, pricing and volume both contributed to sequential company growth—roughly 60% from volume and 40% from pricing. Furthermore, SNDK's New Business Model (NBM) long-term agreements expanded visibility. Structurally, management estimates data centers have risen from approximately 20% of industry NAND bits early in the decade to roughly half today, with bit demand projected to grow approximately 40% year over year in calendar 2027.

How do Competitors Fare Against SNDK?

SanDisk faces stiff competition from Seagate Technologies STX and Micron Technology MU. Seagate is benefiting from increasing data creation, retention and reuse across cloud and enterprise environments. AI inference and agentic applications require persistent historical context, reinforcing the role of cost-efficient HDDs in tiered storage architectures.

Seagate's Data Center revenues rose 63% year over year to $3.45 billion in first-quarter fiscal 2027. Micron's fiscal 2026 results show how AI infrastructure is reshaping memory and storage demand. Fourth-quarter revenues reached $54.23 billion, up 31% sequentially and 379% year over year, while non-GAAP EPS was $33.42. Full-year revenues rose 256% to $133.19 billion.

news.Title: Micron Stock Soared on Monday. I'd Still Buy It, a Little at a Time.
news.Content:
Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) ended last week at $594.51 a share, its lowest close since early May. On Monday, Nov. 23, the shares jumped about 19%, to roughly $710 as I write.

But the memory maker still sits about 41% below its all-time closing high of $1,213.56, hit on June 25.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Micron itself didn't announce anything on Monday. The move came the day Nvidia said it had brought Jensen Huang back as CEO, less than two weeks after he stepped down, and Nvidia's shares surged over 30% as I write. Micron sells memory to artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. It's also co-designing a custom high-bandwidth memory chip (stacked memory that sits beside AI processors) with Nvidia. Its shares seem to have climbed right along with Nvidia's.

I think Micron is still a buy after a day like that, and the company's own forecast is a big reason why.

Image source: Micron.

Micron's earnings are still rising

Nothing about Micron's business changed between Friday and Monday. And that business is still growing fast.

Showing how quickly profits have climbed, Micron's non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share were $33.42 in the three months ending Sept. 3, its fiscal fourth quarter. That was up 33% from fiscal Q3, when earnings per share had already more than doubled from the quarter before. It was also up more than tenfold year over year, from $3.03. For fiscal Q1 of 2027, management forecast $38.15 per share, a 14% sequential gain, and Micron's Dec. 17 report should show if it got there. Revenue is on a similar path, from $54.2 billion in fiscal Q4 to a guided $61.5 billion in fiscal Q1.

Every step up is smaller than the last. But it's still a step up.

Management also expects revenue to rise sequentially in every quarter of fiscal 2027, and it called fiscal Q1 the floor for its gross margin this fiscal year. In other words, Micron sees the current quarter as its weakest of the year, not the start of a slide. By late September, customers had already committed to over 75% of Micron's planned fiscal 2027 shipments, management says.

The stock still prices in a sharp fall

Even after Monday's rally, Micron looks cheap on these earnings.

Say Micron's growth stopped completely, and every quarter of fiscal 2027 only matched the guided $38.15. That would come to around $153 a share for the full year -- well under the $177 or so that analysts expect for fiscal 2027, on average. Even at this no-growth level, a $710 share price works out to less than 5 times earnings.

Story Continues

On the analysts' number, the price-to-earnings ratio is around 4. And on fiscal 2026's adjusted earnings of $75.52 a share, the stock trades at around 9 times earnings.

At these prices, investors arguably expect Micron's profits to drop sharply within a year or two, as they have in past memory downturns.

Sure, it might happen. In fiscal 2023, during the latest memory downturn, Micron's revenue dropped by around half, and it lost about $5.8 billion. And Micron expects to spend around $25 billion on capital expenditures in the first half of fiscal 2027 alone. Management said most of this year's rise in spending is for new plant space, which might eventually loosen supply. But for now, management expects higher revenue in every quarter of this fiscal year.

Micron also has lots of cash. It finished fiscal Q4 with net cash of $68.3 billion (a number that includes cash deposits from customers), or over 8% of its market value. And it plans to return more to shareholders starting Dec. 9, the second anniversary of its CHIPS Act agreements with the U.S. government, with the goal of eventually returning all its excess cash. That might mean bigger buybacks or dividends.

Time to buy?

I think so, even after Monday. Micron trades at under 5 times the earnings it would make if its profits just stopped growing, and management expects them to keep rising.

Still, the stock can move fast. It dropped around 14% on Friday and climbed about 19% on Monday, and swings like those could easily happen again in either direction.

That's why I'd rather buy shares over a few weeks than all at once after a 19% day. I'd also keep the position small, as one part of a portfolio spread across many stocks.

news.Title: 101點燈聲援、政府護盤台股！CNN看黃仁勳回歸：台灣沸騰 當他自己人
news.Content:
輝達（Nvidia）創辦人黃仁勳戲劇性重返執行長職位，讓他的故鄉台灣一片歡騰，也引起國際媒體關注。美國有線電視新聞網（CNN）報導，從黃仁勳請辭後台北101點燈聲援、台股重挫促使政府出手護盤，到如今網友歡慶他回歸，都反映出黃仁勳在台灣的影響力。對許多台灣人而言，這位享譽全球的科技巨擘就是「自己人」。

CNN指出，台灣不僅是黃仁勳的出生地，全球領先的科技供應鏈也與輝達建立密切合作關係，台股更受惠於黃仁勳所推動的AI熱潮。因此，黃仁勳突然恢復執行長職務的消息，讓不少台灣民眾欣喜不已。

有網友直言：「沒有黃仁勳，輝達什麼都不是。」另一名網友則表示：「從來沒有人能像他一樣牽動股市。」還有網友說：「這是他白手起家、一手打造的公司，本來就屬於他。我相信這一次他會更加珍惜，也會做得更好。即使他並不完美，我仍然認為他是台灣之光。」

CNN形容，不少人認為黃仁勳近期的一連串風波比八點檔連續劇還要精彩，網路上也流傳大量調侃整起事件的迷因及AI生成影片。

CNN特別提到，黃仁勳出生於台灣，人生最初5年也在台灣度過，對許多台灣人而言，他就是「自己人」。黃仁勳向來不吝讚美台灣，也大幅提升台灣在國際上的能見度。在他近期歷經種種波折之際，台灣始終與他站在一起。本月稍早，黃仁勳辭去輝達執行長職務時，台北101甚至在夜間點燈，打出聲援他的文字。

報導也指出，由於市場對失去黃仁勳領導的輝達前景感到不安，加上對AI產業整體發展的疑慮，台股上周暴跌17.5%，創下單周跌幅紀錄，促使台灣政府出手護盤。

美聯社則走訪黃仁勳曾光顧的台北蜜餞店及豆花店。一名50歲的蜜餞店員工表示，黃仁勳是相當重要的人物，為人也很好，大家都很喜歡他。

一名豆花店老闆坦言，當初得知黃仁勳下台時相當震驚，如今則認為輝達讓他復職是合理的決定。她以黃仁勳復職後亞洲股市上漲為例，直言：「大家都很高興，投資人也很高興……看來他對AI產業而言是不可或缺的，沒有人可以取代他，非他莫屬。」

news.Title: Jensen Huang is back at Nvidia. Should AMD be worried?
news.Content: When it comes to the AI trade, this has been the year of AMD ( AMD ). AMD's stock has sizzled, up 112% year to date compared to an 11.5% drop for its top rival Nvidia. As Nvidia's ( NVDA ) founder Jensen Huang has been embroiled in scandal and the tech trade has been pressured, AMD shares have hung tough. The stock is down 12.2% over the past month versus a 22% decline for Nvidia. The biggest question for AMD right now is this: Does Huang's stunning return as CEO of Nvidia mean bad news for AMD in 2027 and beyond? Pros think AMD will be just fine, for now. "I don't see how this changes it completely," Moor Insights & Strategy founder Patrick Moorhead said on Sozzi Unleashed . "I was saying early on when Jensen left that nothing changes for 18 months. And the reason is the supply chain is locked, the wafers are locked, data center configurations are locked around Nvidia design. So nothing would change, I think, if Jensen had been removed permanently." Shares of Nvidia fell 5% in premarket trading on Tuesday after a 31.2% surge on news that founder Jensen Huang had been reinstated as CEO. That came just 12 days after he resigned amid a personal scandal and federal chip-export probes. Interestingly, AMD shares rose 6.3% yesterday — a telling move that investors continue to believe in the AMD story. It's a good story to buy into. CEO Lisa Su — Yahoo Finance's 2026 CEO of the Year award winner — surprised everyone by spending $8.2 billion to scoop up World Labs , gaining a true AI innovator that focuses on software for 3D environments. World Labs was founded in 2024 and is led by Fei-Fei Li, a leading AI researcher known in tech circles as the "Godmother of AI." She was once the chief scientist at Google Cloud ( GOOG ). Just a few weeks ago, AMD delivered a strong double beat in its third quarter earnings report. Third quarter sales jumped 45% year over year to a record $13.38 billion, comfortably surpassing Wall Street consensus estimates of roughly $13.06 billion. Adjusted earnings climbed 74% to $2.09 per share, easily topping analyst projections of $1.94 per share. The blowout performance was anchored by AMD's Data Center segment, where revenue surged 97% to a record $8.5 billion on robust demand for EPYC server processors and the production ramp of Instinct MI450 AI accelerators. For the fourth quarter, AMD said it sees 50% sequential growth in data centers. In 2027, Su guided to revenue growing more than 80%, with server revenue doubling and data center AI more than doubling. Story Continues Amid a year of impressive earnings execution, AMD also unveiled its next-generation AI chips, headlined by the Instinct MI450 Series GPUs and the 6th Gen EPYC Venice CPUs. The new chips are designed to power AMD's new Helios rack-scale AI systems , which combine GPUs, CPUs, networking, and software into an integrated platform for training and running large AI models. Microsoft ( MSFT ) said it began deploying Helios across Azure AI services in the second half of 2026. The company also announced a major tie-up with Anthropic ( ANT ), significantly expanding its push to challenge Nvidia in the AI infrastructure market. Anthropic plans to deploy up to 2 gigawatts of the Instinct MI450 GPUs in its Helios system beginning in the first half of 2027 — a deal that could be worth tens of billions of dollars over time. AMD also committed to invest up to $5 billion in Anthropic, marking one of the chipmaker's largest strategic investments ever. More about Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO: 'The exact tick-tock': A prominent Democrat previews what to expect when lawmakers question Jensen Huang Wall Street analysts cheer Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia — but they still have concerns Jensen Huang is back atop Nvidia. He has a long road ahead in Washington. The biggest thing to watch, experts say, is how a hungry-to-prove-himself Huang executes on new chip designs over the next five to seven years. If Huang unlocks an epic gear on the design front, then the entire chip space could be in trouble from a market share perspective. "Jensen will be on a mission," EMJ Capital founder Eric Jackson said on Sozzi Unleashed . For now, though, AMD is still in the AI game in a big way. news.Title: 台股漲停卻沒量？三大法人賣超1230億真相曝　郭哲榮：籌碼洗淨沒人賣
news.Content:
受惠於輝達（NVIDIA）執行長黃仁勳重返戰場，台股今（24）日上演歷史性大反攻，終場狂噴3,310.46點、漲幅高達8.99%，強勢收復四萬點大關，收在40,122.35點；不過，盤面出現台積電（2330）、元大台灣50（0050）全面鎖死漲停，成交金額卻僅4,194.05億元、創下今年新低量的奇景，盤後三大法人更合計賣超1,230.11億元（其中外資賣超503.90億元）。對此， 摩爾投顧投資長郭哲榮（哲哲） 揭開背後真相，直言這並非沒人買，而是 「籌碼已經洗得太乾淨，根本沒人想賣」 ，散戶千萬別被表面數據誤導！

【黃仁勳11天回歸成真 郭哲榮：股市修正如百貨週年慶】

市場先前一度瀰漫悲觀恐慌氣氛，但郭哲榮早在11月21日大盤下探低點時，便率先喊出「1121多頭歸隊」，精準預言黃仁勳絕不會輕言離開一手打造的帝國，並斷言只要回歸消息一出，台股必定上演狂飆千點甚至全線漲停的奇蹟，如今預言在短短11天內全數兌現。郭哲榮感性形容，股市的大幅修正就如同「百貨公司週年慶打折」，聰明的投資人應該看清長期基本面，而非在最低點含淚離場。

【不是沒人買是沒人賣！三大法人賣超真相曝光】

面對今日大盤僅以4,194億元的今年最低量就強勢鎖住漲停，不少投資人心中疑慮重重。郭哲榮點破，成交量萎縮絕非買盤退縮，而是經過前波劇烈震盪後，「籌碼已徹底洗淨，根本沒人願意賣出」；他以高價千金股川湖（2059）為例，今日僅成交19張便直接高掛漲停，足見市場賣壓已完全掏空。至於盤後數據顯示外資賣超逾503億元、三大法人合計賣超1,230億元，郭哲榮深度剖析，這其實是外資與自營商利用主動統一台股增長（00981A）等ETF 進行無風險套利與避險操作 ，並非實質看空台股，散戶切勿自己嚇自己。

【右側交易買點浮現 年底前挑戰4萬5千點】

展望後市佈局，郭哲榮堅定重申「台股目標5萬點、台積電上看3,000元」的超前觀點，並預估年底前大盤就有機會挑戰44,000至45,000點大關。他提醒，在通膨居高不下與新台幣貶值的雙重壓力下，單純守著現金終將被通膨吞噬，資金唯有進入資本市場才能保值增值；隨著國巨*（2327）、欣興（3037）、環球晶（6488）等績優股歷經超跌打折，右側交易的安全買點已正式浮現，投資人應抱緊核心資產，迎接這波波瀾壯闊的多頭反攻行情。

news.Title: The Trade Desk's 100-Plus JBP Pipeline: A Key Revenue Catalyst?
news.Content:
The Trade Desk' s TTD increasing joint business partnership ("JBP") activity is emerging as a notable development as it tries to revive revenue growth. TTD is strengthening the relationships with major advertisers and agencies through JBPs, reflecting its efforts to deepen customer engagement, improve advertising outcomes and unlock incremental spending opportunities.

Through the first nine months of 2026, the number of JBPs increased more than 30% year over year, including growth exceeding 20% during the third quarter. These agreements now cover hundreds of agencies and brands.

Management emphasized that customers operating under JBPs continue to generate meaningfully faster growth than those working under traditional master service agreements. Moreover, The Trade Desk has more than 100 additional JBPs in its pipeline, providing opportunities to deepen customer relationships and potentially capture incremental advertising budgets.

Unlike conventional commercial agreements, JBPs establish a structured framework for advertisers, agencies and The Trade Desk to collaborate on campaign planning, innovation and performance measurement. This approach helps the company transition from being primarily a media-buying platform to a strategic partner focused on delivering measurable business outcomes.

The Trade Desk Revenues (Quarterly)

The Trade Desk revenue-quarterly | The Trade Desk Quote

On the last earnings call, management highlighted that deeper engagement with business leaders across a major financial services customer resulted in millions of dollars in incremental advertising spending from a single business line. Such developments highlight the potential of JBPs to increase spending among existing clients.

The Trade Desk's customer retention remained above 95% in the third quarter. However, its revenues declined 0.5% year over year to approximately $736 million but surpassed management's expectations. The top line benefited from strength in medical health advertising, political spending related to the U.S. midterm elections and a nonrecurring contribution from a strategic partner that added approximately 3 percentage points to revenue growth.

Pressure on consumer-packaged goods and automotive advertising, partly reflecting inflation and elevated interest rates, remains concerning.

Nevertheless, expanding JBP adoption, alongside product innovation, could support a gradual recovery in advertising spending. Converting its sizable pipeline into sustained client spending growth remains critical to strengthening the company's revenue trajectory in 2027.

Story Continues

Mapping the Competitive Terrain

The Trade Desk faces stiff competition from Amazon AMZN and Alphabet GOOGL, which are enhancing their advertising offerings to attract greater advertiser spending.

Amazon's third-quarter 2026 advertising revenues of $19.6 billion surged 12% year over year, excluding foreign exchange movements. Management said the Prime Day shift created an 850-basis-point sequential impact on third-quarter advertising growth. The company also cited the absence of NBA games in the quarter and the change in its search engine marketing programs made in the year-ago quarter.

Amazon expects advertising growth to return to the high teens in the fourth quarter. The company is strengthening its advertising capabilities through AI-powered tools such as Ads Agent, which reduces campaign setup and targeting time.

Alphabet's Google Search & other revenues rose 12% to $63.3 billion, driven primarily by retail and finance advertisers. YouTube advertising revenues increased 9% to $11.2 billion, supported by brand advertising and connected-TV demand. Google Network revenues grew 1% to $7.5 billion.

In November 2026, Google expanded Display & Video 360 by enabling access to Google Audiences across Spotify's audio and video inventory, alongside Pinterest's premium video and display inventory. These initiatives could intensify competition for advertising budgets and challenge The Trade Desk's customer expansion efforts.

news.Title: Meta’s $300 AI Muse Could Be a Breakthrough as Wall Street Sees 52% Upside
news.Content:
Meta Platforms (META) is taking another big swing at artificial intelligence, but this time, it is not building another chatbot or competing smartphone. Instead, the company is reportedly preparing a $300 pocket-sized AI device called Muse Charm, designed to make interacting with its Muse AI agent as effortless as talking to a friend.

The gadget could even come bundled with 12 months of free Verizon 5G data, lowering the barrier for consumers to give it a try. But the bigger story is not how many units Meta can sell or how much money it makes on the hardware. It is whether the company can turn AI into an everyday habit, keeping users engaged across its growing ecosystem.

More News from Barchart

Dear Dollar Tree Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 24

Dear Dell Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 24

CoreWeave's Co-Founder Says He's 'Never Been More Confident' in the Company as He Buys $30 Million of Its Bonds. Why That Matters More Than a Stock Buy for CRWV.

Stop Missing Market Moves: Get the FREE Barchart Brief – your midday dose of stock movers, trending sectors, and actionable trade ideas, delivered right to your inbox. Sign Up Now!

That distinction matters for investors, especially as Meta pours billions into AI infrastructure while facing mounting pressure to prove those investments can generate meaningful returns. And the Charm could become an important test of that strategy.

Meta Stock Is Feeling the Cost of Its AI Ambitions

Meta shares are down about 15% in 2026 as concern over AI costs more than weakness in advertising is growing. Meta expects 2026 capital expenditures of $135 billion to $145 billion, while third-quarter free cash flow was negative $2.12 billion. S&P Global Ratings cut its outlook to negative in October, questioning when AI returns will catch up with spending.

The $300 Charm is an AI distribution bet. Reuters reported on Nov. 19, citing The Information, that Meta is considering a $300 price and up to a year of Verizon 5G data. Unveiled in September, Charm has a roughly two-inch screen, built-in 5G, and a customizable Muse character. A tap opens the agent; it is not a phone and cannot make calls.

The idea is to remove friction. Users reach Muse without unlocking a phone or opening an app, while Meta gains a direct interface that could reduce its dependence on Apple (AAPL) and Google's mobile platforms. If people use Charm to shop, plan trips, or complete tasks, Meta could make AI a recurring habit. The company has not announced a monetization plan, so repeat use matters more than launch sales.

Story Continues

Meta Is Building More Than a Standalone Gadget

Charm will support a larger AI investment push. Meta launched Muse Wonder models in the insurance claim, lease, and building application agent tasks in October. It has also been adding such styles to its AI glasses family during its Connect event in September, topping out at over 100 by the end of the year with Ray-Ban, Oakley and Meta carrying the items. The glasses are also getting the Muse.

AI is already working to make more recommendations and boost ad targeting. While management expects Reality Labs losses to converge to approximately $15 billion in 2027, infrastructure costs still remain extremely high.

The Latest Quarter Shows the Opportunity and the Risk

Meta recently delivered another solid quarter, which topped analysts' estimates.

During the third quarter, revenue grew 26% year over year to $64.6 billion. Its applications saw a daily active user population of 3.64 billion, with ad impressions up 10% and average ad prices up 14% when compared to the previous year.

The cost and expenses also increased by 68% to $51.6 billion, tied to a $9.89 billion legal charge resulting from an agreement with U.S. state attorneys general. If this charge is removed, then diluted EPS would have been $7.40 rather than $3.83. Capital expenditures of $34.91 billion, along with free cash flow of $2.12 billion. Meta is expanding, but it's taking up cash that can be used to invest in returns to come.

Wall Street Still Sees Substantial Upside

During the last few months, analysts have been increasingly bullish on Meta stock, highlighting its moat. 55 Wall Street analysts tracking Meta stock gave a consensus "strong buy" rating with a mean price target of $856. This shows the stock could climb up to 52% from the current price.

Separately, JPMorgan recently added Meta to the bank's Analyst Focus List in November and kept a $940 target, implying a massive 68% upside. He cited stronger AI-driven advertising, highlighting 26% ad growth and estimating Meta generated about $13 billion in incremental ad revenue, roughly twice Google Search's increase.

In addition, Karl Keirstead, an analyst at UBS, initiated coverage with a Buy rating after noting that Muse and Meta Business Agents should help address concerns about capex and cash flow.

But UBS stuck with its $815 target, and the projection ended up 45% higher than the day's close but lower than the $892 forecast. That offering translates to even the bulls feeling a sense of "execution risk." The big one, of course, is if Charm can monetize AI engagement in a sustainable, repeatable, and speedy way that will make it worth the investment.

news.Title: TSM's AI-Driven Growth Accelerates: Is There More Upside Ahead?
news.Content:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited TSM continues to benefit from growing investment in AI infrastructure as it drives demand for advanced semiconductor technologies. The company's third-quarter 2026 performance reflected this momentum, with revenues increasing 41.2% year over year to $46.72 billion. High-performance computing (HPC) contributed 68% of total revenues, increasing 22% sequentially.

The growing adoption of advanced manufacturing technologies also supported performance, with 2-nanometer technology accounting for 8% of wafer revenues, compared with 3% in the preceding quarter. Management expects full-year 2026 revenues to grow approximately 44% in U.S. dollar terms, reflecting sustained demand across its portfolio.

TSM's growth opportunity extends beyond conventional AI accelerators. The company highlighted increasing demand associated with agentic AI, server processors and networking chips, which could broaden semiconductor requirements across data-center infrastructure. The company had previously projected a mid-to-high-50% compound annual growth rate for AI accelerator revenue between 2024 and 2029. However, TSM has now indicated that demand could potentially exceed that outlook.

TSM is steadily expanding its manufacturing capabilities to capture these opportunities. Its N2-family annual capacity is expected to more than double in 2027. The company is also preparing for A14 technology, with volume production planned for 2028. These developments strengthen its position in the advanced semiconductor manufacturing market.

How Are Competitors Faring?

United Microelectronics Corporation UMC, another semiconductor foundry operator, is witnessing improving demand across its technology portfolio. UMC's third-quarter 2026 revenues increased 25.6% year over year to NT$74.24 billion, while capacity utilization reached 92%. Its 22-nanometer technology accounted for a record 18.3% of wafer sales, supported by customer demand for display drivers, automotive radar and Wi-Fi integrated circuits. UMC is also pursuing opportunities in advanced packaging and silicon photonics, which could support additional growth as AI infrastructure requirements increase.

Intel Corporation INTC is also witnessing stronger demand across its data-center and AI operations. Intel's third-quarter 2026 revenues increased 21% year over year to $16.5 billion, while Data Center and AI revenues surged 78% to $7.3 billion. Intel's Foundry segment generated $6.7 billion in revenues, increasing 58% year over year, including intersegment transactions. Intel is seeing robust demand for its Xeon processors and improving manufacturing execution. However, supply constraints remain a near-term challenge.

news.Title: Can Alibaba's Cloud Intelligence Momentum Reshape the Stock's Outlook?
news.Content:
Alibaba Group BABA leans on its cloud business to reshape its investment case, and the latest results suggest the shift is gaining traction. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, revenues from AI Cloud and Compute Services, the segment that combines Cloud Intelligence Group with chip unit T-Head, jumped 53% year over year to RMB61 billion ($9.1 billion), accelerating from 45% growth in the prior quarter. Group revenues rose 10% to RMB271.5 billion.

Growth quality stands out. External customer revenues rose 64%, driven by a 67% surge in recurring revenues and 55% growth in compute equipment solutions. AI-related product revenues reached RMB17.9 billion, delivering triple-digit growth for the 13th straight quarter. Segment adjusted EBITA soared 121% to RMB8.8 billion, lifting the segment's adjusted EBITA margin to 14.5%.

Alibaba is widening its reach. Last month, the company launched its first public cloud region in the Netherlands, taking its footprint to 109 availability zones across 32 regions. Earlier this month, it showcased Qwen4-Max enhancements at its Hong Kong summit, where its local customer base topped 65,000. The T-Head Zhenwu V900 chip is slated for commercial release, alongside a next-generation supernode, in the first quarter of calender 2027.

However, the forward picture is more measured. Management indicated that new U.S. export controls and scarce domestic compute supply could lower next year's cloud growth target to 30-45%, before a potential rebound to 50% or more in 2028 as in-house chip capacity scales. In second quarter fiscal 2027, capital expenditure climbed 60% to RMB50.5 billion, pushing free cash outflow to RMB34.5 billion, and the adjusted EBITA loss at AI Labs and Applications widened to RMB10.5 billion.

Cloud momentum strengthens Alibaba's long-term positioning, but compute constraints, heavy spending and progress toward its positive free cash flow target will determine how far it reshapes the stock's outlook.

How Alibaba's Cloud Push Compares With U.S. Rivals

Alibaba's cloud acceleration places it alongside U.S.-listed hyperscalers Amazon AMZN and Microsoft MSFT, both of which are also benefiting from strong AI demand. Amazon's AWS segment sales rose 39.3% year over year to $46 billion in the third quarter of 2026, while segment operating income climbed to $17.8 billion. Amazon expects AWS growth to exceed 40% in both 2027 and 2028.

Microsoft's Azure revenues grew 48% to $33.17 billion in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, while Microsoft Cloud revenues rose 30% to $63.9 billion in the same time frame. Microsoft's commercial remaining performance obligation increased 73% to $677 billion, offering solid visibility into future cloud revenues.

news.Title: Jensen Huang's return revives an old Wall Street trade: Bet on the comeback CEO
news.Content:
Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia ( NVDA ) could be good for more than a one-day pop in its stock price.

Just look at the evidence from the case studies on the returns of founders like Apple's ( AAPL ) Steve Jobs, Starbucks' ( SBUX ) founder Howard Schultz, and Charles Schwab's ( SCHW ) founder Charles Schwab.

A new analysis of six high-profile CEO returns by Rand Group Research found that four of the six companies outperformed the S&P 500 over the three years after their leaders returned.

The biggest winner was Apple, where Steve Jobs' return in September 1997 was followed by a staggering 414% stock gain, versus 59% for the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ). The stock price gain reflected Jobs' innovation streak, which led to world-changing products like the iPhone and iPod.

Charles Schwab shares climbed 141% after its founder returned in 2004 after a year to rejuvenate the brokerage house, according to a New York Times account .

Starbucks gained 78% under Howard Schultz when he returned in January 2008, compared with a 10% decline for the benchmark. Schultz moved quickly to improve operations from a then floundering business.

Google's Larry Page delivered an 84% gain after returning in 2011, also beating the market.

There were exceptions, however.

Disney ( DIS ) shares rose just 14% after Bob Iger returned in 2022, badly trailing the S&P 500's 67% gain, while Under Armour ( UA ) has fallen 40% since Kevin Plank returned in 2024.

The takeaway for Nvidia investors? A founder's return can be a powerful catalyst, particularly when that founder has a deep understanding of the business and a track record of creating shareholder value.

But it's no guarantee. Jensen Huang has the opportunity to join a pretty impressive comeback club — but he'll still have to deliver.

Shares of Nvidia fell nearly 4% in premarket trading on Tuesday after a 31.2% surge on news that founder Huang had been reinstated as CEO. That came just 12 days after he resigned amid a personal scandal and federal chip-export probes.

"Jensen will be on a mission," EMJ Capital founder Eric Jackson said on Sozzi Unleashed .

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show, the ' Power Players With Brian Sozzi' podcast and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

news.Title: Microsoft vs. Meta: Which AI Infrastructure Stock Has An Edge Now?
news.Content:
Microsoft MSFT and Meta Platforms META sit at the center of the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure race. Both companies are pouring record sums into data centers, custom silicon and frontier models, betting that compute capacity will define the next decade of technology leadership.

Yet their paths diverge. Microsoft monetizes AI largely through Azure and enterprise software, while Meta channels its buildout into advertising and consumer AI. With both lifting spending plans after October 2026 results, the comparison is timely.

Let's delve deeper and closely compare the fundamentals of the two stocks to determine which one is a better investment now.

The Case for MSFT

Microsoft's AI infrastructure strategy is translating into tangible revenues. In first-quarter fiscal 2027, Azure revenues, reported under the new Agents and Infra segment, reached $33.2 billion, up 48% year over year, while Microsoft Cloud revenues rose 30% to $63.9 billion. Commercial remaining performance obligation jumped 73% to $677 billion, offering strong multi-year visibility.

Demand continues to outpace supply. Microsoft expects fiscal second-quarter capital expenditures to exceed $50 billion, taking calendar 2026 spending to roughly $170 billion, with about three-fourths of first-quarter spending directed toward short-lived assets such as GPUs and CPUs. Importantly, management expects to remain free cash flow positive in fiscal 2027, a key differentiator in a capital-intensive cycle.

The AI monetization funnel is broadening. Microsoft Foundry now serves more than 120,000 customers, with revenues more than tripling year over year. Copilot customers consuming credits through usage-based billing grew more than 75% sequentially. At Ignite 2026 in November, Microsoft launched Agent 365 Business Analytics, Copilot Workspaces and Autopilot, made Cobalt 200 virtual machines generally available with up to 50% higher performance, and introduced Azure Catalyst for agent-led modernization.

For the fiscal second quarter, Microsoft guided revenues of $96-$97.1 billion and Azure growth of 49-50% in constant currency, signaling further acceleration ahead.

Challenges remain. Windows OEM and devices revenues fell 22%, Xbox content and services slipped 2% and commercial bookings declined 12% on a tough comparison. Delays in third-party capacity deliveries also constrained supply. Still, Microsoft's diversified enterprise base and expanding AI portfolio position it well for sustained growth.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MSFT's fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $19.65 per share. The estimate indicates 9.47% year-over-year growth.

Story Continues

Microsoft Corporation Price and Consensus

Microsoft Corporation price-consensus-chart | Microsoft Corporation Quote

The Case for META

Meta's core advertising engine remains robust. Third-quarter 2026 revenues rose 26% year over year to $64.6 billion, driven by a 10% increase in ad impressions and a 14% rise in average price per ad. Family daily active people averaged 3.64 billion in September, up 3%.

Meta is building AI capacity in pursuit of personal superintelligence. The company launched Muse and its first frontier model, Muse Wonder, and on Nov. 6 began rolling out specialized Muse Wonder-trained models to Muse and Meta AI users. Newer avenues, including enterprise APIs, subscriptions and business AI, could diversify revenues over time. Meta also announced a new non-voting Class C common stock, which it may use for capital raising, employee compensation and acquisitions.

However, costs are rising. Third-quarter capital expenditures surged to $34.91 billion, exceeding operating cash flow of $32.79 billion and resulting in negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion. Total expenses jumped 68%, partly due to a $9.89 billion legal charge, pushing the operating margin down to 20% from 40%.

For the fourth quarter, Meta expects revenues of $73-$76 billion. Full-year 2026 capital expenditures are projected to be $135-$145 billion and total expenses are expected to be $175-$179 billion. Management anticipates strong revenue growth throughout 2027 but acknowledged that newer AI investments will take longer to generate returns than the core business. Reality Labs losses are expected to narrow to around $15 billion next year.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Meta's 2026 earnings is pegged at $29.29 per share, down 5% over the past 30 days, suggesting a 24.7% rise from the figure reported in 2025.

Meta Platforms, Inc. Price and Consensus

Meta Platforms, Inc. price-consensus-chart | Meta Platforms, Inc. Quote

Unlike Microsoft, Meta lacks an established third-party cloud business to directly monetize its infrastructure. Youth-related litigation and regulatory risks add further uncertainty.

Valuation and Price Performance Comparison

Microsoft shares have gained 2.2% year to date, reflecting confidence in accelerating Azure growth. Meanwhile, Meta shares have declined 9.4% year to date as soaring capital expenditures, negative free cash flow and legal charges weighed on sentiment.

MSFT Outperforms META YTD

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Meta trades at a forward 12-month P/E of 17.87X, a discount to Microsoft's steeper 22.92X. However, Microsoft's premium appears justified, given its $677 billion commercial backlog, direct infrastructure monetization through Azure and positive free cash flow guidance. Investors should track MSFT for its visible growth trajectory, while META holders may stay put until AI spending returns become clearer.

MSFT vs. META P/E Ratio

Conclusion

Microsoft holds a clear edge over Meta in AI infrastructure. Its Azure business directly monetizes data center investments, delivering 48% growth, while a $677 billion commercial backlog provides multi-year visibility. Microsoft's guidance for accelerating Azure growth, broadening Copilot and Foundry adoption, and positive free cash flow despite record capital spending strengthen its case.

Meta's advertising business remains strong, but surging expenses, negative free cash flow, legal charges and uncertain returns on newer AI bets weigh on its outlook. Hence, Microsoft offers better upside potential. Investors should track and hold MSFT stock while waiting for a better entry point for META. Microsoft and Meta carry a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) each. news.Title: 別被3千點漲勢騙了！陳嘉偉警告台股「很快再破底」：黃仁勳已遭架空
news.Content:
輝達（NVIDIA）創辦人黃仁勳重返執行長崗位，激勵台北股市24日早盤跳空大漲逾3,000點，市場多頭紛紛喊出重返5萬點；然而分析師陳嘉偉在節目《股市總司令》中直言，這波強彈並非多頭重啟攻勢，而是讓套牢族「反彈逃命」與空方進場的「送分題」。陳嘉偉不僅鎖定漲停打開的弱勢股進場放空獲利，更點出黃仁勳回歸後核心決策權已遭架空，接下來還得二度赴美國國會接受調查，預言台股反彈過後很快將再度跌破35,542點前波低點。

斷頭警報解除反成放空送分題 鎖定「漲停打開股」出手全勝

針對台股早盤大漲3,310點，陳嘉偉分析，許多個股先前波段跌幅超過70%，包括國巨、環球晶與上詮等，至少需上漲300%才能回本，多頭卻將解套行情包裝成大賺；且大盤先前從5萬點回檔12,131點跌至年線的走勢，發生在黃仁勳辭職前，本就與他無關。

他進一步指出，政府將融資維持率降至120%解除了斷頭危機，加上開盤多數股票跳空漲停、散戶惜售，反而讓盤中漲停打開或未能鎖漲停的個股暴露賣壓，其團隊今日便鎖定開高走低的晶豪科，以及亞光、中磊、富采、鴻準等五檔個股放空全數獲利，其中晶豪科更從開盤漲停一路殺低至尾盤跌4%，單日振幅高達14%。

喻黃仁勳如「63歲喬丹回公牛」 核心晶片銷售決策權遭架空

對於外界看好黃仁勳回鍋能帶領輝達再創高峰，陳嘉偉將其比喻為「63歲的麥可喬丹重返公牛隊」，直言他已失去昔日一人說了算的絕對統治力。陳嘉偉指出，輝達現任董事長留任，黃仁勳回鍋後僅負責研發與台灣供應鏈管理；最關鍵的國家安全與出口管制改由獨立董事監督，董事會更將增設直接向董事會提名並匯報的法務長，等同於把「晶片要賣給誰」的核心決策權徹底拔除，即便重返公司也難有作為。

捲入美國政壇角力風暴 12月二度赴國會恐遭國安調查

除了內部權力受限，陳嘉偉更警告黃仁勳正陷入嚴重的美國政治漩渦。他分析，黃仁勳先前力挺對中開放晶片與開源模型，早已同時得罪民主黨與共和黨建制派；隨著川普期中選舉失利、建制派的盧比歐（Rubio）民調大幅領先范斯（Vance），川普此時介入護航反而讓黃仁勳成為政敵標靶。陳嘉偉表示，黃仁勳原本辭職後已淡出風波，如今高調回歸引發參議院領袖舒默（Schumer）及眾議院議員強烈反彈，揚言徹查其是否出賣美國國安，12月1日更將二度赴國會接受調查，在多重利空夾擊下，相關產業鏈已難回過去榮景。
