news.Title: JPMorgan Has Picked These 2 Stocks as Its Top Internet Bets
news.Content:
Wall Street is hunting for companies that can turn artificial intelligence (AI) investments into real profits. According to JPMorgan (JPM), Meta Platforms (META) and Amazon (AMZN) stand out as top contenders in this race. In a recent move, JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth added Meta to the bank's Analyst Focus List, placing it alongside Amazon as a favored internet stock. This choice highlights two different growth opportunities. Let's explore what sets these companies apart and how investors can act on the opportunity.

Why JPMorgan Picked Meta Platforms

JPMorgan's bullishness on Meta comes down to one important development. Meta's advertising business is showing that AI is paying off. Analyst Doug Anmuth says Meta is showing stronger short-term earnings, especially since its third-quarter ad growth beat expectations. JPMorgan estimates Meta brought in about $13 billion in extra ad revenue, almost double what Google Search added. This strong performance led Meta to replace Alphabet on the bank's list of top internet stocks.

More News from Barchart

Dear Dollar Tree Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 24

Dear Dell Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 24

CoreWeave's Co-Founder Says He's 'Never Been More Confident' in the Company as He Buys $30 Million of Its Bonds. Why That Matters More Than a Stock Buy for CRWV.

Get exclusive insights with the FREE Barchart Brief newsletter. Subscribe now for quick, incisive midday market analysis you won't find anywhere else.

In the most recent third quarter, Family of Apps advertising revenue reached $63.1 billion, up 26% year over year (YOY). Total company revenue also rose 26%, to $64.6 billion. Meta benefited from both higher ad volumes, up 10%, and a 14% increase in the average price advertisers paid per placement. Meta is not just relying on showing more ads but is also increasing the value advertisers get from each placement.

In September, Meta's platforms averaged 3.64 billion daily active users. The company is reaching more people, showing more ads, and charging higher prices per ad. Its AI-driven recommendations and advertising tools are boosting campaign results, which encourages advertisers to spend more. Meta is expanding the limits of AI's commercial potential far beyond advertising. In just one quarter, nearly 10 million advertisers tapped into its generative AI creative tools, while smarter ad-ranking systems boosted conversions across a range of campaigns. Its Muse personal assistant presents another potential monetization opportunity through paid features and business services. Already, over 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had set up Muse within its first six weeks. Still, this remains an emerging opportunity rather than an established earnings contributor.

Story Continues

The biggest concern is the cost of keeping up this growth. Meta's Q3 expenses soared by 68%, weighed down by a hefty $9.9 billion legal charge. Without that charge, operating income would have climbed to $22.9 billion, up from $20.5 billion the previous year. Capital spending surged to $34.9 billion, and free cash flow slipped into negative territory at $2.1 billion. Going forward, management projects capital expenditures for 2026 to land between $135 billion and $145 billion. JPMorgan is effectively betting that stronger advertising returns and new AI-driven revenue opportunities will eventually justify that enormous investment.

Overall, analysts consider META stock a "Strong Buy," with an average target price of $855.96. This indicates a possible 52% increase from the current price. Of 55 analysts, 46 rate it a "Strong Buy," two a "Moderate Buy," and seven a "Hold." META stock is down 13.7% year to date, but the highest price target of $1,050 implies a potential gain of 87%.

Why JPMorgan Picked Amazon

JPMorgan's bullishness on Amazon rests largely on Amazon Web Services (AWS). The bank sees an opportunity for Amazon to capture a much larger share of enterprise AI spending as more companies use AI at scale. Anmuth noted AWS's faster growth, expanding backlog, and better returns on infrastructure investments. He also mentioned that management expects AWS revenue to grow by more than 40% each year in 2027 and 2028, which could help the business reach $1 trillion in annual revenue over the next five to 10 years.

In the third quarter, AWS revenue rose 39.3% year over year to $46 billion, recording its strongest growth in nearly five years. Its backlog also climbed to $578 billion, more than doubling year over year. This backlog shows customer demand that will turn into revenue as Amazon adds more computing capacity. AWS also earned $17.8 billion in operating income, up from $11.4 billion a year ago.

Amazon's custom AI chips provide another reason why JP Morgan is bullish. Trainium accelerators and Graviton processors are seeing more customer interest, and management says revenue commitments for both have grown more than 20 times from last year. Customers using Amazon's chips also saved over $2 billion this quarter. By making its own chips, Amazon can better manage infrastructure costs and offer customers a less expensive computing option. This could help AWS stay competitive and improve profits as AI workloads grow. Additionally, Amazon says it is improving the time required to recover its infrastructure investments, giving JPMorgan another reason to remain optimistic. AWS already operates at an annualized revenue run rate of $184 billion, and management believes its growing AI business can become a substantially larger source of revenue and free cash flow.

Nonetheless, Amazon's spending plans raise major concerns. Management expects to spend about $220 billion in cash capital expenditures in 2026, and even more in 2027. Most of this money will go toward AWS infrastructure. While operating income rose 61% to $28.1 billion in Q3, free cash flow over the past 12 months dropped to negative $42.4 billion as investment picked up. Amazon is betting that customer demand will make this spending worthwhile. If new capacity takes longer to pay off, cash flow could stay under pressure, even if AWS revenue keeps growing quickly.

JP Morgan is effectively betting that Amazon can turn its enormous infrastructure spending into a durable competitive advantage rather than simply chasing the AI boom.

Overall, on Wall Street, AMZN stock has earned a consensus "Strong Buy." Of the 56 analysts covering the stock, 48 have a "Strong Buy," five have a "Moderate Buy" rating, and three analysts rate the stock as a "Hold." AMZN stock has climbed 8.9% year-to-date (YTD). But its mean target price of $328.65 implies 33% potential upside from current levels. Plus, the high target price of $405 suggests that shares could climb as much as 64% over the next year.

Is It Time to Buy META and AMZN?

JPMorgan's picks are backed by solid fundamentals. Meta offers more immediate AI-driven advertising returns, while Amazon provides exposure to the expanding AI infrastructure market. Both have significant growth opportunities, but rising capital expenditure and valuation risks deserve attention. Investors should weigh the growth potential against the cost of sustaining it before deciding.

news.Title: Can Wearables & Mac Revenues Add Fresh Momentum to Apple Stock Ahead?
news.Content:
Apple Inc. AAPL enters the holiday quarter with its Mac business gaining momentum, while its Wearables, Home and Accessories segment is leaning on a refreshed lineup to reverse a slowdown. Whether these categories add fresh momentum to the stock depends on supply and cost management.

For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Apple expects revenues to grow 7-10% year over year, which would mark its best revenue quarter ever. However, the outlook reflects constrained supply, with Mac and iPad limitations driven primarily by memory as demand exceeded expectations. Gross margin is projected at 45-46%, pressured mainly by higher memory costs, while operating expenses are expected between $20.4 billion and $20.8 billion. Apple did not provide category-level guidance.

The product pipeline supports demand. In late October, Apple unveiled the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, bringing Touch to the Mac for the first time, alongside the M6-powered iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro. The company also introduced HomeView, HomePod mini 2 and a new Apple TV 4K, with Apple Home Collection accessories arriving in December. These follow the September launches of AirPods 5, Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4.

In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, Mac revenues rose 24% year over year to $10.8 billion despite supply constraints, driven by MacBook Neo and MacBook Pro and a September-quarter record for new-to-Mac customers. Fiscal 2026 Mac revenues were $37.9 billion versus $33.7 billion a year ago. In contrast, Wearables, Home and Accessories revenues fell 8% to $8.3 billion on a tough comparison against the prior-year launches of Apple Watch SE 3 and AirPods Pro 3.

Fiscal 2026 segment revenues were $35.6 billion versus $35.7 billion a year ago. While a record wearables installed base and new launches offer support, memory-driven supply limits and margin pressure could temper how much Mac and wearables lift Apple's near-term results.

How Apple's Mac and Wearables Stack Up Against HP and Garmin

In PCs, HP Inc. HPQ posted fiscal third-quarter 2026 Personal Systems revenues of $11.8 billion, up 18% year over year, though HP's segment operating margin slipped to 4.6% from 5.4%. HP is scheduled to report fiscal fourth-quarter results on Nov. 24. In wearables, Garmin Ltd. GRMN delivered third-quarter 2026 fitness segment revenues of $694.3 million, up 16%, led by wearables demand. Garmin also launched the CIRQA Smart Band and raised its 2026 revenue outlook to about $8.15 billion. Garmin's momentum contrasts with Apple's 8% decline in Wearables, Home and Accessories, while HP's growth mirrors Apple's Mac gains.

news.Title: Billionaire Philippe Laffont of Coatue Management Sent AMD Shares Packing and Loaded Up on This Hot AI IPO Instead
news.Content:
Although earnings season and Fed meetings tend to hog all the headlines, investors can learn a lot during Form 13F filing season. A 13F allows investors to track which stocks Wall Street's savviest money managers, with at least $100 million in assets under management, purchased and sold in the latest quarter.

Billionaire Philippe Laffont of Coatue Management is easily one of the most successful and closely watched fund managers on Wall Street -- and he was a busy bee during the third quarter. According to Coatue's 13F, Laffont sent shares of Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) packing, while at the same time loading up on shares of one of Wall Street's hottest artificial intelligence (AI) initial public offerings (IPOs), SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Billionaire Philippe Laffont shows Advanced Micro Devices the door

Among Wall Street's billionaire investors, few have embraced the AI revolution quite like Laffont. As recently as mid-2023, his fund held approximately 14 million shares of AMD. By the end of 2025, all 14 million shares were given the heave-ho.

Laffont bought back 95,987 shares in the second quarter of 2026, only to turn around and dump every last share the very next quarter.

Profit-taking is the most logical reason Coatue's billionaire boss bid adieu to AMD. Between April and July, shares of the company soared from around $200 to more than $500. Coatue's average hold time is around three years, signaling a willingness by its chief investor to ring the register when given the opportunity.

However, profit-taking may not be the only reason AMD was jettisoned. While Laffont isn't exactly a value investor, AMD's estimated price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio for 2026 and 2027 was approaching 80 and 40, respectively, toward the end of September. With AMD holding such a small share of the AI-accelerating graphics processing unit (GPU) market, Laffont may have viewed other AI stocks as more intriguing.

Coatue's billionaire boss piled into SK Hynix

Although everyone's talking about Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX) and Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) breaking the IPO record books, they're overlooking SK Hynix, which also debuted in the U.S. in July as a trillion-dollar company. Laffont purchased 9,498,922 shares, worth almost $1.75 billion at the end of the third quarter.

Story Continues

Laffont's attraction to SK Hynix likely has to do with its world-leading position as a supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM). HBM is stacked with GPUs to facilitate ultra-fast transfer speeds in enterprise data centers. Not only is SK Hynix benefiting from strong demand for HBM, but persistent supply shortages are also pushing its pricing power into the stratosphere.

SK Hynix foresees memory shortages potentially lasting through 2030. According to a late-October update, the company has already secured purchase agreements for more than half of its production for 2027 and 2028. Wall Street (and billionaire investor Philippe Laffont) appreciates cash-flow predictability.

But SK Hynix isn't necessarily a slam-dunk investment. While its purchase agreements can temporarily buoy its pricing power, history shows that memory is cyclical and highly commoditized, and strong pricing power is rarely sustainable. If the AI bubble bursts, as history suggests will happen sooner rather than later, SK Hynix's pricing power could take a direct hit.

news.Title: Analog Devices (ADI) Q4 Earnings and Revenues Top Estimates

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +4.37%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this semiconductor maker would post earnings of $3.33 per share when it actually produced earnings of $3.45, delivering a surprise of +3.6%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

news.Title: Sandisk Plunges 44% in a Month: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
news.Content:
Sandisk 's SNDK shares have dropped 44.1% in a month, underperforming the broader Zacks Computer & Technology sector's decline of 18.1%. The selloff appears to reflect investor concerns surrounding the sustainability of elevated profit margins, moderating NAND pricing growth, and slowing sequential revenue and earnings growth. SNDK is also suffering from weakness in consumer and low-end edge markets, and execution risks associated with long-term supply agreements. However, accelerating AI-driven NAND demand, increasing penetration of hyperscale data centers, strong multiyear revenue visibility, an expanding technology portfolio and robust cash generation support Sandisk's long-term growth prospects. So, what should investors do with the stock? Let's find out.

SNDK Suffers From Weak Consumer and Low-End Edge Markets

Sandisk is suffering from weakening consumer demand as customers adjust to higher NAND prices. Consumer revenues declined 39% year over year and 29% sequentially to $397 million in the first quarter of fiscal 2027. Although the Edge business benefited from resilient demand across premium and mainstream markets, weakness in lower-end devices remains concerning. Sandisk expects PC unit shipments to decline in the low-single-digit percentage range in calendar 2027. Prolonged weakness across price-sensitive markets could limit volume growth and pricing flexibility.

Moreover, Sandisk is experiencing a moderation in sequential growth. The company expects fiscal second-quarter revenues of $12.2-$12.6 billion, indicating approximately 12.4% sequential growth at the midpoint compared with 23% growth in the fiscal first quarter. Non-GAAP earnings are expected to increase approximately 13.1% sequentially at the midpoint compared with 26% growth in the preceding quarter.

SNDK's non-GAAP gross margin expanded from 29.9% in the year-ago quarter to 85.1% in the fiscal first quarter of 2027, benefiting from favorable NAND pricing and higher volumes. Sandisk now expects non-GAAP gross margin of 84.5-85.5% in the fiscal second quarter. The marginal sequential contraction at the midpoint, coupled with expectations of only modest NAND price increases throughout the fiscal year, could raise concerns regarding the sustainability of elevated profitability. The inherently cyclical nature of the NAND industry further aggravates these risks.

Sandisk is also suffering from stiff competition from the likes of Micron MU, Seagate STX and Western Digital WDC. In the trailing 12-month period, Sandisk shares have jumped 218.3% while shares of Micron, Seagate and Western Digital have surged 215.2%, 99.3% and 93%, respectively. The broader sector dropped 5.8% over the same time frame.

Story Continues

SNDK's Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Sandisk Rides on Accelerating AI-Driven NAND Demand

Sandisk is benefiting from the growing adoption of NAND flash memory across AI infrastructure. Increasingly complex inference workloads, longer context lengths, multimodal inputs and agentic AI applications are driving demand for high-performance and high-capacity storage solutions. The company expects key-value (KV) cache applications to represent approximately one-third of the AI data center flash market by the end of the decade. Sandisk also expects the AI data center flash opportunity to approach the size of the entire present-day NAND industry, providing a significant long-term growth opportunity.

Sandisk's growing penetration of hyperscale data centers is a key growth catalyst. Fiscal first-quarter data center revenues surged 1,682% year over year and 61% sequentially to $4.8 billion, benefiting from strong customer partnerships, including three major U.S. hyperscalers. The company expects data center bit demand to increase approximately 40% year over year in calendar 2027 after more than doubling in 2026. Data centers are expected to account for more than 55% of industry bit demand in calendar 2027. Sandisk's expanding enterprise SSD portfolio and increasing allocation of NAND supply toward data centers position it to capitalize on this structural shift.

Sandisk's transition toward long-term customer partnerships through its NBMs is expected to improve earnings predictability and reduce exposure to traditional NAND industry cyclicality. SNDK has signed agreements with eight customers across the Data Center and Edge markets. The company's expanding presence across automotive, Internet of Things (IoT) and physical AI applications is expected to diversify its revenue base. Increasing storage content per device, growing adoption of premium smartphones and PCs, and deepening engagements with automotive customers are expected to support long-term growth. Sandisk believes automotive applications could eventually become one of the largest markets within its Edge business.

SNDK's Earnings Estimate Revision Shows Positive Trend

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for second-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings is currently pegged at $6.31 per share, up 10.5% over the past 30 days. The company reported earnings of $6.20 per share in the year-ago quarter.

Sandisk Corporation Price and Consensus

Sandisk Corporation price-consensus-chart | Sandisk Corporation Quote

The consensus estimates for fiscal 2027 earnings are currently pegged at $25.31 per share, up 6.8% over the past 30 days.

SNDK Shares Are Trading at a Discount

Sandisk has a Value Score of A, which suggests the stock is trading at a discount.

In terms of forward-12-month price/earnings (P/E), the company's shares are trading at 3.15X, lower than the broader sector's 14.95X, Micron's 3.85X, Seagate's 10.81X and Western Digital's 9.55X.

SNDK Stock's Valuation

Conclusion

Sandisk's long-term prospects remain promising, driven by accelerating AI-driven NAND demand, growing penetration of hyperscale data centers, long-term customer agreements and expanding automotive and IoT opportunities. Positive earnings estimate revisions and an attractive valuation further strengthen the investment case. However, moderating sequential growth, uncertainty surrounding the sustainability of elevated profit margins, weakness in consumer and low-end edge markets, stiff competition and the cyclical nature of the NAND industry warrant caution. Given these mixed factors, existing investors should hold SNDK shares, while prospective investors may be better off waiting for greater clarity on pricing trends and sustainable profitability before initiating a position.

Sandisk currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: MaxLinear Stock Drops 24% in a Month: Should You Buy it on the Dip?
news.Content:
MaxLinear MXL shares have dropped 24.3% in the past month, underperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's decline of 18.1%. The selloff appears to reflect investor concerns surrounding semiconductor manufacturing capacity constraints, deteriorating operating cash flow, rising debt levels, seasonal weakness in non-infrastructure markets and execution risks associated with next-generation optical connectivity products. However, accelerating demand for AI infrastructure, growing penetration of hyperscale data centers, strong order visibility extending into 2028, an expanding optical and electrical connectivity portfolio and improving operating leverage support MaxLinear's long-term growth prospects. So, what should investors do with MXL stock? Let's find out.

MXL's One-Month Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

MXL Suffers From Semiconductor Supply Constraints

MaxLinear is facing foundry capacity constraints amid accelerating demand for high-speed optical digital signal processors (DSPs). The company has acknowledged that DSP availability remains a significant bottleneck despite easing supply constraints for other optical components. Optical product lead times are currently around 26-28 weeks. Although strong demand underscores the competitiveness of MaxLinear's product portfolio, limited wafer availability could restrict its ability to fulfill customer orders, capitalize on growing AI infrastructure investments and accelerate market share gains. Rising manufacturing costs also pose risks to margin expansion.

Despite strong revenue growth and improving profitability, MaxLinear used approximately $13.6 million in operating activities during the third quarter of 2026. Substantial wafer prepayments, rising inventories and higher accounts receivable have increased working capital requirements. Although these investments are intended to support committed customer orders throughout 2027, negative operating cash flow raises concerns regarding the MXL's ability to translate robust revenue growth into sustainable cash generation.

MaxLinear's growing financing requirements remain a concern. Long-term debt increased to $164.1 million at the end of September 2026 from $123.6 million at the end of December 2025. Meanwhile, cash and cash equivalents totaled $81.1 million at the end of the third quarter. For the fourth quarter, MaxLinear expects interest and other expenses of $3.5-$4.3 million compared with $2.1 million on a GAAP basis in the third quarter. Although the company has expanded its revolving credit facility by $70 million to $200 million, increasing borrowing requirements and financing costs could weigh on profitability.

Story Continues

MXL Shares Trading at a Premium

MaxLinear shares are overvalued, as suggested by a Value Score of F.

MXL stock is trading at a trailing 12-month EV/Sales multiple of 7.06X compared with the broader sector's 6.23X. However, the stock is trading at a discount compared with Broadcom 's AVGO 17.17X, Credo Technology 's CRDO 13.99X and Marvell Technology 's MRVL 13.54X.

MXL Stock's Valuation

Strong AI Infrastructure Demand Aids MXL's Prospects

The sharp pullback reflects some profit-taking following the stock's massive year-to-date (YTD) surge, while investors assess whether MaxLinear can sustain its AI-driven growth trajectory. MXL shares have jumped 188.6% YTD, outperforming the broader sector's drop of 6%. The company has also outperformed peers, including the likes of Marvell Technology, Broadcom and Credo Technology. YTD, shares of Marvell have returned 70.8% while Broadcom and Credo have dropped 9.4% and 14.5%, respectively.

MaxLinear is benefiting from growing investments in AI infrastructure and accelerating demand for high-speed optical interconnects. Infrastructure revenues increased 47% sequentially and 210% year over year in the third quarter of 2026, emerging as the company's largest revenue category. Strong demand for MXL's Keystone 100G-per-lane PAM4 DSP platform, which supports 800G optical connectivity, is driving market share gains across multiple hyperscale customers. news.Title: Can AI Cloud Expansion Anchor NBIS' Ambitious 2027 Growth Expectation?
news.Content:
As demand for AI computing continues to accelerate, Nebius Group N.V. NBIS is investing heavily in GPU-powered data centers, high-performance networking and scalable cloud infrastructure to capture opportunities from hyperscalers, AI developers and enterprise customers. It expects to bring online more than 1 GW of new capacity annually starting in 2027, expanding its presence across the United States and Europe, with additional locations in Israel and other markets.

Nebius is shifting toward greater ownership of its data center infrastructure. Owned facilities can provide better control over construction schedules, capacity deployment and long-term operating economics compared with relying entirely on third-party colocation providers. During the third quarter, four new sites began generating revenue across the United States and Europe. It also delivered its largest quarter-over-quarter increase in active capacity to date. Another key factor supporting Nebius' 2027 outlook is its growing customer base. It reported signing approximately $12 billion in total contract value since the beginning of the third quarter.

Additionally, customer prepayments associated with its quarterly agreements covered more than 100% of the capital expenditure required for the related capacity. NBIS' long-term infrastructure agreement with Meta also highlights the scale of demand for its services. The agreement announced in March 2026 includes $12 billion of dedicated capacity over five years, with deliveries beginning in early 2027. Meta also committed to purchasing additional available computing capacity, potentially bringing the agreement's total value to about $27 billion. Nebius now expects 2027 revenue to quadruple to $12-$13 billion and aims to achieve pretax breakeven in fourth-quarter 2027. It plans to invest $40-$45 billion in CapEx to add more than 1 GW of capacity, with most coming from its own data centers, which offer stronger margins than colocation sites.

Customer prepayments and asset-backed financing are expected to fund 75-85% of this investment, with prepayments projected at $17-$20 billion in 2027. However, NBIS' 2026 revenue outlook has been adjusted to the lower end of its previous $3-$3.40 billion range because some third-party capacity is expected to become operational in the first half of 2027 rather than 2026. This delay creates a near-term execution challenge, but it could also shift additional revenue-generating capacity into 2027.

NBIS Faces Fierce Competition From CoreWeave & Hyperscalers

Story Continues

CoreWeave Inc . CRWV raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $13-$13.30 billion. Adjusted operating income is now projected at $1.28-$1.38 billion, a 26% increase at the midpoint. It expects 2026 capital expenditures of $37-$39 billion, raising the lower end of its previous $35 billion-$39 billion range. It also increased its year-end annualized revenue run-rate outlook to $20-$21 billion. Management expects to exceed 1.85 GW of active power by year-end. Fourth-quarter interest expenses are projected between $1.05 billion and $1.15 billion. CoreWeave expects adjusted net losses to decline meaningfully in 2027, with adjusted net income anticipated in the first half of 2028 and for full-year 2028.

However, third-party GPU capacity delays may weigh on near-term expansion. It expects operating margin to dip slightly, while calendar 2026 CapEx is projected at approximately $170 billion. Despite heavy investments, Microsoft expects to remain free cash flow positive in fiscal 2027. Microsoft's AI investments are converting into measurable commercial traction across its stack. news.Title: Intel Gains From Strong Operating Margin Growth: Will it Last?
news.Content:
Intel Corporation INTC is witnessing a significant improvement in operating profitability, supported by strong demand for server processors, better manufacturing efficiencies and disciplined expense management. The company's third-quarter 2026 results highlighted this progress, with non-GAAP operating income more than doubling year over year to $3.23 billion from $1.52 billion. Consequently, non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 19.6% from 11.2% in the year-ago quarter. There are several factors driving this growth.

Intel's Data Center and AI (DCAI) business was a major contributor to its third-quarter performance. Segment revenues increased nearly 80% year over year to $7.32 billion, reflecting robust demand for server CPUs across hyperscale, enterprise and neo-cloud customers. Higher production volumes and improved supply availability helped Intel capitalize on the expanding AI infrastructure market.

The segment's operating income increased to $3.04 billion from $964 million in the year-ago quarter. Correspondingly, its operating margin expanded to 41.5% from 23.4%. Higher revenues and lower operating expenses supported this improvement.

Intel's manufacturing execution is also contributing to better profitability. Higher yields, shorter production cycles and improved factory utilization have helped reduce production costs. However, despite these strengths, Intel continues to face challenges in its Client Computing and Physical AI Group. Segment revenues declined 5% year over year to $8.1 billion, as higher memory prices, limited availability and constrained IT budgets weighed on PC demand. The segment's operating income declined to $2.29 billion from $2.69 billion in the year-ago quarter. Its operating margin contracted to 28.2% from 31.6%.

Intel's improving server business, lower manufacturing costs and better operating discipline provide a foundation for further profitability gains. Nevertheless, the near-term outlook suggests that maintaining the third-quarter margin level may prove difficult. PC market weakness, supply constraints and continued foundry investments could create volatility in profitability.

How Are Competitors Faring?

Intel faces competition from Advanced Micro Devices AMD and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company TSM in the semiconductor space. During the third quarter, AMD's non-GAAP Operating income surged 75.3% to $3.92 billion, while operating margin improved to 29% from 24%. Non-GAAP operating expenses increased 29.3% to $3.56 billion as AMD expanded investments in data center silicon, systems and software.

In the third quarter, TSM's Operating profit rose 75% year over year in reporting-currency terms. Net income attributable to shareholders reached $23.86 billion, increasing 68.7% on that same local-currency basis. Strong growth in revenues in high-performance computing, smartphone, automotive and IoT boosted margin. However, sequential profit growth was tempered by the absence of Vanguard share disposal and valuation gains recorded in the second quarter.

Story Continues

news.Title: Credo's Optical Expansion: Can It Gain Ground Against Rivals?
news.Content:
Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd CRDO is boosting its presence in the optical connectivity market as rising AI infrastructure investments fuel demand for higher bandwidth, power-efficient and reliable networking solutions. While active electrical cables (AECs) remain its largest business, optics is emerging as the company's fastest-growing business. Credo is leveraging its vertically integrated platform to differentiate itself from competitors through enhanced system performance, reliability and cost efficiencies.

In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Credo's optical digital signal processor (DSP) business generated record revenues, supported by deployments across 50G and 100G-per-lane solutions. The company also recognized its first silicon photonics photonic integrated circuit (PIC) revenues following the DustPhotonics acquisition. Strong customer engagement for 1.6T DSPs, alongside design wins with two major industry players for silicon photonics PICs, bodes well for growth. Initial 1.6T DSP revenues are expected later this fiscal year.

In September 2026, Credo expanded its ZeroFlap optical transceiver portfolio with 224G-based 1.6T solutions, integrating its optical DSP, Kfir200 silicon photonics PIC and PILOT diagnostics platform. These solutions enable proactive detection and mitigation of network disruptions, accelerating cluster deployment and improving uptime. Production shipments of ZeroFlap Optics are underway, with additional customer ramps expected across hyperscalers and NeoClouds in fiscal 2027.

In October, Credo unveiled its 1.6T ZeroFlap active light cable, targeting connectivity distances of up to 50 meters while consuming roughly 30% less power than comparable AECs. Shipments are scheduled for 2027. Additionally, Credo's collaboration with Oracle secured Open Compute Project approval for two optical telemetry specifications in November, reinforcing its role in advancing industry-wide optical reliability standards.

Credo is also pursuing near-package optics opportunities, with confirmed design wins expected to ramp in fiscal 2028. Management believes vertical integration offers advantages in manufacturing costs and average selling prices compared with standards-based solutions.

Credo expects optical revenues to exceed $600 million in fiscal 2027, with ZeroFlap Optics, silicon photonics PICs and optical DSPs each contributing more than $100 million. Sustained innovation, expanding customer adoption and successful production ramps could strengthen Credo's competitive position in the rapidly expanding optical connectivity market.

Story Continues

Taking a Look at CRDO's Competitors

Broadcom AVGO is expanding its optical portfolio, driven by growing demand for higher bandwidth, scalability and power efficiency across AI data centers and large-scale computing clusters. The company continues to invest in optical DSPs, EMLs, VCSELs and continuous-wave lasers while expanding optical component production capacity to address rising semiconductor demand. Its third-generation TH6-Davisson co-packaged optics further strengthens its AI networking portfolio. Broadcom's AI networking revenues increased more than 2.5 times year over year in the third quarter of fiscal 2026. Management expects AI networking revenues to grow at a pace similar to XPUs over the next few years, supporting long-term growth prospects.

Marvell Technology MRVL is strengthening its optical connectivity portfolio on the back of expanding AI clusters and rising bandwidth requirements. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, demand for 800G optical DSPs remained strong, while its 1.6T business ramped up rapidly. Growing AI deployments across multiple data centers are expected to drive demand for coherent-enabled 1.6T ZR and ZR+ modules. Marvell raised its fiscal 2028 outlook for scale-up optics as customers evaluate near-packaged and co-packaged optical architectures. Its expanded NVIDIA partnership and proposed acquisition of Lumentum further strengthen its optical connectivity capabilities, positioning the company to capitalize on growing AI infrastructure investments.

news.Title: Not Apple. Not Microsoft. This Is the "Magnificent Seven" Stock I’d Buy for a 10-Year Hold.
news.Content:
There's no question that Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) and Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) are two great tech stocks. I wouldn't argue with anyone who bought them. But my favorite "Magnificent Seven" stock all year has been Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG), and nothing that has happened so far in 2026 has changed my mind.

Google's advertising business is still delivering

The biggest feather in Alphabet's cap remains its dominance in internet search. Google has 91% of the global search engine market share, which makes it an enormously profitable advertising platform.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Google Search revenue was $63.3 billion in the third quarter, up 12% from a year earlier. And the Google services division, which includes Search, YouTube, and other businesses, brought in $96.3 billion in revenue — a massive revenue stream.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

It's hard to believe that the market once considered artificial intelligence, including AI assistants like ChatGPT and Claude, a fundamental threat to Google's search business. But instead, Google has incorporated its Gemini AI assistant into its search engine, making it even better. It turned a potential threat into an advantage.

Google Cloud is becoming a powerhouse

Google Cloud doesn't bring in as much revenue as the company's advertising engine, but it's catching up fast . Google Cloud revenue was $30.7 billion in the third quarter, up 103% from a year ago. Its operating income more than tripled to $11.1 billion, and its operating margin was an impressive 36.2%.

And just as important, Google Cloud ended the quarter with a $561 billion backlog. Management expects more than 55% of that to convert into revenue within two years.

Alphabet's cloud business is more than just providing computing power to its customers. Google also designs its own custom chips, which it calls Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). These specialized processors are narrowly tailored for AI workloads, but for those specific tasks, they can compete directly with GPUs designed by Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD)for cost-efficiency and power. The company said TPU system sales made a meaningful contribution to third-quarter growth.

Anthropic adds another reason to like Alphabet

Anthropic 's (NASDAQ:ANT) successful IPO on Nov. 19 gave Alphabet another reason to celebrate. According to Anthropic's prospectus, Google has a 13.7% stake in the market's newest trillion-dollar company. And its relationship extends beyond the ownership stake. Anthropic has committed to spending at least $121.3 billion on Google's cloud computing services through July 2033.

Story Continues

Alphabet has a profitable advertising business, a rapidly expanding cloud operation, its own custom AI chips, and a valuable stake in one of the industry's most prominent AI companies. I liked Alphabet at the beginning of 2026 because it had multiple ways to win. Eleven months later, those opportunities look even better.

news.Title: Can Vicor Capitalize on the Shift to 800VDC AI Power Systems?
news.Content:
Vicor Corporation VICR is positioning its power delivery technology to address the increasing power requirements of artificial intelligence (AI) processors. The growing adoption of 800VDC power distribution in AI data centers is creating new opportunities for advanced power management solutions. Vicor believes that the main challenge lies not just in distributing power across the rack but also in efficiently delivering high current to AI processors at the point of load.

Vicor's second-generation Vertical Power Delivery (VPD) technology is designed to address this challenge by providing higher current density and current gain. The company stated that its proprietary ALL-FPA technology can reduce AI processor power loss by 10-15%. It also delivers more than 40 times the current gain of intermediate voltage regulators (IVRs) and three times the current density of voltage regulators, based on the company's claims. These capabilities could help AI processors meet their increasing power requirements while improving efficiency.

Vicor is seeing growing customer interest in its second-generation VPD solutions. During the third quarter of 2026, the company held meetings with major hyperscalers and OEMs, where the customers showed interest in its latest technology. It has also set up demonstration systems for its second-generation VPD and ALL-FPA technologies at its Silicon Valley applications laboratory. While discussions with potential customers are still at an early stage, the company sees opportunities to expand beyond its existing lead customer.

However, manufacturing capacity remains a near-term challenge. Strong demand is putting pressure on the company's existing Fab-1 facility, prompting plans to expand capacity through Fab-2 and Fab-3. Vicor expects initial equipment deployment at Fab-2 in the second quarter of 2027. As AI infrastructure demand increases and data centers move toward 800VDC power distribution, the company's ability to convert customer interest into orders and expand manufacturing capacity will be important to sustaining its growth.

How Competitors Fare Against VICR Stock

Vicor faces competition from companies operating in power management, power conversion and broader data center power delivery markets, including Monolithic Power Systems MPWR and Texas Instruments TXN.

Monolithic Power Systems is expanding its presence in AI data center power solutions. In the third quarter of 2026, MPWR's revenues increased 63% year over year, driven by strong demand in its enterprise data business. The company received its first orders for 48V power solutions and has started sampling gallium nitride based solutions for 800V data center architectures, complementing its existing silicon carbide based designs. MPWR expects the adoption of 800V architectures to begin contributing to revenues toward the end of 2027, with a larger ramp expected in 2028.

Story Continues

Texas Instruments is also benefiting from rising power requirements in data centers. In the third quarter of 2026, its data center business grew approximately 95% year over year. TXN offers a broad portfolio of analog and embedded processing chips that support power management, monitoring and other functions in data center systems. Management highlighted that increasing power density and higher voltage requirements in data centers are creating additional opportunities for its products. The company currently supplies approximately 10,000 different generic part numbers to the data center market and continues to develop new products for this end market. Its growing exposure to data centers could support further growth as AI infrastructure investments increase.

VICR's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Shares of Vicor have gained 29.6% year to date against the Zacks Electronics - Miscellaneous Components industry's decline of 35.4%.

VICR Forward 12-Month (P/S) Valuation Chart

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for VICR's 2026 and 2027 earnings implies year-over-year growth of 51% and 66.4%, respectively. The estimates for fiscal 2026 and 2027 have remained unchanged over the past 30 days.

news.Title: 輝達升級2.0版台股明年穩了？野村「老字號」團隊教戰：避開消費電子 改抱緊這些產業
news.Content:
隨著輝達 (NVDA-US)執行長黃仁勳重返掌舵，AI產業與台股能否迎來轉骨契機？逢野村鴻利基金滿37周年、野村投信今（24）日舉辦2027年台股投資展望記者會，估台灣出口在電子產品帶動下仍有支撐，2027年台股企業獲利成長率可望在30%。面對科技股短線震盪，AI規格升級趨勢未變，建議投資人聚焦半導體、電源散熱與高速傳輸等核心供應鏈，並透過長期穩健的選股策略掌握成長紅利。

今年以來外資對台股呈現大幅賣超，持股比例較高點下滑約1個百分點，引發市場擔憂。野村投信國內股票投資部副總經理姚郁如分析，部分外資與避險基金因今年獲利豐厚，提前於10月至11月關帳了結，加上單一持股上限規範，導致大型權值股遭調節。她強調，目前2027年企業獲利預估並未下修，供應鏈產能依舊極度緊俏，甚至有廠商訂單能見度已看到2028年，投資人無須過度恐慌。

針對AI需求與基礎建設進度，姚郁如表示，AI應用正從模型訓練延伸至推論與代理型AI，雲端服務營收與資料中心使用率是重要觀察指標。機構法人預估，大型雲端業者資本支出可望由2026年約1兆美元，增至2027年近1.8兆美元。雖然美國期中選舉後，部分地方政府對資料中心供電與環保審批轉趨嚴格，但AI基建已成美國經濟成長核心引擎，預期相關專案僅是小幅遞延而非砍單。

談及輝達人事波動對供應鏈的實質影響，姚郁如坦言，黃仁勳兼具創辦人、研發推手與超級業務員特質，與台灣供應鏈關係深厚，短期內財務背景接班人確實難以完全取代。不過，AI發展已是全球不可逆的趨勢，目前2027年基本面與訂單並未改變，評估台廠營運時應區分交期遞延與需求轉弱，持續追蹤設備交付與現金流，確認訂單轉化為實質獲利。

在2027年產業布局方面，姚郁如指出，隨著AI晶片複雜度提高，客製化晶片（ASIC）需求大幅擴張，至2027年高階ASIC比重甚至可望超越傳統GPU，帶動先進製程、封裝及系統級測試商機。此外，伺服器功耗飆升推動電源與散熱升級，預期2027年800V直流電源櫃開始出貨、液冷電源導入市場，高階銅箔基板、ABF載板與800G、1.6T光模組同樣具備強勁成長動能。

相較於AI硬體規格全面升級，姚郁如提醒，受記憶體與零組件漲價影響，2027年PC、手機等消費性電子需求仍較為平淡，科技產業成長步調不一，選股難度隨之提高。她認為，投資團隊必須深入比較企業的技術門檻、客戶認證進度與評價水準，避開缺乏競爭力的廠商，才能在波動加劇的市場中，精準辨識出真正受惠規格升級的贏家。

面對市場震盪，野村投信投資策略部資深協理黃韻潔表示，野村台股全系列基金加上ETF與代操，總規模已超過1兆元。旗下9檔國內股票型基金全數成立逾20年，平均年資約30年，截至2026年10月底規模合計1,972.8億元，堪稱台股基金老字號。今年適逢野村鴻利基金滿37周年、野村成長基金滿27周年及00935滿3周年，展現跨越景氣循環的深厚研究實力。

黃韻潔進一步說明，野村所有台股產品皆共享由平均年資超過20年團隊建立的股票池，並依不同風格滿足投資需求。例如旗艦級野村優質基金周轉率極低，強調長線波段從魚頭吃到魚尾；野村鴻運基金則在大小型股間靈活操作；野村台灣高股息基金至少配置6成高息股，在震盪市況中具備較佳抗跌力，建議投資人可善用多元配置平衡風險。

Getting the tax benefit would be a crucial element in its investment choice, the chipmaker said, and Arizona remained an option site. news.Title: Nasdaq Futures Plunge as Nvidia-Fueled Rally Fades
news.Content:
December Nasdaq 100 E-Mini futures (NQZ26) are down -1.80% this morning following the index's previous-session surge, as the initial euphoria over Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia faded and investors refocused on the broader risks surrounding the AI trade.

Nvidia (NVDA) slid over -5% in pre-market trading, giving back some of yesterday's jump, which added nearly $950 billion to its market capitalization. Other chipmakers and AI infrastructure stocks also retreated, with Micron Technology (MU) slumping over -7% and Intel (INTC) sinking more than -6%. Meanwhile, Anthropic (ANT) fell to near its $83 IPO price. Huang's return resolves Nvidia's leadership crisis but leaves unanswered other major questions that have been weighing on the AI trade, ranging from returns on massive AI investments to the prospect of stricter regulation and higher borrowing costs. Some investors are now questioning whether Monday's Nvidia-driven rally on Wall Street will prove to be a so-called dead cat bounce — a temporary rebound in a plunging market.

More News from Barchart

Dear Dollar Tree Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 24

Dear Dell Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 24

Stop Missing Market Moves: Get the FREE Barchart Brief – your midday dose of stock movers, trending sectors, and actionable trade ideas, delivered right to your inbox. Sign Up Now!

Treasuries rose across the curve as the pullback in AI-related stocks sent investors back into the safety of government debt. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield fell five basis points to 4.90%.

Elsewhere in markets, WTI crude fluctuated on Tuesday as traders weighed whether the latest diplomatic efforts to end the U.S.-Iran war would help sustain the recovery in oil supplies. Axios reported that U.S. Vice President JD Vance spoke with Qatar's prime minister on Monday about negotiations with Iran. Still, the U.S. and Iran are struggling to bridge their differences. Tehran said it would tighten its grip on the Strait of Hormuz until its demands are met and claimed that more tankers hit mines on Tuesday.

Later in the day, investors will focus on a fresh batch of U.S. economic data and earnings reports from several high-profile companies.

In yesterday's trading session, Wall Street's main stock indexes closed sharply higher as Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO supercharged the AI trade, turning an overnight bounce in stock futures into the biggest rally since April 2025. Nvidia (NVDA) popped over +31% and was the top percentage gainer in the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq 100 after the chip giant's board announced Huang's immediate reinstatement as president and CEO. Also, chipmakers and other AI-related stocks rallied on the news of Huang's return, with CoreWeave (CRWV) jumping over +22% and Micron Technology (MU) surging more than +19%. In addition, Arm Holdings (ARM) climbed over +16% after the company announced that CEO Rene Haas extended his contract to remain at the helm through 2033. On the bearish side, CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) slumped more than -8% and was the top percentage loser in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 after agreeing to acquire Zscaler in an all-stock deal.

Story Continues

Economic data released on Monday showed that U.S. business activity grew at the slowest pace in four months in November as elevated prices, shipping delays, and capacity constraints weighed on manufacturers and service providers. The S&P Global flash U.S. manufacturing PMI fell to 54.5 in November, in line with expectations, while the S&P Global flash services PMI slid to 54.7, weaker than expectations of 55.6.

"A key concern is the elevated cost of living and resulting pressures on affordability, and the survey price gauges remain at levels consistent with inflation running well above the Fed's 2% target in the coming months," said Chris Williamson, chief business economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence.

New York Fed President John Williams said on Monday that the central bank still has "work to do" to curb inflation, which remains too high. "We must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2% goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis," Williams said.

U.S. rate futures are currently pricing in a 97.6% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike and a 2.4% probability of a 50-basis-point rate hike at the December FOMC meeting.

Today, investors will focus on the U.S. Conference Board's consumer confidence index, which is set to be released in a couple of hours. Economists forecast that the board's consumer confidence index will rise to 92.4 in November from 91.7 in October.

The U.S. S&P/CS HPI Composite - 20 n.s.a. will also be released today. Economists project the index to rise +2.7% y/y in September, matching August's pace.

The Richmond Fed manufacturing index will be released today as well. Economists expect the index to come in at -2 in November, unchanged from October.

On the earnings front, server maker Dell Technologies (DELL), analog chipmaker Analog Devices (ADI), enterprise software provider Workday (WDAY), and PC and printer maker HP Inc. (HPQ) are among the prominent companies scheduled to report quarterly results today.

In the bond market, the yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury note is at 4.90%, down -0.93%.

The Euro Stoxx 50 Index is down -0.41% this morning, giving back some of the previous session's gains as investors take profits and await fresh catalysts. Mining stocks led the declines as copper and gold prices pulled back following Monday's rally. Technology stocks also slid as optimism sparked by Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia faded. At the same time, healthcare stocks advanced, boosted by a more than +5% jump in Sanofi (SAN.FP) after it agreed to acquire U.S. drugmaker Insmed for $41 billion. A survey released on Tuesday showed that German business confidence strengthened further in November, reaching its highest level in more than three years. "Companies were happier with their current business conditions and revised their expectations for the next six months upward," said Clemens Fuest, president of the Ifo Institute. Elsewhere, Eurozone government bond yields declined on Tuesday, tracking the drop in Treasury yields. In other corporate news, Balfour Beatty (BBY.LN) gained over +4% after the infrastructure group raised its full-year guidance amid improving U.K. margins and growing U.S. data-center demand.

Germany's Ifo Business Climate Index was released today.

The German November Ifo Business Climate Index stood at 90.6, stronger than expectations of 90.5.

Asian stock markets settled in the green today. China's Shanghai Composite Index ($CHSC) closed up +0.27%, and Japan's Nikkei 225 Stock Index ($NKY) closed up +3.91%.

China's Shanghai Composite Index closed slightly higher today, lagging a strong rally among its regional peers fueled by Jensen Huang's return to the helm of Nvidia. Semiconductor and other AI-related stocks were among the biggest gainers, though they gave up most of their earlier advances by the close. Zeng Wanping at Beijing Monolith Fund Management said Huang's return would benefit Chinese companies in Nvidia's supply chain, but cautioned that the U.S. was unlikely to ease its chip restrictions on China. In the latest sign of Washington's restrictive stance, the U.S. Commerce Department on Monday added seven companies in Singapore, Thailand, and Malaysia, including Alibaba-owned Apex Enterprise Solutions, to its trade blacklist as part of efforts to curb China's access to advanced U.S. chips. Meanwhile, China extended the suspension of its ban on exports of several critical minerals to the U.S., preserving a key component of the fragile trade truce despite mounting technology-related tensions. In corporate news, Cathay Pacific fell over -2% in Hong Kong after conglomerate Swire Pacific announced plans to sell 252.66 million shares of the airline through a share placement. Investor attention this week is on China's industrial profits data for October.

Japan's Nikkei 225 Stock Index closed sharply higher today as Jensen Huang's return to the helm of Nvidia reignited enthusiasm for the AI trade. Chip-related and other AI-linked stocks jumped, tracking the overnight rally in their U.S. peers. Chip-testing equipment maker Advantest surged over +12%, memory-chip maker Kioxia Holdings climbed nearly +10%, and tech investor SoftBank Group rose more than +4%, providing a significant boost to the Nikkei. The benchmark posted its biggest one-day percentage gain since July 31. Meanwhile, Japanese government bond yields fell on Tuesday as lower oil prices eased inflation concerns. On the economic front, a survey showed on Tuesday that Japan's manufacturing activity expanded at a slightly faster pace in November as stronger demand for semiconductors and electronics boosted output and export orders. In corporate news, Mercari gained over +5% after SMBC Nikko Securities upgraded the stock to Outperform from Neutral. Investor focus this week is on Japan's Tokyo core CPI for November, a leading indicator of nationwide inflation trends, with the annual rate expected to accelerate to a 16-month high of 2.9%. That would strengthen the case for an interest-rate hike by the Bank of Japan next month. Ahead of the inflation release, investors will closely watch remarks from BOJ board member Naoki Tamura, who has advocated raising interest rates sooner rather than later amid upside risks to inflation. The Nikkei Volatility Index, which takes into account the implied volatility of Nikkei 225 options, closed down -4.72% at 31.51.

The Japanese November S&P Global Manufacturing PMI (preliminary) stood at 53.7, stronger than expectations of 53.5.

Pre-Market U.S. Stock Movers

Nvidia (NVDA) slid over -5% in pre-market trading, giving back some of yesterday's surge sparked by Jensen Huang's return to the helm of the company.

Other chipmakers and AI infrastructure stocks retreated in pre-market trading as enthusiasm for the AI trade waned. Micron Technology (MU) slumped over -7%, Intel (INTC) sank more than -6%, and Sandisk (SNDK) fell over -5%.

Cloud-computing stocks declined in pre-market trading. Nebius Group N.V. (NBIS), CoreWeave (CRWV), and Applied Digital (APLD) each dropped -3% or more.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) tumbled more than -11% in pre-market trading after the IT infrastructure company's FQ1 revenue guidance failed to impress investors.

Insmed (INSM) jumped over +14% in pre-market trading after Sanofi agreed to acquire the company for $41 billion.

news.Title: 台股狂飆全漲停！他揭1壞消息「笑不出來」股民全懂：好想哭
news.Content:
台股今（24日）上演史詩級反彈，終場大漲3310點收在40122點，不少個股更攻上漲停，然而一名網友卻坦言，雖然今天好消息是手上的股票全部漲停，但壞消息卻是帳面損益「全部都還是綠色的」，笑不出來的心情瞬間引發大量股民共鳴，紛紛直呼「好想哭」並分享各自的套牢處境。

原PO在Threads發文，簡短寫下反差心聲，先是提到「今天好消息：我的股票全部都漲停了」，緊接著卻無奈表示「今天壞消息：全部都還是綠色的」，即便單日攻上漲停板，先前累積的跌幅仍讓整體損益尚未翻紅。

貼文曝光後迅速吸引數千人按讚與留言討論，不少投資人對這種「漲停卻無感」的處境感同身受。有人透露自己帳面仍虧損達19%甚至34%，也有人表示還得再好幾根漲停才能由負轉正，甚至有人直呼「要連漲停10天才有感」，也有人自嘲買在相對高點卻只有幾張；同時也有網友安慰原PO，至少沒有在噴漲前夕殺低賣出，算是回血一大段，「你該慶幸你沒賣，昨天賣掉的已經在屋頂」、「更壞消息 夜盤又崩了」。

回顧台股24日盤勢，大盤終場狂飆3310點、漲幅達8.99%，成交量放大至4194.05億元，權值股台積電全日鎖死漲停收在2230元，收盤時仍有逾2萬張買單排隊搶買，多檔正2 ETF漲幅也逼近2成。在指數強彈與個股漲停的熱鬧氣氛下，股民們「漲停卻還在綠」的慘況，意外成為話題。

news.Title: 快訊》台指期夜盤失守4萬大關！一度重摔988點 輝達盤前慘跌逾5％
news.Content:
黃仁勳回歸輝達執行長後，該公司單日大漲31.48%，台股今（24）天也受到激勵，猛漲3310.46點，收在40122.35點。然而，周二輝達盤前下跌超過5%，部分AI企業也出現下滑的趨勢。台指期夜盤稍早雖延續漲勢，一度上漲576點，報40900點，隨後卻一路震盪走低，一度暴跌988點，報39336點，失守4萬點大關，截至晚間8點左右，下跌624點，暫報39700點。

隨著市場謹慎情緒回升，科技股反彈行情未能延續。周二美股期貨再度走低。納斯達克100指數期貨下跌2%，而道瓊工業平均指數期貨下跌259點，跌幅0.5%。標普500指數期貨下跌1%。周二盤前交易中，美國半導體股出現下跌的情況，稍微回吐了前一天因黃仁勳重新擔任輝達執行長而引發的漲勢。

另Anthropic於美股盤前跌幅一度擴大到6.7%，暫報81.71美元，跌破IPO時的發行價。美股盤前表現疲軟，是否會對台股產生影響，還有待後續關注。

黃仁勳回歸雖推動那指單日大漲逾6%，但高盛科技板塊專家Peter Callahan表示，客戶仍在追問「這是真的嗎？」。多頭認為空倉部位已經基本出清，調整主要由情緒推動；空頭則擔憂AI投資回報率、監管調查及行業增長前景，認為市場風險尚未出清。

news.Title: 台積電226億美元新廠落腳德州？能否減稅成關鍵
news.Content:
據《路透》周二(24日)報導，台積電(2330-TW)(TSM-US)旗下子公司正評估斥資226億美元，在美國德州布拉索斯郡(Brazos County)興建先進晶片製造設施，但能否取得財產稅減免，將是決定投資案是否落腳當地的關鍵。亞利桑那州仍是競爭選址之一。

根據周一提交德州主計長辦公室的申請文件，規劃中的廠區占地超過3,200英畝，將包含一座或多座晶圓廠，以及相關支援基礎設施，採用2奈米或更先進製程，生產供人工智慧(AI)、高效能運算(HPC)及行動裝置使用的晶片。

台積電子公司是依據德州「就業、能源、技術與創新」(JETI)計畫提出申請，希望透過財產稅課稅限制取得租稅優惠，降低在當地設廠的成本。

不過，德州尚未確定取得這筆投資。台積電在文件中指出，選擇在亞利桑那州擴建，可能享有「特定營運與經濟優勢」。該子公司總部位於亞利桑那州，台積電也自2024年底起在當地營運半導體製造廠。

文件明確表示，能否獲得此次申請的財產稅優惠，將決定台積電是否承諾推動德州投資案。依照申請內容估算，這項計畫預計在未來40年間，直接創造至少2,099個工作機會。

布拉索斯郡政府表示，目前申請仍屬評估程序的一環，計畫須取得必要核准，並由台積電作出最終投資決定。JETI申請須經德州主計長審查，以及州長與當地學區董事會批准。

news.Title: 反彈無力 比特幣跌破6萬美元大關 資金外流與升息疑慮夾擊
news.Content:
受美股科技股回檔與宏觀政策不確定性影響，加密貨幣市場再度迎來劇烈震盪。比特幣在周二(24日)亞洲交易時段跌破 60,000 美元大關，最低下探至 59,404 美元，較前一日高點回檔將近 8%，幾乎抹平輝達(NVDA-US)董事會宣布恢復黃仁勳執行長職務後所引發的短線漲幅。

根據 CoinGlass 數據，過去 24 小時內加密貨幣全網爆倉金額高達 8.26 億美元。

市場資金顯現持續撤出跡象，美國比特幣現貨 ETF 周一錄得 5.697 億美元的單日淨流出，已連續四周呈資金淨流出態勢，累計撤離金額超過 40 億美元。

針對市場反彈無力，做市商 GSR 共同創辦人 Rich Rosenblum 表示，黃仁勳復職所帶動的反彈對比特幣上行空間有限，因為風險資產走揚將使美國聯準會(Fed)在 12 月升息更加順理成章。

BitMEX 共同創辦人 Arthur Hayes 認為，美股上漲對加密貨幣持倉並非好事，市場需要美股修正以迫使聯準會重新啟動印鈔政策。

此外，傳統避險資產黃金近期正經歷近 44 年來最嚴重的拋售潮。Commodity Report 分析師 Lukas Kuemmerle 指出，這是一場起源於 AI 科技股的流動性事件，進而引發骨牌效應，將資金從各類市場中抽離。DHF Capital 執行長 Bas Kooijman 分析，聯準會發出的鷹派訊號與科技股重挫交織，促使投資人拋售資產以籌集現金。

在鏈上數據方面，鏈上分析平台 CryptoQuant 貢獻分析師警告，持有至少 155 天的長期持有者(LTH)平均虧損已達 33% 並出現投降式拋售，雖然歷史上這常接近局部底部，但拋售過程恐持續並限制未來的反彈空間。

news.Title: Prediction: This Is What Will Happen to Broadcom’s Stock Price in December
news.Content:
Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) stock has been crushed in recent months, falling 35% from the 52-week high it reached on June 3, amid dwindling confidence in the semiconductor sector.

Chip stocks, which have delivered incredible gains over the past four years amid the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, have taken a big beating lately. The hotter-than-expected inflation, a hawkish Federal Reserve, and the sustainability of the heavy spending on AI data center infrastructure have led investors to press the sell button and book profits. This explains why Broadcom has taken a big beating lately.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Investors, however, will be looking for a turnaround in the stock's fortunes when it releases its fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter results on Dec. 9. Let's see if the upcoming quarterly results could indeed give Broadcom stock a much-needed boost.

Image source: Getty Images.

Broadcom could crush expectations once again

Broadcom has beaten Wall Street's earnings per share (EPS) expectations in each of the last four quarters. Broadcom's AI business has played a central role in its outperformance, which isn't surprising as it is the market share leader in custom AI processors, and is also benefiting from the booming demand for networking components.

The company reportedly controls an estimated 60% of the fast-growing custom AI processor market, according to Counterpoint Research. Not surprisingly, Broadcom's shipments of custom AI processors increased by 3.5x year over year in the third quarter of fiscal 2026. Meanwhile, its revenue from sales of AI networking components is also increasing at a solid pace, jumping 2.5x year over year in fiscal Q3.

Broadcom expects $34.8 billion in fiscal Q4 revenue, an improvement of 93% from the year-ago period. That will be a significant jump over the 28% growth it delivered in the same period last year. The company's AI revenue is expected to have increased by 236% year over year in the previous quarter to $21.7 billion.

However, Broadcom's revenue could exceed expectations. That's because the demand for its AI chips is exceeding supply. It has been working to secure additional supply, which is why its financial performance may be better than expected. Moreover, Broadcom sees phenomenal growth in its AI revenue over the next two fiscal years.

Story Continues

It anticipates AI revenue will almost double in fiscal 2027 to $115 billion, compared with the fiscal 2026 estimate of $58 billion. What's more, it sees $230 billion in AI chip revenue in fiscal 2028. However, these estimates are based on the supply that it has already secured, which explains why Broadcom management noted on the September earnings call that it may increase guidance as it strengthens its supply chain.

On the other hand, the demand for optical networking components that Broadcom designs is "far surpassing supply out there in the industry." This supply shortage should ideally lead to higher prices for optical networking components, which is why Goldman Sachs estimates that optical networking revenue will increase from an estimated $15 billion this year to $154 billion in 2028. The investment bank also notes that an increase in average selling price (ASP) could boost the gross margins of optical component suppliers.

All this suggests Broadcom's revenue and earnings could once again surpass Wall Street's expectations when it reports results next month. Additionally, the company has dropped enough hints that it could continue to upgrade its guidance as supply chain improvements materialize. As such, Broadcom's guidance may surpass expectations, setting the company up for a strong rally in December.

The cheap valuation and strong earnings growth can help Broadcom end the year on a high

Analysts predict a 71% jump in Broadcom's fiscal 2026 EPS to $11.65, well above the 33% average earnings growth estimated for S&P 500 companies. The chip designer is expected to post another solid 66% increase in EPS next year to $19.33, again exceeding the 17% jump that S&P 500 companies are expected to deliver. The fiscal 2028 EPS estimate is also quite impressive.

AVGO EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts

Broadcom's forward earnings multiple of 16 is slightly lower than the S&P 500 index's forward earnings multiple of 18. This semiconductor stock should ideally be trading at a premium valuation due to its market-beating EPS growth. Assuming Broadcom trades at 25 times earnings after a year and its EPS reaches $19.33 in fiscal 2027 (based on the consensus estimate seen in the chart above), its stock price could reach $483.

That implies a potential 54% jump in a year. Analysts, however, are more upbeat about Broadcom's performance, as its 12-month median price target of $522 implies 66% gains. All this suggests that Broadcom could be a solid buy ahead of its quarterly report, as strong results could supercharge the stock in December and pave the way for a much-improved performance in 2027.

news.Title: Should UCTT Be in Your Portfolio After Plummeting 51% in Six Months?
news.Content:
Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. 's UCTT shares have plunged 51% in the past six months compared with the industry's decline of 44.3% despite improved quarterly performance and strengthening growth prospects. Robust semiconductor equipment demand, fueled by accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure investments, is creating significant growth opportunities for the company.

However, elevated working capital requirements, supply-chain constraints, customer concentration and aggressive capacity expansion remain concerns. With the stock witnessing a significant correction, let us delve a little deeper to gauge whether investors should capitalize on the buying opportunity or remain on the sidelines.

Six-Month UCTT Stock Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

AI-Driven Semiconductor Demand Bodes Well for UCTT

Ultra Clean is benefiting from increasing investments in advanced logic, high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and gate-all-around transistor technologies, driving demand for its critical semiconductor manufacturing subsystems.

In the third quarter of 2026, revenues surged 48.8% year over year to a record $759 million, while adjusted earnings jumped 379.2% to $1.15 per share. Products segment revenues increased 53.2% to $681.9 million, while Services revenues rose 18.6% to $77.1 million.

Ultra Clean's exposure to leading semiconductor equipment manufacturers, including Lam Research Corporation LRCX and Applied Materials Inc. AMAT, positions it favorably to capitalize on increasing wafer fabrication equipment spending.

UCT 3.0 Strategy to Drive Long-Term Growth

Ultra Clean's UCT 3.0 strategy emphasizes customer collaboration, technological innovation and operational efficiencies. The company secured eight new product development program wins during the third quarter across etch, deposition and lithography applications, which should increase its content per semiconductor manufacturing tool.

UCTT is targeting $4 billion in annualized revenue capacity by the first quarter of 2027. Management's target of achieving a 20% gross margin at approximately $4 billion in annual revenues reflects significant operating leverage opportunities.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Ultra Clean expects revenues of $800-$860 million and adjusted earnings of $1.11-$1.35 per share, indicating sustained business momentum.

Weak Cash Flow and Rising Investments Remain Concerns

However, Ultra Clean's aggressive production ramp is weighing on cash generation. Operating cash outflow was $42.3 million in the third quarter, while inventories increased to $723.3 million from $390.9 million at the end of 2025.

The company's additional capacity expansion plans entail incremental investments of $80-$100 million through 2027 and 2028. Equity issuances to support its growth initiatives also pose shareholder dilution risks.

Moreover, Lam Research and Applied Materials collectively accounted for 61% of quarterly revenues, exposing UCTT to fluctuations in their spending patterns. Persistent component shortages could also impede near-term growth.

Story Continues

Should Investors Buy UCTT Stock?

Ultra Clean's improving earnings trajectory, expanding manufacturing capabilities and growing exposure to AI-related semiconductor investments underpin its long-term growth prospects. Despite near-term cash flow and execution challenges, the significant share price correction offers an attractive entry point for investors willing to withstand volatility. Investors with the ability to tolerate elevated risk may consider staying invested in UCTT for long-term growth.

UCTT carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Xiaomi's Sales Slip After Memory Shortages Weigh on Smartphones
news.Content:
(Bloomberg) -- Xiaomi Corp. ( 1810.HK ) reported a revenue contraction for the third quarter in a row while it grapples with a global memory crunch that's hobbled the world's biggest smartphone makers.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Nvidia Board Reinstated CEO Without Consulting Management

Stocks Jump Most Since April 2025 as Huang Is Back: Markets Wrap

Yardeni Cuts S&P 500 Target Again, Says Bear Market Is Unlikely

The Beijing-based maker of smartphones and cars saw revenue drop 5.2% in the three months ended September to 107.2 billion yuan ($16.1 billion). Analysts on average expected a 6% decline. Net income tumbled 68% to 3.9 billion yuan during the same period.

AI's voracious demand for memory chips has created a dire shortage of conventional chips that's hitting consumer electronics makers around the globe. That's compelled smartphone makers from Apple Inc. to Xiaomi to raise prices on their devices.

Xiaomi's budget smartphones have been especially vulnerable to skyrocketing memory costs, forcing the company to sharply curtail production of low-end devices to stem losses. Its smartphone shipments have been shrinking since the first quarter this year, sliding nearly 30% in the third quarter versus the overall market's 20% decline, according to market tracker Counterpoint Research.

Still, Counterpoint says a double-digit increase in Xiaomi's average selling prices has stabilized its smartphone revenue, as it shifts away from entry-level devices toward premium phones.

Xiaomi's latest Xiaomi 18 Fold, released at the end of the third quarter, is priced at more than 10,000 yuan and is contending with Apple's iPhone Duo and similar gadgets from Huawei Technologies Co. in the premium segment.

The company also launched a new line of hybrid sports utility vehicles in the third quarter. Robust initial demand for the SkyNomad series are expected to help offset the company's flagging electric-vehicle deliveries.

news.Title: Tesla Leads Goldman's Hedge Fund Short List With $26.4 Billion in Bearish Bets
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Tesla ( TSLA , Financials ) had the highest hedge fund short position among S&P 500 firms , Goldman Sachs said, with $26.4 billion in outstanding short interest.Palantir Technologies was second at $10.3 billion and Walmart third at $9 billion, the bank's analysis found.Goldman looked studied holdings at 1,001 hedge funds with $5.1 trillion in gross equity positions at the start of the fourth quarter of 2026.The ranking is based on the firms with the greatest dollar value of short interest, not the greatest percentage of shares sold short.To ensure there is enough liquidity, Goldman excluded companies having more than 10% short interest in their float-adjusted shares.Other big names were Exxon Mobil at $8.5 billion, Costco Wholesale at $8 billion and Palo Alto Networks at $7.5 billion.Moderna was next at $7.4 billion. Western Digital and Lumentum posted $7.1 billion and $6.8 billion, respectively. Rounding out the top 10 was Lam Research with $6.6 billion in short interest.Short selling enables investors to benefit from dropping share prices, but the positions can also serve as a buffer against hazards in the overall portfolio.The statistics provide a snapshot of positions around the start of October and may not reflect current hedge fund exposure.Investors will look to later holdings announcements and short-interest updates for changes in positioning among large S&P 500 equities.

news.Title: 反向ETF也翻車！今年還沒完　台股違約交割34.8億達去年3倍
news.Content:
台股近來震盪劇烈，連帶違約交割連日連環爆。證交所今（24）日公告，反向型ETF元大台灣50反1（00632R）遭國泰板橋券商通報違約交割，金額為3,946.9萬元。

今年前10個月累計34.8億元　為去年3倍

金管會統計顯示，今年前10個月的違約交割金額已達34.8億元，去年全年僅約11億元，今年累計金額是去年的3倍。

證期局副局長黃仲豪24日在例會上坦言，違約交割比重確實「有一點增加」，並指出有兩大原因。首先是市場成交值大幅攀升，再者是外在不確定因素較多，價格波動幅度跟著放大。他提醒，投資人若沒有事先備妥交割款，在行情劇烈波動時，比較容易碰上違約交割。

news.Title: Chip stocks led a $3 trillion comeback on Monday — now comes Turnaround Tuesday: Chart of the Day
news.Content:
Wall Street threw its biggest party in more than a year and a half on Monday. History says the cleanup could take a while.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) jumped nearly 5%, its best day since April 2025 , and added about $3 trillion in market value. Only that April 9 rebound added more.

The spark was Nvidia ( NVDA ). Its board brought back Jensen Huang after 12 days , and the stock soared 31%, adding about $950 billion. That's the biggest one-day gain any company has ever posted , more than double the old record.

President Trump took a bow. "I don't think anybody could revive the stock like it's being revived right now," he said.

Chip stocks did the rest. All 62 in a Yahoo Finance basket rose, adding about $2 trillion a week after their worst week since 2001 . SK Hynix ( SKHY ) and Micron ( MU ) each jumped about 20%. Six companies, from Alphabet ( GOOGL ) to Tesla ( TSLA ), added $100 billion or more.

Not everyone got an invitation. CrowdStrike ( CRWD ) fell 9% after agreeing to buy Zscaler ( ZS ) for $43.9 billion. Anthropic ( ANT ) slipped as its options and leveraged ETFs debuted , though General Catalyst managing director Madhu Namburi isn't worried. "I do believe this could be the first $10 trillion company," he said on Deirdre Bosa Live.

Now comes Turnaround Tuesday

The old Wall Street saying that Tuesday undoes Monday has a point. In the 20 times since 1993 that the SPDR S&P 500 ETF ( SPY ) opened Monday 2% or more higher, it rose the next day only 9 times, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. By Friday, it was a coin flip.

Patience usually paid. A year later, SPY was higher in 17 of the 20 cases, with a typical gain of about 26%.

The bad cases were really bad, though. In a quarter of them, SPY fell 12% or more within three months. Five of the 20 came in the fall of 2008.

Speed may be on the bulls' side

The S&P 500 took just 33 trading days to go from a record to a correction, and only three of the 10 fastest drops like that became bear markets, Carson Group's Ryan Detrick noted . The catch is that 33 days also matches October 2007, the start of a bear market that more than halved the index.

Watch Friday's low, about 6,880 on the S&P 500. Half of those 20 big Mondays slipped back below the prior Friday's low within three months .

Naveen Rao, CEO of Unconventional AI, reached for an older comparison on Deirdre Bosa Live. "Nvidia is so big and baked into so much of the growth of the US right now," he said. "It was a little bit like the banking crisis. You know, back in the 2008 time frame."

Internal AI tools helped analyze interview transcripts, research, and draft this post. Humans reviewed, edited, and fact-checked this post before publication.
