news.Title: Marvell Stock Fell Almost 12% in a Single Day. I'd Consider Buying Shares Now.
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) stock fell almost 12% on Nov. 20 to close at $122.28. The chipmaker's shares hadn't closed this low since April. And they stood at around 39% of the record close they hit on June 4 -- $316.43.

Most of that slide happened over the past month. Marvell closed around $252 on Oct. 28, the last trading day before news broke that it was in talks to buy optical parts maker Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE). The stock had lost over half its value by Nov. 20.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Shares rebounded sharply on Nov. 23, but I think the sell-off has still gone further than the business justifies. At this price, the stock is valued as if Marvell's growth was about to fade into something ordinary. Its data center business is doing the opposite, so I'd buy the shares now.

Image source: Getty Images.

Data center growth keeps speeding up

Data centers account for most of Marvell's sales. They made up 79% of its revenue in the fiscal second quarter of 2027 (the period ended Aug. 1, 2026).

Showing how quickly demand has picked up, Marvell's data center revenue reached around $2.17 billion in fiscal Q2, up 46% year over year. That was faster than the 27% growth in fiscal Q1 and the 21% growth in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. Plus, management guided for data center revenue to grow around 75% from a year earlier in the fiscal third quarter, which ended Oct. 31. And profits are keeping up with sales. Marvell's non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share climbed 40% year over year in fiscal Q2.

The fourth-quarter report, released in March, was still Marvell's latest earnings update the last time the stock closed this low, on April 9. Since then, the data center business has moved from 21% growth to a guided 75%, but the share price has landed right back near where it was.

Marvell's data center business brought in around $2.2 billion for all of fiscal 2024. In fiscal Q2 alone, it brought in almost as much.

Marvell reports fiscal third-quarter results on Dec. 1, which will show if data center sales met that guide. But on Nov. 2, the company said preliminary total revenue for the quarter was consistent with its guidance.

Priced close to an average stock

At around $146, Marvell's price-to-earnings ratio is about 20 using the adjusted per-share earnings analysts expect for fiscal 2028 (it ends in January 2028). For comparison, FactSet puts the forward price-to-earnings ratio of the S&P 500 at about 17, based on expected earnings for the next 12 months. Marvell's fiscal 2028 goes a few months further out than that period, but the two multiples are not far apart.

Story Continues

So investors are now paying only a little more than a market-average price for Marvell's expected earnings.

Marvell's own plan for fiscal 2028 is far from average. Management's outlook, given at an Oct. 6 investor day, calls for around $20 billion in revenue that year. That would be about 67% above the roughly $12 billion it expects this fiscal year. I'd expect a market-average price for a company whose growth was slowing, not accelerating.

Sure, chip demand often runs in cycles, so a chipmaker arguably deserves a lower valuation multiple than a business with steadier demand. But at about 20 times expected earnings, I think a lot of that risk is already in the price.

Is the Lumentum deal a reason to wait?

Much of the fall followed the Lumentum news, and it's clear why. Under the deal announced on Nov. 2, Lumentum shareholders will get 4.5 Marvell shares for every share they hold, and current Marvell shareholders will have around 67% of the merged company. Each existing share will be a smaller part of a bigger business.

But management expects the deal to lift adjusted earnings per share in the first year after closing, and it sees a path to over $1 billion in yearly cost savings. And Marvell expects to close the deal sometime in the first half of calendar 2028, so those new shares are probably more than a year off.

Sure, a deal this big can go wrong, and AI spending by Marvell's largest customers could slow before it closes.

But the data center business keeps accelerating, and the stock trades close to a market-average price for its expected earnings. I think around 20 times earnings is a good price for a company growing so fast.

I'd buy Marvell stock here. With the stock swinging this hard from one day to the next, though, I'd space my buying out over the next several months.

news.Title: 助攻台積電全球擴產　Tokyo Electron獲2026卓越量產支援獎
news.Content:
晶圓代工龍頭台積電加速推進全球產能擴張，背後關鍵設備供應鏈角色備受矚目，日系半導體設備大廠Tokyo Electron（TEL）在2026年台積電年度供應鏈管理論壇中，憑藉研發支援與敏捷供貨能力，正式獲頒「2026年卓越量產支援獎」，成為推升晶圓代工龍頭全球布局的重要推手。

台積電年度供應鏈管理論壇旨在表揚在創新、技術合作、全球生產支援、綠色製造、自動化系統及晶圓廠建設管理等領域表現突出的合作夥伴。TEL在2026年期間對台積電業務發展做出重大貢獻，尤其在面對全球擴產需求時，展現出靈活的供應調度與研發支援實力，協助台積電順利推進產能版圖。

隨著製程技術難度持續拉升，晶圓廠對設備穩定度與製程整合的要求更趨嚴格。TEL透過廣泛的產品組合與全球支援網絡，提供涵蓋多元製程的技術解決方案與技術服務，確保客戶生產線維持穩定運作，降低擴產過程中的量產磨合風險。

面對半導體技術持續演進，TEL未來將持續投入研發計畫，並透過強化全球生產與技術服務能量，深化與晶圓代工大廠的技術合作，支撐半導體製程的長期發展與量產需求。

news.Title: 〈兆豐金法說〉輝達狂飆36%帶旺台股！企金與海外放款雙位數成長 明年股利配發率站穩7成
news.Content:
輝達（NVDA-US) 創辦人黃仁勳閃電回鍋激勵輝達股價昨 (23) 日一度瘋漲逾 36%，帶動台股今 (24) 日強勢反攻大漲近 9%。兆豐金控 (2886-TW) 今舉行 2026 年第三季線上法說會，透露受惠 AI 需求暢旺與半導體擴張，兆豐銀行前三季企金與海外放款均呈雙位數成長，推升集團獲利創同期新高，股利配發率亦穩守 7 成。

針對市場高度關注的黃仁勳回鍋影響，兆豐金總經理張傳章表示，短期內有助於穩定市場對輝達經營方向及 AI 供應鏈訂單的信心，進而帶動科技股估值與投資人風險偏好回升，這對證券、財富管理及資產管理等業務發展均具正面助益，不過相關晶片出貨管制政策仍面臨較高變數。

張傳章進一步提醒，就長期而言，AI 產業估值將更重視公司治理、現金流量與差異化能力。隨著美中科技競爭及國安審查常態化，他呼籲台灣金融業必須持續提升跨境法遵與風險管理能力，而台灣科技業者也須更重視供應鏈多元化及海外產能布局，以因應地緣政治挑戰。

檢視基本面表現，兆豐金截至 9 月底累計稅後淨利達 328.48 億元、年增 16%，每股純益 2.21 元；累計前 10 月稅後淨利更突破 343.31 億元、年增 13%，每股純益 2.31 元。旗下銀行、證券、票券及產險等主要子公司獲利全數較去年同期成長，非銀行子公司合計獲利貢獻約 26%，收益多元化成效顯著。

對於投資人最關心的明年股利政策，張傳章指出，在綜合考量現金流量及未分配盈餘稅等因素後，兆豐金近 3 年股利配發率約維持在 7 成左右。未來集團將在兼顧股東權益與公司業務發展的前提下，維持穩定的配息政策，並隨著公司獲利持續成長，同步提升每股股利以回饋股東。

核心子公司兆豐銀行受惠 AI 供應鏈強勁動能，表現同樣亮眼。兆豐銀副總經理陳建中表示，全球 AI 與高效能運算需求強勁，帶動半導體、電子零組件及科學園區廠商擴產與周轉金需求大增。截至第三季末，兆豐銀整體放款餘額達 2.82 兆元、年增 19%，放款市占率進一步攀升至 5.55%。

從企金放款結構來看，兆豐銀前三季國內企金平均餘額達 1.5 兆元、年增 14.35%。其中大企業平均放款成長 19%，期末餘額更暴增 30%；中小企業平均放款亦穩健成長 8%，期末達 12%。陳建中強調，AI 供應鏈投資與營運周轉金融資需求旺盛，已成為國內放款成長的核心推力。

海外與跨境融資方面，兆豐銀前三季外幣平均放款折合新台幣 6333 億元、年增 14%。陳建中說明，隨著台商供應鏈加速赴美設廠與全球布局，兆豐銀積極運用美國四家分行及海外信保機制，承作多筆電子科技與製造業赴美購廠、建廠及併購融資，帶動海外業務動能持續增溫。

聯貸市場表現更是一枝獨秀，依據 LSEG 統計，兆豐銀前三季在管理行與主辦行均蟬聯市場第一。展望第四季與 2027 年，陳建中指出，集團將緊扣 AI 資料中心、電力建設、儲能及台商赴美設廠等四大商機，並結合上下游供應鏈與同業共同主辦，持續擴大優質新企業客群與手續費收入。

news.Title: Down 40% or More for the Year, Are Any of These Top Cryptocurrencies Worth Buying Right Now?
news.Content:
It's been a difficult year for the crypto market, to say the least. Market bellwether Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) is down 30% for the year. And six of the top 20 cryptocurrencies, as ranked by market cap, are down 40% or more for the year.

I wouldn't touch five of these beaten-down altcoins with a 10-foot pole right now. They are simply too risky. But there is one cryptocurrency that could be worth a closer look, as long as you're willing to accept a significant amount of volatility.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The six cryptocurrencies

The six top cryptocurrencies down 40% or more for the year are: Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH), XRP (CRYPTO:XRP), Solana (CRYPTO:SOL), Dogecoin (CRYPTO:DOGE), Cardano (CRYPTO:ADA), and Bitcoin Cash (CRYPTO:BCH).

A few of these are an easy "no." Why would anyone want to invest in a speculative meme coin such as Dogecoin right now? Why invest in Bitcoin Cash if you can invest in Bitcoin instead?

And why invest in Cardano, given that it's trading 95% below its all-time high? This crypto has essentially dropped to zero, and even its co-founder Charles Hoskinson has warned of "a wave of failures" within the Cardano blockchain ecosystem.

Image source: Getty Images.

That leaves XRP, Ethereum, and Solana. Stablecoins continue to erode the core use case for the XRP token, and this cryptocurrency, too, is best left on the sidelines. During the past 90 days, XRP has been one of the worst-performing major cryptocurrencies, and its price has now dropped below the psychologically important level of $1.

So, if you're looking for a potential deep value play right now, that leaves Ethereum and Solana. My personal pick is Solana, given that it has emerged as Ethereum's top rival. In fact, it has often been characterized as a potential Ethereum killer due to its much faster speeds, lower costs, and higher throughput.

The case for buying Solana now

Moreover, if you look at crypto price performance during the past 90 days, three of the top-performing cryptocurrencies in the world have actually been Solana-related. These three cryptocurrencies are Raydium (CRYPTO:RAY), Jupiter (CRYPTO:JUP), and Pyth Network (CRYPTO:PYTH).

Raydium and Jupiter are decentralized exchanges for Solana, while Pyth is a blockchain oracle, similar to Chainlink (CRYPTO:LINK), bringing real-world data to blockchains. Their ability to outperform the broader market during the past quarter could suggest that Solana blockchain activity is rebounding and that key pieces of the Solana blockchain ecosystem remain healthy.

Story Continues

In part, this is due to Solana doubling down on decentralized finance (DeFi) as a potential growth avenue. DeFi is one of the most important niches of the blockchain world, and Solana has established itself as the No. 2 Layer-1 blockchain network in DeFi, trailing only Ethereum.

Based on the above, Solana could be undervalued at just $73 (as of Nov. 23). The crypto is trading more than 75% below its all-time high of $294 from January 2025. There's just too much potential upside to ignore, and I'm fully expecting a Solana price rally in 2027.

news.Title: 黃仁勳重返輝達AI科技股歡騰　亞股勁揚台韓日股猛漲
news.Content:
（中央社香港2026年11月24日綜合外電報導）美國人工智慧（AI）晶片大廠輝達（Nvidia）將不到2週前因婚外情風波辭職的前執行長黃仁勳復職，激勵美國股市在科技股引領下大漲，亞洲股市今天跟進，以台股飆漲近9%為首。

法新社報導，AI產業推動科技革命及全球經濟繁榮，而黃仁勳在業界扮演排解難題及提供遠見的角色，被外界視為攸關輝達未來及AI建設的重要人物。

不過，AI概念股先前已因獲利能力及巨額投資等疑慮承受賣壓，黃仁勳12日辭職的消息再帶來震撼，令類股大受打擊。

黃仁勳遭英美媒體披露有婚外情，對象之一是輝達客戶、新加坡公司Megaspeed的前高層主管黃樂（AliceHuang）。這家公司因疑似協助中國企業取得輝達最高階晶片，而遭到美國等多方調查。

輝達董事會昨天在美股開盤後不久宣布黃仁勳復職消息，立刻點燃股市漲勢。輝達股價收盤狂飆31.5%，市值暴增9000多億美元。

其他美國科技業巨擘股票也爆出亟需的買氣，終場那斯達克指數大漲逾6%、標普500指數揚升4.7%，道瓊工業指數上漲3%。

亞洲股市今天也應聲擺脫昨天疲軟走勢，終場普遍樂觀勁揚。其中台北股市在台積電和聯發科皆大漲近10%拉抬下，收盤創下史上最大漲點3310.46點。

首爾股市也在權值股SK海力士（SK Hynix）和三星（Samsung）跳升加持下，收盤上漲6.3%。東京股市則收高3.9%，其中愛德萬測試（Advantest）、東京威力科創（Tokyo Electron）和鎧俠（Kioxia）分別大漲12.5%、7.7%和10%。

上海股市收盤上揚0.3%，雪梨、新加坡、威靈頓和馬尼拉股市也都收高。

不過，香港股市收跌0.7%，反映中國科技企業股價未能受惠全球漲勢。

儘管美國總統川普（Donald Trump）表示，黃仁勳是在他直接聯繫輝達董事會後復職；但分析師提醒，這不意味相關調查就此結束，AI類股過去6個月籠罩的不確定性也未消除。輝達仍受到美國聯邦調查局（FBI）及美國國會的調查。

news.Title: 路透：台積電評估德州設廠　房產稅減免成關鍵條件
news.Content:
（中央社紐約2026年11月24日綜合外電報導）路透社報導，台積電有意在美國德州布拉左斯郡（BrazosCounty）投資226億美元興建晶片製造設施，但台積電旗下事業單位已告知德州官員，能否獲得房產稅減免將是決定性因素。

上述消息出自昨天提交給德州主計長辦公室的文件。而該文件同時指出，亞利桑那州仍是與之競爭的設廠選項之一。

根據路透社，這項計畫擬在德州布拉左斯郡逾3200英畝（約1295公頃）的土地上，興建一座或多座晶圓廠及相關支援基礎設施。

該廠區擬採用2奈米或更先進製程技術，生產用於人工智慧（AI）、高效能運算及行動裝置的晶片。

台積電是透過德州「就業、能源、科技與創新」（JETI）計畫，向德州主計長辦公室提出申請。

台積電並表示，在亞利桑那州擴大投資，可能帶來「某些營運及經濟優勢」。全球最大晶圓代工廠台積電自2024年底起，已在亞利桑那州營運一座半導體製造廠。

台積電還說，能否取得其要求的房產稅優惠，將左右公司是否承諾在德州推動這項計畫。

根據提交的文件，這座廠區預計將在未來40年間，創造至少2099個直接就業機會。

news.Title: 台股飆漲空單影響　聚焦外資借券賣出和期貨風控
news.Content:
（中央社記者鍾榮峰台北2026年11月24日電）黃仁勳回任輝達（NVIDIA）執行長等要職消息，激勵台股今天飆漲3310.46點，創歷史收盤最大漲點，市場關注對外資和投資人空單影響。法人分析，外資在台指期淨空單水位仍超過10萬口，主要是與投信在台指期淨多單對作，外資在現貨市場可借券賣出管道已大幅限縮。

期貨人士分析，台股飆漲超過3000點，若投資人期貨空單保證金餘額不足，期貨商可進行風控作業，向投資人發布高風險通知，若投資人期貨帳戶風險指標低於25%時，期貨商可執行代沖銷全部空單部位（強制平倉）；至於投資人「想走走不掉」被強制砍倉的情況，主要在股市連續性漲跌停或是流動性明顯不足的情境下發生。

三大法人今天合計賣超台股1230.11億元，其中自營商賣超810.25億元，投信買超84.04億元，外資及陸資賣超503.9億元。根據統計，外資連7個交易日賣超台股達2980億元，10月迄今僅6個交易日買超台股，今年迄今累計賣超達3.28兆元。

在台指期淨部位，三大法人淨空單減少3148口至5401口，外資淨空單減少250口至10萬3182口。

兆豐國際投顧董事長留政鈺接受記者電訪分析，台指期夜盤大漲3170點，加上台股現貨今天開高走高大漲逾3000點，621檔上市櫃公司鎖漲停，代表投資人惜售，外資買單「買不到」，但配對交易賣單成交，因此成交量相對萎縮砍半至4194億元。

觀察台股飆漲對外資在期現貨空單布局影響，留政鈺分析，外資在台指期淨空單水位仍超過10萬口，主要是與投信在台指期淨多單對作，由於投信ETF正2發行規模越來越大，反映投信未平倉口數也會增加。

留政鈺指出，外資在台股現貨市場賣壓觀察指標，主要看借券賣出成交量值，不過主管機關已將盤中可借券賣出委託數量比重大幅調降至1%，外資賣壓相對減緩，此外ETF可借券額度已經降低。至於對一般投資人融券放空影響，留政鈺分析，理論上融券量值已縮小。

因應台股近期波動劇烈，金管會19日宣布，20日起調整每日盤中借券賣出委託數量，由原不超過有價證券前30個營業日的日平均成交數量的3%，調降至1%。

news.Title: 施羅德看明年：台股重要性提升、多元報酬來源迎新變局
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-24 18:47:14 陳怡潔 發佈

施羅德發表明(2027)年全球投資關鍵十大預測(附表)並指出，全球市場投資版圖正隨人工智慧(AI)等結構演變而呈重新組合態勢，其中台灣股市憑藉完整的AI供應鏈與持續上修的企業獲利預期，在全球及新興市場配置中的重要性進一步提升；同時，股債平衡迎來新變局，建議投資人未來應逐步納入可轉債、證券化信用資產、新興市場當地貨幣債券、避險基金及實質資產，以更多元的報酬來源因應新的市場環境。

施羅德投資亞洲多元資產團隊最高主管近藤敬子(Keiko Kondo)指出，展望2027年，美國企業獲利成長可望由大型科技公司擴散至更多產業，而台灣則受惠於AI需求與供應鏈優勢，成為施羅德十大預測中重要的區域配置觀點。

然而，AI發展、地緣政治風險、通膨與利率環境的轉變，也正同步改寫市場結構。當股票與債券的相關性由過去的負相關轉為正相關，傳統股債平衡配置的分散效果面臨挑戰，投資人需要重新檢視資產配置策略，也進一步凸顯透過主動管理靈活調整投資組合的價值。施羅德認為，投資人未來不僅需要掌握台灣與AI等結構性成長機會，也應逐步納入可轉債、證券化信用資產、新興市場當地貨幣債券、避險基金及實質資產，以更多元的報酬來源因應新的市場環境。

近藤敬子進一步表示，台灣的投資價值不僅來自AI題材，更在於其橫跨半導體、零組件、伺服器及相關基礎建設的完整產業鏈，使投資人得以從不同環節參與AI的長期發展。從區域配置來看，台灣企業獲利預期持續上修，使其相較整體新興市場更具吸引力。在其他股票市場方面，美國企業獲利成長可望逐步擴散至更多產業；AI的影響也將由科技業延伸至醫療保健，協助提升藥物研發效率並改善醫療體系成本。歐洲及日本銀行股則有望受惠於殖利率曲線趨陡與結構性較高的利率環境。

在固定收益與另類資產配置上，施羅德認為，投資人應由「持有債券以分散股票風險」的單一思維，轉向辨識不同信用、利率與流動性溢酬。可轉債兼具參與股票上漲與緩衝下跌的特性；非投資等級債券、證券化信用資產及新興市場當地貨幣債券，則可提供不同於傳統公債的收益來源。當股債同步波動的情況增加，避險基金可透過總體、股票多空或市場中性等策略強化多元配置及拓展報酬來源；實質資產則受惠於通膨防護、基礎建設融資，以及AI資料中心等基建帶動的長期電力需求。能源轉型與資料中心亦推升銅需求，加上供應限制，工業金屬相較原油更具結構性支撐。

近藤敬子表示：「2027年全球投資市場將持續受到地緣政治等各種不確定性影響，靜態、單一的配置已經不能滿足大部分投資人的投資需求。隨著通膨與利率環境轉變，固定收益在投資組合中的角色也正在改變。投資人需要重新思考傳統股債配置方式，並透過更多元的資產布局提升投資組合韌性，在因應市場變化的同時，掌握長期資本增值與收益機會。」

近藤敬子總結，2027年的投資關鍵不是放棄股債，而是打破只靠股債完成分散的慣性。投資人需要依據不同經濟情境，主動調整股票、信用、另類策略與實質資產的配置；在掌握台灣、AI等長期成長趨勢的同時，也為地緣政治、通膨與利率風險預留緩衝。施羅德提出的十大預測，正是以更廣泛的報酬來源重新組合投資版圖，讓多元資產配置從股債配比，進一步發展為跨市場、跨策略與跨風險因子的動態配置。

施羅德並表示，回顧2026年，施羅德十大投資預測中，共有七項表現符合預期，涵蓋美國股票、亞洲科技股、歐洲銀行與工業類股、全球可轉債、新興市場當地貨幣債券及私募資產等。施羅德投資每年檢視並公開預測成果，透過全球研究與投資團隊持續追蹤總體環境、產業趨勢與市場結構，並依據新資訊適時調整觀點與布局。這項長期實踐，體現施羅德投資重視研究紀律、資訊透明及審慎管理受託資產的理念。

(圖表來源：施羅德)

news.Title: 單日飆漲超30%一天後 輝達美股盤前回跌逾4%
news.Content:
輝達(NVDA-US)董事會重新任命黃仁勳擔任總裁兼執行長後，股價周一(23日)狂飆 31.5% 收在 165.05 美元，單日市值激增超過 1 兆美元。然而在周二美股盤前交易中，隨著市場謹慎情緒回升，輝達股價回檔修正約 3.5%。

此波高層回歸同時帶動亞洲半導體供應鏈反彈，台灣晶片代工龍頭台積電(2330-TW)(TSM-US)在台股大漲逾 9%，日本愛德萬測試(Advantest)飆升逾 12%，南韓記憶體大廠三星電子與 SK 海力士雙雙上揚超過 6%。

黃仁勳於 11 月 12 日辭職，部分原因是涉入與新加坡雲端企業 Megaspeed 負責人的緋聞，這家公司因涉嫌將受限的輝達 AI 晶片轉運至中國而面臨調查。儘管美國情報機構曾提出反情報隱憂，但未提出間諜罪指控，商務部已將 Megaspeed 列入實體清單。輝達董事會與美政府官員協商後通過復職案，並強調黃仁勳的回歸「不構成國家安全風險」。

美國總統川普對此表達強力支持，在 Truth Social 上發文稱讚黃仁勳是「偉大的愛國者與國家寶藏」，強調其回歸對輝達及美國經濟至關重要，並表示政府並無任何違法或國安風險的證據。

對於黃仁勳的回歸，Raymond James 分析師在研究報告中表示：「我們很高興看到黃仁勳重掌評級為『強烈買進』的輝達，但輝達無法重來一遍。黃仁勳的回歸雖消除了部分不確定性，但陰霾依然存在。」

高盛分析師則指出，黃仁勳的回歸對整體 AI 生態系統而言是一項「積極利多」。

Rabobank 全球戰略師Michael Every提醒未來的合規與審查隱憂：「黃仁勳將在幾周內面臨國會的嚴厲質詢，必須解釋他對規避 AI 晶片出口管制了解多少——如果不是川普，這一切最後會歸咎於誰？」

目前輝達正成立由獨立董事組成的國家安全與出口管制委員會，並著手尋找首任首席合規官(CCO)。黃仁勳預計 12 月初出席美國國會聽證會接受質詢。

news.Title: Walmart Just Raised Its Outlook Again. 3 Numbers Show Why Its Scale Advantage Keeps Growing.
news.Content:
Investors shouldn't label Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) a slow-moving and outdated retail enterprise. The business is performing well in today's internet-driven economy. And it shows. Shares generated a market-thumping total return of 154% in the past three years (as of Nov. 19).

Walmart's fiscal 2027 third-quarter (ended Oct. 31) financial results were very encouraging. It beat analyst estimates on the top and bottom lines. And following last quarter's renewed outlook, management once again raised sales and profit guidance. This is a positive trend as the critical holiday shopping period is upon us.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The retail stock 's scale is the highlight. Here are three numbers that show why this key competitive advantage continues to grow.

Image source: Getty Images.

1. 23% e-commerce growth

The first number is 23%. That's how fast Walmart's U.S. e-commerce sales grew in the third quarter. By comparison, Walmart's U.S. comparable sales, which measure growth at stores and digital channels open at least a year, rose 2.9% (excluding fuel).

This might come as a surprise. After all, Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) wrote the online retail playbook, and it dominates online shopping.

But Walmart has something the e-commerce giant can't easily copy. Its 5,200 domestic stores sit within 10 miles of 90% of the U.S. population. Many of those sites were secured decades ago. Today, they double as delivery hubs.

That creates density for the logistics network. More orders flowing through the same buildings and trucks means a lower cost per package. And Walmart can spread its heavy investments in automation over hundreds of billions of dollars in annual sales. That's hard to compete with.

2. 37% advertising growth

Walmart U.S. advertising revenue jumped 37% in the third quarter. This is where scale starts paying a second dividend. And it shows the business is leaning into the advantage that its data offers.

Walmart Connect, the company's ads platform, sells brand placements across its website, app, and stores. The pitch is simple. Walmart knows what 150 million weekly U.S. shoppers actually buy, not just what they click on. Brands want to reach those intentional shoppers at the moment of purchase.

There's a positive feedback loop here. Walmart's massive revenue base gives it negotiating leverage with suppliers. That leverage helps keep prices low, which drives customer traffic. And traffic is exactly what advertisers pay for.

Story Continues

The economics are exceptional. The audience and infrastructure already exist, so each additional ad dollar costs little to bring in, leading to "over 70% margins," according to Walmart Connect senior vice president Ryan Mayward. Groceries, by contrast, are a low-margin business. Ad revenue has a much bigger positive impact on the bottom line.

3. 20% membership growth

Global membership fee revenue grew 17%. This includes Sam's Club membership fees and Walmart+, the company's subscription service that goes head-to-head with Amazon Prime and offers free delivery and other benefits.

Membership fees are recurring and high-margin. Customers pay up front, and Walmart's job is to make that fee feel like a bargain. Its lean supply chain helps to make that possible. Low operating costs allow the company to bundle perks such as free delivery, streaming, and discounts without giving up its price advantage.

That changes shopping behavior. People will favor spending with a retailer they've already paid, and members spend four times more than non-members. More spending makes Walmart larger. A larger Walmart negotiates better prices. And these better prices attract more members.

This is every retailer's dream. A paid membership program can only work if the value proposition is strong enough. Walmart's everyday low prices lay the foundation.

Watch the bottom line

Put these three numbers together, and the quarter's most important figure comes into focus. Reported operating income rose 5.5% (on a constant-currency basis), faster than revenue. Over the past three years, adjusted operating income climbed 24%, while sales were up 17%.

Walmart's success in e-commerce, advertising, and memberships is a tailwind. Shareholders should watch whether profits keep outgrowing revenue. This would indicate that the scale-based flywheel is still working.

news.Title: 台股大漲外資反手大賣　新台幣盤中觸33元、收32.939元
news.Content:
（中央社記者潘姿羽台北2026年11月24日電）輝達（Nvidia）執行長黃仁勳重磅回歸，亞股同步歡慶，台股重返4萬點大關，不過新台幣匯率逆勢走弱，今天收盤收32.939元，貶4.4分，台北及元太外匯市場成交金額34.88億美元。

黃仁勳戲劇性回歸，激勵AI概念股強彈，台股開高走高，收在40122.35點，終場上漲3310.46點，創下史上收盤最大漲點。

台股暴漲之際，外資卻擴大減碼，今天續砍台股503.9億元，連續7個交易日站在賣方。

新台幣匯率也與股市脫鉤，今天以32.87元開出，在台股強漲帶動下，升抵盤中高點32.848元，但外資趁勢調節部位、賣股匯出，加上美元強勢表態，匯價應聲翻貶，且最低觸及33元整數價位，終場收在32.939元，終止連3升。

外匯交易員分析，黃仁勳強勢回歸大大提振投資人信心，台股直接上演報復性反彈，但市場對AI巨額投資疑慮未能散去，加上外資擴大提款，還未能確定警報已解除。

另一方面，外匯交易員指出，市場對美國聯準會升息預期升溫，美元指數站上104大關，亞幣表現受抑。

外匯交易員認為，近期觀察重點仍是台股能否甩開陰霾，進而吸引外資回流，否則強勢美元壓境，若加上外資賣股匯出，雙重壓力夾擊，新台幣將難擺脫弱勢格局。

news.Title: US futures, European stocks slip as Nvidia rally cools
news.Content:
By Sruthi Shankar

Nov 24 (Reuters) - US stock futures and European shares came under pressure on Tuesday as the early euphoria following Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia faded, with investors cautious about further AI-driven gains and upcoming US inflation data.

Asian stocks jumped following a US stock ‌market surge on Monday, when Nvidia's shares soared 31.5% after the AI chip giant reinstated Huang as CEO under pressure from US President Donald ‌Trump.

The market bounce, however, failed to hold for a second day. Nasdaq futures dropped 0.9% after the tech-heavy index rallied nearly 7% a day earlier. The pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 0.1%, weighed down ​by a sharp drop in mining stocks. [.EU]

Huang's comeback capped a whirlwind week of events that whipped markets and tore through the AI ecosystem, which has relied on Nvidia for everything from supplying chips to bankrolling the industry's massive buildout. But it also left unanswered questions over Huang, who had resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged spy for China.

"With Jensen's return, it assures people massively and gives hope that the data centre construction continues and that boosts US GDP," said Chris Beauchamp, ‌chief market analyst, IG Group in London.

"But it then ⁠opens up a whole list of questions that may not be answered very quickly. What did he know? What else did he do? How much went to China? And these questions will continue to chip away at market confidence."

Nvidia's shares fell nearly 4% ⁠in US premarket trading, a day after marking their biggest daily percentage gain in 23 years and restoring nearly $1 trillion in value to the company.

In Asia, Taiwanese shares shot up 9% from an eight-month low, with Nvidia's primary contract chip manufacturer TSMC and assembler Foxconn both nearly 10% higher at their daily limits.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan ​climbed ​nearly 4%, bouncing back from an eight-month low and recording its biggest single-day gain since ​July 31.

"By the end of the day, these businesses need to ‌make enough money to justify investors' expectations. My point is: Jensen's return does not solve this. So, the sentiment is more emotional than sensible, in my opinion," Glenn Yin, director of research at online trading platform ACCM, told the Reuters Global Markets Forum.

Chinese shares were an exception to the relief rally, making only small gains due to concerns that tighter curbs on the exports of US chips are in the works.

Story Continues

DOLLAR, YIELDS AWAIT INFLATION DATA

Investors are set to focus on Wednesday's PCE Index data, the last key data set ahead of the Federal Reserve's final meeting of 2026 in December.

news.Title: Why 1 Billionaire Investor Just Poured $3 Billion Into Amazon, Meta, and Alphabet
news.Content:
Billionaire Stephen Mandel's Lone Pine Capital fund was busy loading up on shares of Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META), and Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG) in the third quarter, investing an estimated nearly $3 billion in the trio of hyperscalers. All three are now top-10 positions.

Let's look at what may have attracted Lone Pine to these AI stocks .

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Amazon

Amazon was Lone Pine's biggest purchase in Q3, with the fund pouring an estimated $1.4 billion into the e-commerce and cloud computing leader to establish a new position and make it its largest holding at over 9% of its portfolio. It's easy to see what Lone Pine may like about Amazon, with both its core businesses firing on all cylinders.

Amazon's cloud computing unit, AWS (Amazon Web Services), is its main driver, with revenue accelerating as the company aggressively builds out its AI infrastructure. The company is getting strong returns on its investments, locking in five-year or longer contracts and recouping its investment within two to three years. As it grows its AI accelerator business, I think its payback period could shrink, and demand for its chips is so high that it plans to begin selling them externally late next year. Overall, Amazon sees the potential for AWS to grow into a $1 trillion revenue business.

Meanwhile, often overlooked is how strongly Amazon's e-commerce business has been performing. The company is the world's leading manufacturer and operator of mobile robotics. Combined with its investments in AI, this is driving incredible operating efficiency and surging profitability in this business.

Meta Platforms

Lone Pine was also aggressively buying Meta shares in the quarter, with the new position becoming the fund's third-largest holding.

Meta has demonstrated that it has one of the best AI flywheel businesses, with investments in algorithm improvements that lead to users being fed more relevant content and ads. This, in turn, has been boosting ad loads and increasing conversions and ad prices, driving strong revenue growth.

Meanwhile, Meta is not sitting still. The introduction of its AI Muse agents puts it in a strong position to take a leadership role in the emerging consumer AI agent market. While Meta's AI Muse agents can perform many tasks for users, Meta benefits the most when they facilitate transactions on users' behalf, as it will receive either affiliate or transaction fees. This will give Meta a whole new non-advertising revenue stream and position the company as a major player in e-commerce. Just the ability to monetize its Facebook Marketplace with these agents should be a nice growth driver.

Story Continues

Alphabet

Lone Pine significantly increased its Alphabet position in Q3, making Alphabet its seventh-largest holding. As the company with the most complete AI stack, Alphabet is a popular holding among many large hedge funds.

Alphabet's biggest edge is the ecosystem it builds around its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), making its computing platform a strong alternative to Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA). This has given it a large cost advantage in developing and running inference on its own AI models, as well as in cloud computing, where it can get a payback within a year when using its own chips. Semianalysis recently reported that TPUs have shown a price-to-performance edge over Nvidia's GPUs. This comes at a great time as Alphabet also begins selling these chips externally to customers.

Alphabet's core search business, meanwhile, continues to see growth driven by increased usage of its AI-powered tools, including AI Overviews and AI Mode. While search is still in a bit of a transition with AI, it should benefit as Alphabet creates new ad formats. Meanwhile, its ownership of Chrome and Android, and a revenue-sharing deal with Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) , still give it a huge distribution advantage.

news.Title: Nvidia Turmoil: How Big Is the Risk for CoreWeave?
news.Content:
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) is the bellwether for the artificial intelligence (AI) industry, and for CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV), it's even more. The former is an AI chip giant, and the latter is a neocloud company, offering customers access to such chips. Nvidia has played a key role in CoreWeave's growth, with support including stock purchases, revenue guarantees, and credit backing.

All of this helped CoreWeave's shares climb in its early months of trading last year. Though the stock gave up some gains from its market debut, it continued to offer those early investors positive performance all the way through last month. But in recent weeks, general concern about a tighter credit market and the pace of the AI build-out weighed on CoreWeave and peers. Then troubles at key partner Nvidia added to the pressure.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Nvidia chief Jensen Huang stepped down earlier this month following allegations of affairs, then was reinstated earlier this week. Amid the turmoil at Nvidia, how big is the risk for CoreWeave? Let's find out.

Image source: Getty Images.

CoreWeave works exclusively with Nvidia

First, let's take a closer look at the Nvidia-CoreWeave relationship and consider what's at stake. As mentioned, CoreWeave offers AI chips, but not just any. The company works exclusively with Nvidia and has even been the first cloud provider to make Nvidia's latest updates generally available. CoreWeave offers its customers a fleet of Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs) that they can rent for short or long periods of time to run their workloads, and demand has been soaring. In the recent quarter, CoreWeave reported a 168% increase in revenue to $3.6 billion.

Nvidia has been a strong supporter of this young AI company, starting with its 10% stake in CoreWeave. The tech giant owns more than 47 million CoreWeave shares, making it the third-largest position in Nvidia's investment portfolio. Nvidia has also pledged revenue support; for example, it's agreed to purchase any unused capacity through April 2032. Nvidia, thanks to its solid credit rating, has acted as a backstop for CoreWeave as it seeks borrowings to build out. And Nvidia has also funded companies that then turn to CoreWeave for access to chips.

However, with investors keenly focused on Nvidia's financing support for neoclouds, the situation moving forward could become more difficult for these AI cloud specialists. During Huang's brief departure, Nvidia finance chief Colette Kress said that financial guarantees for neocloud agreements depend on those companies' ability to secure their own capital for the build-out.

Story Continues

Nvidia's recent turmoil

At the same time, Nvidia faces headwinds that may shift its focus somewhat in the coming months. The company is investigating an alleged spy effort that targeted Jensen Huang. And, separately, press reports say the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has launched a probe concerning Nvidia's accounting practices.

CoreWeave, however, may not be as dependent on Nvidia's attention to its financial situation as we might have thought. CoreWeave offered a positive message in its earnings call, saying, "Our growth is supported by multiple sources of funding, including financing backed by customer contracts, operating cash flow, and approximately $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits expected in the next three months alone."

And Jensen Huang early last month expressed confidence in CoreWeave's financial position.

So, considering all of this, how big of a risk is the Nvidia turmoil for CoreWeave? I think any potential Nvidia challenges could weigh on appetite for CoreWeave stock due to the companies' close relations.

CoreWeave is a highly leveraged company, with most of its build-out funded by debt.

CRWV Debt to Equity Ratio data by YCharts

This, too, may represent a headwind today as investors worry about the sustainability of AI spending on AI infrastructure. And as Democrats take leadership in the House and Senate early next year, this feeling may intensify. Democratic leaders have been known for a cautious approach when it comes to developing AI.

All of this means that CoreWeave, amid current uncertainty and its dependence on Nvidia, carries significant risk. It's crucial to keep an eye on Nvidia's comments regarding neoclouds in the months to come — even if CoreWeave has gained financial strength, investors still feel reassured by Nvidia's support. It will also be important to monitor messages from the government about the AI build-out to get a better idea of what's next for CoreWeave.

news.Title: Nvidia Lost $2.75 Trillion in 45 Days -- More Than the Market Cap of 496 S&P 500 Companies -- and Investors Wagering on a Quick Bounce to New Highs May Be Disappointed
news.Content:
For the better part of the last four years, the evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) has been the stock market's leading catalyst, and Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) has been at the center of this revolution. Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs) are what make AI-accelerated data centers tick, with none of its competitors particularly close to rivaling the compute capabilities of its GPUs.

But over the previous seven weeks (ending Nov. 20), it's been an entirely different story for what had been Wall Street's largest publicly traded company. In a span of 45 calendar days (33 trading sessions), Nvidia has lost $2.75 trillion in market value -- more than the market cap of 496 S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) companies and all but four of more than 5,200 publicly traded companies, one of which is Nvidia.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

It's logical to expect a now-historically inexpensive Nvidia to bounce back in a big way over the coming weeks, potentially to new highs. But investors wagering on a quick rebound to new highs may be sorely disappointed.

Nvidia lost investors' trust and is facing extensive legal gray clouds

It's no secret that the resignation of co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO rattled Nvidia and Wall Street following his admission of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. On Monday, Nov. 23, shares rallied following his reinstatement as CEO by the Nvidia board.

However, Huang's return isn't a panacea for the loss of investors' trust in Nvidia. While the company has its visionary back, this leadership flip-flop has potentially jeopardized the numerous circular financing deals Huang orchestrated and could further contract Nvidia's earnings multiple as investors express skepticism about the company's still-clouded near-term outlook.

Additionally, Wall Street's now-former largest public company is facing a litany of investigations that can cloud its outlook for the foreseeable future. This includes a Securities and Exchange Commission investigation into its accounting practices, as well as a separate investigation by U.S. authorities into whether Nvidia's chips were smuggled to China via shipments to third countries.

None of these issues will be resolved anytime soon.

Structural issues persist within the AI trade, too

Story Continues

However, there's more going on than just lost trust and investigations. Several structural issues with the AI trade are likely to weigh on Nvidia for the foreseeable future.

For example, the bond market has been sounding a warning about the otherworldly amount of capital being spent on the AI data center build-out for a majority of the year.

When public companies issue debt, it should trade around par value. However, bond prices for several neoclouds and hyperscalers have plunged throughout the year, including Nvidia, whose 2060 notes have hit record lows. There's tangible skepticism about companies' ability to pay their debt obligations.

Furthermore, every major tech innovation since the mid-1990s has endured an early-innings bubble-bursting event. The reason these bubbles continue to form and burst is that investors overestimate the pace of optimization for new technologies.

For instance, it took until well after the dot-com bubble had burst for businesses to finally optimize internet-driven solutions to boost their sales and profits. AI companies are likely to follow a similar path, with the underlying technology needing ample time to mature.

While the long-term outlook for AI and Nvidia remains bright, there's no quick fix for what ails either at the moment.

news.Title: Brookfield Corporation Expects to Complete Its Corporate Restructuring on Dec. 1. What Changes for Its Stock?
news.Content:
Next week, Canadian asset management and holding company Brookfield Corporation (NYSE:BN) plans to complete a consolidation transaction to simplify its complex business structure. On Dec. 1, Brookfield will combine with Brookfield Wealth Solutions (NYSE:BNT), or BWS for short.

Management has high hopes for the combination, which will result in an entity known as Brookfield Corporation Ltd. Still, this combination may not achieve an objective shareholders may want addressed as soon as possible: closing the valuation gap between the stock and the company's underlying per-share value.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Brookfield and its upcoming reorganization

Brookfield Corporation has long had a complex organizational structure. Not only does the company have multiple publicly traded, majority-owned subsidiaries, such as Brookfield Asset Management (NYSE:BAM), but Brookfield also currently holds full economic interest in BWS, which is domiciled in Bermuda. The Bermuda-based entity is also publicly traded, but its shares have always been exchangeable for shares in Canadian-domiciled Brookfield Corporation.

However, this is changing at the start of next month. Per a proposed transaction approved by shareholders last summer, Brookfield Corporation and BWS agreed to merge into a new Bermuda-based holding company, Brookfield Corporation Ltd. This company will continue to trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX) and the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) under the ticker symbol "BN."

Completing this transaction could bring numerous benefits. For one, combining the two entities enables direct access to the former Brookfield Corporation's permanent capital base. Because the deal also helps to increase the stock's free float outstanding, the shares could benefit from future index inclusion. However, Brookfield's corporate structure will stay largely opaque, which may make it difficult for the company to make any progress eliminating the issues that have long made it a value stock .

The takeaway for investors: buy, sell, or hold?

Last year, Brookfield's management estimated that the stock's underlying value was $68 per share, almost 75% higher than recent prices. Furthermore, management expressed its belief that continued growth of Brookfield's asset management and insurance businesses, coupled with investment returns on its permanent capital, could result in the stock's underlying value reaching $140 per share by 2030.

Story Continues

However, since this projection, Brookfield Corporation shares have pulled back. In my view, this valuation gap still exists for two reasons. First, much of Brookfield's value comes from its 73% stake in Brookfield Asset Management. It's common for Wall Street to apply a discount to holding companies with complex structures. A further simplification, like a full consolidation of Brookfield Asset Management into Brookfield Corporation Ltd., may be necessary to close the valuation gap.

Management's estimate also includes the value of Brookfield's other holdings in publicly traded and privately held investment entities, including the net present value of its carried interest, or profit based on the performance of its investments. In addition, given Brookfield's high exposure to areas like private credit and AI data centers, investors could also be factoring in the potential for the respective booms in either area to give way to a slowdown, or worse, a meltdown.

Brookfield appears to be a solid value opportunity among financial stocks , although patience is necessary. With impending changes that may mark just the start of further simplification in the years ahead, the stock could rise as investors become more confident in management's valuation argument.

news.Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Is Back, and Stock Investors Just Got More Great News About the AI Chip Giant
news.Content:
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) has become the cornerstone of the artificial intelligence boom. The company has established itself as an indispensable supplier of data center infrastructure.

Shareholders received troubling news earlier this month when co-founder and longtime CEO Jensen Huang resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs. His exit created considerable uncertainty because he played an instrumental role in developing Nvidia's competitive advantages and cultivating relationships with customers and suppliers.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Fortunately, Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang on Nov. 23, just 11 days after he resigned. But shareholders have a few more reasons to celebrate: Nvidia recently reported stellar third-quarter financial results, Wall Street's latest forecasts suggest AI spending is growing more quickly than anticipated; much higher in the future, and most analysts think the stock is deeply undervalued.

Here are the important details.

Jensen Huang. Image source: Getty Images.

Nvidia delivered stellar third-quarter financial results

Nvidia is a semiconductor company best known for its graphics processing units (GPUs), chips that accelerate artificial intelligence workloads. But its competitive edge extends beyond semiconductor design. Nvidia employs a full-stack strategy that combines GPUs, CPUs, networking equipment, and software into integrated computing systems.

Nvidia delivered stellar third-quarter financial results. Revenue increased 103% to $116 billion, the second straight quarter of triple-digit sales growth. Gross margin expanded 1.4 percentage points to 74.8%, an indication of durable pricing power. And non-GAAP earnings surged 111% to $2.68 per diluted share.

Colette Kress, interim CEO at the time of the report, said the new Vera Rubin compute platform was off to an "explosive start." Vera Rubin is particularly consequential because it allows Nvidia to capture a larger share of data center spending than previous chip architectures.

Jensen Huang quantified the opportunity on the previous earnings call. "In the case of Hopper, we were at about $18 billion per gigawatt. For Grace Blackwell, we're about $25 billion per gigawatt. And for Vera Rubin, it's about $40 billion per gigawatt."

Story Continues

Since the report, several Wall Street analysts have raised their earnings forecasts, such that the consensus estimate now calls for adjusted earnings of $9.65 per diluted share in fiscal 2027 (102% growth) and $16.78 per diluted share in fiscal 2028 (74% growth), according to LSEG.

Wall Street has consistently underestimated AI infrastructure spending

Wall Street has a long history of underestimating transformative technology markets. Initial forecasts underestimated the number of personal computer users in 2000 by 57%, internet users in 2000 by 138%, and smartphone shipments in 2013 by 55%, according to Morgan Stanley . Analysts also underestimated revenue across the top three cloud providers in 2020 by 28%.

Wall Street is making the same mistake with AI infrastructure. In January, the consensus estimate said capital expenditure (capex) spending among the five largest hyperscalers -- Alphabet , Amazon , Meta Platforms , Microsoft , and Oracle -- would total $530 billion in 2026, but that figure has since been raised to $799 billion, according to JPMorgan Chase .

Upward revisions for subsequent years have been even more dramatic. As shown in the chart, Wall Street's consensus capex forecasts for 2027 and 2028 have increased 82% and 97%, respectively, since December 2025.

Image source: Author.

Importantly, the figures shown in the chart detail capex among the five largest hyperscalers, meaning they understate the full scope of the AI infrastructure boom. For instance, when Space Exploration Technologies , CoreWeave , and Nebius Group are included, Morgan Stanley estimates capex will approach $1.6 trillion in 2027 and $1.8 trillion in 2028.

Wall Street says Nvidia stock is a screaming buy

On Nov. 23, Nvidia shares rocketed higher following reports that Jensen Huang had been reinstated as CEO. However, most Wall Street analysts still see the stock as a bargain. The median target price of $230 per share implies 39% upside from the current share price of $167.

What's driving that optimism? Nvidia currently trades at 18 times earnings. Excluding the past month, that is the cheapest valuation in a decade. The stock looks especially cheap today because Wall Street expects earnings to grow at 49% annually over the next three years. Long-term investors should consider buying a small position.

news.Title: Nvidia Could Generate $741 Billion in Revenue Next Year. Here’s What That Means for the Stock.
news.Content:
Nvidia 's (NASDAQ:NVDA) earnings report last week, without Jensen Huang leading the company, went better than expected. Revenue climbed 103% year over year to $115.8 billion, and earnings per share climbed to $2.70, up 108%. Both came in above analysts' expectations.

Perhaps more important was CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress's fiscal 2028 guidance. Last quarter she said she expects 70% revenue growth. This quarter, she increased it to 75%. That's despite higher-than-expected revenue growth last quarter and strong fourth-quarter guidance.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Her fourth-quarter guidance calls for $130 billion in revenue, bringing fiscal 2027 total revenue to $423.7 billion. A 75% growth rate implies $741 billion in revenue next year. Here's what that means for the stock.

Image source: Nvidia.

Nvidia stock is incredibly cheap right now

With the recent sell-off in shares, the company has a market cap of about $4 trillion as of this writing. That means the stock is priced just over 5 times next year's sales. Its stock price has dropped to 10 times analysts' expectations for next year's earnings.

There are a few reasons why a stock would be so cheap.

The market may be indicating that the analysts are overconfident in the business and their estimates are too high. Kress's increased 2028 outlook decreases that likelihood, although it's possible Kress is overconfident as well.

The market may be indicating that the earnings aren't sustainable and an earnings downcycle will hit extremely hard in the not-too-distant future. But Nvidia is an asset-light, fabless semiconductor stock , so while earnings might drop and its margin might contract, it doesn't face the same cyclical pressure as semiconductor stocks with huge capital investment requirements.

The market believes the risks to the company are extremely high, requiring a larger margin of safety to buy the stock. With growing uncertainty about the future of artificial intelligence stocks, this is the clear reason for Nvidia's current stock price.

Kress looked to put investors at ease during the earnings call . She said her 75% revenue growth outlook is based on "data center readiness, the strength and durability of end customer demand, and our customers' access to capital." She noted the $32 billion in financial commitments to neocloud companies require those partners to secure their own capital for data centers first. She stressed that Nvidia has a multi-year roadmap in place and it's "business as usual."

Story Continues

Is it time to buy shares of Nvidia?

While Nvidia shares look incredibly cheap right now, there's a lot of uncertainty about the business. While Huang has been reinstated as CEO, investors need to know whether he knowingly or unknowingly sold chips that ultimately landed in China, and what percentage of Nvidia's sales they accounted for. There could be legal repercussions as well, in the form of fines and further sales restrictions, which would impact Nvidia's bottom line.

Nvidia is also increasingly reliant on neocloud companies continuing to build quickly, a trend that faces both regulatory and credit risks. While Nvidia's GPUs remain best-in-class and can remain so even without Huang, the risk is that hyperscalers and leading AI labs will run more of their software on custom silicon instead of GPUs.

To be sure, the market appears to be pricing in the risks to Nvidia at the current price. But there are other AI stocks that have been caught up in the broader AI sell-off and look like great opportunities with less uncertainty. For now, a wait-and-see approach may be most prudent for Nvidia stock.

news.Title: The Perpetual Futures Market Is Booming. That Might Not Be as Bullish for Hyperliquid as Some Investors Think.
news.Content:
The perpetual futures boom will probably continue to be great for the business of Hyperliquid (CRYPTO:HYPE), but it's also luring an entire roster of well-funded rivals that will be sharply contesting its advance every step of the way. On Nov. 18, CoinDesk reported that one emerging challenger, Variational, raised $110 million in capital at a $1.5 billion valuation to target Hyperliquid's loyal customer base and future prospects. It plans to launch its own token, VAR, before the end of 2026.

It's true that a growing perpetual futures market could present the opportunity for yet another clean win for its leaders. But rivals like Robinhood Markets (NASDAQ:HOOD) and Coinbase Global (NASDAQ:COIN) already have millions of customers, while Hyperliquid and its smaller peers need to convert new users one wallet at a time.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Here's which players are in the competitive landscape right now, and how much they might threaten Hyperliquid down the line.

Image source: Getty Images.

Retail investor favorites from the traditional financial sector are about to hit the scene in a big way

Among decentralized exchanges (DEXs), which execute trades on a public blockchain rather than through an intermediary, Hyperliquid's lead is lopsided.

As of Nov. 23, it received 72% of the fees generated by all DEXes, with $2.7 million for that 24-hour period, compared to its smaller competitors Aster (CRYPTO:ASTER), which only brought in about $102,500, and $146,400 for Lighter (CRYPTO:LIT)in the same period.

Centralized platforms with a strong presence in the traditional financial sector are the bigger threat by far, as they're guaranteed to have both large user bases and ample capital of their own to deploy as they contest the market. Hyperliquid's $718.7 billion in volume in the third quarter of 2026 was only 69% of Robinhood's volume of about $1 trillion.

In May, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) cleared Coinbase to list crypto perpetuals, and on Sept. 29, Robinhood said it would offer U.S. perps in the coming months at a commission of 0.01% per trade through the end of the year. Robinhood had 28.7 million customers with funded accounts as of the end of the third quarter, and Coinbase had 7.4 million monthly users who made transactions that quarter. In contrast, Hyperliquid has voluntarily made itself off-limits to Americans in advance of securing regulatory permission to operate in the U.S., and it's not clear what the status of seeking or attaining that permission is as of late November.

Story Continues

Importantly, Robinhood has also chosen a decentralized exchange as its favorite, meaning it can erode Hyperliquid's market share from two directions. Its venture arm has backed Lighter, and outside the U.S., its wallet app sends users to Lighter's perpetuals.

In other words, the customers who could fuel the next legs of the perpetuals boom mostly belong to someone other than Hyperliquid. And its centralized competitors also have platforms that are significantly easier to start using, as they can leverage their traditional financial infrastructure to eliminate the need to fund a new crypto wallet and transfer funds into it, as on Hyperliquid.

Can Hyperliquid capture and retain someone else's customers?

Hyperliquid has some allies in its corner, too.

On Sept. 16, the Kraken crypto exchange's parent company, Payward, said it planned to list Hyperliquid-based perpetuals for its U.S. clients, pending regulatory approval. Payward had 6.6 million funded accounts as of June 30, so Hyperliquid could be positioned to settle a good amount of additional trading activity, which would boost the price of its HYPE coin by way of converting its transaction fees into buybacks of its token.

However, that access to Payward's user base comes at a cost of its own, which might prove troublesome. Users of markets built by outside operators, as Payward's would be, need to pay roughly double Hyperliquid's normal fees. Pricier contracts are a tough sell next to Robinhood's promotional rates.

Hyperliquid is still worth buying for risk-tolerant investors with a multiyear holding horizon, but it's no longer the only big fish in the perpetuals pond. Of course, perps aren't its only line of business -- it also offers prediction markets, spot trading, and other revenue-generating features too -- so it will likely be resilient even if it has to fight harder to advance.

news.Title: The Buffett Indicator Is More Than 70 Points Above Its Dot-Com Peak. Here’s What That Means for Long-Term Investors.
news.Content:
In a 2001 Fortune article, Warren Buffett publicly mentioned the idea of gauging the stock market's valuation by comparing the country's total equity market capitalization to its GDP. This concept was introduced just after the technology bubble burst.

Before that, at the dot-com peak in the spring of 2000, the Buffett indicator was just under 150%. This was a level that suggested the stock market was extremely overvalued. That proved to be the correct view; Over the following decade, the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) produced a negative single-digit total return.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Relative to what was going on at the turn of the century, the current Buffett indicator of 222%, more than 70 percentage points above the dot-com record, is in the stratosphere. It's not far off the highest reading ever from three months ago in August. Investors have definitely been concerned.

Here's how to interpret the Buffett indicator as 2026 nears its end.

Image source: Getty Images.

History argues for caution

If you perfectly mistimed your investment allocation and bought an S&P 500 exchange-traded fund, such as the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEMKT:SPY) in early 2000 when the Buffett indicator was around 150%, as mentioned, your portfolio suffered by losing money in the subsequent decade. The stock market was performing well prior to the housing market meltdown, however, a generational event that led to a severe economic crisis. It's impossible to have predicted this would happen.

Nonetheless, investors might be skeptical that buying stocks is the right move today. With the Buffett indicator at 222%, what does this mean for the equity market over the next 10 years?

All else equal, history says that high starting valuations result in lower forward returns. The tech bubble is the clearest example. This is true even though past trends aren't guaranteed to repeat.

According to research from J.P. Morgan (NYSE:JPM) Asset Management, the bank believes that U.S. large-cap stocks will produce an annualized total return of 7.5% in the next 10 to 15 years. That's not alarming, but it's significantly below the 14.7% yearly pace of the prior decade (as of Nov. 18). And considering above-normal inflation, the real projected return is lower.

But investors should understand the Buffett indicator's limitations. It ignores revenues that businesses collect outside the U.S., as this doesn't get captured in the GDP figure that's in the denominator. The biggest companies, especially those that operate in the technology sector , have substantial foreign operations, which naturally skews the Buffett indicator higher.

Story Continues

The market is underestimating one tailwind

Investors shouldn't be deterred. The right response to this information is still to build a diversified portfolio. If you can't help but be worried, then maybe it's best to increase your cash position. This will enable you to take advantage of opportunities that come up. And of course, always focus on buying high-quality names.

If you're someone who's staring at a multi-decade time horizon until retirement, it's recommended that you stay optimistic and bullish over the long term. Over any 20-year rolling period, the S&P 500 index has generated a positive return.

Waiting for a cheaper valuation seems like the right move. However, you shouldn't try to time the market. When the Buffett indicator was first thought of, a reading over 120% might have been considered expensive. Today, it's plausible that a Buffett indicator of over 200% is normal.

The nature of the monetary landscape is worth exploring. Since 2000, the M2 money supply in the U.S. has ballooned more than 400%. Furthermore, the U.S. federal debt has increased 7x during that same period. I think these are underappreciated tailwinds. There's no way that all of this liquidity, which supports risk assets and nominal earnings growth, hasn't had a profound impact on the stock market. Looking ahead, that trend will continue to be a constant propellant.

Be mindful of the Buffett indicator. But don't let it distract you. Time should continue to work in long-term investors' favor.

news.Title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq futures mixed as investors test Nvidia-fueled rally
news.Content:
US stock futures were mixed on Tuesday, building on a blistering rally, as investors took stock of what's next for Nvidia ( NVDA ) and the AI trade now that Jensen Huang is back as CEO.

Futures on the Dow Jones Industrial Average ( YM=F ) rose 0.1%, while those on the S&P 500 ( ES=F ) hovered near the flat line. Contracts for the Nasdaq-100 ( NQ=F ) fell 0.3% after stocks logged their best day since the "Liberation Day" recovery of April 2025.

Tech stocks were little changed after chip stocks roared back . Nvidia shares declined 3% following a 31% surge. Asian stocks, however, carried over the momentum, with South Korea's Kospi index ( ^KS11 ) up 7% and Japan's Nikkei ( ^N225 ) index up nearly 4%.

After paring back bets of a rate hike in December, traders shifted their odds again to forecast a 95% probability that the Federal Reserve will increase rates by 25 basis points and 5% odds of a jumbo 50 basis point hike. The AI rally stoked inflation concerns, while oil prices fell by about 1%.

Several companies are getting their earnings reports in before the Thanksgiving and Black Friday holidays, including Dell Technologies ( DELL ), Dollar Tree ( DLTR ), HP ( HP ), Best Buy ( BBY ), and Dick's Sporting Goods ( DKS ).

On the economic data front, investors will get a reading on consumer confidence and ADP's weekly change in employment.

LIVE 3 updates

just now Grace O'Donnell

How fear of AI displacement is fueling a hiring recession

Yahoo Finance's Hamza Shaban writes in today's Morning Brief newsletter:

The US labor market has proved remarkably resilient in the post-pandemic era. But as anyone looking for a job can tell you, it's rough out there. Just getting your resume past AI screeners and in front of a real person is a small victory in itself.

What's been described as a hiring recession is a labor market that has low unemployment but also one that has settled into a low-hire, low-fire environment. One of the reasons workers are staying put and fewer people are being welcomed aboard is artificial intelligence.

After a surge in people quitting their jobs or switching careers during the pandemic, workers are settling back in. But the lower levels of churn, or workers moving between jobs, are especially evident in industries closer to AI, suggesting a connection between a lack of labor dynamism and concerns around the technology.

"Churn has fallen further below pre-pandemic levels in industries with greater AI adoption and automation potential, as workers increasingly stay put amid rising job insecurity," analysts at Goldman Sachs wrote in a research report published Monday.

AI market whipsaw puts Kevin Warsh's rate-hike strategy to the test

Yahoo Finance's Jennifer Schonberger reports:

When stocks tanked last week, Wall Street briefly bet the Federal Reserve would ease up on interest rate hikes. Now Monday's massive rebound — sparked by Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia — has revived bets on at least two more interest rate hikes.

Yet with AI stocks still off their highs, the sector's volatility is emerging as a critical test for Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh and the central bank's path for rate hikes.

"AI stress is not mostly due to the Fed. But it is not a coincidence it is occurring when the Fed is hiking," said Krishna Guha, head of central banking and the economy for Evercore ISI. "Talk of 50-basis-point hikes or faster tightening adds to stress. Fed Chair Warsh not talking is a problem. It leaves the market guessing: Is he a hardcore hawk or a market-sensitive hawk? The gap is filled by others whose views can lag the leadership."

"This is a serious test for Warsh," Guha added.

news.Title: Nvidia's long-time CFO and now former interim CEO Colette Kress was left in the dark about Jensen Huang's return: Report
news.Content:
Colette Kress has been the CFO of Nvidia ( NVDA ) since 2013, helping to build the company at the center of the AI boom alongside founder and public face Jensen Huang.

She stepped into the line of fire for 12 days as interim CEO while Huang worked behind the scenes to return.

She withstood fresh reports of Huang berating her in meetings, and President Trump saying in an interview that she did a poor job in her post-earnings TV interview last week.

In the end, Nvidia's longtime CFO Colette Kress — a widely respected figure on Wall Street — has been left holding the bag.

And, apparently, left out of the loop on Huang's return.

"The talks that culminated in an Nvidia board meeting late on Sunday were so secretive that even interim chief executive officer Colette Kress was kept out of the discussions," a new report on Tuesday from the Financial Times said, citing people familiar with the matter.

An Nvidia spokesman didn't respond to Yahoo Finance's request for comment.

Shares of Nvidia fell nearly 4% in premarket trading on Tuesday after a 31.2% surge on news that founder Jensen Huang had been reinstated as CEO. That came just 12 days after he resigned amid a personal scandal and federal chip-export probes.

Kress is returning to the CFO role, though her LinkedIn profile still says interim CEO.

The dramatic reversal followed intense lobbying from President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, who intervened directly with directors and said Huang had been cleared of national security concerns.

Upon returning to Nvidia's Silicon Valley headquarters, Huang promised employees he would be a better CEO the second time around.

Despite the rally , Nvidia still faces ongoing DOJ and SEC investigations into alleged chip smuggling through blacklisted Singapore-based firm Megaspeed, prompting the board to appoint a new chief compliance officer.

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show, the ' Power Players With Brian Sozzi' podcast and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

news.Title: CVS Has Beaten Earnings Estimates 6 Quarters Straight. Why Is the Stock Under $90?
news.Content:
CVS Health (NYSE:CVS) has consistently beaten Wall Street's earnings expectations, raised its financial guidance, and improved profitability across its major businesses. Yet its stock continues trading below $90. In fact, CVS closed at $81.35 on Nov. 18, down 5.2% for the day, despite reporting another strong quarter earlier this month.

The company's latest results included $108.4 billion in revenue, up 5.4% year over year, and adjusted earnings of $2.09 per share, compared with $1.60 a year earlier. Analysts had expected roughly $1.65 per share. Management also raised its full-year adjusted earnings forecast to at least $8.20 per share, up from its previous range of $7.90 to $8.10.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

So why isn't Wall Street rewarding CVS for its improving financial performance?

Image source: Getty Images.

Earnings are improving, but concerns remain

CVS has spent the past several years managing rising healthcare costs, particularly in its Aetna insurance business. When patients require more medical care than insurers anticipated, insurance companies must pay more in claims. Unless premiums rise enough to offset those expenses, profitability suffers. CVS experienced precisely that problem.

In 2024 and part of 2025, its insurance business struggled with elevated medical costs, particularly among Medicare Advantage members. Those pressures contributed to disappointing financial results and forced management to reconsider pricing, benefits, and membership growth. Fortunately, the latest numbers show improvement.

In Q3, Aetna's medical benefit ratio fell to 91.3%, compared with 92.8% a year earlier. That ratio measures how much of an insurer's premium revenue goes toward paying medical claims. A lower number generally means the company retains more money to cover administrative expenses and generate profits. Still, a 91.3% medical benefit ratio leaves relatively little room for unexpected increases in healthcare costs.

CVS just announced a major breakup

On Nov. 4, CVS announced plans to separate into two publicly traded companies. One will include Aetna, CVS Caremark, CVS Specialty, Oak Street Health, and Signify Health. The other will operate approximately 9,000 CVS pharmacies, as well as MinuteClinic and related businesses. Management expects to complete the separation during the first half of 2028.

Story Continues

The announcement surprised investors. As a result, CVS shares plunged 12.5% that day, despite the company's earnings beat and improved guidance.

The decision also marks a departure from the strategy CVS pursued when it acquired Aetna for approximately $70 billion in 2018. At the time, management argued that combining insurance, pharmacies, and healthcare services would create a more efficient healthcare company. Now, CVS believes separating its retail pharmacy operations from its insurance and healthcare services businesses will provide greater flexibility and allow each company to focus on its own priorities.

Pharmacy profits face their own challenges

CVS also faces pressure in its pharmacy and pharmacy benefit management businesses. Pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) negotiate drug prices and manage prescription benefits for insurers and employers.

CVS Caremark is one of the country's largest PBMs, but the industry faces increasing regulatory scrutiny over drug pricing, rebates, and transparency. Changes to reimbursement arrangements could reduce profitability.

Meanwhile, CVS's retail pharmacy business continues to deal with reimbursement pressure and competition. Third-quarter retail pharmacy revenue declined 2% to approximately $35.5 billion, although adjusted operating income increased 10.6% to $1.64 billion. Prescription volume also increased. Those results suggest the business remains financially healthy, but revenue growth isn't guaranteed.

The valuation looks unusually inexpensive

At $81.35 per share, CVS trades for approximately 9.9 times management's projected 2026 adjusted earnings of at least $8.20 per share. That's a relatively modest valuation for a company expected to generate more than $420 billion in annual revenue.

CVS also generated $15.3 billion in operating cash flow during the first nine months of 2026, and management recently increased its full-year operating cash flow guidance to at least $15.5 billion, up from its previous forecast of at least $11.5 billion. The company also expects adjusted earnings of at least $8.65 per share in 2027.

At $81.35, the forward price-to-earnings ratio is approximately 9.4. However, adjusted earnings exclude certain expenses, and strong operating cash flow doesn't automatically translate into free cash flow available to shareholders. CVS still needs to fund capital expenditures, service its debt, and finance the planned separation.

Is CVS stock worth buying?

CVS's valuation suggests investors have already priced in considerable uncertainty. The insurance business is recovering, pharmacy profitability is improving, and management continues raising earnings expectations. But the proposed breakup complicates the outlook, while rising medical costs and regulatory changes remain legitimate concerns.

I'd be reluctant to dismiss CVS simply because its stock has struggled, though. If management delivers on its 2027 earnings guidance and successfully separates the businesses, today's valuation could prove attractive.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

Continue »

news.Content:
Digesting a historic day for the markets — and for AI chip champion Nvidia ( NVDA ).

Shares of Nvidia fell nearly 4% in premarket trading on Tuesday after a 31.2% surge on news that founder Jensen Huang had been reinstated as CEO. That came just 12 days after he resigned amid a personal scandal and federal chip-export probes.

The dramatic reversal followed intense lobbying from President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, who intervened directly with directors and said Huang had been cleared of national security concerns.

Upon returning to Nvidia's Silicon Valley headquarters, Huang promised employees he would be a better CEO the second time around.

Despite the rally, Nvidia still faces ongoing DOJ and SEC investigations into alleged chip smuggling through blacklisted Singapore-based firm Megaspeed, prompting the board to appoint a new chief compliance officer.

Wall Street analysts were universally positive on the stunning turn of events, and think the rally may just be starting.

news.Title: European shares pause as tech rally fades, Sanofi gains
news.Content:
By Anjana Jayakrishnan Nair

Nov 24 (Reuters) - European shares edged lower on Tuesday after their strongest session in six months, as a technology-led rebound lost momentum, while Sanofi gained after the French ‌drugmaker announced the acquisition of US-based Insmed.

The pan-European STOXX 600 edged down 0.16% to 635.92 ‌points by 0920 GMT after posting its biggest daily jump since early May the day before.

European technology stocks rose more than 4% ​on Monday in their biggest one-day jump since early April, after Jensen Huang's surprise reinstatement as CEO of US chipmaker Nvidia lifted risk appetite for the sector.

However, the rally fizzled out on Tuesday, with the index down 0.87%.

Aixtron retreated 8.8%, unwinding part of the previous session's gains after UBS downgraded the chip systems manufacturer to "sell". Peers Infineon ‌and ASM International dropped over 2% each.

"Nvidia ⁠got heavily oversold and the reaction was excessive ... it's perhaps no surprise that there was a degree of rebound when people looked at the cold light of day ⁠about what was actually going to happen," said Mike Coop, chief investment officer at Morningstar Wealth.

"We're in the late innings of this whole AI-led bull market. You're going to get more vulnerable swings around sentiment."

Huang's exit created a leadership ​overhang ​at the AI bellwether and investors unsatisfied with returns from ​AI investments and hefty valuations dumped tech ‌stocks recently, analysts said. The rout pushed the S&P 500 and the Dow into a technical correction last week.

Miners were the biggest percentage losers, down almost 3% as prices of gold and copper slipped. Anglo American and Antofagasta were among the STOXX 600's biggest decliners, each down over 5%.

Conversely, Sanofi gained 5.6% and was among the STOXX 600's top performers after the drugmaker said it would acquire US drug company Insmed for $41 billion, ‌marking the largest acquisition of CEO Belen Garijo's tenure.

It boosted ​healthcare stocks 0.1%.

Brent crude fell 0.95% to a near three-month low ​as rising supply outweighed Middle East tensions, lifting ​the travel and leisure index, which rose 0.2%.

Budget carrier Wizz Air rose 2.7% and ‌German airline Lufthansa gained 0.7%.

Among individual stocks, caterer ​Compass Group gained about 3.7% ​after reporting fiscal 2026 organic revenue growth above expectations and reaffirming plans to shift its primary listing to New York.

Balfour Beatty gained 4.5%, boosting the construction and materials sector after the construction group ​said revenue from operations was expected ‌to be 10% higher than in 2025.

Home improvement retailer Kingfisher slipped 4% as weaker trading in France ​and Poland overshadowed a modest profit guidance upgrade.

(Reporting by Anjana Jayakrishnan Nair and Purvi Agarwal ​in Bengaluru; Editing by Subhranshu Sahu and Janane Venkatraman)
