news.Title: Rocket Lab and Nebius Are Each About 66% Below Their Highs. I'd Buy Both and Hold Through 2030.
news.Content:
Rocket Lab (NASDAQ:RKLB) and Nebius Group (NASDAQ:NBIS) posted their record closes about three weeks apart this year. Rocket Lab peaked at $150.23 on May 27, and Nebius peaked at $286.69 on June 18.

As I write this, the space company trades around $51 and the artificial intelligence (AI) cloud provider trades near $97 -- each about 66% below its high.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The starting points differ, though. Rocket Lab is down around 27% this year, but Nebius still sits about 16% above where it finished 2025.

I think both stocks are worth owning at today's prices for investors willing to hold until 2030. But each hinges on a different bet.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Neutron is selling before it flies

Rocket Lab booked eight Neutron launches with five customers in the third quarter, worth over $515 million in all. Neutron, the company's reusable medium-lift rocket, hasn't flown yet, and its first launch is targeted for no earlier than 2027.

Still, several of these missions sold at a new $70 million base price, up from $55 million. The rocket's manifest now has 16 missions, and Rocket Lab says the next open launch slots are in the 2030s.

Customers are agreeing to pay more for an untested rocket, and the company credits tightening launch availability across the industry.

Of course, the business Rocket Lab already runs is growing, too. Its third-quarter revenue hit a record $268 million, up 73% year over year. This followed around $200 million in the first quarter and $234 million in the second, a steady climb of about $34 million each quarter. Fourth-quarter guidance of $270 million to $290 million implies the climb slowing, putting 2026 revenue near $980 million. Plus, backlog rose 52% in the third quarter to around $3.6 billion.

Yes, Rocket Lab is still losing money. Its third-quarter net loss was around $80 million, over four times the year-ago loss. Almost all of that jump comes from a one-time charge for canceling an unused bridge loan and a tax benefit that cut last year's loss. But for a 2030 holder, I think the Neutron order book matters more than this year's loss.

Nebius is spending far ahead of its revenue

In its Nov. 12 update, the AI cloud provider said it now expects 2026 revenue at the low end of its $3.0 billion to $3.4 billion range, because capacity at some third-party sites slipped into the first half of 2027. And it raised its 2026 capital expenditure outlook to around $27 billion, over its earlier $20 billion to $25 billion range.

Story Continues

That's about $9 of capital spending for every $1 of revenue this year. Nebius had spent around $15.4 billion through September, so the fourth quarter alone could pass $11 billion.

But the ratio should improve next year as that capacity starts earning. For 2027, Nebius expects to spend $40 billion to $45 billion and pull in $12 billion to $13 billion of revenue. That means spending should drop to around $3.40 per $1 of revenue.

Nebius says up-front customer payments and debt backed by its contracts should fund 75% to 85% of next year's spending. The rest might come from its $7.4 billion in cash or new outside capital, which may mean more debt or more shares.

How much is already priced in?

Rocket Lab has around 681 million shares (counting convertible preferred stock), giving it a market cap near $35 billion. That's about 35 times the revenue it's on track for this year.

If the sales multiple fell to 10 times sales by 2030, Rocket Lab would need around $3.5 billion in annual revenue just to stay worth $35 billion. This means growing revenue around 37% a year -- slower than its 66% rate through September, but probably only possible with Neutron flying on time.

And this leaves out its pending purchase of satellite operator Iridium Communications , which would add revenue and shares once it closes, expected by mid-2027.

Investors are paying far less for Nebius' plan. Its market cap of around $28 billion is only about 2.3 times the sales it expects in 2027 (at the midpoint). For a company expecting 2027 sales around four times this year's, that's a low price. I think investors either doubt the 2027 targets or expect shareholders to fund part of the build-out.

Would I buy both and hold them through 2030? Yes, in small amounts. Neutron may slip again, and Nebius might face more delays at sites it doesn't control.

I'd consider opening a small position in each today, adding to Rocket Lab after Neutron's first flight and to Nebius when its 2027 revenue starts showing up.

news.Title: The S&P 500 Just Had Its Worst Week in 18 Months. Is This a Buying Opportunity?
news.Content:
I can sum up last week's stock market performance in three letters: U-G-H. The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) had its worst week in 18 months, sinking nearly 9% over five days. At the market close on Friday, the index had entered correction territory. So had the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI).

Many investors could be wondering if the sell-off has only just begun. Others could be more hopeful. Is last week's market carnage a buying opportunity?

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

What's behind the decline

Any time the stock market pulls back sharply, it's smart to figure out why. With last week's sell-off, we only have to look at which stocks were hit the hardest to understand what's behind the decline.

Artificial intelligence (AI) stocks were absolutely hammered. Both Micron Technology 's (NASDAQ:MU) and Nvidia 's (NASDAQ:NVDA) shares plunged 23%. Google parent Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL), chipmaker Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO), and Facebook parent Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) saw their stocks tumble more than 10%. Microsoft 's (NASDAQ:MSFT) shares fell nearly 8%. Of the so-called "Magnificent Seven" stocks, only Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) managed to avoid a decline of more than 4%.

Investors are worried about tech giants' massive AI infrastructure spending, specifically whether it will pay off. Nvidia is still reeling from the resignation of co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO the previous week, amid allegations of misconduct that included a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. New U.S. chip export restrictions added to the pressure.

Some observers have warned about an AI bubble for a while. With all of the above factors at work, along with what appears to be a growing backlash against AI data centers in the U.S., it's possible that they were right -- and we're seeing that bubble burst.

Looking to the past

Before we succumb to a doom-and-gloom mentality, though, it's helpful to look to the past. As the old saying goes, "History doesn't always repeat itself, but it often rhymes."

The median return of the S&P 500 over the 12 months following a weekly decline of 5% or more is roughly 18.8%, according to an analysis by the Institute of Business and Finance (IBF). That's well above the index's average annual return of around 10% since its 1957 launch with 500 companies. Investors haven't usually had to wait a full year for a rebound after a steep sell-off, though. IBF found that the S&P 500 bounced back by a median of around 7% within 12 weeks of a weekly decline of at least 5%.

Story Continues

Granted, there have been periods where the market didn't recover so quickly. For example, it took more than seven years for the S&P to recover all of its losses when the dot-com bubble burst in 2000. For what it's worth, the S&P 500 Shiller CAPE (cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings) ratio is near its highest level since then.

Still, lengthy recoveries are the exception rather than the rule. Importantly, the U.S. economy remains resilient despite inflationary pressures. Corporate earnings were strong in the third quarter of 2026. All 11 sectors of the S&P 500 delivered year-over-year earnings growth.

There's also another historical precedent for investors to consider. Historically, stock market performance in the year following midterm elections has been strong. The S&P 500 has delivered positive returns over the 12 months after all 19 previous midterm elections, with an average gain of roughly 15%, according to JPMorgan Chase (NYSE:JPM).

A buying opportunity?

Let's return to the original question: Is last week's S&P 500 sell-off a buying opportunity? I think the answer is "yes." The latest stock market decline seems to be driven more by investor sentiment than by a fundamental deterioration. Sentiment can change quickly.

Sure, it's possible that the correction could last longer than I expect. Perhaps more signs of an AI bubble bursting will become apparent. However, I believe that tech companies' AI infrastructure spending will generate strong returns on investment over the next few years. I'm not in the "sky-is-falling" crowd.

If history is any guide, buying high-quality stocks or diversified exchange-traded funds (ETFs) now should pay off handsomely over the long term. And buying on the dip just might pay off over the short term, too.

news.Title: 禁空令與國安基金齊發威！龔明鑫解析台股震盪 明年出口拚破1兆美元
news.Content:
經濟部長龔明鑫今（23）日出席行政院「產業及金融業界代表座談」，於會中發表近期國內外產業與金融情勢分析，指出近期全球股市面臨劇烈震盪，台股重挫20.30%。不過台灣經濟基本面極為強勁，今年全年經濟成長率預估超過12%，可望創下39年來新高。政府已啟動國安基金護盤並祭出多項穩定資本市場措施，龔明鑫更樂觀預期，受惠於AI需求，2027年台灣出口有望突破1兆美元大關。

針對今年台灣總體經濟表現，龔明鑫引述主計總處與國發會數據指出，第3季經濟成長率概估達14.36%，全年可望突破12%，寫下39年來最佳紀錄。10月景氣對策信號綜合判斷分數為41分，連續10個月亮出紅燈，創下1984年以來最長連紅紀錄，顯示內需與外貿動能依舊暢旺。

在對外貿易與投資方面，受惠於新興科技應用需求強勁，今年前10月出口值已達7582.87億美元，較去年同期大幅成長47.68%。同期外銷訂單金額也超過9400億美元，全年將突破1.1兆美元。此外，10月資本設備進口年增率高達105.99%，反映企業對未來景氣深具信心，持續擴大在台投資規模。

然而，近期國際金融市場卻出現明顯回檔。龔明鑫分析，主要受到三大國際政經變數干擾，包括市場對AI龐大資本支出產生疑慮、美國大選後AI資料中心建置政策轉向，以及美國加強對中國AI與算力管制。同時，美伊地緣政治衝突推升國際油價與通膨壓力，導致聯準會升息預期升高，加上輝達高層人事異動，進一步引發全球市場恐慌。

在多重利空夾擊下，10月30日至11月20日期間全球主要股市同步走跌，並非只有台灣受創。美股費城半導體指數重挫21.33%，標普500指數下跌8.83%，道瓊指數跌幅7.00%。亞洲股市同樣未能倖免，日經指數下跌10.83%，韓國股市跌15.02%，台股則由45211點回檔至36033點，跌幅達20.30%。

為穩定資本市場秩序，政府已全面啟動六大護盤與穩市機制。除了國安基金正式進場護盤外，金管會也宣布全面禁止平盤以下放空，並將上市櫃有價證券融券保證金成數由130%調高至150%。此外，政府暫停受理發行認售權證上市櫃案件，鼓勵金融機構暫停對外出借股票，並將上市櫃公司實施庫藏股納入今年ESG評鑑指標，全力凝聚市場買氣。

在支持企業營運與產業轉型方面，經濟部因應美國關稅變數，已編列460億元韌性特別預算，透過外銷貸款優惠保證、中小微企業多元發展貸款、研發轉型補助及爭取海外訂單等四大方案力挺業者。同時，政府推動8年1000億元預算方案，每年投入250億元協助中小微企業升級，並結合公股銀行與中國輸出入銀行，提供融資利息減碼與輸出保險費用減免。

展望後市，龔明鑫強調，高效能運算與雲端服務需求將持續擴增，預估2027年台灣出口總額有望一舉突破1兆美元里程碑。面對短期國際金融波動，政府將持續傾聽產業界建言，與企業界攜手合作，以堅實的產業基本面作為後盾，共同穩定國內金融與市場信心。

news.Title: 《陸股》滬指漲0.15%、日K連二紅；創業板指漲3.08%
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-23 17:04:44 數位內容中心 發佈

中國A股今(23)日延續回升，上證指數收於3,538.95點，上漲0.15%，日K連二紅；深證成指收於10,454.37點，上漲1.93%；創業板指收於2,280.20點，上漲3.08%，為三大指數中表現最強；科創50指數收於1,227.89點，下跌0.26%。盤勢呈現成長題材走強、權值與科創相對分化的格局。

依盤勢來看，市場超過4,600檔個股上漲，盤中人形機器人概念爆發，AI漫劇概念走強，PCB與CPO族群也同步活躍，帶動指數由弱轉強。早盤一度承壓的創業板指午後探底回升，成為修復主軸。成交量方面，滬市今日成交7,385億元(人民幣,下同)，深市成交8,144億元，兩市成交額1兆5,529億元，較前一交易日量增約9%。

市場回暖與週末釋出的調整措施有關，包括融資保證金比例下限由100%調降至80%，以及交易所和中國結算推出一攬子降費措施。這些變化帶動風險偏好回升，也為流動性與交易情緒提供支撐。

類股方面，創業板指強勢反彈，反映資金回流成長與題材方向；上證指數小幅收高，顯示大盤整體偏穩。相較之下，銀行類股震盪調整，科創相關權重偏弱，科創50指數收跌，與題材族群走強形成對照。

《陸股》滬指跌1.23%，惟日K翻紅；創業板指跌3.54%

《日股》AI、半導體撐盤，日經收漲1.31%

資料來源- MoneyDJ理財網

news.Title: 散戶被嚇跑？台股史上最苦10月 證券劃撥餘額月減逾5千億元破紀錄
news.Content:
10月市場對AI產業前景出現雜音，台股單月跌2729點寫下史上最慘10月牽動資金移動，10月底上市櫃融資餘額8454億元仍續創歷史新高，不過，證券劃撥存款餘額單月卻大減5,000多億元，寫下史上最大，金額降至4.19兆元。

針對證券劃撥存款大減逾5,000億元，央行經研處行務委員劉淑敏解釋，現今銀行數位轉帳與資金調度極為快速，加上證券劃撥帳戶的活存利率較低，投資人一旦沒有立即買股需求，便會迅速將資金轉出作其他配置，因此該指標的資金流動速度極快，不一定是散戶全面退場。

此外，在集中市場交易動向方面，10月包括本國自然人（散戶）、本國法人（本土法人）與僑外法人（外資）的成交金額其實全面較9月成長，其中本國自然人由18兆153億元增至18兆7,538億元，本國法人由3兆6,967億元增至4兆2,839億元，僑外法人則由13兆5,157億元增至13兆9,140億元。

不過，受各類投資人增幅消長影響，10月集中市場成交金額占比出現微幅拉鋸，本國自然人比重由9月的51.1%微降至50.7%，僑外法人由38.3%降至37.6%，本國法人則由10.5%上升至11.6%。

在外匯存款動向方面，10月底外匯存款年增率降至9.24%，較上個月的13.55%明顯回落。劉淑敏說明，外匯存款年增率趨緩主要有兩大原因：第一是企業賺取的貨款多留在海外支付貨款或進行海外投資，匯回台灣的外匯減少，與國際收支趨勢一致；第二則是部分社會保險及退休基金增加海外投資，使國內外匯存款水位隨之下降。

（陳景淵／審核）

陳依旻／財經特派記者副組長，主跑央行、證交所、投信投顧等

news.Title: Adobe's Next Report Is Dec. 9. Here's How the Stock Reacted to Each of the Last 10.
news.Content:
Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE) stock has fallen in reaction to six of the company's last 10 December earnings reports. And the drops have been far bigger than the gains. None of the four up days topped 4%, while four of the six down days were worse than 6%, including a nearly 14% dive in December 2024.

The creative software company will hold its next earnings call after the close on Wednesday, Dec. 9.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

But the stock heads into this one in a much different place. Shares closed at around $222 on Nov. 19, down about 37% so far this year, and trade at about 9 times what Adobe earned on a non-GAAP (adjusted) basis in its last four quarters.

The stock didn't go into any of those 10 reports this cheap. And I think the price matters more than the track record.

Image source: Getty Images.

Six drops and four gains

Adobe normally posts results after the close and hosts its call at 2 p.m. Pacific time, so the reaction comes the next trading day. In 2020 and 2021, it reported before the open and held a meeting with financial analysts, so those rows use the same day's move.

The last column divides the stock price at the start of each report by the adjusted earnings per share for the fiscal year the report covers.

Data source: Yahoo Finance and Adobe. Calculations by author.

The four gains averaged less than 3%. The six drops averaged almost 7%.

What drives the stock on report day?

In recent years, the December report is also where Adobe lays out its targets for the next fiscal year. And those targets seem to matter more to the stock than the quarter itself.

Showing how much the outlook can weigh on shares, Adobe ended fiscal 2024 with revenue of $21.5 billion, up 11%, and its fiscal 2025 target called for $23.30 billion to $23.55 billion. That worked out to growth of about 9% at the midpoint. The stock sank almost 14% the next day.

The year before, Adobe's fiscal 2024 target implied growth of around 10%, in line with fiscal 2023's rate. The stock still lost about 6% after the report, though it had gained about 85% that year going in.

Story Continues

Adobe's starting price seems to matter most

Last December's outlook looked a lot like the one from December 2024. Fiscal 2025 revenue was $23.8 billion, another 11% rise, and the fiscal 2026 target of $25.90 billion to $26.10 billion called for growth of around 9% at the midpoint. Interestingly, this time shares gained about 2% the next day.

The difference, I think, was the price. Adobe traded at around 30 times its adjusted earnings ahead of the December 2024 report, but only about 16 times its adjusted earnings heading into last year's. Much of the bad news was arguably already baked into the stock.

The rest of the table lines up, too. All six drops came with the stock at around 30 times adjusted earnings or higher, while the two cheapest setups, in 2022 and 2025, both brought gains.

Sure, valuation doesn't explain every move. Shares also climbed in 2017 and 2019 at roughly 40 times adjusted earnings, and 10 reports is a small sample. But if investors pay a high price, the outlook might need to impress them. At a low price, it may just need to avoid a disappointment.

The price may be low enough this time

Adobe now trades far below even last December's valuation. And the business is ahead of its original outlook. The original fiscal 2026 target called for around 9% revenue growth. After revenue climbed 13% year over year for the quarter ended Aug. 28, management lifted its revenue target in September to between $26.58 billion and $26.63 billion. This implies growth of around 12%, faster than fiscal 2025's 11% rate.

The report also lands eight days after Anil Chakravarthy, who heads Adobe's customer experience business and field operations, becomes CEO, with Shantanu Narayen shifting to executive chair. It'll probably have the first full-year targets set under him. Sure, a new CEO might pick a cautious starting point.

Still, at this price, I don't think the targets need to impress for the stock to hold up. The reaction might look more like 2025's gain than 2024's drop. But it's just a guess, and one trading day says little about where the stock heads from here.

I'm more confident about the valuation. For a company still growing revenue by double digits, around 9 times adjusted earnings looks cheap to me, and I think Adobe stock is worth considering before Dec. 9, whichever way it moves the next day.

news.Title: 台股劇震槓桿投資風險浮現　房仲憂房市盤整期拉長
news.Content:
（中央社記者潘姿羽台北2026年11月23日電）房仲指出，今年前3季全國建物買賣移轉棟數減少，抵押權設定棟數卻逆勢增加，雙貸族人數也創新高，推測民眾透過房屋增貸等作法取得資金投入股市是原因之一。不過近期股市劇震，槓桿投資風險浮現，房仲憂心若信心未能回穩，恐拉長房市盤整期。

台灣房屋今天發布新聞稿指出，內政部資料顯示，今年前3季全國建物買賣移轉棟數約19.4萬棟，較去年同期微減0.7%，同期間設定建物抵押權棟數不減反增，總計約46.2萬棟，年增5.7%，房屋抵押設定的熱度高於市場買氣。

台灣房屋集團趨勢中心執行長張旭嵐說明，建物抵押權設定是將房屋作為借款的擔保品，以保障債權人權益；房屋設定抵押權以辦理購屋貸款為大宗，屋主轉增貸週轉、債務整合等，也是常見的原因。抵押權設定除了受房市交易量牽動，也與屋主運用房產取得資金的需求息息相關。

張旭嵐進一步指出，台股今年從年初不到3萬點，至10月上旬直逼5萬點，不少民眾運用房屋增貸或申辦理財型房貸，取得資金投入股市；加上部分縣市新案交屋潮湧現，也帶動申貸購屋量能，使今年的建物抵押權設定較去年成長。

不過近期台股劇烈震盪，台灣房屋集團趨勢中心資深經理陳定中表示，過度利用不動產操作槓桿投資，可能讓原本穩定的房產面臨財務風險；台股上週崩跌逾7000點，以房屋抵押取得資金的投資人，除了股市損失，還須持續償還房屋融資的本利，若現金流不足，還可能被迫出售股票或處分房產填補缺口。

信義房屋也指出，聯徵中心資料顯示，今年7月雙貸族（房貸加信貸）數量已經突破43萬人，數量寫下歷史新高，且仍處於持續增加的趨勢。

信義房屋不動產企研室專案經理曾敬德表示，台股急速下殺，借錢投資風險浮現，不只對槓桿投資的民眾帶來壓力，也可能進而影響房市，衝擊大小關鍵在於股災時間長短；若短時間內可以回穩，便可降低對房市影響，但若時間拉長，可能打擊民眾的信心與購買力，資金調度的需求也隨之增加。

住商機構盤整證交所與內政部資料，比對後發現，歷年12次重大股災中，扣除尚無完整房市數據的2025、2026年股災，其餘10次有5次股災後隔年房市買氣不減反增。

住商不動產企劃研究室執行總監徐佳馨分析，股市與房市存在資金連動關係，不過兩者流動性不同，股市短期重挫，不代表房市立即出現拋售潮，但可能影響原本要買房的民眾意願。至於房市何時迎來轉機，除了觀察股市能否止穩，後續央行信用管制、銀行放款態度及整體經濟表現，才是更值得關注的指標。

大家房屋企劃研究室公關襄理賴志昶則說，房市當前信用管制壓力續存，若股市長期低迷，政府救市措施未能發揮顯著效果，恐使購屋人資金面臨更大壓力，進一步延長房市盤整期。

news.Title: 不只國安基金出手？專家揭台股87度往上噴關鍵：那個男人救援
news.Content:
台股上周遭遇史詩級賣壓，單周重挫7641.83點，跌幅高達17.5%，創下近35年來最劇烈的單周跌幅，市場信心受到重創。政府緊急出手穩定市場，金管會也祭出「限空令3.0」，但台股今（23）日開盤仍然走弱一度下探35442.41點，再創波段新低，隨後因為「1個轉折」突然翻盤，終場大漲778點，收在36,811點，漲幅2.16%，成交值約1.07兆元，讓投資人驚呼行情大逆轉。

投資達人葉育碩在臉書發文指出，上周五美股重挫，台指期暴跌1881 點，原本市場普遍擔憂台股周一開盤恐怕還有另一波賣壓。不過，周末行政院緊急召開財經會議，金管會宣布實施「限空令3.0」，加上韓國、大陸也陸續推出穩定市場措施，讓市場多了一些支撐，但台股盤中仍然多空激烈交戰，指數上下震盪達1665.79 點。

真正讓盤勢出現變化的關鍵，則是美國總統川普公開力挺輝達前執行長黃仁勳。葉育碩表示，川普上午10時54分透過社群平台發文，希望輝達董事會重新聘用黃仁勳，並認為這將是對輝達及美國最好的決定。貼文發布後，台股隨即出現明顯拉升，原本在低檔震盪的指數彷彿打了一劑強心針，他甚至形容行情「直接87度往上噴」。

葉育碩認為，政府限空措施確實為市場提供一定支撐，但川普力挺黃仁勳的發文，意外成為盤中市場情緒反轉的焦點。他也幽默表示，最後讓市場突然振作起來的，還是「那個男人」川普。

黃仁勳動向備受關注，除了美國總統川普第三度力挺他回鍋，財長貝森特（Scott Bessent）曾公開表態輝達董事會應該從外部尋找執行長，如今態度也放軟，他昨（22）日受訪表示，「黃仁勳現在已在外部」，上述回應被部分外媒解讀不反對黃仁勳回鍋。

news.Title: Nvidia vs. SpaceX: Here's Which Stock I'd Put $1,000 Towards Right Now
news.Content:
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) are popular artificial intelligence ( AI) stocks and, no doubt, household names right now.

SpaceX continues to expand its rocket launch business, artificial intelligence services, and Starlink internet service. Led by Elon Musk, SpaceX's businesses appear to be on an upward trajectory, though the company's spending is accelerating and profits remain sparse.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Nvidia is still growing like a weed, too, with sales and earnings surging in its recently reported third-quarter fiscal 2027 results. But with co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang recently resigning after admitting to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, some wonder what the future holds for this leading AI company.

Which is the better company to put $1,000 toward right now? My bet is on Nvidia stock. Here's why.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

SpaceX rising

SpaceX reported impressive Q3 2026 (which ended Sept. 30) results, including the 161% jump in revenue to $14.6 billion. The soaring sales helped SpaceX swing to a profit, achieving net income of $4.4 billion, up from a loss of $1.1 billion in the year-ago quarter.

SpaceX's three core business segments -- Starlink, Space Launch, and Super Intelligence (what is calls artificial intelligence) -- all expanded in the quarter. Starlink sales were up 69% to $5.2 billion, Space Launch revenue climbed 6% to $1.8 billion, and the company's Super Intelligence was a standout success, soaring 830% to $7.6 billion.

AI growth was certainly the headline for the quarter. The company rents cloud computing capacity to other tech companies and also has its own Grok AI model. The company is spending heavily to expand its AI infrastructure, which is clearly paying off but could continue to weigh on profitability.

Capital expenditures (capex) rose 185% to $19.6 billion in the quarter, with 83% going to AI. And SpaceX's management says AI spending will be between $35 billion and $40 billion in Q4 alone, making a sizable acceleration of spending.

Nvidia's drama

Jensen Huang is currently trying to mount a comeback to the Nvidia CEO role, but it's unlikely to succeed. Nvidia Board Chair Harvey Jones said in the fiscal 2027 Q3 (ended Oct. 25) that the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."

Story Continues

That's for the better. Despite Huang being instrumental in growing Nvidia into an AI juggernaut, there are serious unanswered questions about whether his actions affected national security and if Nvidia knew that some of its chips were being smuggled into China. In short, Nvidia's drama is far from over even with CFO Colette Kress taking the helm as interim CEO at the company.

Putting all of that aside for a moment, Nvidia actually had a fantastic quarter. The company's sales more than doubled to $115.8 billion, and its earnings popped 111% to $2.68 per share. Nvidia's chips are in high demand as the AI boom surges on, helping the company earn enviable gross margins of nearly 75%.

The company's important data center segment was a standout success, with revenue rising 110% from the year-ago quarter to $107.6 billion.

More growth for the company is likely on the way, too. Nvidia's management said Q4 sales will be $130 billion, rising 90% year over year. And leadership raised fiscal 2028 revenue guidance to 75%, up from its previous guidance of 70%.

Why I'd put $1,000 toward Nvidia over SpaceX right now

Even with all of Nvidia's drama, and given SpaceX's recent growth, I still believe that putting $1,000 toward Nvidia is currently the better move.

The reasons are pretty straightforward. Nvidia is much more profitable than SpaceX and spends far less to grow its business. That doesn't mean SpaceX can't be a good long-term investment, but it puts Nvidia in a much better financial position.

What's more, Nvidia's shares are far cheaper. Nvidia stock has a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of around 10, which is below the tech sector average and far below SpaceX's forward P/E ratio of 49.

Nvidia has a lot of drama to overcome, but its high profitability and its cheaper price tag give it the win in this matchup.

news.Title: 《韓股》AI題材疑慮未減 KOSPI續跌3.31%
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-23 16:38:28 數位內容中心 發佈

news.Title: 台股11月急跌逾20％ 端460億銀彈護產業 龔明鑫說話了
news.Content:
面對台股波段重挫20.3％，政府全面啟動穩市與產業紓困。行政院23日召開「產業及金融業界代表座談」，經濟部長龔明鑫指出，除國安基金進場護盤並祭出6大穩市措施外，經濟部編列460億元韌性特別預算力挺企業，看好高效能運算與雲端需求續強，明年台灣出口有望突破1兆美元。

龔明鑫在簡報中指出，10月30日至11月20日全球股市同步修正，費半跌21.33％、台股由45211點跌至36033點（跌20.3％）、韓股跌15.02％、日經跌10.83％，標普與道瓊也分別跌8.83％與7％。

主因來自3大國際變數：市場對AI龐大資本支出存疑、美國選後AI資料中心政策改變及加強管制中國算力；美伊衝突推升油價通膨與聯準會升息預期；以及輝達高層人事異動引發震盪。

儘管股市劇烈洗牌，台灣基本面依然強勁。主計總處概估今年第3季經濟成長率達14.36％，全年估逾12％，將創39年新高；10月景氣指標41分，連亮10顆紅燈，改寫1984年以來最長紀錄。前10月出口達7582.87億美元、年增47.68％，外銷訂單破9400億美元，全年可望衝破1.1兆美元；10月資本設備進口更年增105.99％，擴產動能未減。

為穩住市場信心，龔明鑫指出，政府除啟動國安基金護盤，並實施禁平盤下放空、保證金成數調高至150％、暫停認售權證、庫藏股納入2026年ESG評鑑及鼓勵暫停借券等6大措施。產業端則以460億元特別預算提供研發轉型補助與外銷貸款保證，搭配8年1千億元中小微企業方案與輸出入銀行融資減碼，協助台廠穩住全球供應鏈布局。

news.Title: 台股有底氣！證交所祭出秘密武器　這兩項穩定市場信心
news.Content:
財經中心／綜合報導

近期台股受國際金融市場波動影響，惟臺灣產業長期競爭優勢穩固，更持續在全球科技發展中扮演關鍵角色。尤其臺灣憑藉完整的人工智慧(AI)產業生態系與供應鏈優勢，長期成長前景穩健。為展現對臺灣產業實力的高度信心並協助市場回歸基本面，證交所董事長林修銘致函全體上市公司，並由證交所專人致電，鼓勵上市公司實施庫藏股計畫及辦理法人說明會，透過強化資訊揭露與投資人溝通，凝聚市場信心。

鼓勵實施庫藏股計畫 企業買回自家股票

證交所與上市公司保持密切溝通，請各公司在市場波動期間，主動評估各項維護股東權益及提升企業價值之措施。對於財務體質健全、營運展望穩定且具備充裕資金之上市公司，建議實施庫藏股措施，以展現企業對自身營運前景的信心，並強化投資人對上市公司長期價值之認同。金管會並已宣布，企業實施庫藏股措施，若於115年度至116年第1季期間屆滿或執行完畢，可納入115年ESG評鑑指標得分。

積極推動辦理法人說明會 增加市場認知

為使投資人能即時掌握上市公司最新營運情形，證交所鼓勵上市公司提高辦理法人說明會頻率，由企業主動對外說明經營成果及未來營運展望，讓投資人充分瞭解企業經營現況與長期成長潛力，避免市場情緒影響投資判斷。證交所將持續鼓勵上市公司強化投資人關係，並透過公開資訊觀測站等多元管道提供投資人查詢，協助各界掌握企業最新發展，進一步提升市場信心。

證交所董事長林修銘表示，臺灣資本市場歷經多次國際政經情勢變化與金融市場考驗，始終展現高度韌性，上市公司憑藉創新技術優勢與全球布局，具堅實的產業競爭基礎，長期穩健發展的基本面並未改變。面對短期外部因素干擾，投資人宜理性看待市場變化，回歸企業基本面與長期發展前景。證交所將持續與全體上市公司密切合作，強化資訊透明並共同展現企業價值，推動臺灣資本市場穩健成長。

news.Title: 台積電注入強心針　AI長期看好先進製程持續供不應求
news.Content:
（中央社記者張建中新竹2026年11月23日電）AI市場前景疑慮升高，重創全球股市。晶片代工廠台積電 (2330) 今天表示，全球AI需求與日俱增，長期展望持續看好，市場對於先進製程技術的需求依然強勁，產能持續供不應求。

美國期中選舉民主黨大獲全勝，市場憂心美國人工智慧（AI）資料中心政策恐將轉變。全球人工智慧（AI）晶片龍頭輝達（NVIDIA）前執行長黃仁勳辭職，美國政府又發布新規進一步限制晶片出口至海外資料中心，更加深市場對於AI前景的疑慮，重創全球股市。

台積電今天指出，全球對AI的需求與日俱增，長期展望持續看好。隨著應用場景逐漸從聊天機器人轉向AI助理，代理式AI的普及更進一步推升了整體需求。

台積電表示，半導體在AI大趨勢中依舊扮演不可或缺的核心角色。隨著半導體在全球供應鏈中的價值持續攀升，不僅為全球客戶開創值得掌握的龐大商機，也為台積電帶來更多高價值潛力，因為無論客戶採用何種架構方案，都需要最先進的半導體製程技術作為後盾。

台積電指出，零組件價格上漲與總體經濟的不確定性為消費性產品及價格敏感的終端市場帶來挑戰。不過，台積電強大的技術差異化優勢與廣泛的客戶群支持，市場對先進製程技術的需求依然強勁，先進的半導體製程產能持續供不應求。

news.Title: 《美股主題週報》新式核能—OKLO、LEU、CEG
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-23 16:25:33 數位內容中心 發佈

Oklo（OKLO.US）

11月，Oklo與Centrus Energy簽署具約束力的多年期高含量低濃縮鈾（HALEU）供應合約，2029年開始交付，供應量足以支援最多5座Aurora powerhouses。這筆燃料安排也對應俄亥俄州1.2GW園區第一階段部署。

Centrus Energy（LEU.US）

本週Centrus Energy將與Oklo的合作推進為正式HALEU供應合約，2029年啟動交付，並由Oklo預付款支持新濃縮產能擴建。公司並揭露，新增產能對應的低濃縮鈾（LEU）與HALEU合約及承諾總額已達54億美元。

Constellation Energy（CEG.US）

本週Constellation Energy最明確的訊號是科技客戶正直接支持既有核電擴容。Google合約支撐超過43億美元投資、涵蓋11座核電機組，預計為PJM電網增加約890MW增量容量，首次擴容預定2028年實現。

X-energy（XE.US）

11月12日，X-energy揭露德州Long Mott Generating Station取得美國核能管理委員會（NRC）施工許可。這是美國近60年來首個高溫氣冷式反應爐施工許可，也讓Xe-100由設計與審查階段推進到實體建設節點。

Fluor（FLR.US）

本週Fluor獲X-energy選定，將為華盛頓州Cascade Advanced Energy Facility提供核島工程、設計與供應鏈服務。該案首期部署4座Xe-100、合計320MW，顯示其角色已延伸到先進反應爐核島工程與供應鏈整備。

GE Vernova（GEV.US）

本週GE Vernova相關SMR進度出現時程壓力。Ontario Power Generation表示，安大略省GE Vernova Hitachi SMR專案可能無法達成原訂2030年10月投運目標；首座機組容量300MW，初始總預算約54億美元。

NANO Nuclear Energy（NNE.US）

11月19日，NANO Nuclear Energy與SJ Group旗下Surbana Jurong Infrastructure簽署非約束性合作備忘錄，重點放在東南亞的知識交流、能力建構與潛在應用評估。其KRONOS微型模組化反應爐（MMR）單機發電能力最高15MW。

NuScale Power（SMR.US）

11月23日，NuScale Power宣布在商業化部署流程中導入Everstar的核能人工智慧（AI）平台Gordian，應用於執照申請、專案管理與供應鏈。公司同步重申，其反應爐設計仍是美國NRC第一且唯一完成設計認證的小型模組化反應爐（SMR）。

news.Title: Hedge funds post worst week since April 2025, sparks defensive shift
news.Content:
By Summer Zhen and Anirban Sen

HONG KONG, Nov 23 (Reuters) - Global hedge funds lost more than 3% in the week ended November ‌20 amid a brutal tech-led selloff, their biggest drawdown since April ‌2025, when markets were hit by tariff-induced turmoil, according to a client note from JPMorgan on ​Friday.

That exacerbated hedge funds' average loss for November to 4%, the bank said, accelerating a broader de-risking by fund managers.

Semiconductor and other AI-linked shares were sold heavily as investors reassessed the technology's profit capabilities following AI bellwether Nvidia's crisis ‌and Anthropic's volatile Nasdaq debut.

The ⁠tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite slumped 10% last week, its largest weekly loss since March 2020 and dipped into negative territory for ⁠the year. Nvidia tumbled 23% for the week.

In Asia, Taiwan's stock market plunged 17.5% last week, recording its worst week in more than three decades, while Korea's ​Kospi tumbled ​8%.

"Hedge funds have struggled amid the ​recent surge in equity market volatility," ‌Goldman Sachs said in a hedge fund note.

These funds have cut exposure and lowered leverage aggressively with "equity long/short net exposures now rival April 2025 as the lowest levels since pre-COVID," Goldman Sachs said, based on an analysis of the holdings of 1,001 hedge funds with positions worth $5.1 trillion.

As the AI trade ‌unwinds, non-AI stocks have emerged as rising ​stars, with fund managers rotating into financials, consumer ​discretionary and industrials, Goldman added.

JPMorgan ​analysts said the defensive shift has also driven hedge fund ‌positioning in US consumer staples distribution ​and retail stocks ​to historical highs, while the healthcare sector has attracted large inflows.

Even so, investment banks believe the selloff may not be over yet.

JPMorgan analysts led ​by John Schlegel said ‌they are waiting to see whether there's a broader capitulation as ​the position level is still above more severe washout levels.

(Reporting by ​Summer Zhen, Editing by Louise Heavens)

news.Title: 國安基金護盤還不夠？葉育碩揭台股噴漲真相：全靠「那個男人」神助攻
news.Content:
台股 今（23）日上演戲劇性絕地大反攻！在經歷上週狂瀉逾7,600點、台指期夜盤一度暴跌超過1,600點的震撼教育後，大盤早盤雖一度急殺近600點，但隨後買盤大舉湧入，終場狂飆778.60點，收在36,811.89點，成交金額高達1兆791.65億元。究竟是誰成功挽救了台股？ 財經專家葉育碩 觀察，政府祭出穩市措施、國安基金進場護盤，原本已替市場帶來支撐，但真正讓氣氛突然轉變的，還是美國總統川普對輝達人事案的最新表態。

【週末多國緊急救市 台股早盤仍載浮載沉】

回顧上週五夜盤暴跌逾1,600點，市場原本預期今（23）日開盤將迎來一場腥風血雨。葉育碩指出，所幸台灣政府在週末緊急開會，於今日正式啟動「禁空令3.0」與 國安基金 進場護盤，韓國與中國也趁著假日同步推出穩定市場政策，讓台股早盤得以開出比夜盤預期更穩健的走勢。然而，盤中多空雙方依然持續拉鋸、走勢載浮載沉，市場氣氛明顯還在等待一個能夠徹底扭轉局勢的重磅消息。

【川普10:54發文挺黃仁勳 台股秒打強心針87度狂噴】

「直到那個沉默很久的男人，終於出來說話了！」葉育碩在社群平台興奮點出轉折關鍵，美國總統川普於 台灣時間早上10點54分 再度發文公開喊話：「我希望輝達（NVDA）董事會重新聘用黃仁勳。這對這家公司，同時也對美國，都會是最好的決定。」貼文一出立刻引爆市場多頭情緒，葉育碩形容，原本還在水面載浮載沉的台股大盤，瞬間像是打了強心針一般「直接87度往上噴」，成為今日台股狂漲778點的最強催化劑。

【權值股全面點火反攻 聯電直攻漲停、台積電強彈30元】

在 政府護盤措施 與黃仁勳可望重返輝達的雙重利多激勵下，台股 今日高低震盪超過1,200點 ，成功化解市場恐慌。權值股全面領軍反攻，護國神山台積電（2330） 強彈上漲30元，晶圓代工大廠 聯電（2303）更是跌深強勢直攻漲停板，聯發科（2454） 與 廣達（2382）也同步走揚。葉育碩笑稱，今天救市的功臣雖然包含台灣政府、韓國與中國的政策利多，但最後真正一舉扭轉乾坤、讓台股重燃信心的，「還是那個男人！」

news.Title: 證交所董座親筆信「催庫藏股」穩台股！網推：找魏哲家開記者會更快
news.Content:
台股歷經一個多月重挫逾1萬4千點的劇烈修正後，今（23）日看到曙光，站回3萬6千點大關，為進一步凝聚多頭信心，證交所董事長林修銘今日發出親筆信並專人致電上市公司，鼓勵企業實施庫藏股與舉辦法說會，隨即在PTT股板掀起兩派熱議，一派力挺「自己股價自己救」，另一派則認為是「情緒勒索」，甚至喊話不如直接找台積電董事長魏哲家開記者會比較快。

相關新聞： 台股站回3萬6！證交所董座親筆信「催油門」 請企業買回庫藏股

歷經前幾日的劇烈震盪，台股今（23）日站回3萬6千點大關，為了進一步凝聚多頭氣勢，證交所董事長林修銘今日致函全體上市公司並由專人致電，鼓勵企業實施庫藏股計畫及辦理法人說明會，期盼透過強化資訊揭露與投資人溝通，穩固市場信心。

回顧近期盤勢，台股自10月初一度衝上49,968點、逼近5萬點大關，但到今日盤中最低點35,442點，短短一個多月內重挫超過1萬4千點，若當時在高點看多進場的投資人，帳面等於面臨逾三成的劇烈修正。在市場信心急著等待修復之際，政府與主管機關接連喊話成為許多股民的重要定心丸，因此，證交所祭出「道德勸說」的消息一出，立刻在PTT股板掀起兩派激烈討論。

支持企業出手自救的網友紛紛留言表示，「這才是最重要的，自己股價不自救還要別人來救?」、「自己的股票自己救，快救我！」、「自己公司股價不救，還指望國安」、「糖漿有限 請支援護盤」，並對金管會將執行庫藏股納入評鑑的配套表示「可納入今年度ESG評鑑指標得分 高招」。

不過，另一派網友則對官方大動作喊話抱持不同看法，除了有人幽默調侃這波勸說簡直是「道德勸說（X）情緒勒索（O）」、「不買庫藏股就是缺德」、「庫藏股也能道德勸說喔」、「情勒大會」、「做功德勸說」；也有股民從漲幅與基本面切入，直呼「台股今年還漲快三成 要護成這樣？」、「基本面不是良好？」、「請公司吃基本麵，但是公司自己有基本麵」，更有人點出籌碼面問題，直言「先勸說自營阿從頭到尾賣的比外資還狠」，甚至有網友建議證交所乾脆直接求助護國神山台積電董事長魏哲家，打趣寫道：「要不要乾脆把CC抓去開記者會更快一點。」

儘管網路兩派討論，仍有股民務實指出「我相信還是有點用 畢竟還是得賣點面子」。

事實上，在證交所董事長林修銘發出親筆信鼓勵實施庫藏股後，市場隨即出現實質響應，半導體載具大廠家登（3680）今日率先開出第一槍，宣布明（24）日起兩個月內，以每股240至450元買回3,000張庫藏股轉讓員工，最高斥資約13.5億元；此外，包括上周逆勢護盤的榮剛（5009），以及今日同步跟進的南俊國際（6584），也相繼加入實施庫藏股留才的行列。

news.Title: 華邦電攜成大成立共同研發中心 聚焦四大核心技術領域
news.Content:
記憶體大廠華邦電(2344-TW)攜手國立成功大學成立「華邦－成大共同研發中心」，華邦電每年將投入1,000萬元，聚焦AI半導體製程優化、先進封裝熱管理、次世代電容元件及智慧製程等四大技術領域，並結合獎學金、實習及半導體學程，深化產學合作與人才培育。

共同研發中心日前由華邦電總經理陳沛銘與成大校長沈孟儒共同揭牌。陳沛銘表示，隨著AI與新興應用持續發展，半導體產業對記憶體效能、製程技術及系統整合的要求不斷提升，此次成立共同研發中心，是雙方既有合作的延伸，也是深化前瞻技術布局與人才培育的重要里程碑。

在技術研發方面，雙方將聚焦四大核心領域，包括AI驅動半導體製程優化與積體電路設計、先進封裝與記憶體架構熱管理、次世代電容元件與AI輔助模擬，以及智慧製程與機器學習維運(MLOps)，透過跨領域技術整合，加速新材料、新製程及新元件開發，強化記憶體技術競爭力。

人才培育方面，華邦電與成大自2022年起合作推動「華邦×成大半導體領導學程」，並持續深化記憶體電路設計課程、獎學金及產學合作計畫。未來也將整合成大材料、電機、微電子、資訊及工業與資訊管理等跨院系資源，透過業師授課、專題研究、企業參訪及實習媒合，促進學術研究與產業實務接軌。

沈孟儒表示，大學應在不同時期回應國家與社會需求，透過學術研究協助國家發展。成大適逢創校95週年，此次與華邦電成立共同研發中心，也進一步彰顯產學合作推動技術創新的重要價值。

華邦電與成大至今已累計推動13項產學合作計畫，共同研發中心成立後，將建立長期合作及定期交流機制，並由雙方高層組成指導委員會，持續檢視技術研發方向與合作成果，另將於成大自強校區啟端館設置共同研究與交流空間，進一步整合學界研究能量與產業需求，提升台灣半導體產業長期競爭力。

news.Title: 台股反彈助攻，新台幣逼近33關口後翻升，收32.895元
news.Content:
【財訊快報／陳孟朔】台灣新一波穩市措施週一(23日)上路，台股開低走高，新台幣兌美元也由貶轉升，終場收在32.895元，較上週五的32.936元升值4.1分或約0.12%。新台幣午間最弱觸及32.999元，距33元關卡僅一步之遙，其後回升至最強32.890元，收盤貼近日高，銀行間成交量為22億300萬美元。台股上週重挫17.5%，居全球主要股市跌幅前列，為1990年以來最慘單週。金管會週末宣布五項穩市措施，自週一起禁止投資人以低於前一交易日收盤價融券或借券賣出，並將最低融券保證金成數由130%提高至150%、暫停受理認售權證發行申請，同時鼓勵企業實施庫藏股及金融機構暫停出借股票。國安基金也證實已進場護盤。在政策支撐下，台股週一翻漲778.60點或2.16%，報36,811.89點。

新台幣上週累計貶值9.8分或0.3%，週線連三黑。據匯銀人士看法，外資動向仍是本週匯價的關鍵，預估新台幣將在32.8至33.1元區間整理。台股能否延續反彈，以及外資賣股後的匯出需求是否降溫，將影響新台幣能否延續升勢。

華僑銀行(OCBC)外匯策略團隊近期調高美元兌新台幣預測，理由是美元仍強、外資流出台股，加上市場對AI相關股票轉趨謹慎。該行指出，儘管台灣科技出口強勁、經常帳維持順差，出口商傾向保留外幣收入，限制了出口對新台幣的支撐。若外資賣壓緩和、美元轉弱，該行預期新台幣可在2027年稍晚收復部分失地。

news.Title: InterDigital Targets Double-Digit Revenue Growth as Streaming Push Accelerates
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in InterDigital, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

InterDigital is targeting double-digit growth in recurring revenue and an adjusted EBITDA margin of about 60%; its fourth-quarter guidance assumes only existing contracts, with new deals providing potential upside.

The company sees growth in PC licensing and streaming: it covers about 70% of the PC market and aims to expand that closer to 100%. Its Amazon licensing agreement is advancing faster than planned, with $60 million conservatively recognized while financial terms go to arbitration.

InterDigital is pursuing licensing disputes through arbitration and litigation, including a pending decision involving Lenovo and enforcement actions against TCL. Longer term, it is investing in wireless, video and AI research for future licensing opportunities.

InterDigital (NASDAQ:IDCC) CEO Liren Chen said the patent-licensing company is pursuing growth in streaming services and connected devices while targeting double-digit growth in recurring revenue and an adjusted EBITDA margin of around 60%.

Speaking at a company news event, Chen said InterDigital's fourth-quarter guidance was based solely on existing contracts, leaving any new agreements as potential additions. He said the company had already exceeded its annual guidance before accounting for any new business that might close in the fourth quarter.

→ 3 Dividend ETFs Offering Steadier Footing in a Shaky Market

InterDigital develops technology for wireless connectivity, video and artificial intelligence and licenses its patents to customers including Apple and Samsung. Chen described the business as a subscription-like model, with contracts generally lasting three to five years.

PCs and streaming offer room for growth

Chen said InterDigital has more than 85% penetration of the smartphone industry and about 70% coverage of the PC market after signing a top-five PC customer last quarter. Lenovo and HP are among the company's PC licensees, he said.

→ Cracks in the Crockery? Williams-Sonoma Insiders Sell Shares

InterDigital wants to expand its PC coverage closer to 100%, Chen said. Licensing economics for cellular-enabled PCs are "practically identical" to those for high-end smartphones, he said, while expectations are adjusted for devices that rely only on Wi-Fi.

Streaming is another area of focus. Chen said InterDigital agreed earlier this year to license Amazon's services and devices, including Amazon Prime services, with financial terms to be determined through arbitration. He said the company is conservatively recognizing $60 million in revenue under accounting guidance.

Story Continues

→ If NVIDIA Tightens Its Wallet, These 3 Stocks Could Feel It

Chen described the streaming effort as ahead of the schedule laid out in 2024, when InterDigital identified the business as a potential growth opportunity beyond 2030. He said video codec technology enables streaming providers to compress traffic while maintaining the user experience.

Licensing disputes and arbitration

Chen said more than 80% of the approximately 60 vendor agreements InterDigital has completed during his five years at the company were reached through negotiation. When financial terms cannot be agreed upon, the company prefers binding arbitration to litigation, he said.

In an arbitration involving Lenovo, a hearing was completed in October and the company is awaiting the arbitrator's decision, which Chen said he expects early next year. The proceeding covers both Lenovo's PC business and its smartphones sold under the Motorola brand.

InterDigital is also pursuing intellectual-property enforcement against TV maker TCL in Brazil, the United States and Europe. Chen said a Brazilian court issued a preliminary injunction concerning technology used in the HEVC video standard. He described the decision as a first step toward a license agreement and said InterDigital generally seeks global licenses while accounting for each customer's geographic footprint.

Long-term research and financial targets

Chen said InterDigital invests with a five- to 10-year horizon across wireless communications, video and AI. Potential future licensing opportunities include robotics, augmented and virtual reality, gaming and additional cloud applications, although he said many are years away.

The CEO pointed to the acquisition of London-based AI research company Deep Render as an example of how InterDigital evaluates deals for talent and technology. He said InterDigital has demonstrated an AI-native video codec and is working to persuade the industry to consider it for a future video coding standard.

Chen said historical research and development spending has been close to 50% of recurring revenue. He added that the company is seeking to balance investment with profitability rather than maximize margins.

Addressing concerns that InterDigital's results can be uneven, Chen said new licenses often include one-time payments for past use of its technology alongside ongoing fees. The company breaks out those catch-up payments from annualized recurring revenue, he said, adding that it has collected approximately $800 million in catch-up payments during his tenure.

About InterDigital (NASDAQ:IDCC)

InterDigital, Inc. is a technology research and development company whose work focuses on wireless communications, video and related digital technologies. Rather than selling consumer devices, the company develops technology and licenses its intellectual property to companies that make and use connected products and services. Its research spans cellular communications, including technologies used in 4G and 5G networks, as well as Wi-Fi, video compression and other areas. InterDigital holds patents covering technologies incorporated into industry standards and licenses its portfolio to companies around the world.

news.Title: 《台股盤後》量增收漲778點、日K翻紅，37K得而復失
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-23 16:12:30 新聞中心 發佈

台股今(23)日在盤初聯電、聯發科強勢表態，加上股價跌幅已深的台達電、台光電/南亞/台玻齊攻漲停、川湖反彈5.4%、記憶體股南亞科漲6.2%及群聯收漲停，同時融資已有效減肥的群創、友達收紅，搭配多頭適時點火台積電、日月光投控，雖創意僅打開跌停/鴻海收黑、且金控股下跌2.7%，不過央行全場力守台幣不破33元、台塑及華新及國巨*集團多有表態，同時NASDAQ電子盤反彈幅度擴大、韓股跌幅漸收斂，多頭信心明顯獲提振，加權指數終場以36811.89點作收、37K得而復失，上漲778.60點或2.16%、日K翻紅，成交量放大至1兆791.65億元。

輝達遭查帳消息導致其股價上週五暴跌14%，並再度拖累市場對AI股的持股信心，美國四大指數20日慘遭血洗、全面收黑，並以費半指數跌幅近11%最重、NASDAQ今年來漲幅則全數回吐轉為下跌。亞股方面，日本股市因適逢國定假日「勤勞感謝日」休市一天；韓國KOSPI指數雖伴隨有政府10兆韓元的救市政策、仍收跌3.31%。

台股今日開低走高、上下震盪幅度超過1600點。電子股普遍上揚，權王台積電於平盤附近震盪整理，終場收在2030元、上漲1.50%，聯發科、台達電、聯電、台光電、智邦攻上漲停，奇鋐、南亞科分別勁揚逾7%、6%，日月光投控、川湖、國巨*、欣興、緯穎紛紛走揚。然而，創意則逆勢下跌超過半根停板，鴻海、健策亦同步收黑。

觀察29大類股表現，今日以玻璃陶瓷類股表現最為亮眼、漲幅達9.01%，塑膠類股漲7.12%、電子零組件類股也有6.61%的漲幅，成為盤面最強三大族群。反觀金融保險類股則表現最弱、下跌2.65%，居家生活類股跌1.81%、貿易百貨類股也收跌1.80%，成為表現最差的三大族群。

三大法人動向方面，今日三大法人合計賣超511.77億元；其中，自營商賣超190.01億元，投信賣超32.28億元，外資及陸資賣超289.48億元。

news.Title: 命中率70%！施羅德2027十大預測一表看 台股供應鏈首度上榜即居冠
news.Content:
國際投資機構施羅德投資發布2027年全球投資關鍵十大預測，亞洲多元資產團隊最高主管近藤敬子今(23)日來台指出，在過去一年高度波動的環境下，團隊2026年十大預測命中率高達70%，今年更首度將台灣股票納入十大趨勢並喊出相對新興市場做多台股。面對美國通膨僵固與聯準會降息空間受限，傳統股債平衡配置已失去避險效果，投資人必須透過美股等權重布局、歐日銀行股、可轉債、工業金屬與避險基金打造多元資產第二曲線。

施羅德投信總經理陳思名表示，機構舉辦十大投資預測已超過10年，今年首度看到台股成為國際級投資機構關注的十大趨勢之一，這不僅反映人工智慧（AI）的長線成長趨勢，更凸顯台灣在AI科技供應鏈與全球產業的關鍵地位已被國際看見。在近期市場波動加劇下，施羅德堅持每年公開檢視前一年度預測成果，透過高度透明度與研究紀律為投資人指引方向。

近藤敬子回顧指出，兩年前美國總統大選川普當選後，為全球市場帶來許多地緣政治事件與劇烈波動，但過去12個月在正向成長環境帶動下，施羅德2026年十大投資預測仍成功命中7項，整體命中率高達70%。其中表現最強勁的核心正是亞洲科技類股，截至10月底累計漲幅仍高達15%以上，而台灣正處於這波成長浪潮的核心位置。

展望2027年宏觀經濟環境，近藤敬子提出三大關鍵觀察，首先是美國消費支出強勁且勞動市場維持低失業率與薪資增長，加上油價推升能源價格與核心服務通膨，預期聯準會不僅難以啟動降息，未來甚至仍有升息空間。此外，自2022年升息以來股債相關性已由負轉正，股市下跌時債券也跟著走跌，加上地緣政治衝突已從偶發事件變成新常態，靜態股債配置已無法滿足避險需求。

針對2027年股票市場的四大配置觀點，施羅德建議做多美國股票、相對新興市場做多台灣股票、做多醫療保健類投資，以及做多歐洲及日本銀行股。近藤敬子分析，美股高度集中於少數大型科技股，建議改採S&P 500等權重指數或主動選股廣泛布局；新興市場中相較韓國股市集中於兩大權值股，台灣擁有橫跨半導體、零組件與伺服器的完整AI價值鏈，近期市場震盪反而是空手投資人的買進良機。

在產業輪動與區域銀行方面，近藤敬子指出AI投資題材將從純科技股向外擴張，醫療保健產業在AI輔助下能大幅縮短新藥研發時間與成本，成為首要受惠者。同時為平衡科技股高波動，建議配置受惠於殖利率曲線趨陡與利差擴大的歐洲及日本銀行股，避開較易受資本市場波動影響的美國金融業，在經濟韌性支撐下穩健獲取獲利。

在固定收益與原物料配置上，施羅德看好可轉債與美國非投資等級債、證券化信用資產、新興市場當地貨幣債，並建議相對原油做多工業金屬。由於大型雲端服務供應商紛紛發行可轉債，投資人可藉此參與科技漲幅並兼顧下檔防禦；能源轉型與AI資料中心建置推升銅等工業金屬需求，在供給受限下具結構性支撐，反觀油價漲多後上行空間有限適合獲利了結。

面對股債失去避險效果的新局，施羅德也將避險基金與實質資產納入十大預測，透過避險基金可做多亦可放空的彈性提供下檔保護，並藉由不動產與基礎建設創造穩定抗通膨現金流。至於市場關注的黃金為何未入列，近藤敬子坦言高利率環境使無息資產吸引力下降，且近期黃金走勢與股市高度連動失去分散風險功能，因此更偏好股票與多元收益資產。

news.Title: Stock Market Sell-Off: 4 ETFs I'd Buy Now and Hold Through 2030
news.Content:
On Nov. 5, the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) fell 4.4%, its worst day since April 2025. The Nasdaq 100 declined 5.5% and has slid into correction territory where it's still about 18% below its all-time high.

With volatility rising, investors are clearly getting worried that the possibility of slower artificial intelligence (AI) spending could be a drag on economic growth and send U.S. stocks into a full-blown bear market.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

For the past few years, investors have relied heavily on tech, growth, and AI stocks to deliver big performance for their portfolios. But are those days finally coming to an end? Should people start seriously considering other areas of the market for future returns?

If you still have several years to invest, here are four ETFs that I'd look at right now.

Image source: Getty Images.

1. Vanguard S&P 500 ETF

The Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (NYSEMKT:VOO) is the standard bearer of core portfolio construction. It holds 500 of the largest U.S. companies and is one of the cheapest ETFs in the world to own. And it's one of the best choices available for long-term wealth building.

Yes, there's currently a bit of a concentration problem in the S&P 500. But it's important to consider that a function of where U.S. economic growth is coming from. If advances in healthcare become the next big revolution, the odds are good that its influence in the index will grow. It's a mechanism that helps rebalance toward what's working over time.

But if you're looking for an alternative to the currently top-heavy Vanguard S&P 500 ETF , keep reading.

Best for: Anyone starting from scratch.

Skip if: You already own tech elsewhere and want less AI risk.

2. Invesco QQQ ETF

The Invesco QQQ ETF (NASDAQ:QQQ) is broadly used as a large-cap tech proxy even though the fund is technically only two-thirds invested in the sector. But it's one of the best-performing funds of the past 15 years, even with the current 18% correction factored in.

If you believe that the AI build-out will continue for several more years (and I believe it will), you should be at least modestly excited about paying 18% less for shares of the Invesco QQQ ETF today than you did a month and a half ago. Even if growth slows here as anticipated, earnings growth has been strong and is likely to be for at least the next couple of years. Volatility in this sector is normal, which is why it's a better option if you plan on holding for several years instead of several months.

Story Continues

Best for: Investors with long time horizons and strong stomachs.

Skip if: You're near or in retirement.

3. Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF

The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (NYSEMKT:RSP) is a great option if you want to focus your exposure in U.S. large caps but want to avoid the high-tech concentration risk. This fund owns all the same companies in the S&P 500 index but puts them on a level playing field. Instead of a 35% concentration in tech, the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF has 10% to 16% allocation in five different sectors.

The investment case for this fund is strengthened by the fact that what we've seen over the past month hasn't been an outright sell-off in equities. It's been a rotation within equities. Healthcare, consumer staples, real estate, and utilities have all delivered positive gains, while tech is selling off. As long as earnings keep holding up and we don't see a major economic slowdown, this could easily be the better way to own the S&P 500.

Best for: VOO owners who want a less top-heavy portfolio.

Skip if: You want maximum exposure to AI winners.

4. Vanguard S&P Small-Cap 600 ETF

The Vanguard S&P Small-Cap 600 ETF (NYSEMKT:VIOO) is a little less intuitive but no less important to consider owning here. And choosing the S&P Small-Cap 600 index for small-cap exposure isn't an accident. Since it focuses on profitable small-cap companies instead of all small caps, you get a built-in quality tilt. That's important when investing in this area of the market where there are a lot of troubled companies.

Plus, small caps have lagged large caps for years, so they're plenty overdue for a lengthy run of leadership. Their earnings outlook has improved considerably, and valuations are much more attractive. It's an underinvested area in a lot of portfolios but one that has a lot of potential over the next several years.

Best for: Investors with long time horizons who can handle volatility.

Skip if: You'd panic at the idea of a 20% drop.

news.Title: 《美股主題週報》量子運算—NVDA、IBM、IONQ
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-23 16:00:35 數位內容中心 發佈

NVIDIA（NVDA.US）

近期NVIDIA宣布與IBM及Fermilab推進模組化量子－經典協同設計平台，並發布CUDA-Q量子糾錯（QEC）0.9.0。新解碼演算法TCBP-JOBS宣稱可帶來最高13,000倍加速，並把新量子電腦設計研究時間由12週縮短至45分鐘。

近期IBM公布Quantum Nighthawk r2，可在120個量子位元上執行最多7500次雙量子位元操作，速度達每秒100,000次取樣。相較IBM Quantum Heron，其吞吐量提升25倍，並持續把量子處理器納入超算工作流。

IonQ（IONQ.US）

11月IonQ揭露將以全股票方式收購Zero Trust資安公司Elisity，交易金額為11.5億美元，另含最高1.5億美元追加給付。資料並指出交易完成後備考現金部位為37億美元，並同步切入cryptographic migration需求。

AMD（AMD.US）

近期AMD擴大與PsiQuantum合作，將Instinct GPU、EPYC CPU與ROCm軟體平台整合至其平台，並計畫進行股權投資。另在Pelagos量子糾錯合作中，8顆GPU配置下，MI355X系統端到端吞吐量較1顆GPU提升6.23倍。

D-Wave Quantum（QBTS.US）

近期D-Wave Quantum的主軸落在付費應用落地。資料指出，NTT DOCOMO已把第2個由D-Wave驅動的工具導入日常營運，用於網路流量優化，並使某一類尖峰網路通訊量下降約三分之二，對應其Bookings年增611%。

Rigetti Computing（RGTI.US）

11月11日Rigetti Computing公布108量子位元系統Cepheus-1-108Q的中位雙量子位元閘保真度達99.5%，高於前一季約99.1%。同一資料並列出其2026年第三季營收為141.1萬美元，顯示硬體指標改善已先於收入放大。

news.Title: Futures bounce after AI selloff; Bessent on Nvidia probe - what’s moving markets
news.Content:
Investing.com - Futures linked to the main U.S. stock averages rally, ahead of a holiday-shortened trading week that will likely be overshadowed by anxieties over the artificial intelligence trade that triggered a steep selloff in technology stocks last week. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the U.S. is looking for answers about Nvidia's sale of chips to China under former CEO Jensen Huang, while Wall Street strategist Ed Yardeni once again slashes his year-end forecast for the S&P 500.

Our AI stock portfolio is beating the S&P 500 by 118%. Discover the stocks we're buying and the opportunities we're watching next. Exclusive for Yahoo! Finance readers: 55% off for Black Friday, plus an extra 15% at checkout. Subscribe today! »

1. Futures rally

U.S. stock futures bounced on Monday. By 01:20 ET (06:20 GMT), the Nasdaq 100 futures contract had risen by 740 points, or 2.9%, S&P 500 futures had added 143 points, or 2.1%, and Dow futures had gained 680 points, or 1.4%.

Jittery is perhaps an apt word to describe the current sentiment in financial markets after the Nasdaq Composite cratered by more than 5% on Friday, ending the worst week for the tech-heavy index since the 2020 COVID-19 crisis.

While there is debate over the use of the word "bubble" to describe the turmoil surrounding AI, air may well be leaking from what was once soaring enthusiasm for the nascent technology that has underpinned a 4-year-old bull market. Worries have abounded over the potential returns from massive -- sometimes debt-fueled -- expenditures on AI infrastructure, as well as increased regulation over the export of cutting-edge chips following the shock departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

Solid earnings from Nvidia last week were not enough to quell concerns over the chip designer's future after the exit of Huang, who built the company into a corporate lynchpin that supplied the key components powering AI systems and even bankrolled some of its own customers.

Anthropic's record-smashing initial public offering also did little to clear away the clouds around AI. The Claude chatbot maker's early pop after the first-time share sale fizzled out, although the stock remains above its IPO price.

Traders turned to the relative safety of U.S. Treasuries, with the benchmark 10-year bond yield sliding back below 5%. The rate-sensitive 2-year yield logged its biggest drop since August 2025 as investors stopped fully pricing in at least a quarter-point interest rate hike at the Federal Reserve's December meeting. The yields were both higher on Monday, guided by the climb in stock futures.

Story Continues

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent cautioned the Fed that overtightening monetary policy could imperil the American economy, pointing to the swoon in financial markets.

2. Bessent on Nvidia investigation

On Sunday, Bessent also hinted at an intensifying probe into Nvidia's dealings with China, a side of the business that has come under mounting scrutiny since revelations surfaced that Huang had an affair with an executive suspected of having ties to Chinese intelligence.

Speaking to CBS's "Face the Nation," Bessent said the government will look into Nvidia's chip sales to China and will discover who oversaw compliance at the company.

"We've been in touch with the ​temporary management, with the lead directors, with their lawyers, and we do ​need answers," Bessent said. He added that he had confidence Nvidia's board would deliver a "very fulsome" response.

Huang and Nvidia's general counsel are due to appear before U.S. Congressional committees early next month, while the FBI has opened investigations into the matter. Investors have proposed a class-action lawsuit against Nvidia.

Although U.S. President Donald Trump has backed Huang's reinstatement as CEO, the White House has reacted to the controversy by tightening restrictions on the remote access Chinese firms have to high-end chips made by companies like Nvidia.

Stop chasing stocks after they've already rallied. Find your next investment opportunity with AI stock picks, earnings insights, and market-moving news. Yahoo! Finance readers get an extra 15% off on top of the 55% off Black Friday price. Join today! »

3. Yardeni cuts year-end S&P prediction

Those harsher rules have hit chipmaking stocks especially hard, strategist Ed Yardeni flagged in a research note over the weekend cutting his predicted level for the benchmark S&P 500 at the end of the year for the second time in roughly two months.

Yardeni said he now sees the index, which has slumped into a technical correction, finishing 2026 at 7,500 points, compared to an already lowered target of 7,900 previously.

The S&P 500 closed at 6,910.39 on Friday. Since touching a record high on October 6, the average has dropped by 11.6%.

"We expected a pullback. It has turned into a correction," Yardeni said. In particular, he highlighted fears that tighter export controls could lower demand for chips, causing a price drop that sparks a chain reaction of falling valuation multiples, slower earnings growth, "or even an outright drop in earnings."

4. Hewlett Packard Enterprise to report

While the quarterly earnings season has unofficially come to an end, a trickle of reports are still set to be released this week.

Following the closing bell on Monday, Hewlett Packard is scheduled to report its fiscal fourth-quarter returns. Earlier this year, the company lifted its annual forecasts, citing AI-driven demand for its powerful servers.

However, in an interview with Reuters at the time, finance chief Marie Myers warned of a global bottleneck in memory chips, saying "demand is far outstripping supply."

For its fiscal 2027, HPE projected revenue growth of 13% to 17% and adjusted earnings per share growth of 16% to 20%.

5. Brent choppy

Oil prices oscillated around the flatline as traders weighed renewed attacks on commercial shipping and energy infrastructure across the Persian Gulf against signs of resilient crude exports.

Benchmark Brent crude futures hovered below $93 a barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate was around $83 a barrel. Both benchmarks lost ground last week, with Brent falling 4% and WTI declining 5%.

Iran-aligned Houthi militants in Yemen claimed an attack on a Saudi Arabian oil refinery over the weekend, while the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency reported multiple incidents involving commercial vessels in the Gulf and near the Strait of Hormuz.

Despite expectations of a growing global supply surplus, the latest developments underscored the ongoing threat to energy infrastructure and shipping despite efforts to negotiate an end to the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran.

news.Title: Arm vs. Marvell Technology: Which Artificial Intelligence Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
The expansion of artificial intelligence has pushed investors toward high-growth hardware providers. Choosing between Arm Holdings (NASDAQ:ARM) and Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) requires a careful look at their different roles in the chip ecosystem.

Arm provides the energy-efficient architecture used in almost every smartphone, while Marvell specializes in high-speed networking and data center infrastructure. Both companies are positioned to benefit from the rising demand for accelerated computing, yet they offer distinct risk profiles and valuation levels. This comparison helps you determine which path fits your investment strategy through 2027.

The case for Arm Holdings

In the rapidly evolving world of semiconductor stocks , Arm is unique because it did not actually manufacture chips historically. Instead, it designs the primary architecture and licenses its intellectual property. Its energy-efficient designs are in over 99% of smartphones, although the company is now expanding into cloud data centers and automotive applications, and plans to produce its own chips at last.

The company has shifted toward more complete chip designs to command higher royalty rates. This model creates a high-margin recurring revenue stream. Since it serves almost every major chipmaker, it sits at the heart of the tech sector.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached $5.5 billion, representing growth of 23.8% compared to the prior year. This expansion is supported by the adoption of its latest v9 architecture, which carries higher royalty rates than previous generations. The company reported net income of $936.0 million during this period.

As of its March 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 0.1x. This ratio compares total debt to shareholder equity to help you understand how much a company relies on borrowing. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term obligations with current assets, was a robust 6.0x.

In the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, free cash flow reached $979.0 million. Free cash flow is the cash remaining after a business pays for operations and equipment. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented roughly 69% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Marvell Technology

Marvell focuses on the infrastructure that makes modern data centers and telecommunications networks possible. The company specializes in data processing units, networking silicon, and storage controllers. Its recent growth is driven by the need for high-speed connectivity between servers in artificial intelligence clusters.

Story Continues

The company faces significant customer concentration, as its ten largest customers represented roughly 82% of net revenue in its latest annual report. One distributor accounted for approximately 37% of sales, which adds a layer of risk to the business. Despite this, its specialized silicon is vital for major cloud service providers.

In the 12 months ended Aug. 1, 2026, revenue reached $9.5 billion. This reflects a growth rate of 30.6% over the previous twelve-month period. During this same window, the company generated net income of $2.6 billion, showing significant improvement from previous years.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 0.3x, indicating a low reliance on debt. The current ratio stood at roughly 2.0x, indicating a healthy ability to meet short-term financial commitments.

In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, free cash flow was $1.4 billion. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 33.8% of operating cash flow.

Risk profile comparison

Arm faces risks related to the concentration of the smartphone market. If global phone sales slow, its royalty revenue could stagnate. The company also competes with open-source alternatives like RISC-V, which some manufacturers may prefer to avoid licensing fees. Furthermore, its heavy reliance on the licensing model means any loss of key partnerships with giants like Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) or Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM) could impact its long-term growth prospects.

Marvell Technology deals with significant customer concentration and geopolitical uncertainty. Trade restrictions and export controls regarding China have created supply chain challenges and impacted demand. The company is also navigating a massive $115 billion all-stock acquisition of Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE), which carries integration risks and potential shareholder dilution. Additionally, it recently settled patent litigation with Credo Technology Group Holding (NASDAQ:CRDO), highlighting the constant legal threats in the specialized silicon market.

Valuation comparison

Marvell Technology appears more attractive on a valuation basis, offering lower Forward P/E and P/S ratio multiples than Arm.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

For investors seeking exposure to the artificial intelligence boom, Arm and Marvell are two compelling stocks to own. Between the two, I would prioritize picking up shares of Marvell going into 2027.

Marvell sports a much lower share price valuation than Arm, providing a greater opportunity for a superior return. Arm arguably deserves the elevated valuation multiples because of its high-margin licensing moat. However, given its foray into making its own semiconductor chips, it risks compressing those robust margins due to manufacturing costs.

Marvell's stock was beaten down after it announced it was acquiring Lumentum. I think the acquisition is a smart move. Lumentum provides high-speed optical capabilities for transferring massive amounts of data, a key competitive advantage to winning AI customers. The appeal of Lumentum's solutions is illustrated by its sales of $1.3 billion for its fiscal first quarter, ended Sept. 26, which represented 137% year-over-year growth.

Moreover, Marvell's business is exploding. It generated revenue of $8.2 billion in its 2026 fiscal year, ended Jan. 31, 2026, and the company expects sales to soar to a range between $70 billion to $90 billion by its 2031 fiscal year. That growth does not include Lumentum's sales. With a lower valuation and spectacular, multi-year growth ahead, Marvell looks like the better stock to buy now.

news.Title: Google’s 2027 chip plan is bad news for Broadcom
news.Content:
Most people never think about what happens after they ask their phone a question, but Google had to. More than a decade ago, its engineers ran the numbers on voice search using the chips they had at the time.

If people used it for three minutes a day, "we would have had to double the number of Google data centers," Google Fellow Norm Jouppi wrote in a 2017 company blog post .

Instead of doubling its data centers, Google built its own chip, the Tensor Processing Unit.

The chip had been running in Google's data centers since 2015, according to the same post. By 2017, Google said TPUs sat behind every search query and powered products such as Google Photos.

The TPU also became a serious business for Broadcom (AVGO), which co-designs the chip with Google. J.P. Morgan analysts estimated in 2023 that Broadcom could earn $3 billion from Google that year, Reuters reported .

Also read: Marvell vs. Broadcom: the custom silicon shift

Now Google is pulling back on part of that business. Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo says Google has cut about 1 million Broadcom-designed chips from its 2027 shipment plans and is leaning more on MediaTek. Broadcom stock fell more than 11% on Friday, Nov. 20.

Wall Street has worried about this since 2023

The fear is not new. That same Reuters report from 2023 said Google executives had discussed dropping Broadcom as a chip supplier as early as 2027. The talks reportedly followed a standoff over chip prices, and Broadcom shares fell as much as 4.3% that day, according to Reuters.

Google pushed back. A spokesperson told Reuters, "They have been an excellent partner and we see no change in our engagement." The partnership held, and Broadcom kept working on new TPUs.

The doubts kept coming back. In August, Broadcom fell about 5% after Marvell Technology disclosed an expanded custom chip partnership with Google. Broadcom still holds an April deal to supply future generations of Google's custom chips through 2031, its strongest defense.

On Nov. 13, Rothschild & Co Redburn downgraded Broadcom to Hold and cut its price target to $398 from $595, according to Stock Analysis . A week later, the bear case got its numbers.

Google is putting its frontier models first

Kuo, of TF International Securities, laid out the details on X . The cut equals roughly 20% of 2027 shipments of the Broadcom-designed TPU 8i series, he wrote. Most of it falls on the higher-priced 8i Max, code-named Whalefish.

Google is not simply buying less. Kuo said it plans to ship more of its TPU 8t series, which MediaTek designs, though the details are not final.

Story Continues

His explanation matters more than the numbers. Google has repeatedly stressed that "frontier model development gets first call on compute," Kuo wrote. He tied the shift to tight supply and data center power limits.

Google built the 8t for heavy training work and says it can cut frontier model development "from months to weeks," according to a company blog post . The 8i handles fast inference. When power runs low, Google appears to prioritize feeding the chip that trains its next models.

Unlike the reported 2023 price fight, this looks like a contest for scarce power and supply. A lower price alone may not win it back.

The timing stings. In September, CEO Hock Tan said Broadcom's "engagement with Google has never been stronger". As of Friday, neither company had commented on Kuo's figures, which remain unconfirmed.

Broadcom stock is paying for its Google exposure

Friday's drop came during a broad chip selloff, with the PHLX Semiconductor Index down 8% by early afternoon. Broadcom still fell harder than the index.

Broadcom was worth about $1.66 trillion before the slide, Stock Analysis data show. The drop erased close to $200 billion.

Google's business helped build that value. Broadcom earned $38.3 billion on $89.1 billion in revenue over the past 12 months, according to Stock Analysis. A profit margin of nearly 43% made the TPU partnership worth defending.

More Broadcom:

Broadcom CEO says capital is 'available' after banks wavered

Jim Cramer praises Broadcom and recommends buying another iconic stock

Broadcom fought AT&T over VMware: Now a telecom giant is all in

Before Friday, the stock traded at about 20 times forward earnings, by Stock Analysis' count. That was modest for a fast grower, but it assumed 2027 would go according to plan.

Analysts expect Broadcom's revenue to climb about 65% in fiscal 2027, according to Stock Analysis forecasts . A 20% cut to one Google chip line lands largely in that fiscal year, so this quiet change matters more than its size suggests.

Wall Street has not turned on the stock. In mid-November, before Kuo's note, 40 of the 51 analysts tracked by Stock Analysis rated Broadcom a Strong Buy , eight a Buy , and three a Hold . Their average target of about $529 is now being tested.

Custom chips are no longer a one-partner business

Custom chips were long seen as the sticky corner of the AI trade, because a customer and its design partner build each one together. Google now spreads that work across Broadcom, MediaTek and Marvell, and it is willing to shift volume between partners.

Power is becoming a real gatekeeper. When a data center can draw only so many megawatts, chips compete for slots, and the slot goes to the top priority.

Broadcom reports fiscal fourth-quarter results on Dec. 9, its first chance to address Google's 2027 plans, according to Stock Analysis. The number to watch is not last quarter's revenue. It is whether management still sounds as sure about Google in 2027 as Tan did in September.

news.Title: Here's What a $1,000 Investment in Broadcom Stock Could Be Worth By 2035
news.Content:
Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) has become one of the biggest winners of the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure boom. Demand for its custom AI chips and networking gear is surging as tech giants pour billions of dollars into data centers. Last quarter, its AI semiconductor revenue rocketed 221% to $16.7 billion, and management expects that business to double in fiscal 2027 and again in fiscal 2028.

The stock, however, already prices in a lot of that success. While it currently trades about 30% below its 52-week high, it's still up nearly 250% over the past three years. Here's a look at what a $1,000 investment in Broadcom could be worth by 2035.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Broadcom's AI growth runway is enormous

Broadcom's fiscal 2026 third quarter was its best yet. Total revenue rose 86% to $29.6 billion, and AI semiconductor revenue climbed 221% to $16.7 billion. For the fourth quarter, the company guided to $21.7 billion in AI revenue, up 236%. Management has also laid out a path to roughly $58 billion of AI semiconductor revenue in fiscal 2026, $115 billion in fiscal 2027, and $230 billion in fiscal 2028. Custom accelerators for customers such as Anthropic and OpenAI drive that growth, along with the Ethernet switching and optical connections that link those chips together.

Broadcom isn't just an AI chip story. Its infrastructure software business, anchored by VMware, recorded nearly $8.8 billion in revenue last quarter, up 29%. That high-margin business generates growing recurring revenue for the company.

What could derail Broadcom's growth?

Investor expectations are as big as the AI opportunity. So are the risks. Broadcom depends on a small group of AI infrastructure customers, so a spending pullback by even one could hurt. AI spending could also cool once the current build-out peaks, and some customers may struggle to finance or monetize their data centers. Worries about AI financing and customer concentration have already driven a sell-off in chip stocks.

Margins are another watch item. As lower-margin custom accelerators account for a larger share of sales, margins could shrink. Competition from rivals and in-house chip designs also adds margin risk.

The question isn't whether AI infrastructure spending will grow over time. It's whether Broadcom can deliver the profits that investors already assume.

Story Continues

Here's what $1,000 in Broadcom could be worth by 2035

Broadcom recently traded around $325 per share. Analysts expect about $19.39 in adjusted earnings per share (EPS) for fiscal 2027, which puts the stock at roughly 17 times that estimate. Wall Street is bullish: none of the 50 analysts covering the company rate it a sell, and the average price target is over $525 a share. That estimate already assumes more than 60% upside from the recent price.

To cover all the bases, I modeled three scenarios to 2035:

Bear case: 4% annual EPS growth and a 14x earnings multiple.

Base case: 9% annual EPS growth and a 20x earnings multiple.

Bull case: 14% annual EPS growth and a 25x earnings multiple.

Here's what a $1,000 investment in Broadcom stock would be worth in 2035 under those scenarios:

Image source: The author.

All three scenarios include estimated cash dividends, without reinvestment, and assume a purchase at today's price. The base case is conservative next to management's own goal: CEO Hock Tan has said Broadcom is on target to exceed $30 of EPS in fiscal 2028, while my base case implies about $21 that year. However, even in a conservative base case, Broadcom could deliver a nearly 150% return. Meanwhile, the bull case is even stronger.

An attractive investment opportunity right now

Broadcom has a compelling opportunity in custom AI chips and networking, and its software business adds another source of profitable growth. Under my base case, a $1,000 investment in the semiconductor stock could grow to about $2,500 by 2035, a nearly 11% annualized total return. That's an attractive return, and it doesn't require Broadcom to sustain its extraordinary near-term growth indefinitely. While the outcome depends on the company meeting very ambitious earnings expectations, Broadcom looks like a compelling AI stock to buy right now.

news.Title: Micron Technology vs. Sandisk: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
news.Content:
The explosion of artificial intelligence has sparked a fierce race for high-performance memory. Deciding between Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) and Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) means choosing between two giants powering the next era of computing infrastructure.

Micron provides a massive range of memory and storage solutions across several high-growth markets. Sandisk focuses its expertise on advanced flash storage technologies for everything from mobile phones to massive server farms. Investors are comparing these companies as they look to capitalize on the sustained demand for data storage and processing power.

The case for Micron Technology

Micron Technology specializes in creating semiconductor memory and storage products like DRAM, NAND, and NOR. These components are essential for smartphones, data centers, and automotive electronics. The company operates 15 manufacturing sites and 21 design centers globally to meet this demand. The business relies heavily on its top 10 customers, which account for over 50% of revenue, and it primarily serves the data center market. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 3, 2026, revenue reached nearly $133.2 billion, representing a significant 256.3% increase over the prior period. This represents a massive jump from the $37.4 billion in revenue reported just one year earlier. Net income for this timeframe was approximately $85.0 billion. The rapid revenue growth is indicative of the broader expansion occurring among semiconductor stocks tied to modern computing.

As of its September 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 0.0x. This ratio measures total debt relative to shareholders' equity, and a value of zero suggests a very conservative use of borrowed funds. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term obligations with current assets, was roughly 3.3x. In the fiscal year ended Sept. 3, 2026, free cash flow totaled nearly $59.0 billion. Free cash flow is the cash a company generates after accounting for cash outflows to support operations and maintain its capital assets.

The case for Sandisk

Sandisk designs and produces advanced flash storage solutions for businesses and consumers. Its products are found in cloud infrastructure, AI systems, and connected edge devices like tablets and wearables. The company employs over 10,000 people and maintains a presence in more than 30 countries. Unlike many rivals, no single customer accounted for more than 10% of its revenue in 2026. This indicates a more diversified base of buyers compared to some industry peers.

Story Continues

In the 12 months ended Oct. 2, 2026, revenue reached approximately $29.0 billion. This marked a 272.4% increase compared to the previous 12-month period. The company also reported net income of nearly $19.4 billion during this time. This jump in profitability represents a significant recovery from the net losses the company reported in the previous two fiscal years. This turn toward profitability highlights the strong market reception for its latest storage technologies.

According to its July 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 0.0x. This level indicates the company currently does not rely on debt to fund its operations relative to its equity. The current ratio was close to 2.3x, showing a healthy ability to cover short-term financial obligations with its current assets. In the fiscal year ended July 3, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $11.5 billion. This cash generation provides the business with the flexibility to reinvest in its flash storage research and development.

Risk profile comparison

Micron Technology faces significant risks from the inherent cyclicality of the memory market, where selling prices can fluctuate wildly. The company is also highly dependent on a small group of large data center customers. Intense competition from firms like Samsung and SK hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) keeps pressure on innovation and pricing. Furthermore, trade restrictions involving China, as well as the CAC's restrictions on purchasing its products, could disrupt its global operations or limit its market access.

Sandisk relies heavily on strategic joint ventures, specifically with Flash Ventures and Kioxia , which can limit its ability to make independent operational decisions. The company also faces intense competition, which can lead to lower average selling prices for flash memory. Forecasting the specific needs of AI infrastructure remains difficult, creating a risk of supply imbalances. Additionally, its recent separation from Western Digital (NASDAQ:WDC) introduces ongoing regulatory and compliance complexities.

Valuation comparison

Sandisk carries a lower multiple relative to future earnings estimates, while Micron looks more attractive based on its current relationship with trailing sales.

The Forward P/E uses future earnings estimates to gauge value, while the P/S ratio measures market cap against sales over the past twelve months.

Which stock would I buy for 2027?

Both stocks need the same thing to go right: AI data center spending has to keep growing. Last week's AI sell-off, which dragged chip stocks lower and gave the S&P 500 its worst week in more than a year and a half, showed how quickly investors can doubt that. It hit Micron and Sandisk alike, so the drop tells you little about which business is better built.

What separates them is how each handles a slowdown. Micron runs its own fabs, sells across DRAM, HBM and NAND, and holds far more cash than debt, so it can keep investing through a rough patch. Sandisk runs leaner and spends little on capital, but it sells only NAND and relies on one joint venture partner for its wafers.

For a long-term investor, that points to Micron. Last week lowered the price you pay, but it didn't make memory any less cyclical, and drops like this can run further. Build a position in stages rather than all at once, and size it so another leg down wouldn't force you to sell. If your timeline is 2027 and beyond, the real test is whether you can hold through the swings, not whether you catch the bottom.
